title: "Running OpenCode Durably on Vercel"
description: "Run OpenCode v2 inside a Vercel Function with its session in a durable log, so a crashed turn resumes in a new function."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.036Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/opencode"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Running OpenCode Durably on Vercel

[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v2 keeps every change to a session as an event. `durable-harness` mirrors those events into a durable log, so any function can rebuild the session and continue it. On Vercel, OpenCode runs inside the function that runs the turn. To learn how durability works, see [Running Agent Harnesses Durably](/docs/agent-harnesses).

## Get started

- ### Install the packages
  ```bash package-manager
  npm i durable-harness @opencode/client@2.0.22 @opencode/core@2.0.22 @opencode/schema@2.0.22 @opencode/server@2.0.22
  ```
  `durable-harness` supports one OpenCode version at a time, so install the one it pins, and keep it exact in `package.json`, with no `^`. It checks the installed versions before each turn. You don't install `effect`: OpenCode's packages bring the version they need.

- ### Create the agent
  ```ts {3} filename="lib/agent.ts"
  import { opencode } from 'durable-harness/opencode';

  export const agent = opencode({ model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5' });
  ```
  The model must be in the model catalog of the OpenCode version `durable-harness` pins.

- ### Add the chat route
  `POST` sends a message and streams its turn as server-sent events, and `GET` reconnects to a turn that's still running:
  ```ts filename="app/api/chat/route.ts" framework=nextjs-app
  import { agent } from '@/lib/agent';
  import { withSessionOwnership } from '@/lib/session-ownership';

  export const { GET, POST } = withSessionOwnership({
    createRoute: (authorize) => agent.chatRoute({ authorize }),
    start: () => agent.sessions.start({ config: { traceAudience: 'unknown' } }),
  });
  ```
  ```ts filename="api/chat.ts" framework=other
  import { agent } from '../lib/agent.js';
  import { withSessionOwnership } from '../lib/session-ownership.js';

  export const { GET, POST } = withSessionOwnership({
    createRoute: (authorize) => agent.chatRoute({ authorize }),
    start: () => agent.sessions.start({ config: { traceAudience: 'unknown' } }),
  });
  ```
  Add the [`withSessionOwnership` helper](/docs/agent-harnesses/security#check-session-ownership) to `lib/session-ownership.ts` and implement its authentication and persistent ownership store. It records the owner before submitting a session's first message, and checks ownership on later messages and reconnects.
  > **⚠️ Warning:** In production (`NODE_ENV=production`, which includes every Vercel deployment),
  > a chat route without `authorize` refuses every request with a 401. To serve
  > anyone, pass `authorize: 'public'`. With `workspace: sandbox()`, every session
  > starts a Sandbox, so a public route also needs `allowPublicSandbox: true` and a
  > finite `sandbox({ budget: { sessionUsd } })`, which doesn't count OpenCode's
  > model calls.
  > Whoever can use the route runs the agent on your AI Gateway credits. See
  > [Security](/docs/agent-harnesses/security#chat-routes).
  POST `{ "text": "..." }` to start a session, and read its ID from the `x-session-id` header. Send `{ "sessionId": "...", "text": "..." }` for the next message. To redirect a running turn or reconnect to one, see [Steer a running turn](#steer-a-running-turn) and [Reconnect to a running turn](#reconnect-to-a-running-turn).

- ### Add the queue route
  [Vercel Queues](/docs/queues) delivers each turn to a queue route that runs it, with your plan's [maximum duration](/docs/functions/limitations#max-duration). Set it up in `vercel.json`, or let `durable-harness` write the same settings with `harnessFunctions()` in `vercel.ts` or with `withDurableHarness` on Next.js:
  #### vercel.json
  ```ts {3,6} filename="api/flow.ts"
  // A Vercel Function in your api directory. It imports the module that
  // makes your agent, so it can run the agent's turns.
  import '../lib/agent.js';
  import { flowHandler } from 'durable-harness';

  export const POST = flowHandler();
  ```
  ```json filename="vercel.json"
  {
    "functions": {
      "api/flow.ts": {
        "maxDuration": "max",
        "experimentalTriggers": [
          {
            "type": "queue/v2beta",
            "topic": "__harness_wkf_workflow_*",
            "retryAfterSeconds": 5,
            "initialDelaySeconds": 0
          }
        ],
        "includeFiles": "node_modules/{web-tree-sitter,tree-sitter-{bash,powershell}}/*.wasm"
      },
      "api/chat.ts": {
        "includeFiles": "node_modules/{web-tree-sitter,tree-sitter-{bash,powershell}}/*.wasm"
      }
    }
  }
  ```
  The trigger subscribes `api/flow.ts` to the queue. `includeFiles` adds OpenCode's parser files, which Vercel's file tracing doesn't find, to the functions that run turns: the queue route and the chat route. These paths are for npm. `npx durable-harness vercel-json --write` writes these entries into your `vercel.json`, with the paths of your install.
  #### vercel.ts
  ```ts {3,6} filename="api/flow.ts"
  // A Vercel Function in your api directory. It imports the module that
  // makes your agent, so it can run the agent's turns.
  import '../lib/agent.js';
  import { flowHandler } from 'durable-harness';

  export const POST = flowHandler();
  ```
  ```ts {8} filename="vercel.ts"
  // The same settings as in vercel.json, worked out from the packages you
  // installed when the project builds. Install @vercel/config as a dev
  // dependency.
  import type { VercelConfig } from '@vercel/config/v1';
  import { harnessFunctions } from 'durable-harness/vercel';

  export const config: VercelConfig = {
    functions: harnessFunctions(),
  };
  ```
  #### Next.js
  ```ts {11} filename="next.config.ts"
  // Writes the queue route and its trigger, includes OpenCode's parser files
  // in the routes that run turns, and keeps the harness packages out of the
  // server bundle. You don't add a queue route or a vercel.json.
  import type { NextConfig } from 'next';
  import { withDurableHarness } from 'durable-harness/next';

  const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
    // your existing config
  };

  export default withDurableHarness(nextConfig);
  ```
  If the app also uses the Workflow SDK, wrap both, as in `withWorkflow(withDurableHarness(nextConfig))`. The queue route then moves to `/.well-known/durable-harness/v1/flow` and needs one `vercel.json` entry, which `npx durable-harness vercel-json --write` adds, or `harnessFunctions()` in `vercel.ts`. Without it, the build on Vercel fails and prints the entry.

- ### Deploy
  ```bash
  vercel deploy
  ```
  On your machine, run `vercel link` and `vercel env pull` first, so model calls, and a Sandbox if your tools use one, authenticate with your project's OIDC token. For model calls alone, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` also works. `next dev` (or `vercel dev` for other frameworks) keeps sessions in `.workflow-data`, so add it to `.gitignore`. On its first request, it resumes the sessions a stopped server left mid-turn.

## Steer a running turn

Send a message with `"kind": "steer"` while a turn runs to redirect it. OpenCode adds it to the running turn at its next step. From the browser, post it to the chat route:

```ts {4}
await fetch('/api/chat', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ sessionId, text: 'Use TypeScript instead', kind: 'steer' }),
});
```

The response streams the turn, like any other message. From server code, such as a webhook, call `agent.sessions.send(sessionId, text, 'steer')`.

## Reconnect to a running turn

If the stream drops, the turn keeps running. Reconnect with `GET /api/chat?sessionId=...&cursor=...`, where the cursor is the last event `id` you read. The stream continues with the next event, with nothing lost or repeated. An `EventSource` on that URL reconnects by itself if its connection drops, and the stream ends with an `end` event when the turn is done:

```ts {1,7}
const source = new EventSource(`/api/chat?sessionId=${sessionId}&cursor=${lastEventId}`);

source.onmessage = (event) => {
  lastEventId = event.lastEventId;
  render(JSON.parse(event.data)); // your own UI
};
source.addEventListener('end', () => source.close());
```

If a crash cut off the turn, the turn resumes and the model starts its reply over. Before the new reply, the stream sends a `{ type: 'restart', text }` event: show its `text` in place of the turn's text so far, then append what streams after it.

## Run more than one agent

An app can make several agents, each with its own chat route. The queue route serves them all. Two agents of the same harness need a `name` each:

```ts {3-4} filename="lib/agents.ts"
import { opencode } from 'durable-harness/opencode';

export const reviewer = opencode({ name: 'reviewer', model: 'anthropic/claude-opus-5.5' });
export const fixer = opencode({ name: 'fixer', model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5' });
```

Keep each name stable, because sessions that already started carry it. Two agents with the same name throw when their module loads, so the build fails.

## Tools

OpenCode starts with no tools: the model can call only the tools you pass in `tools`. To give it OpenCode's own shell, read, write, edit, patch, glob, and grep, pass a `workspace`. They run OpenCode's own code on the workspace, never on your function's disk or in its processes, which other sessions on the instance share:

#### Virtual workspace

```bash package-manager
npm i just-bash
```

```ts {1,4} filename="lib/agent.ts"
import { virtual } from 'durable-harness';
import { opencode } from 'durable-harness/opencode';

export const agent = opencode({ model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5', workspace: virtual() });
```

The tools run on a [virtual workspace](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools#a-virtual-workspace-in-the-log) in your function, where commands can't reach the function's files, processes, or environment. Each call's file changes commit with its result in the session's log, so the files follow the session to any function, and a call that a crash interrupts changed nothing.

#### Vercel Sandbox

```bash package-manager
npm i @vercel/sandbox
```

```ts {1,4} filename="lib/agent.ts"
import { sandbox } from 'durable-harness';
import { opencode } from 'durable-harness/opencode';

export const agent = opencode({ model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5', workspace: sandbox() });
```

The tools run in the session's own [Vercel Sandbox](/docs/sandbox), with its files on a [Drive](/docs/sandbox/concepts/drives) at `/workspace` that lasts across turns. OpenCode itself stays in your function, and the Sandbox starts at the first tool call. A call that changes files or runs a command never runs twice: if a crash interrupts it, the model is told it may have partly run. On your machine, run `vercel link` and `vercel env pull` first: the Sandbox starts on Vercel, under the linked project. A long command early in a turn can be cut off: see [A Vercel Sandbox with a Drive](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools#a-vercel-sandbox-with-a-drive).

To give it only some of OpenCode's tools, pass `builtins`, as in `builtins: ['read', 'grep']`. Pass tools you write in `tools`, next to them. See [Tools, files, and documents](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools) and [Security](/docs/agent-harnesses/security).

## What happens when a function crashes

If the function running a turn fails with an error, another function resumes the turn right away. If it disappears without a trace, for example when it runs out of memory, the queue redelivers the turn once its message lease runs out, and the turn resumes from the log.

## Self-host on another World

On Vercel, sessions live in Vercel's World, and on your machine in `.workflow-data`. To keep them in another [World](https://workflow-sdk.dev/worlds), such as Postgres on your own servers, install it and set `WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD`:

```bash filename=".env"
WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD="@workflow/world-postgres"
WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL="postgres://user:password@host:5432/database"
```

To use a World you create, pass it as `opencode({ model, world })`, and start it yourself, as [Pass a World yourself](/docs/agent-harnesses/self-hosting#pass-a-world-yourself) shows.

For the tables, the server, and recovery at startup, see [Self-hosting durable agent harnesses](/docs/agent-harnesses/self-hosting).

## Limitations

- A running OpenCode session uses a lot of memory, so give the functions that run turns enough of it.
- OpenCode needs `effect` 4.0.0-rc.112, so an app that already depends on another version of `effect` can't use it yet.
- With other versions of OpenCode's packages or `effect`, a turn fails with a message that names the versions to install. The session is kept, and the next message works once they're installed.

## More resources

- [`durable-harness` on GitHub](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness)
- [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai)

# Running Agent Harnesses Durably on Vercel

An agent harness is the loop around a model: its prompts, its tools, and how it manages context. These guides show how to run Pi, fx, OpenCode, eve, Claude Code, and Codex on Vercel so a conversation survives a crash, a function timeout, or a redeploy.

## How it works

Most harnesses keep a turn in the memory of the process running it, so when that process dies mid-turn, the turn dies with it. Run the same turn without durability and with `durable-harness`, then kill the function to compare how each recovers:

Each session lives in a durable log: the conversation, the turn in flight, and every model call and tool call. Each turn has a message on [Vercel Queues](/docs/queues) behind it, so when its function dies, a new function reads the log and continues where the first one stopped:

[Video: A support agent refunds an order. Its function dies mid-reply, and a new function resumes the turn from the session's log.](https://7nyt0uhk7sse4zvn.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/front/docs/agent-harnesses/durable-harness-recovery.mp4)

*A support agent refunds an order, and its function dies while it writes the
reply. A new function reads the session's log, runs only the interrupted
model call again, and the customer is refunded once.*

A turn can also outlive one function's [maximum duration](/docs/functions/limitations#max-duration), and a client that disconnects reconnects to a turn that's still running.

You keep your harness, its options, and its tools. The log lives behind a **World**, the storage interface of the open-source [Workflow SDK](https://workflow-sdk.dev): Vercel's World on Vercel, files on your machine, or another World, such as Postgres, on your own servers. See [Self-hosting](/docs/agent-harnesses/self-hosting).

## Choose a harness

| Harness                                                         | Package                               | Runs in                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Pi](/docs/agent-harnesses/pi)                                  | `durable-harness/pi-durable` or `/pi` | Your function, with files in a virtual workspace or a Sandbox |
| [fx](/docs/agent-harnesses/fx)                                  | `libfx`                               | Your function, with files in a virtual workspace or a Sandbox |
| [OpenCode](/docs/agent-harnesses/opencode)                      | `durable-harness/opencode`            | Your function, with files in a virtual workspace or a Sandbox |
| [eve](/docs/agent-harnesses/eve)                                | `eve`                                 | An eve app, durable by default                                |
| [Claude Code](/docs/agent-harnesses/claude-code) (experimental) | `durable-harness/claude-code`         | A Vercel Sandbox                                              |
| [Codex](/docs/agent-harnesses/codex) (experimental)             | `durable-harness/codex`               | A Vercel Sandbox                                              |

The `durable-harness` guides share one setup: the agent, a chat route, and the route that [Vercel Queues](/docs/queues) delivers turns to. Each guide shows this set up for Next.js and other frameworks. fx and eve are durable on their own, so their guides use `libfx` and `eve` directly. Each guide uses [AI Gateway](/docs/ai-gateway) for model calls. On Vercel, the harnesses authenticate with the deployment's [OIDC token](/docs/oidc). Locally, run `vercel link` and `vercel env pull`. For model calls alone, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` also works, but a Sandbox needs the linked project.

## What's durable

The session is durable: the conversation, the turn in flight, and recovery after a crash. Every harness starts with no tools. Your own tools run in your function, and each has a replay rule that says what happens to a call a crash interrupts. Commands and files that the model picks never run on your function's disk: they run in a virtual workspace that the session's log keeps, or in a Vercel Sandbox with a Drive. Claude Code and Codex run only in a Sandbox. See [Security](/docs/agent-harnesses/security) and [Tools, files, and documents](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools).

## Recovery

If the function running a turn fails with an error, another function resumes the turn right away. If the function disappears without a trace, for example when it runs out of memory or its instance is lost, the queue redelivers the turn once its message lease runs out. Either way, the turn resumes from the log:

- **A model call that was running** runs again.
- **A tool call that was running** runs again or not, by its [replay rule](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools#what-happens-to-a-tool-call-after-a-crash): Pi reruns a `'safe'` tool. Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode tell the model it is safe to repeat. Other interrupted calls come back to the model as possibly run.
- **Between calls**, nothing runs again. Every call the log has an outcome for is read back from it, and the turn goes on from the next step. A call that finished just before the crash may not be in the log yet, and then it counts as running.

## More resources

- [`durable-harness` on GitHub](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness)
- [Observability for durable agent harnesses](/docs/agent-harnesses/observability)
- [Security for durable agent harnesses](/docs/agent-harnesses/security)
- [Self-hosting durable agent harnesses](/docs/agent-harnesses/self-hosting)
- [Vercel Workflows](/docs/workflows)
- [Workflow SDK Worlds](https://workflow-sdk.dev/worlds)

# Running Pi Durably on Vercel

[Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) is an open-source agent harness. `durable-harness` makes it durable on Vercel in one of two ways, and in both, a turn that loses its function continues in a new one. We recommend `durable-harness/pi-durable`. To learn how durability works, see [Running Agent Harnesses Durably](/docs/agent-harnesses).

## Choose a variant

- **`durable-harness/pi-durable`** (recommended) runs Pi 1.0's `Harness`, from `@earendil-works/pi-durable`, on a storage in the log, so each of Pi's commits is an event in the log. You write Pi's own code.
- **`durable-harness/pi`** runs Pi's agent loop, `Agent` from `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core`, and records each model call and tool call as a step in the log.

|                | `durable-harness/pi-durable` (recommended)                     | `durable-harness/pi`                     |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Best for       | Most Pi agents                                                 | Agents that need only Pi's agent loop    |
| What you write | Your Pi code, on `openWorldStorage()`                          | `pi({ model, tools })`                   |
| Pi features    | Pi's full Harness, including extensions, compaction, and forks | Pi's agent loop and tools                |
| Speed          | Each step waits for the log, so turns are slower               | Durability adds little latency           |
| Steering       | Steering from another request takes the session over           | Redirect a running turn from any request |
| Reconnecting   | The stream resends the response in progress from its start     | The stream continues from the last event |

Pick `durable-harness/pi-durable`. It's Pi 1.0's full Harness, so your agent gets Pi's extensions, compaction, and forks, and if you already have Pi code, only the storage changes. Pick `durable-harness/pi` for Pi's agent loop alone: durability adds less latency, and it works like every other harness in these guides.

## Get started with `durable-harness/pi-durable`

- ### Install the packages
  ```bash package-manager
  npm i durable-harness @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/chord @earendil-works/pi-ai
  ```

- ### Register your Harness
  Write your Pi code as Pi's documentation shows, or keep the code you have. In a module of its own, pass the function that opens your Harness to `resumeWith`, so the queue route can reopen a session after a crash:
  ```ts {10} filename="lib/pi.ts"
  import { BACKGROUND_CONTEXT as ctx } from '@earendil-works/chord/context';
  import { createRegistry, Harness, type Storage } from '@earendil-works/pi-durable';
  import { gatewayModels, GATEWAY_PROVIDER, resumeWith } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable';

  const models = gatewayModels(); // or your own pi-ai models
  const registry = createRegistry(); // your tools and extensions

  export { ctx };
  export const agent = { model: { provider: GATEWAY_PROVIDER, modelId: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5' } };
  export const open = resumeWith((storage: Storage) => Harness.open(storage, { models, registry }, ctx));
  ```
  `gatewayModels()` gives Pi its models through [AI Gateway](/docs/ai-gateway) with the deployment's credentials. A build on Vercel fails if the app opens pi-durable sessions and no module calls `resumeWith`.

- ### Open sessions on the World
  Where Pi would open SQLite, JSONL, or memory storage, open the session's storage on the World:
  ```ts {4}
  import { openWorldStorage } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable';
  import { open } from './pi';

  const storage = await openWorldStorage(sessionId);
  const harness = await open(storage);
  ```
  Without an ID, `openWorldStorage` starts a new session, and `storage.sessionId` is its ID. Everything after that is Pi's own API: `harness.root()`, `root.submit()`, `submission.wait()`, and `watchEvents()`.

- ### Add the chat route
  Your app sends each message to a chat route and reads the turn back from it. `chatRoute` is that route, ready-made: `POST` submits a message to Pi and streams the turn as server-sent events, `GET` reconnects to a turn that's still running, and it keeps the request alive until Pi's work is done. It has the same events and `authorize` rule as every chat route in these guides:
  ```ts filename="app/api/chat/route.ts" framework=nextjs-app
  import { chatRoute, openWorldStorage } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable';
  import { withSessionOwnership } from '@/lib/session-ownership';
  import { agent, ctx, open } from '@/lib/pi';

  export const { GET, POST } = withSessionOwnership({
    createRoute: (authorize) => chatRoute({ open, agent, authorize }),
    start: async () => {
      const storage = await openWorldStorage(undefined, { traceAudience: 'unknown' });
      const sessionId = storage.sessionId;
      await storage.close(ctx);
      return { sessionId };
    },
  });
  ```
  ```ts filename="api/chat.ts" framework=other
  import { chatRoute, openWorldStorage } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable';
  import { withSessionOwnership } from '../lib/session-ownership.js';
  import { agent, ctx, open } from '../lib/pi.js';

  export const { GET, POST } = withSessionOwnership({
    createRoute: (authorize) => chatRoute({ open, agent, authorize }),
    start: async () => {
      const storage = await openWorldStorage(undefined, { traceAudience: 'unknown' });
      const sessionId = storage.sessionId;
      await storage.close(ctx);
      return { sessionId };
    },
  });
  ```
  Add the [`withSessionOwnership` helper](/docs/agent-harnesses/security#check-session-ownership) to `lib/session-ownership.ts` and implement its authentication and persistent ownership store. It records the owner before submitting a session's first message, and checks ownership on later messages and reconnects.
  > **⚠️ Warning:** In production (`NODE_ENV=production`, which includes every Vercel deployment),
  > a chat route without `authorize` refuses every request with a 401. To serve
  > anyone, pass `authorize: 'public'`. With `env: sandboxEnv()`, every session
  > starts a Sandbox, so a public route also needs `allowPublicSandbox: true` and a
  > finite `sandboxEnv({ budget: { sessionUsd } })`, which doesn't count Pi's own
  > model calls.
  > Whoever can use the route runs the agent on your AI Gateway credits. See
  > [Security](/docs/agent-harnesses/security#chat-routes).
  POST `{ "text": "..." }` to start a session, and read its ID from the `x-session-id` header. Send `{ "sessionId": "...", "text": "..." }` for the next message. To redirect a running turn or reconnect to one, see [Steer a running turn](#steer-a-running-turn) and [Reconnect to a running turn](#reconnect-to-a-running-turn).

  If your app already has a route that runs Pi, you can keep it instead: open the session with `openWorldStorage`, submit with Pi's `root.submit()`, and close the Harness once the submission finishes. Closing with work left hands it to the queue route.

- ### Add the queue route
  [Vercel Queues](/docs/queues) delivers each turn to a queue route that runs it, with your plan's [maximum duration](/docs/functions/limitations#max-duration). Set it up in `vercel.json`, or let `durable-harness` write the same settings with `harnessFunctions()` in `vercel.ts` or with `withDurableHarness` on Next.js:
  #### vercel.json
  ```ts {3,6} filename="api/flow.ts"
  // A Vercel Function in your api directory. It imports the module that
  // calls resumeWith, so it can run the agent's turns.
  import '../lib/pi.js';
  import { flowHandler } from 'durable-harness';

  export const POST = flowHandler();
  ```
  ```json filename="vercel.json"
  {
    "functions": {
      "api/flow.ts": {
        "maxDuration": "max",
        "experimentalTriggers": [
          {
            "type": "queue/v2beta",
            "topic": "__harness_wkf_workflow_*",
            "retryAfterSeconds": 5,
            "initialDelaySeconds": 0
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
  ```
  The trigger subscribes `api/flow.ts` to the queue. `npx durable-harness vercel-json --write` writes this entry into your `vercel.json`.
  #### vercel.ts
  ```ts {3,6} filename="api/flow.ts"
  // A Vercel Function in your api directory. It imports the module that
  // calls resumeWith, so it can run the agent's turns.
  import '../lib/pi.js';
  import { flowHandler } from 'durable-harness';

  export const POST = flowHandler();
  ```
  ```ts {8} filename="vercel.ts"
  // The same settings as in vercel.json, worked out from the packages you
  // installed when the project builds. Install @vercel/config as a dev
  // dependency.
  import type { VercelConfig } from '@vercel/config/v1';
  import { harnessFunctions } from 'durable-harness/vercel';

  export const config: VercelConfig = {
    functions: harnessFunctions(),
  };
  ```
  #### Next.js
  ```ts {10} filename="next.config.ts"
  // Writes the queue route and its trigger, and keeps the harness packages
  // out of the server bundle. You don't add a queue route or a vercel.json.
  import type { NextConfig } from 'next';
  import { withDurableHarness } from 'durable-harness/next';

  const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
    // your existing config
  };

  export default withDurableHarness(nextConfig);
  ```
  If the app also uses the Workflow SDK, wrap both, as in `withWorkflow(withDurableHarness(nextConfig))`. The queue route then moves to `/.well-known/durable-harness/v1/flow` and needs one `vercel.json` entry, which `npx durable-harness vercel-json --write` adds, or `harnessFunctions()` in `vercel.ts`. Without it, the build on Vercel fails and prints the entry.

- ### Deploy
  ```bash
  vercel deploy
  ```
  On your machine, run `vercel link` and `vercel env pull` first, so model calls, and a Sandbox if your tools use one, authenticate with your project's OIDC token. For model calls alone, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` also works. `next dev` (or `vercel dev` for other frameworks) keeps sessions in `.workflow-data`, so add it to `.gitignore`. On its first request, it resumes the sessions a stopped server left mid-turn.

### Differences from Pi's own storage

- **A request that opens a session takes it over.** The request that had it open stops at its next write: the World refuses the write, so nothing more of that request lands. The new request continues the turn from where the agent was. If two requests open a session at the same time, the first to write keeps it. `chatRoute` handles both: the first request's stream follows the session's log to the end, and a request that lost retries once with the same `requestId`. In a route of your own, open the session again after a refused write, and submit again with the same `requestId`.
- **Background work finishes after you close.** `submission.wait()` and `waitForIdle()` don't wait for background work, such as compaction or a background subagent. When you close the Harness, the queue route finishes that work. `chatRoute` waits for it.
- **A request stays alive while its work runs.** It ends when the work is done, or after `recoverAfterMs` (120 seconds by default) with no commit.
- **A long silence can look like a crash.** If a session commits nothing for `recoverAfterMs` while it has unfinished work, another function can take it over. A tool that writes no output or a model call that streams nothing can do that, so raise the limit for them with `openWorldStorage(sessionId, { recoverAfterMs })`.
- **Give Pi's tools a workspace, not your function.** Pi's `env`, where its tools run, isn't saved with the session. Don't give it your function's directory or processes, such as a `NodeExecutionEnv`: other sessions on the same instance could reach them, and a resumed turn can run on another instance without them. Use `virtualEnv()`, a [virtual workspace](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools#a-virtual-workspace-in-the-log), or `sandboxEnv()`, the session's Vercel Sandbox, as [Tools](#tools) shows. See [Security](/docs/agent-harnesses/security).

## Get started with `durable-harness/pi`

- ### Install the packages
  ```bash package-manager
  npm i durable-harness @earendil-works/pi-agent-core @earendil-works/pi-ai
  ```

- ### Create the agent

  ```ts {3} filename="lib/agent.ts"
  import { pi } from 'durable-harness/pi';

  ```

- ### Add the chat route

  > model calls.

To redirect a running turn or reconnect to one, see [Steer a running turn](#steer-a-running-turn) and [Reconnect to a running turn](#reconnect-to-a-running-turn).

- ### Add the queue route
  [Vercel Queues](/docs/queues) delivers each turn to a queue route that runs it, with your plan's [maximum duration](/docs/functions/limitations#max-duration).   ```json filename="vercel.json"

  The trigger subscribes `api/flow.ts` to the queue. `npx durable-harness vercel-json --write` writes this entry into your `vercel.json`.
  #### vercel.ts

## Steer a running turn

Send a message with `"kind": "steer"` while a turn runs to redirect it. From the browser, post it to the chat route:

```ts {4}
await fetch('/api/chat', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ sessionId, text: 'Use TypeScript instead', kind: 'steer' }),
});
```

The response streams the turn, like any other message.

#### pi-durable

Pi takes the steer after the tool calls that are running. A steer from another request takes the session over, and that request continues the turn. From server code, such as a webhook, submit with Pi's `whenBusy: 'steer'`:

```ts {7}
import { openWorldStorage } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable';
import { agent, ctx, open } from './pi';

const harness = await open(await openWorldStorage(sessionId));
const root = await harness.root(ctx, { agent });
await root.submit(
  { type: 'input', content: 'Use TypeScript instead', requestId: crypto.randomUUID(), whenBusy: 'steer' },
  ctx,
);
await harness.close(ctx); // the queue route finishes the turn
```

#### pi

The steer reaches the model at the turn's next model call, whichever request sends it. From server code, such as a webhook, call `agent.sessions.send`:

```ts {3}
import { agent } from './agent';

await agent.sessions.send(sessionId, 'Use TypeScript instead', 'steer');
```

## Reconnect to a running turn

If the stream drops, the turn keeps running.

#### pi-durable

With `chatRoute`, reconnect without a cursor. The response starts again from the beginning of the model response in progress, so replace the text you showed for it. A `rewind` event means a model call restarted, so drop its text. When the session is idle, `GET` answers 204:

```ts {1}
const source = new EventSource(`/api/chat?sessionId=${sessionId}`);

source.onmessage = (event) => render(JSON.parse(event.data)); // your own UI
source.addEventListener('end', () => source.close());
```

#### pi

Reconnect with `GET /api/chat?sessionId=...&cursor=...`, where the cursor is the last event `id` you read. The stream continues with the next event, with nothing lost or repeated. An `EventSource` on that URL reconnects by itself if its connection drops, and the stream ends with an `end` event when the turn is done:

```ts {1,7}
const source = new EventSource(`/api/chat?sessionId=${sessionId}&cursor=${lastEventId}`);

source.onmessage = (event) => {
  lastEventId = event.lastEventId;
  render(JSON.parse(event.data)); // your own UI
};
source.addEventListener('end', () => source.close());
```

## Run more than one agent

An app can make several agents, each with its own chat route. The queue route serves them all.

#### pi-durable

Give each Pi setup a `name`, and pass it to `resumeWith`:

```ts {3-4} filename="lib/pi.ts"
const openHarness = (storage: Storage) => Harness.open(storage, { models, registry }, ctx);

export const openReviewer = resumeWith(openHarness, { name: 'reviewer' });
export const openFixer = resumeWith(openHarness, { name: 'fixer' });
```

Open each one's sessions with the same name, as in `openWorldStorage(sessionId, { name: 'reviewer' })`, or `chatRoute({ open: openReviewer, agent, name: 'reviewer', authorize })`. Keep each name stable, because sessions that already started carry it.

#### pi

Give each agent a `name`:

```ts {3-4} filename="lib/agents.ts"
import { pi } from 'durable-harness/pi';

export const reviewer = pi({ name: 'reviewer', model: 'anthropic/claude-opus-5.5' });
export const fixer = pi({ name: 'fixer', model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5' });
```

Keep each name stable, because sessions that already started carry it. Two agents with the same name throw when their module loads, so the build fails.

## Tools

#### pi-durable

A Harness has no tools until you install them in your registry. Install Pi's own `read`, `write`, `edit`, and `bash` with `CodingTools` from `durable-harness/pi-durable`, and give them a workspace with `virtualEnv()`. Add tools of your own with Pi's `defineTool()`:

```ts {7-16,20-21,26} filename="lib/pi.ts"
import { BACKGROUND_CONTEXT as ctx } from '@earendil-works/chord/context';
import { Type } from '@earendil-works/pi-ai';
import { createRegistry, defineExtension, defineTool, Harness, type Storage } from '@earendil-works/pi-durable';
import { CodingTools, gatewayModels, GATEWAY_PROVIDER, resumeWith, virtualEnv } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable';
import { getOrder } from './orders'; // your own code

const getOrderTool = defineTool({
  name: 'get_order',
  description: 'Looks up an order',
  replay: 'safe', // safe to run again after a crash
  parameters: Type.Object({ id: Type.String() }),
  execute: async (args, api) => {
    api.output(JSON.stringify(await getOrder(args.id)));
    return {};
  },
});

const models = gatewayModels();
const registry = createRegistry();
registry.install(CodingTools); // Pi's read, write, edit, and bash
registry.install(defineExtension({ name: 'orders', tools: [getOrderTool] }));

export { ctx };
export const agent = { model: { provider: GATEWAY_PROVIDER, modelId: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5' } };
export const open = resumeWith((storage: Storage) =>
  Harness.open(storage, { models, registry, env: virtualEnv() }, ctx),
);
```

`virtualEnv()` is a [virtual workspace](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools#a-virtual-workspace-in-the-log) at `/workspace`. Each call's file changes commit with its result in the session's log, so the files follow the session to any function. Also install `just-bash`. After a crash, a `'safe'` tool runs again, and any other comes back to the model as interrupted.

To run the same tools in the session's own [Vercel Sandbox](/docs/sandbox), pass `sandboxEnv()` instead, and install `@vercel/sandbox`:

```ts {1,4}
import { sandboxEnv } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable';

export const open = resumeWith((storage: Storage) =>
  Harness.open(storage, { models, registry, env: sandboxEnv() }, ctx),
);
```

The files are on a [Drive](/docs/sandbox/concepts/drives) at `/workspace` that lasts across turns, and the Sandbox starts at the first tool call. Pi itself stays in your function. A command that a crash interrupts may have partly run, so it comes back to the model as interrupted and never runs again. On your machine, run `vercel link` and `vercel env pull` first: the Sandbox starts on Vercel, under the linked project.

#### pi

`durable-harness/pi` starts with no tools. Pass Pi `AgentTool`s or `HostTool`s as `tools`, each with a `replay` rule. `createCodingTools(virtual())` adds Pi's own `read`, `bash`, `edit`, and `write` on a [virtual workspace](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools#a-virtual-workspace-in-the-log):

```ts {5-11,15} filename="lib/agent.ts"
import { virtual, type HostTool } from 'durable-harness';
import { createCodingTools, pi } from 'durable-harness/pi'; // also install just-bash
import { getOrder } from './orders'; // your own code

const getOrderTool: HostTool = {
  name: 'get_order',
  description: 'Looks up an order',
  replay: 'safe', // safe to run again after a crash
  inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id'] },
  execute: async ({ id }) => JSON.stringify(await getOrder(id)),
};

export const agent = pi({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5',
  tools: [...createCodingTools(virtual()), getOrderTool],
});
```

After a crash, a `'safe'` tool runs again, and any other comes back to the model as interrupted.

To run Pi's tools in the session's own [Vercel Sandbox](/docs/sandbox), pass `sandbox()` instead, and install `@vercel/sandbox`:

```ts {1,4}
import { sandbox } from 'durable-harness';
import { createCodingTools, pi } from 'durable-harness/pi';

export const agent = pi({ model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5', tools: createCodingTools(sandbox()) });
```

The files are on a [Drive](/docs/sandbox/concepts/drives) at `/workspace` that lasts across turns, and the Sandbox starts at the first tool call. Pi itself stays in your function. What a call wrote stays on the Drive even if a crash interrupts it, so after a crash `read` runs again, and `bash`, `edit`, and `write` come back to the model as interrupted. On your machine, run `vercel link` and `vercel env pull` first: the Sandbox starts on Vercel, under the linked project. A long command early in a turn can be cut off: see [A Vercel Sandbox with a Drive](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools#a-vercel-sandbox-with-a-drive).

For files, documents, and how to write tools safely, see [Tools, files, and documents](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools).

## What happens when a function crashes

Both variants read finished steps back from the log, run the model calls and `'safe'` tools that were running again, and return an interrupted `'never'` tool to the model as possibly run. If the function running a turn fails with an error, another function resumes the turn right away. If it disappears without a trace, for example when it runs out of memory, the queue redelivers the turn once its message lease runs out, and the turn resumes from the log. With `durable-harness/pi-durable`, the storage stands behind its own commits: a turn that dies silently resumes within `recoverAfterMs` of its last commit, and right away if the Harness closed with work left.

## Self-host on another World

Both variants keep sessions on the environment's World: Vercel's World on Vercel, and `.workflow-data` on your machine. To keep them in another [World](https://workflow-sdk.dev/worlds), such as Postgres on your own servers, install it and set `WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD`:

```bash filename=".env"
WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD="@workflow/world-postgres"
WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL="postgres://user:password@host:5432/database"
```

To use a World you create, pass it to `durable-harness` and start it yourself:

#### pi-durable

```ts {10,12,14-15} filename="lib/pi.ts"
import { BACKGROUND_CONTEXT as ctx } from '@earendil-works/chord/context';
import { createRegistry, Harness, type Storage } from '@earendil-works/pi-durable';
import { createWorld } from '@workflow/world-postgres';
import { registerQueue } from 'durable-harness';
import { gatewayModels, GATEWAY_PROVIDER, resumeWith } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable';

const models = gatewayModels();
const registry = createRegistry();

export const world = createWorld({ connectionString: process.env.WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL! });
export const agent = { model: { provider: GATEWAY_PROVIDER, modelId: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5' } };
export const open = resumeWith((storage: Storage) => Harness.open(storage, { models, registry }, ctx), { world });

registerQueue(world); // before start: deliver durable-harness's queue to this process
await world.start();
```

Open its sessions on the same World, with `openWorldStorage(sessionId, { world })` or `chatRoute({ open, agent, world, authorize })`.

#### pi

```ts {6,8,10} filename="lib/agent.ts"
import { createWorld } from '@workflow/world-postgres';
import { recoverSessions, registerQueue } from 'durable-harness';
import { pi } from 'durable-harness/pi';

export const world = createWorld({ connectionString: process.env.WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL! });
export const agent = pi({ model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5', world });

registerQueue(world); // before start: deliver durable-harness's queue to this process
await world.start();
await recoverSessions(world); // resume the sessions a stopped server left mid-turn
```

An agent with its own World takes its queue deliveries through `agent.handler`, so mount `agent.handler` instead of `flowHandler()` at the queue route.

For the tables, the server, and recovery at startup, see [Self-hosting durable agent harnesses](/docs/agent-harnesses/self-hosting).

## More resources

- [`durable-harness` on GitHub](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness)
- [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)

title: "Security for Durable Agent Harnesses"
description: "What a durable agent harness may run in your Vercel Function, where the commands and files a model picks run instead, and how to write tools that a model calls safely."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.036Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/security"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Security for Durable Agent Harnesses

An agent harness runs what a model decides. On Vercel, the harness runs in your function, and with [Fluid compute](/docs/fluid-compute) one instance serves many requests at once, including turns of other sessions and other users. This page covers what may run in your function, where everything else runs, and how to write tools that a model calls safely. It applies to every harness in these guides.

## The rule

Your function runs only code you wrote. The model chooses arguments, never code that runs in your function. Commands and files that the model picks run in a virtual workspace or a [Vercel Sandbox](/docs/sandbox), never on your function's disk, in its processes, or with its environment.

A tool that runs a real shell or uses the real disk in your function would let one session's model read another session's files, and your function's environment variables, such as `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` and the deployment's [OIDC token](/docs/oidc). A prompt injection in a web page, a file, or a message can steer a model to try.

## Where each harness runs

| Harness                                          | Runs in               | Commands and files                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [Pi](/docs/agent-harnesses/pi), both variants    | Your function         | Your own tools, a virtual workspace, or a Vercel Sandbox                 |
| [fx](/docs/agent-harnesses/fx)                   | Your function         | Your own tools, a virtual workspace, or a Vercel Sandbox                 |
| [OpenCode](/docs/agent-harnesses/opencode)       | Your function         | Your own tools, a virtual workspace, or a Vercel Sandbox                 |
| [Claude Code](/docs/agent-harnesses/claude-code) | A Vercel Sandbox only | Your own tools, or its own with `builtins: true`, on the session's Drive |
| [Codex](/docs/agent-harnesses/codex)             | A Vercel Sandbox only | Your own tools, or its own with `builtins: true`, on the session's Drive |

Every harness starts with no tools, so an agent can do only what you give it. For eve, see the [eve documentation](/docs/frameworks/agents/eve).

### Why Claude Code and Codex run only in a Sandbox

Pi, fx, and OpenCode are libraries built to serve many sessions in one process. OpenCode ships an embedded server and a profile that replaces its process spawner and its access to the host's files, and `durable-harness` replaces them the same way. Claude Code and Codex are command-line tools built for one user, and they keep their state on disk. Today's versions can be kept apart, but they ship often, and nothing promises that the next version won't keep state that one session leaves behind for another.

So Claude Code and Codex run only in a Vercel Sandbox, one per session, where their own tools, once you turn them on with `builtins: true`, work on the session's [Drive](/docs/sandbox/concepts/drives). `durable-harness` refuses to run them anywhere else, including in a function or on a server of your own.

### What runs in the Sandbox

The Sandbox holds no secrets: no World credential, no AI Gateway key, and no OIDC token. Your function still drives the turn and writes the session's log:

- **Your function makes the model calls.** The CLI's requests go to your function, which sends them to AI Gateway with your deployment's credentials.
- **Your app reads the log.** Your app's browser streams the turn from the session's log, as it does for every harness, so a new Sandbox doesn't interrupt it.
- **Only your function reaches the CLI.** The Sandbox's port accepts a connection only with a token your function arms for each attach.
- **Sandbox time has a cap.** A session's Sandbox runs for at most 4 hours by default. Model spend has no cap unless you set one with `sandbox({ budget })`, per turn or per session.
- **Files live on the Drive.** A session that moves to a new Sandbox keeps its files and resumes its conversation. The Drive isn't transactional: a command that a crash interrupts may have partly run, and the model is told.

> **💡 Note:** With Vercel Sandbox, set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` to a key that can only call
> AI Gateway. Without it, your function authenticates model calls with the
> project's OIDC token, which also opens the session's World and the Sandbox
> API.

## Your own tools

A tool you write, a `HostTool`, runs in your function, with its environment variables and its access to your systems. Your tool's code is trusted. Its arguments aren't: the model writes them, and a prompt injection can steer them.

- **Validate every argument** against what the tool allows. A JSON schema tells the model what to send, but it doesn't stop it from sending something else.
- **Authorize from the session, never from an argument.** Find the session's user from your own records, not from an argument such as `userId`.
- **Keep arguments out of a shell, `eval`, and file paths.** To give the model a shell or files, use a [virtual workspace or a Sandbox](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools#files). Don't give a harness a tool or environment that spawns a process or touches the real disk in your function, such as Pi's `NodeExecutionEnv`.
- **Be careful what a result returns.** It reaches the model, the person using the session (it streams to their browser), the session's log, and the session's trace in [Agent Runs](/docs/agent-harnesses/observability). With Claude Code and Codex, it also reaches the session's Sandbox, where the CLI keeps its transcript and the model's commands can read it.
- **Make side effects run once.** For a tool that changes something, such as a refund or an email, use `replay: 'never'`, so a call never runs again after a crash, and pass the system it calls an idempotency key, so a call the model repeats doesn't repeat the effect.

This tool checks that the order belongs to the session's user before it returns anything, and returns only the fields the model needs:

```ts {10-11,13} filename="lib/tools.ts"
import type { HostTool } from 'durable-harness';
import { getOrder, ownerOfSession } from './orders'; // your own code

export const getOrderTool: HostTool<{ id: string }> = {
  name: 'get_order',
  description: "Looks up one of the signed-in user's orders",
  replay: 'safe',
  inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id'] },
  async execute({ id }, io) {
    const userId = await ownerOfSession(io.ctx.runId); // from your records, not the arguments
    const order = typeof id === 'string' ? await getOrder(id) : undefined;
    if (!order || order.userId !== userId) return 'No order with that ID.';
    return JSON.stringify({ id: order.id, status: order.status }); // only what the model needs
  },
};
```

## Commands and files the model picks

Give the model a shell and files in one of two places. [Files](/docs/agent-harnesses/tools#files) compares them:

- **A virtual workspace** runs [just-bash](https://www.npmjs.com/package/just-bash) on a virtual filesystem in your function. Its commands can't reach your function's files, processes, or environment. It isn't a virtual machine, so give work that needs one, such as installing packages or running a build, a Sandbox.
- **A Vercel Sandbox** is a virtual machine for the session, with its files on a Drive. Its commands run apart from your function and from every other session.

## What these controls don't cover

- **A Sandbox allows all outbound traffic by default.** A prompt-injected model can send its own session's files to the internet. To block it, pass `network: 'deny-all'` to `sandbox()`, or allow only the hosts your agent needs with `network: { allow: ['registry.npmjs.org'] }`.
- **Codex can fall back to full access in its Sandbox.** With `builtins: true`, Codex runs commands under its own sandbox inside the Sandbox when it can start one. When it can't, its commands run with full access to the Sandbox. The Sandbox still holds no secrets, but the model's commands can then make model calls through your function directly, on your AI Gateway credits, within any `budget` you set.
- **Provider-hosted tools ignore the Sandbox's network.** Tools that the model provider runs, such as web search, reach the internet from the provider, whatever the Sandbox allows.
- **Images in your UI are a channel too.** If your UI renders a remote image from model output, such as a markdown image, the browser requests a URL the model chose, without a click. Render no remote images from model output, or load them on click.
- **Settings you pass are visible to the model.** Every environment variable you give a Sandbox can be read by the model's commands, so pass none that's secret.

## Chat routes

Whoever can use a chat route runs your agent, on your AI Gateway credits. In production (`NODE_ENV=production`, which includes every Vercel deployment), a chat route without `authorize` refuses every request with a 401. `authorize` checks that the caller may use the session. `authorize: 'public'` serves anyone, so pass it only for an agent whose tools anyone may use.

Every session of Claude Code or Codex starts a Sandbox, and so does every session of Pi or OpenCode whose tools run in one, so anyone who can use a public route can make you pay for Sandboxes. For an agent whose sessions start a Sandbox, `authorize: 'public'` also needs `allowPublicSandbox: true` and a finite `sandbox({ budget: { sessionUsd } })`. Without them, the route throws when it's created. Each session checks again before its Sandbox starts, so a route built some other way can't skip the check. pi-durable's `chatRoute` takes the same options, and checks them before each session's Sandbox starts.

`sessionUsd` caps model spend only for Claude Code and Codex, whose model calls go through `durable-harness`. Pi's and OpenCode's model calls run in your function, so `sessionUsd` doesn't count them: cap each session's Sandbox time with `sandbox({ budget: { vmSeconds } })`, and limit model spend in your `authorize`, or with an [AI Gateway budget](/docs/ai-gateway/observability-and-spend/budgets) on the project.

An fx agent's chat route is your own, so with `fxTools(sandbox())`, check who's calling yourself. Its model calls are libfx's own, so `sessionUsd` doesn't count them: cap each session's Sandbox time with `sandbox({ budget: { vmSeconds } })`.

### Check session ownership

Signing in doesn't grant access to every session. The chat routes in these guides use `withSessionOwnership` to authenticate each request, save a new session's owner before submitting its first message, and reject requests for sessions owned by someone else. It accepts `POST { "text": "..." }` for a new session and preserves the chat route's streaming response and `x-session-id` header.

Add this helper to `lib/session-ownership.ts`. Implement `getUser`, `ownsSession`, and `saveSession` in your app's `lib/auth.ts`: `getUser(request)` returns the authenticated user or no user, `saveSession(user, sessionId)` persists ownership, and `ownsSession(user, sessionId)` checks that record. Use persistent storage shared by all your app's instances, and derive the user from authentication, never from the request body:

```ts filename="lib/session-ownership.ts"
import type { ChatAuthorize, ChatRoute } from 'durable-harness';
import { getUser, ownsSession, saveSession } from './auth';

export function withSessionOwnership({ createRoute, start }: {
  createRoute: (authorize: ChatAuthorize) => ChatRoute;
  start: () => Promise<{ sessionId: string }>;
}): ChatRoute {
  const chat = createRoute(async (request, sessionId) => {
    const user = await getUser(request);
    if (!user) throw new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });
    if (!sessionId || !(await ownsSession(user, sessionId))) {
      throw new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });
    }
  });

  return {
    GET: chat.GET,
    async POST(request) {
      const user = await getUser(request);
      if (!user) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });

      let input: unknown;
      try {
        input = await request.json();
      } catch {
        return new Response('Expected a JSON body', { status: 400 });
      }
      if (!input || typeof input !== 'object' || Array.isArray(input)) {
        return new Response('Expected a JSON object', { status: 400 });
      }
      const body = input as Record<string, unknown>;
      if (typeof body.text !== 'string' || !body.text) {
        return new Response('text is required', { status: 400 });
      }
      if (body.sessionId !== undefined && typeof body.sessionId !== 'string') {
        return new Response('sessionId must be a string', { status: 400 });
      }
      if (body.kind !== undefined && (
        typeof body.kind !== 'string' ||
        !['prompt', 'steer', 'followUp'].includes(body.kind)
      )) {
        return new Response('Invalid message kind', { status: 400 });
      }
      if (body.requestId !== undefined && typeof body.requestId !== 'string') {
        return new Response('requestId must be a string', { status: 400 });
      }

      if (body.sessionId === undefined) {
        const { sessionId } = await start();
        await saveSession(user, sessionId);
        body.sessionId = sessionId;
      }

      const headers = new Headers(request.headers);
      headers.set('content-type', 'application/json');
      headers.delete('content-length');
      return chat.POST(new Request(request.url, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers,
        body: JSON.stringify(body),
        signal: request.signal,
      }));
    },
  };
}
```

`start()` must create an empty session without submitting a prompt or opening the Harness. If saving ownership fails, the helper doesn't submit the message. Authentication remains required during local development. For a custom World or a named Pi setup, use the same World and name when creating the session and the chat route.

- [Vercel Sandbox](/docs/sandbox)
- [Fluid compute](/docs/fluid-compute)
- [just-bash](https://www.npmjs.com/package/just-bash)

title: "Self-Hosting Durable Agent Harnesses"
description: "Keep durable agent harness sessions in another World, such as Postgres, and run Pi, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and fx on your own servers."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.038Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/self-hosting"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Self-Hosting Durable Agent Harnesses

A durable harness keeps its sessions behind a World, the storage and queue interface of the open-source [Workflow SDK](https://workflow-sdk.dev). On Vercel, that's Vercel's World. To run the harnesses on your own servers, or to keep sessions in your own database, choose another World. This page covers Pi, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode with `durable-harness`, and fx with `libfx`. For eve, see [Self-host eve](https://eve.dev/docs/guides/deployment/self-hosting).

> **⚠️ Warning:** These integrations are experimental: `durable-harness` is in beta. Package
> names and APIs can change before they're stable.

## How the World is chosen

`durable-harness` chooses the World the way the Workflow SDK does:

| Where the app runs                         | World                                                                                  | Sessions live in                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| On Vercel                                  | `@workflow/world-vercel`                                                               | [Vercel Workflows](/docs/workflows) storage                     |
| Anywhere else                              | `@workflow/world-local`                                                                | Files in `WORKFLOW_LOCAL_DATA_DIR`, by default `.workflow-data` |
| Anywhere, with `WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD` set | The World it names: `vercel`, `local`, or a package such as `@workflow/world-postgres` | That World's storage                                            |

The local World keeps sessions in files on one machine. It suits development, and a single server whose disk persists. To run more than one server, or to keep sessions in a database, use the [Postgres World](https://workflow-sdk.dev/worlds/postgres). fx chooses its World on its own: see [fx](#fx).

## Self-host with Postgres

Use Node.js 22 or later and a Postgres database.

- ### Install the Postgres World
  ```bash package-manager
  npm i @workflow/world-postgres
  ```
  Use `@workflow/world-postgres` 5.0.4 or later.

- ### Create its tables
  ```bash
  WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL="postgres://user:password@host:5432/database" npx --package=@workflow/world-postgres bootstrap
  ```
  It's safe to run again. Run it again after you upgrade the package.

- ### Point your app at it
  ```bash filename=".env"
  WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD="@workflow/world-postgres"
  WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL="postgres://user:password@host:5432/database"
  AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY="your-ai-gateway-api-key"
  ```
  Without `WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL`, the World reads `DATABASE_URL`. Create an [AI Gateway API key](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/api-keys) for model calls outside Vercel. This key does not authenticate Vercel Sandbox requests; those need separate [Sandbox credentials](#claude-code-codex-and-opencode).

- ### Start the World with your server
  #### Next.js
  `withDurableHarness` already serves the queue route. To resume the sessions a stopped server left mid-turn as soon as the server starts, rather than on its first request, start the World in `instrumentation.ts`. Import every module that makes an agent first, so the World's deliveries reach it:
  ```ts {3,5} filename="instrumentation.ts"
  export async function register() {
    if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME !== 'nodejs') return;
    await import('./lib/agent'); // every module that makes an agent
    const { getWorld } = await import('durable-harness');
    await getWorld();
  }
  ```
  #### Your own server
  Serve the chat route and the queue route from any server that takes a Fetch API `Request`. `vercel.json` and `vercel.ts` don't apply on your own server, so it mounts the queue route itself. This one uses Hono's Node.js server and the [session ownership helper](/docs/agent-harnesses/security#check-session-ownership) to authenticate callers and save each new session's owner before submitting a message:
  ```bash package-manager
  npm i hono @hono/node-server
  ```
  ```ts filename="server.ts"
  import { serve } from '@hono/node-server';
  import { FLOW_ROUTE, flowHandler, getWorld } from 'durable-harness';
  import { agent } from './lib/agent.js';
  import { withSessionOwnership } from './lib/session-ownership.js';

  const chat = withSessionOwnership({
    createRoute: (authorize) => agent.chatRoute({ authorize }),
    start: () => agent.sessions.start({ config: { traceAudience: 'unknown' } }),
  });
  const flow = flowHandler();

  await getWorld(); // start the World before the first request

  serve({
    port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000),
    fetch(request) {
      const { pathname } = new URL(request.url);
      if (pathname === '/api/chat') return request.method === 'POST' ? chat.POST(request) : chat.GET(request);
      if (pathname === FLOW_ROUTE) return flow(request); // the queue route
      return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });
    },
  });
  ```
  `await getWorld()` creates the World, consumes the queue in this process, and resumes the sessions a stopped server left mid-turn. Without it, that happens on the first request that reaches an agent.
  > **⚠️ Warning:** In production (`NODE_ENV=production`, which includes every Vercel deployment),
  > a chat route without `authorize` refuses every request with a 401. To serve
  > anyone, pass `authorize: 'public'`. Whoever can use the route runs the agent
  > on your AI Gateway credits.

- ### Run it
  #### Next.js
  ```bash
  next build && next start
  ```
  #### Your own server
  In an ES module project (`"type": "module"` in `package.json`), run it with your `.env` loaded. For example, install [tsx](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tsx) with `npm i -D tsx` and run `node --env-file=.env --import tsx server.ts`, or compile it first.

  You can run several servers on one database: each one consumes the queue, and the World lets one server at a time drive a session.

## Pass a World yourself

Every `durable-harness` factory takes a `world`, so you can create the World in your own code. A World you create is yours to start: register `durable-harness`'s queue on it, start it, and resume the sessions a stopped server left:

```ts {6,8,10} filename="lib/agent.ts"
import { createWorld } from '@workflow/world-postgres';
import { recoverSessions, registerQueue } from 'durable-harness';
import { pi } from 'durable-harness/pi';

export const world = createWorld({ connectionString: process.env.WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL! });
export const agent = pi({ model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5', world });

registerQueue(world); // before start: deliver durable-harness's queue to this process
await world.start();
await recoverSessions(world); // resume the sessions a stopped server left mid-turn
```

An agent with its own World takes its queue deliveries through its own `agent.handler`, so mount `agent.handler` instead of `flowHandler()` at the queue route.

## Run more than one server

Every process that starts the World on your database does one of two things before `world.start()`, which re-enqueues every open session:

- **It makes your agents.** It imports the module that creates them and starts the World with `getWorld()`, or with `registerQueue(world)` for a World you pass in, so it runs their turns itself.
- **It forwards the queue.** A process that makes no agents, such as a queue worker of its own or the Workflow SDK's worker, calls `forwardQueue(world)`. It sends `durable-harness`'s queue to your app's queue route, and runs none of it:

```ts {5} filename="worker.ts"
import { createWorld } from '@workflow/world-postgres';
import { forwardQueue } from 'durable-harness';

const world = createWorld(); // reads WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL
forwardQueue(world); // before start(), which re-enqueues every open session
await world.start();
```

Set `WORKFLOW_LOCAL_BASE_URL` in the worker to your app's base URL, or `PORT` when the app runs on the same machine. A process that starts the World and does neither sends open sessions to the Workflow SDK's queue route, which refuses them.

- **Mount the queue route where the worker sends it.** Your app serves `flowHandler()` at `/.well-known/durable-harness/v1/flow` (`FLOW_ROUTE`), as the server above does, or `agent.handler` for an agent with its own World. On Next.js without the Workflow SDK, `withDurableHarness` serves it at `/.well-known/workflow/v1/flow`, so pass that path: `forwardQueue(world, { route: '/.well-known/workflow/v1/flow' })`. For a path of your own, pass `{ route }`, or set `DURABLE_HARNESS_FLOW_ROUTE` in both processes.
- **A worker can start before your app.** Its deliveries fail and are retried, so open sessions resume late, once the app is back.
- **Protect the queue route.** The Postgres World doesn't authenticate its deliveries. Restrict the route at your network edge, such as a reverse proxy or firewall, and leave `/.well-known/durable-harness/` out of middleware matchers.
- **One server drives a session at a time.** When a second server starts driving a session, the World refuses the first one's next write, so the first one stops.

## Each harness on another World

### Pi

`durable-harness/pi-durable` uses the environment's World, as above. To pass your own, give it to both `resumeWith` and `openWorldStorage`. `durable-harness/pi` works as above:

```ts {5,7}
import { createWorld } from '@workflow/world-postgres';
import { openWorldStorage, resumeWith } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable';

export const world = createWorld({ connectionString: process.env.WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL! });
export const open = resumeWith((storage: Storage) => Harness.open(storage, { models, registry }, ctx), { world });

const storage = await openWorldStorage(sessionId, { world });
```

### Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode

OpenCode works as above. Its own tools work only on a virtual workspace or a Vercel Sandbox, never on your server's disk. Claude Code and Codex run only in a Vercel Sandbox, on your own server too: your server drives the turn and writes the session's log, and the CLI runs in a Sandbox with the session's files on a Drive. Give `sandbox()` a Vercel access token and the team and project its Sandboxes belong to, as the [Claude Code guide](/docs/agent-harnesses/claude-code#self-host-on-another-world) shows. See [Security](/docs/agent-harnesses/security#why-claude-code-and-codex-run-only-in-a-sandbox).

### fx

libfx chooses where sessions live by itself: Vercel's World on Vercel, and files in `FX_SESSIONS_DIR`, by default `$TMPDIR/libfx/sessions`, in Node.js elsewhere. It doesn't read `WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD`. To keep sessions in another World, pass it to `world()` from `libfx/durable-world`:

```ts {7,13} filename="lib/agent.ts"
import { createFxAgent } from 'libfx';
import { world } from 'libfx/durable-world';
import { createWorld } from '@workflow/world-postgres';
import { tools } from './tools';

// libfx's own queue topics and jobs, apart from the rest of the app.
const sessions = createWorld({ connectionString: process.env.WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL!, namespace: 'libfx', jobPrefix: 'libfx_' });
await sessions.start();

export const agent = createFxAgent({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5',
  tools,
  durability: world(sessions, { queueDurable: true }),
});
```

libfx never starts or closes a World you pass in, so start it before the agent's first prompt, and close it after `agent.close()`. The Postgres World delivers to the agent in its process. For a World that delivers over HTTP, mount `agent.wakeHandler()` where it delivers.

### eve

eve selects its World in `agent.ts`. See [Self-host eve](https://eve.dev/docs/guides/deployment/self-hosting).

## Limitations

- Give each app its own database or data directory, and its own worker. A server that starts resumes every open session it finds, so apps that share one would run each other's sessions with their own agents. A separate `WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_JOB_PREFIX` doesn't keep two apps apart.
- The Postgres World is a reference implementation. It doesn't authenticate its routes or encrypt its data, and it isn't tuned for scale. Read [its documentation](https://workflow-sdk.dev/worlds/postgres) before you run it in production.
- The Postgres World runs its queue worker in a long-lived process, so it doesn't run in Vercel Functions. On Vercel, use Vercel's World.

## More resources

- [Workflow SDK Worlds](https://workflow-sdk.dev/worlds)
- [Postgres World](https://workflow-sdk.dev/worlds/postgres)
- [`durable-harness` on GitHub](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness)
- [`libfx` on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/libfx)
