# Deployments

Create and inspect deployments for your projects, including their files and build output. You can cancel a deployment or access a protected deployment to verify its content.

## `cancel_deployment`

Cancel a deployment.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type    | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | string  | Yes      | The unique identifier of the deployment.                    |
| `teamId`      | string  | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string  | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | unknown | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

## `create_deployment`

Create a [deployment](/docs/deployments) from a Git source or files. Put `name`, `project`, `gitSource` or `files`, and `projectSettings` inside `requestBody`. Use `requestBody.target: "production"` for production, or omit `target` for a preview. Follow the tool's input schema for file formats and build settings.

**Sample prompt:** "Create a preview deployment of my project's main branch"

## Parameters

| Parameter                       | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `forceNew`                      | string | No       | Forces a new deployment even if there is a previous similar deployment. Set to `1` to bypass deployment deduplication and always trigger a fresh build. Allowed values: `"0"`, `"1"`.                                                                                                               |
| `skipAutoDetectionConfirmation` | string | No       | Set to `1` to skip framework auto-detection and proceed without confirmation. By default, if Vercel detects a framework that differs from the project setting, the API returns a `400` asking you to confirm. Use this to suppress that check in automated pipelines. Allowed values: `"0"`, `"1"`. |
| `teamId`                        | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `slug`                          | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `requestBody`                   | object | Yes      | Request body for this tool.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## `deploy_to_vercel`

Deploy a small, simple project from inline file contents only when the Vercel CLI is unavailable and no usable remote git repository exists, or the user explicitly requests an inline file deployment. Prefer the Vercel CLI for local projects. It reads and uploads files directly without reproducing source as model output. If the intended source is pushed to a repository's production branch, use create\_git\_project. Do not reconstruct medium or large projects, binary assets, or dependency trees in tool arguments. This remote tool cannot read local paths or attachments. Files with actual contents are required. Limits: 300 files, 3 MiB per file, 4 MiB total encoded contents. Creation is asynchronous. Poll get\_deployment until READY, ERROR, or CANCELED before reporting the build outcome.

## Parameters

| Parameter         | Type             | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------- | ---------------- | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target`          | string           | Yes      | -       | Required. "preview" for a shareable non-production URL, or "production" to go live. Allowed values: `"preview"`, `"production"`.                                                                                           |
| `name`            | string           | Yes      | -       | Project name. Vercel creates the project if it does not already exist.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `files`           | Array\<object> | Yes      | -       | Required non-empty array of source files with their actual contents. A project name or local path alone cannot deploy. Do not include node\_modules, .git, .env files, or secrets. Vercel installs dependencies and builds. |
| `teamId`          | string           | No       | -       | The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `projectSettings` | object           | No       | -       | Optional build settings. Omit to let Vercel auto-detect the framework.                                                                                                                                                     |

This workflow is available on root connections that expose `deploy_to_vercel`. Project-scoped connections do not register it. Use `create_deployment` when your scoped connection exposes that tool.

## `get_access_to_vercel_url`

Create a temporary [shareable link](/docs/deployment-protection/methods-to-bypass-deployment-protection/sharable-links) that grants access to protected Vercel deployments.

| Parameter | Type   | Required | Default | Description                                                              |
| --------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `teamId`  | string | No       | -       | The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource.                |
| `url`     | string | Yes      | -       | The full URL of the Vercel deployment (e.g. "https://myapp.vercel.app"). |

**Sample prompt:** "myapp.vercel.app is protected by auth. Please create a shareable link for it"

## `get_deployment`

Get a [deployment](/docs/deployments) by ID or hostname.

| Parameter         | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrUrl`         | string | Yes      | The unique identifier or hostname of the deployment.                                                                                                |
| `withGitRepoInfo` | string | No       | When `true`, the response includes the `gitSource` object with the commit SHA, branch name, and connected repository metadata. Defaults to `false`. |
| `teamId`          | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                                                                                                  |
| `slug`            | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                                                                                         |

**Sample prompt:** "Get details about my latest production deployment"

## Workflow connection parameters

If your connection exposes the smaller workflow tool list, use these parameters instead. Follow your connection's tool schema.

| Parameter | Type   | Required | Default | Description                                               |
| --------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrUrl` | string | Yes      | -       | The unique identifier or hostname of the deployment.      |
| `teamId`  | string | Yes      | -       | The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource. |

## `get_deployment_build_logs`

Get the build logs for a deployment by ID or URL, to investigate why a build failed. Returns the most recent lines by default (where build errors appear). Use errorsOnly to see just the failing lines. Omit since and until for latest logs. Use since to narrow the window, and omit until when the end should be the current time.

## Parameters

| Parameter    | Type    | Required | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------ | ------- | -------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrUrl`    | string  | Yes      | -        | The unique identifier or hostname of the deployment.                                                                                                                                    |
| `direction`  | string  | No       | `"tail"` | Which end of the build log to return. "tail" (default) returns the most recent lines, where build errors appear. "head" returns the earliest lines. Allowed values: `"tail"`, `"head"`. |
| `errorsOnly` | boolean | No       | `false`  | Return only error, stderr, exit, and fatal events.                                                                                                                                      |
| `limit`      | number  | No       | `100`    | Maximum number of log lines to return.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `since`      | string  | No       | -        | Start of the window as an ISO date or relative lookback from now (e.g. "1h", "30m").                                                                                                    |
| `until`      | string  | No       | -        | Optional end of the window as an ISO date, relative lookback, or "now". Omit this when the end should be the current time.                                                              |
| `buildId`    | string  | No       | -        | Filter to a specific build ID (bld\_...) for multi-build deployments.                                                                                                                   |
| `teamId`     | string  | Yes      | -        | The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource.                                                                                                                               |

## `get_deployment_feature_flags`

Retrieve the feature flags of a deployment.

## Parameters

| Parameter      | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| -------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deploymentId` | string | Yes      | The deployment ID.                                          |
| `teamId`       | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`         | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |

## `get_deployment_file_contents`

Get Deployment File Contents.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| --------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | string | Yes      | The unique deployment identifier                            |
| `fileId`  | string | Yes      | The unique file identifier                                  |
| `path`    | string | No       | Path to the file to fetch (only for Git deployments)        |
| `teamId`  | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`    | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |

## `get_git_deployment_context`

List your teams, their plans, linked Git projects, and connected Cursor Origin workspaces. This tool takes no parameters and is available on the root MCP connection.

**Sample prompt:** "Which of my Git repositories already have Vercel projects?"

This tool is available on the root connection. Project-scoped connections already bind a team and project and do not register this discovery tool.

## `import-claude-design-from-url`

Import a self-contained HTML bundle from Claude Design and deploy it to Vercel. The bundle must use a public HTTPS `claudeusercontent.com` URL and include all images, fonts, and styles.

| Parameter                  | Type   | Required | Default | Description                                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`                      | string | Yes      | -       | Public HTTPS URL to the design file. Valid for ~1 hour. Fetched server-side.                  |
| `title`                    | string | No       | -       | Suggested title for the imported design.                                                      |
| `claude_design_project_id` | string | No       | -       | Stable Claude Design project identifier. Reuse it to update the same imported Vercel project. |

**Sample prompt:** "Import this Claude Design into Vercel: https://claudeusercontent.com/example"

## `list_deployment_events`

Get deployment events, including build output. Use `direction: "backward"` for recent events and numeric timestamps for `since` and `until`.

| Parameter    | Type             | Required | Description                                                                                                           |
| ------------ | ---------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrUrl`    | string           | Yes      | The unique identifier or hostname of the deployment.                                                                  |
| `direction`  | string           | No       | Order of the returned events based on the timestamp. Allowed values: `"backward"`, `"forward"`. Default: `"forward"`. |
| `follow`     | number           | No       | When enabled, this endpoint will return live events as they happen. Allowed values: `0`, `1`.                         |
| `limit`      | number           | No       | Maximum number of events to return. Provide `-1` to return all available logs.                                        |
| `name`       | string           | No       | Deployment build ID.                                                                                                  |
| `since`      | number           | No       | Timestamp for when build logs should be pulled from.                                                                  |
| `until`      | number           | No       | Timestamp for when the build logs should be pulled up until.                                                          |
| `statusCode` | number \| string | No       | HTTP status code range to filter events by.                                                                           |
| `delimiter`  | number           | No       | Allowed values: `0`, `1`.                                                                                             |
| `builds`     | number           | No       | Allowed values: `0`, `1`.                                                                                             |
| `teamId`     | string           | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                                                                    |
| `slug`       | string           | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                                                           |

**Sample prompt:** "Show me the latest build logs for the failed deployment"

## Parameters

| `teamId`    | string | No       | The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource.                                                                                                                                                                                   |

## `ui_get_build_log_excerpt`

The deployments card uses this app-only tool to read its latest build-log lines. App-capable clients expose it to the card. Use `get_deployment_build_logs` for the standalone workflow when your connection exposes it.

This tool appears with the deployments card. Its response includes log entries and `latestAt`. Pass the previous `latestAt` as `since` to fetch newer events. Build logs are separate from runtime logs.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                 |
| --------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `teamId`  | string  | Yes      | The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource.                                                                   |
| `idOrUrl` | string  | Yes      | The unique identifier or hostname of the deployment.                                                                        |
| `limit`   | integer | No       | How many of the most recent log lines to return. Defaults to 120. Minimum: 1. Maximum: 1000.                                |
| `since`   | number  | No       | Only events after this timestamp (ms), oldest first, so a live view can fetch just what is new. Pass the previous latestAt. |

## `upload_file`

Upload Deployment Files.

## Parameters

| Parameter       | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| --------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `contentLength` | number | No       | The file size in bytes                                      |
| `xVercelDigest` | string | No       | The file SHA1 used to check the integrity                   |
| `xNowDigest`    | string | No       | The file SHA1 used to check the integrity                   |
| `xNowSize`      | number | No       | The file size as an alternative to `Content-Length`         |
| `teamId`        | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`          | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody`   | string | No       | Provide this binary value as a base64 string.               |

## `web_fetch_vercel_url`

Fetch content directly from a Vercel deployment URL (with [authentication](/docs/deployment-protection/methods-to-protect-deployments/vercel-authentication) if required).

| Parameter | Type   | Required | Default | Description                                                                                         |
| --------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`     | string | Yes      | -       | The full URL of the Vercel deployment including the path (e.g. "https://myapp.vercel.app/my-page"). |

**Sample prompt:** "Make sure the content from my-app.vercel.app/api/status looks right"

# Documentation, CLI, and Feedback

Find Vercel documentation for a task and get guidance on the Vercel CLI commands to use. These tools help you configure or deploy your projects and share feedback with Vercel.

## `search_vercel_documentation`

Search Vercel documentation for specific topics and information.

| Parameter | Type   | Required | Default | Description                                                                    |
| --------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `topic`   | string | Yes      | -       | Topic to focus the documentation search on (e.g., 'routing', 'data-fetching'). |
| `tokens`  | number | No       | `2500`  | Maximum number of tokens to include in the result.                             |

**Sample prompt:** "How do I configure custom domains in Vercel?"

## `use_vercel_cli`

This tool is available through the `https://mcp.vercel.com/cli/mcp` connection.

Instructs the LLM to use Vercel CLI commands with --help flag for information.

| Parameter | Type   | Required | Default | Description                                 |
| --------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `command` | string | No       | -       | Specific Vercel CLI command to run.         |
| `action`  | string | Yes      | -       | What you want to accomplish with Vercel CLI |

**Sample prompt:** "Help me deploy this project using Vercel CLI"

## `submit_feedback`

Send feedback to Vercel when you want to report a problem or suggest an improvement. This tool requires sign-in and is available on root and project-specific connections when enabled for your account. The documentation-only and CLI-only connections don't expose it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | string | Yes | - | Your feedback. Must contain non-whitespace text. |
| `context` | object | No | - | Relevant details, such as the affected tool and expected behavior. |

**Sample prompt:** "Send Vercel feedback that the deployment error should explain which environment variable is missing."

For example, call `submit_feedback` with:

```json
{
  "message": "Please name the missing environment variable in deployment errors.",
  "context": {
    "tool": "deploy_to_vercel",
    "expected": "An error that identifies the missing variable."
  }
}
```

The tool returns:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Vercel accepted the feedback."
}
```

Acceptance confirms that the feedback endpoint accepted the submission. It doesn't guarantee delivery to every internal destination or a response from Vercel.

## Privacy and limits

Send feedback only when you intend to share it with Vercel. Include relevant details, and leave out credentials, secrets, and full conversations. Vercel applies automatic redaction before forwarding feedback internally.

The tool attaches the MCP server version and your OAuth client ID, plus your user ID when available. It also includes the team and project IDs when you use a project-specific connection. Vercel records the source as `MCP`. Your complete submission must be smaller than 1 MiB.

If authentication fails before anything is sent, the error includes a CLI fallback. Use [`vercel feedback`](/docs/cli/feedback) with Vercel CLI 64.5.0 or newer to send the same message. To preserve optional context, pass it as a JSON string with `--field 'context={...}'`. CLI submissions use the `CLI` source and CLI metadata.

If the error says the feedback service is unavailable and nothing was submitted, try again later. The tool doesn't offer a CLI fallback for this service failure.

If a request times out or returns an uncertain outcome, it may already have reached Vercel. The error won't offer a CLI fallback. Submitting again, including through `vercel feedback`, can create a duplicate. Decide whether to send another copy. If you reach a rate limit, wait before trying again.

# Domains and DNS

Check domain availability and pricing, then manage domains connected to your account or team. You can inspect and update DNS records, manage certificates, and track domain orders or contact verification.

## `buy_domains`

Register domains individually with [`get_purchase_quote`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/billing/get_purchase_quote) and [`buy_domain`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/billing/buy_domain). This tool does not execute purchases.

## `buy_single_domain`

To register a domain, use [`get_purchase_quote`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/billing/get_purchase_quote) followed by [`buy_domain`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/billing/buy_domain). This tool does not execute purchases.

## `check_domain_availability_and_price`

Check if domain names are available for purchase and get pricing information

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type             | Required | Default | Description                                                                         |
| --------- | ---------------- | -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `names`   | Array\<string> | Yes      | -       | Array of domain names to check availability for (e.g., \["example.com", "test.org"]) |

## `create_or_transfer_domain`

Add an existing domain to the Vercel platform.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | Yes      | Request body for this tool.                                 |

## `create_record`

Creates a DNS record for a domain.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `domain`      | string | Yes      | The domain used to create the DNS record.                   |
| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |

| `teamId`                | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                                                      |
| `slug`                  | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                                             |

title: "create_flags_project_connection"
description: "Grant another project access to a project"
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.058Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/feature-flags/create_flags_project_connection"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# create_flags_project_connection

Connect two projects in the same team. The source owns the flags; the consumer receives read and evaluate access across environments. Your consumer project's OIDC token selects the environment. Connections do not permit flag changes.

Set `projectIdOrName` to the source and `requestBody.consumerProjectId` to the consumer. Confirm both projects before creating the connection. On a project-scoped MCP connection, connect to the source project.

## Example

```json
{
  "teamId": "team_example",
  "projectIdOrName": "prj_source",
  "requestBody": {
    "consumerProjectId": "prj_consumer"
  }
}
```

The response identifies both projects and the connection's creator and creation time. Read it back with `list_flags_project_connections`. An existing connection returns a conflict; inspect it before retrying.

## Required permissions

Your MCP OAuth grant must cover both projects. You need permission to manage connections on the source and view the consumer. See [Project Connections permissions](/docs/flags/vercel-flags/project-connections#required-permissions).

## Parameters

| Parameter         | Type   | Required | Description                 |
| ----------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------- |
| `projectIdOrName` | string | Yes      | The project id or name      |
| `teamId`          | string | No       | Team ID.                    |
| `slug`            | string | No       | Team slug.                  |
| `requestBody`     | object | Yes      | Request body for this tool. |

title: "get_flags_project_disconnection_link"
description: "Open the dashboard to disconnect a project"
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.058Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/feature-flags/get_flags_project_disconnection_link"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# get_flags_project_disconnection_link

Get the source project's Flags Connections page, where you can disconnect the selected consumer. This tool checks the source project's team and returns `requires_user_action` with `mutationExecuted: false`. It does not revoke access.

Set `projectIdOrName` to the source and `consumerProjectId` to the consumer. On a project-scoped MCP connection, connect to the source project.

## Example

```json
{
  "teamId": "team_example",
  "projectIdOrName": "prj_source",
  "consumerProjectId": "prj_consumer"
}
```

Open the returned URL, find the consumer under projects that can read the source's flags, and select **Remove Connection**. This removes access across environments. Use `list_flags_project_connections` to verify removal.

You need permission to manage connections on the source to complete this action. You don't need access to the consumer. See [Project Connections permissions](/docs/flags/vercel-flags/project-connections#required-permissions).

## Parameters

| Parameter           | Type   | Required | Description                       |
| ------------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------- |
| `projectIdOrName`   | string | Yes      | The project id or name            |
| `consumerProjectId` | string | Yes      | The connected consumer project id |
| `teamId`            | string | Yes      | Team ID.                          |

# list_flags_project_connections

List the flag connections for a project within one team.

Use `role: "source"` (the default) to list projects that can read this project's flags. Use `role: "consumer"` to list projects whose flags it can read. Connections apply across environments.

On a project-scoped MCP connection, the selected project and team come from the route. Your OAuth grant must include that project, and you need permission to list its connections.

## Example

```json
{
  "teamId": "team_example",
  "projectIdOrName": "prj_source",
  "role": "source"
}
```

The response contains a `data` array with the source and consumer project IDs, available names, and creation details.

## Parameters

| Parameter         | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projectIdOrName` | string | Yes      | The project id or name                                                                                                |
| `role`            | string | No       | List connections where this project is the source (default) or the consumer Allowed values: `"source"`, `"consumer"`. |
| `teamId`          | string | No       | Team ID.                                                                                                              |
| `slug`            | string | No       | Team slug.                                                                                                            |

Use `GET /v1/projects/:id/feature-flags/flags/:flagIdOrSlug?withMetadata=true` for single-flag lookups that need creator metadata. |

Repeat the parameter for multiple tags (all must match).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

# create_kms_issuer

Create a KMS issuer with server-generated signing keys for your team. Configure its name, signing algorithm, claims schema, and initial policy. MCP does not accept private-key imports.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

Set `requestBody.name` when creating an issuer. You can also supply
`algorithm`, `claimsSchema`, and an initial `policy` inside `requestBody`.
The API generates the signing key. Do not send a PEM key or either import field.

| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

## `create_kms_issuer`

Create a KMS issuer with server-generated signing keys for your team. Configure its name, signing algorithm, claims schema, and initial policy. MCP does not accept private-key imports.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

Set `requestBody.name` when creating an issuer. You can also supply
`algorithm`, `claimsSchema`, and an initial `policy` inside `requestBody`.
The API generates the signing key. Do not send a PEM key or either import field.

## `create_kms_issuer_policy`

| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |

| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

| `sort`      | string  | No       | Sort by name in ascending order, or by creation or update time in descending order. Allowed values: `"name"`, `"createdAt"`, `"updatedAt"`.                                                            |

| `requestId` | string | Yes      | The Vercel CLI request ID associated with the trace         |
| `teamId`    | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`      | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |

# get_runtime_errors

Get grouped runtime error clusters for a project. Each cluster includes the error name, occurrence count, affected routes, sample messages, and when the error was first and last seen. Use this tool to investigate production errors before querying individual entries with `get_runtime_logs`. Time ranges can span up to 7 days.

| Parameter   | Type   | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                         |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projectId` | string | Yes      | -       | The project ID to get runtime errors for.                                                                                           |
| `teamId`    | string | Yes      | -       | The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource.                                                                           |
| `since`     | string | No       | -       | Start of the window as an ISO date or relative lookback from now (e.g. "1h", "24h", "7d"). Defaults to 24h ago. Max lookback is 7d. |
| `until`     | string | No       | -       | Optional end of the window as an ISO date, relative lookback, or "now". Omit this when the end should be the current time.          |
| `routes`    | string | No       | -       | Comma-separated route paths to filter by (e.g. "/api/checkout").                                                                    |

**Sample prompt:** "Why is my production app throwing errors?"

title: "get_runtime_logs"
description: "Use get_runtime_logs with Vercel MCP."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.073Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/observability/get_runtime_logs"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# get_runtime_logs

Get runtime logs for a project or deployment. Runtime logs include application output such as console.log messages, errors, and other execution details from [Vercel Functions](/docs/functions) during requests. You can filter logs by environment, log level, source, time range, and full-text search. Use `group_by` to return counts instead of individual lines. For production errors, start with `get_runtime_errors`.

| Parameter      | Type             | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ---------------- | -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projectId`    | string           | Yes      | -       | The project ID to get runtime logs for.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `teamId`       | string           | Yes      | -       | The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `deploymentId` | string           | No       | -       | Filter logs to a specific deployment ID or URL.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `environment`  | string           | No       | -       | Filter by environment: "production" or "preview". Allowed values: `"production"`, `"preview"`.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `level`        | Array\<string> | No       | -       | Filter by log level(s). Can specify multiple levels. Allowed values: `"error"`, `"warning"`, `"info"`, `"fatal"`.                                                                                                                                           |
| `source`       | Array\<string> | No       | -       | Filter by raw log source(s): function or daemon. Allowed values: `"function"`, `"daemon"`.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `since`        | string           | No       | -       | Start of the window as an ISO date or relative lookback from now (e.g., "1h", "30m", "7d"). Defaults to the 50 minutes before until (or now), within Hobby's retention window.                                                                              |
| `until`        | string           | No       | -       | Optional end of the window as an ISO date, relative lookback, or "now". Omit this when the end should be the current time.                                                                                                                                  |
| `limit`        | integer          | No       | -       | Maximum number of log entries to return. Defaults to 50, max 100.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `query`        | string           | No       | -       | Full-text search query to filter logs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `requestId`    | string           | No       | -       | Filter by specific request ID.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `group_by`     | string           | No       | -       | Return counts grouped by this attribute instead of individual log lines. Use for "how many errors", "source breakdown", "top paths". Fast even over wide time ranges. Allowed values: `"requestPath"`, `"level"`, `"source"`, `"deploymentId"`, `"branch"`. |

**Sample prompt:** "Show me the runtime error logs for my project from the last hour"

# Tools

Vercel MCP tools let your AI assistant work with your projects, deployments, logs, and other Vercel resources. Describe what you want to do, and your assistant selects the tools and supplies their parameters.

## Sign in and grant team access

Before using tools that access your Vercel resources:

1. [Connect your AI client to Vercel MCP](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp#setup).
2. Complete the sign-in flow in your browser with the Vercel account you want to use.
3. Authorize your AI client and grant access to the teams you want it to work with.

Adding the server to your client does not complete authorization. Your assistant needs access to the team that owns a project before it can work with that project's deployments or logs. Your existing Vercel permissions still apply.

Ask your assistant to list your teams and projects to check its access. If a team is missing, check that you're signed in to the right account and have granted the connection access to that team.

## Tool availability

Your connection's tool list shows the tools you can call and their current parameters. This reference covers catalog tools and workflow or widget tools. Availability depends on server configuration, client support, and team or project scope. Some connections expose a smaller workflow tool list. Tools with the same name can have different parameters on those connections. Follow the schema returned by your connection.

A listed tool still requires the relevant OAuth grant and Vercel permissions. Tools available in one AI client might not be available in another. This reference does not guarantee that every listed tool has approval for every client.

## Unavailable tools

The MCP catalog excludes endpoints that require unsupported credentials or permissions. It does not create AI Gateway API keys, exchange SSO tokens, import KMS private keys, or sign KMS messages or tokens. Use the relevant Vercel dashboard or [CLI](/docs/cli) workflow when MCP does not expose the action.

MCP and CLI use separate authentication. Keep the same team, project, and resource when switching. After an uncertain write, inspect the resource before retrying. A successful CLI request does not prove that your MCP OAuth connection has the same access.

## Frequently used tools

Start with these tools to find your resources, inspect deployments, and troubleshoot errors:

| Tool                                                                                              | What you can do                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [`list_deployments`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/deployments/list_deployments)         | List deployments for a project.                                                      |
| [`get_deployment`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/deployments/get_deployment)             | Inspect a deployment's status and details.                                           |
| [`web_fetch_vercel_url`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/deployments/web_fetch_vercel_url) | Fetch content from a deployment URL, including protected deployments you can access. |
| [`get_runtime_logs`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/observability/get_runtime_logs)       | Read and filter runtime logs for a project or deployment.                            |
| [`list_projects`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/projects/list_projects)                  | Find projects in a team.                                                             |
| [`list_teams`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/teams/list_teams)                           | Find the teams you can access.                                                       |
| [`get_project`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/projects/get_project)                      | Inspect a project's configuration and details.                                       |
| [`get_runtime_errors`](/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools/observability/get_runtime_errors)   | Investigate grouped runtime errors and affected routes.                              |

For example, ask: "Find my project's latest deployment and check its runtime errors." Your assistant can use several tools to complete the request. Include the team and project name so it can find the right resources.

## Tools by category

Browse the categories below, or expand a category in the sidebar to find a tool.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# list_project_domains

Retrieve project domains by project by id or name.

## Parameters

| Parameter             | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrName`            | string | Yes      | The unique project identifier or the project name                                                                                                                |
| `production`          | string | No       | Filters only production domains when set to `true`. Allowed values: `"true"`, `"false"`. Default: `"false"`.                                                     |
| `target`              | string | No       | Filters on the target of the domain. Can be either "production", "preview" Allowed values: `"production"`, `"preview"`.                                          |
| `customEnvironmentId` | string | No       | The unique custom environment identifier within the project                                                                                                      |
| `gitBranch`           | string | No       | Filters domains based on specific branch.                                                                                                                        |
| `redirects`           | string | No       | Excludes redirect project domains when "false". Includes redirect project domains when "true" (default). Allowed values: `"true"`, `"false"`. Default: `"true"`. |
| `redirect`            | string | No       | Filters domains based on their redirect target.                                                                                                                  |
| `verified`            | string | No       | Filters domains based on their verification status. Allowed values: `"true"`, `"false"`.                                                                         |
| `limit`               | number | No       | Maximum number of domains to list from a request (max 100).                                                                                                      |
| `since`               | number | No       | Get domains created after this JavaScript timestamp.                                                                                                             |
| `until`               | number | No       | Get domains created before this JavaScript timestamp.                                                                                                            |
| `order`               | string | No       | Domains sort order by createdAt Allowed values: `"ASC"`, `"DESC"`. Default: `"DESC"`.                                                                            |
| `teamId`              | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                                                                                                               |
| `slug`                | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                                                                                                      |

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# list_projects

List [projects](/docs/projects) in your account or selected team. The tool also supports repository and project-setting filters.

| Parameter                   | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `from`                      | string  | No       | Query only projects updated after the given timestamp or continuation token.                                                                                                                    |
| `gitForkProtection`         | string  | No       | Specifies whether PRs from Git forks should require a team member's authorization before it can be deployed Allowed values: `"0"`, `"1"`.                                                       |
| `limit`                     | string  | No       | Limit the number of projects returned                                                                                                                                                           |
| `search`                    | string  | No       | Search projects by the name field                                                                                                                                                               |
| `repo`                      | string  | No       | Filter results by repo. Also used for project count                                                                                                                                             |
| `repoId`                    | string  | No       | Filter results by Repository ID.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `repoUrl`                   | string  | No       | Filter results by Repository URL.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `excludeRepos`              | string  | No       | Filter results by excluding those projects that belong to a repo                                                                                                                                |
| `edgeConfigId`              | string  | No       | Filter results by connected Global Config ID                                                                                                                                                    |
| `edgeConfigTokenId`         | string  | No       | Filter results by connected Global Config Token ID                                                                                                                                              |
| `deprecated`                | boolean | No       | -                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `elasticConcurrencyEnabled` | string  | No       | Filter results by projects with elastic concurrency enabled Allowed values: `"0"`, `"1"`.                                                                                                       |
| `staticIpsEnabled`          | string  | No       | Filter results by projects with Static IPs enabled Allowed values: `"0"`, `"1"`.                                                                                                                |
| `buildMachineTypes`         | string  | No       | Filter results by effective build machine types. Accepts comma-separated values. Use "elastic" for projects with elastic selection and "default" for projects without a build machine type set. |
| `buildQueueConfiguration`   | string  | No       | Filter results by build queue configuration. SKIP\_NAMESPACE\_QUEUE includes projects without a configuration set. Allowed values: `"SKIP_NAMESPACE_QUEUE"`, `"WAIT_FOR_NAMESPACE_QUEUE"`.        |
| `teamId`                    | string  | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `slug`                      | string  | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                                                                                                                                     |

**Sample prompt:** "Show me projects in my team"

## Workflow connection parameters

If your connection exposes the smaller workflow tool list, use these parameters instead. Follow your connection's tool schema.

| Parameter | Type   | Required | Default | Description                                               |
| --------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `teamId`  | string | Yes      | -       | The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource. |

# Projects

Create projects from scratch or connect an existing Git repository to Vercel. You can inspect and update project settings, manage domains and deployment protection, or pause and resume a project.

## `accept_project_transfer_request`

Accept project transfer request.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`        | string | Yes      | The code of the project transfer request.                   |
| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

## `add_project_domain`

Add a domain to a project.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrName`    | string | Yes      | The unique project identifier or the project name           |
| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | Yes      | Request body for this tool.                                 |

## `create_git_project`

Create or reuse a Vercel project linked to an accessible Git repository. By default, it creates a preview deployment from the repository's production branch.

| Parameter       | Type    | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------- | ------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `repo`          | string  | Yes      | -       | Repository as "owner/name", or a repository URL such as https://github.com/owner/name or https://origin.cursor.com/owner/name.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `teamId`        | string  | Yes      | -       | The team ID or slug. Use the team that owns the resource.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `provider`      | string  | No       | -       | Git provider to link. Inferred from recognized repository URLs. Otherwise defaults to "github". Use "cursor-origin" for Cursor-hosted repositories at origin.cursor.com. Ignored when the project already exists. Allowed values: `"github"`, `"gitlab"`, `"bitbucket"`, `"cursor-origin"`. |
| `projectName`   | string  | No       | -       | Vercel project to create or reuse. Defaults to the lowercased repository name.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `rootDirectory` | string  | No       | -       | Root-relative directory to build in a monorepo. Only applied when creating the project.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `deploy`        | boolean | No       | `true`  | Whether to create a preview deployment from the linked repository's production branch. Defaults to true. Set false only when the user explicitly requests link-only behavior.                                                                                                               |

**Sample prompt:** "Create a Vercel project for my team's GitHub repository and deploy a preview"

## `git_namespaces`

Lists git namespaces for a supported provider. Supported providers are `github`, `gitlab` and `bitbucket`. If the provider is not provided, it will try to obtain it from the user that authenticated the request.

## Parameters

| ---------------- | ------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`           | string  | No       | The custom Git host if using a custom Git provider, like GitHub Enterprise Server                  |
| `provider`       | string  | No       | Allowed values: `"github"`, `"github-limited"`, `"github-custom-host"`, `"gitlab"`, `"bitbucket"`. |
| `viewerMetadata` | boolean | No       | When true, includes the viewer object for each namespace.                                          |

## `list_project_domains`

Retrieve project domains by project by id or name.

## Parameters

| Parameter             | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrName`            | string | Yes      | The unique project identifier or the project name                                                                                                                |
| `production`          | string | No       | Filters only production domains when set to `true`. Allowed values: `"true"`, `"false"`. Default: `"false"`.                                                     |
| `target`              | string | No       | Filters on the target of the domain. Can be either "production", "preview" Allowed values: `"production"`, `"preview"`.                                          |
| `customEnvironmentId` | string | No       | The unique custom environment identifier within the project                                                                                                      |
| `gitBranch`           | string | No       | Filters domains based on specific branch.                                                                                                                        |
| `redirects`           | string | No       | Excludes redirect project domains when "false". Includes redirect project domains when "true" (default). Allowed values: `"true"`, `"false"`. Default: `"true"`. |
| `redirect`            | string | No       | Filters domains based on their redirect target.                                                                                                                  |
| `verified`            | string | No       | Filters domains based on their verification status. Allowed values: `"true"`, `"false"`.                                                                         |
| `limit`               | number | No       | Maximum number of domains to list from a request (max 100).                                                                                                      |
| `since`               | number | No       | Get domains created after this JavaScript timestamp.                                                                                                             |
| `until`               | number | No       | Get domains created before this JavaScript timestamp.                                                                                                            |
| `order`               | string | No       | Domains sort order by createdAt Allowed values: `"ASC"`, `"DESC"`. Default: `"DESC"`.                                                                            |
| `teamId`              | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                                                                                                               |
| `slug`                | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                                                                                                      |

| `passwordProtection` | object | No       | -       | Enable or disable password protection. Omit to preserve the current setting.                  |
| `ssoProtection`      | object | No       | -       | Enable or disable Vercel Authentication. Omit to preserve the current setting.                |
| `trustedIps`         | object | No       | -       | Enable or disable Trusted IPs. Omit to preserve the current setting.                          |

# get_rolling_release

Get the active rolling release information for a project.

## Parameters

| Parameter  | Type   | Required | Description                                                                            |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrName` | string | Yes      | Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)                                               |
| `state`    | string | No       | Filter by rolling release state Allowed values: `"ACTIVE"`, `"COMPLETE"`, `"ABORTED"`. |
| `teamId`   | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                                     |
| `slug`     | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                            |

# list_promote_aliases

Gets a list of aliases with status for the current promote.

## Parameters

| Parameter    | Type    | Required | Description                                                                   |
| ------------ | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projectId`  | string  | Yes      | The project ID.                                                               |
| `limit`      | number  | No       | Maximum number of aliases to list from a request (max 100). Maximum: 100.     |
| `since`      | number  | No       | Get aliases created after this epoch timestamp.                               |
| `until`      | number  | No       | Get aliases created before this epoch timestamp.                              |
| `failedOnly` | boolean | No       | Filter results down to aliases that failed to map to the requested deployment |
| `teamId`     | string  | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                            |
| `slug`       | string  | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                   |

# Rolling Releases

Control how a new deployment receives production traffic for your project. You can start and advance a rolling release, update its settings, or roll back to a previous production deployment.

## `approve_rolling_release_stage`

Update the active rolling release to the next stage for a project.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrName`    | string | Yes      | Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)                    |
| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

## `complete_rolling_release`

Complete the rolling release for the project.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrName`    | string | Yes      | Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)                    |
| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

## `get_rolling_release`

Get the active rolling release information for a project.

## Parameters

| Parameter  | Type   | Required | Description                                                                            |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrName` | string | Yes      | Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)                                               |
| `state`    | string | No       | Filter by rolling release state Allowed values: `"ACTIVE"`, `"COMPLETE"`, `"ABORTED"`. |
| `teamId`   | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                                     |
| `slug`     | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                            |

## `get_rolling_release_billing_status`

Get rolling release billing status.

## Parameters

| Parameter  | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrName` | string | Yes      | Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)                    |
| `teamId`   | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`     | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |

## `get_rolling_release_config`

Get rolling release configuration.

## Parameters

| ---------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |

## `list_promote_aliases`

Gets a list of aliases with status for the current promote.

## Parameters

| Parameter    | Type    | Required | Description                                                                   |
| ------------ | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projectId`  | string  | Yes      | The project ID.                                                               |
| `limit`      | number  | No       | Maximum number of aliases to list from a request (max 100). Maximum: 100.     |
| `since`      | number  | No       | Get aliases created after this epoch timestamp.                               |
| `until`      | number  | No       | Get aliases created before this epoch timestamp.                              |
| `failedOnly` | boolean | No       | Filter results down to aliases that failed to map to the requested deployment |
| `teamId`     | string  | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                            |
| `slug`       | string  | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.                   |

## `request_promote`

Point production traffic to a given deployment.

## Parameters

| Parameter      | Type    | Required | Description                                                 |
| -------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projectId`    | string  | Yes      | The project ID.                                             |
| `deploymentId` | string  | Yes      | The deployment ID.                                          |
| `teamId`       | string  | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`         | string  | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody`  | unknown | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

## `request_rollback`

Point production traffic to a previous production deployment by ID.

## Parameters

| Parameter      | Type    | Required | Description                                                 |
| -------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projectId`    | string  | Yes      | The project ID.                                             |
| `deploymentId` | string  | Yes      | The ID of the deployment to rollback *to*                   |
| `description`  | string  | No       | The reason for the rollback                                 |
| `teamId`       | string  | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`         | string  | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody`  | unknown | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

## `start_rolling_release`

Start a rolling release for the project.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idOrName`    | string | Yes      | Project ID or project name (URL-encoded)                    |
| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |

# get_alias

Retrieves an Alias for the given host name or alias ID.

## Parameters

| Parameter   | Type   | Required | Description                                                           |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `from`      | number | No       | Get the alias only if it was created after the provided timestamp     |
| `idOrAlias` | string | Yes      | The alias or alias ID to be retrieved                                 |
| `projectId` | string | No       | Get the alias only if it is assigned to the provided project ID       |
| `since`     | number | No       | Get the alias only if it was created after this JavaScript timestamp  |
| `until`     | number | No       | Get the alias only if it was created before this JavaScript timestamp |
| `teamId`    | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                                    |
| `slug`      | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.           |

# list_aliases

List aliases.

## Parameters

| Parameter              | Type                       | Required | Description                                                    |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `domain`               | Array\<string> \| string | No       | Get only aliases of the given domain name                      |
| `from`                 | number                     | No       | Get only aliases created after the provided timestamp          |
| `limit`                | number                     | No       | Maximum number of aliases to list from a request               |
| `projectId`            | string                     | No       | Filter aliases from the given `projectId`                      |
| `since`                | number                     | No       | Get aliases created after this JavaScript timestamp            |
| `until`                | number                     | No       | Get aliases created before this JavaScript timestamp           |
| `rollbackDeploymentId` | string                     | No       | Get aliases that would be rolled back for the given deployment |
| `teamId`               | string                     | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                             |
| `slug`                 | string                     | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.    |

# Routing

Control where requests go with project routing rules, redirects, and deployment aliases. You can stage changes, review version history, and promote or restore a routing configuration.

## `add_route`

Add a routing rule.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type   | Required | Description                                                 |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `projectId`   | string | Yes      | The project ID.                                             |
| `teamId`      | string | No       | Team ID to use for this operation.                          |
| `slug`        | string | No       | Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId. |
| `requestBody` | object | No       | Request body for this tool.                                 |
