# AI Gateway Session Affinity

A provider's prompt cache lives on the provider account that served your request. When the next request in a conversation goes somewhere else, that cache is cold and you pay full price for the prompt again.

Session affinity keeps a conversation on the provider that already holds its cache. AI Gateway groups related requests into a session, remembers which provider served the session's last request, and tries that provider first on the next one. Session affinity is on by default for text and chat requests, so existing traffic benefits without code changes. For the most reliable results, [send a session ID](#identify-a-session).

Session affinity doesn't apply to other request types, such as embeddings, images, or realtime sessions. They have no prompt cache to keep warm.

Session affinity also improves cache hits upstream. AI Gateway forwards the `x-session-affinity` header to the provider, which can route the request to the same inference cluster. See [Improve cache hits with session affinity](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/automatic-caching#improve-cache-hits-with-session-affinity).

## How it works

1. **Identify the session.** AI Gateway reads a [session ID](#identify-a-session) from the request. If you don't send one, AI Gateway [fingerprints the conversation](#fingerprint-requests-without-a-session-id).
2. **Pin the provider.** When a provider accepts a request, AI Gateway saves that provider as the session's pin for the model that served the request. For session IDs you send and for Claude Code sessions, the pin also names the exact credential, because each account keeps its own cache.
3. **Promote the pin.** On the next request in the session, AI Gateway moves the pinned provider to the front of the providers it already planned to try. It never adds a provider that your routing settings exclude.
4. **Renew or expire.** Each successful request renews the pin. A pin expires shortly before the provider's cache does. See [Pin lifetime](#pin-lifetime).

If the pinned provider fails, AI Gateway tries the next provider as usual. A request that fails after the provider accepted it removes that pin, so the next request can choose again.

## Interaction with your routing settings

Session affinity runs after AI Gateway applies your filters, so it only reorders providers you already allow.

| Setting                                         | Behavior with session affinity                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `only` and compliance settings, such as zero data retention | Filters apply first. AI Gateway ignores a pinned provider that the filters removed.                                                        |
| `order`                                         | The pinned provider goes first, ahead of your order. Set `sessionAffinity: false` to keep your order exactly.                              |
| `sort`                                          | The pinned provider goes ahead of the sort winner. A warm cache usually lowers latency and cost, which is what sorting aims for.           |
| Provider health                                 | AI Gateway never promotes a provider that it treats as down.                                                                               |
| BYOK credentials                                | A pin reorders only within its own group. It never moves a system credential ahead of your BYOK credentials, or the reverse.               |

## Identify a session

Send a session ID that stays the same for every request in a conversation, agent run, or workflow. Use an opaque value of up to 256 characters. AI Gateway hashes longer values, so grouping stays stable. Don't include personal data, and don't reuse one ID across unrelated work.

AI Gateway checks these sources in order and uses the first one it finds:

| Priority | Source                           | How to set it                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1        | `sessionId` provider option      | `providerOptions.gateway.sessionId`. On Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages, the top-level `session_id` body field sets the same option. The provider option wins.       |
| 2        | `x-session-id` header            | Send it as an HTTP header, or with the AI SDK `headers` option.                                                                                                                                |
| 3        | `x-session-affinity` header      | Same as `x-session-id`.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 4        | `prompt_cache_key`               | The OpenAI request field. See the note below.                                                                                                                                                  |
| 5        | `x-claude-code-session-id` header | Claude Code sends it automatically.                                                                                                                                                            |
| 6        | Conversation fingerprint         | AI Gateway derives it from the request. See [Fingerprint requests without a session ID](#fingerprint-requests-without-a-session-id).                                                           |

Many callers share one `prompt_cache_key` across users, for example one key per prompt template. AI Gateway treats it as a label for a shared prefix instead of one conversation. It pins only the provider, not the credential, so shared traffic doesn't pile onto a single account.

AI Gateway also forwards the `x-session-id` and `x-session-affinity` headers to the provider it selects, so providers that use them for their own cache routing can.

#### Send a session ID with the AI SDK

Set `sessionId` in `providerOptions.gateway` on each call:

```typescript filename="session-id.ts"
import { streamText } from 'ai';

const result = streamText({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5',
  prompt: 'Hello world',
  providerOptions: {
    gateway: {
      sessionId: 'sess_8f3KQ2vXr9mT',
    },
  },
});
```

#### Send a session ID with compatibility APIs

AI Gateway reads `x-session-id` and `x-session-affinity` through its OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, and OpenResponses API formats. Set the header as a default SDK client header or include it in each HTTP request:

#### Chat Completions

```typescript filename="chat-completions.ts"
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const openai = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY,
  baseURL: 'https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1',
  defaultHeaders: {
    'x-session-id': 'sess_8f3KQ2vXr9mT',
  },
});

const response = await openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello world' }],
});
```

#### OpenAI Responses

```typescript filename="responses.ts"
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const openai = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY,
  baseURL: 'https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1',
  defaultHeaders: {
    'x-session-id': 'sess_8f3KQ2vXr9mT',
  },
});

const response = await openai.responses.create({
  model: 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731',
  input: 'Hello world',
});
```

#### Anthropic Messages

```typescript filename="messages.ts"
import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';

const anthropic = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY,
  baseURL: 'https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh',
  defaultHeaders: {
    'x-session-id': 'sess_8f3KQ2vXr9mT',
  },
});

const message = await anthropic.messages.create({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5',
  max_tokens: 1024,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello world' }],
});
```

#### OpenResponses

```typescript filename="openresponses.ts"
const response = await fetch('https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/responses', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY}`,
    'x-session-id': 'sess_8f3KQ2vXr9mT',
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    model: 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731',
    input: [
      {
        type: 'message',
        role: 'user',
        content: 'Hello world',
      },
    ],
  }),
});
```

## Fingerprint requests without a session ID

When a request has no session ID, AI Gateway derives one from the conversation itself. Every request in a conversation repeats the same opening, so the opening identifies the conversation.

AI Gateway hashes these parts of the request with SHA-256, together with your team ID:

- The first system or developer message.
- The first message that isn't a system or developer message.
- The set of tools, including each tool's name, description, and schema.

The hash works like this:

- **Text only.** AI Gateway uses at most the first 4,096 characters of each message.
- **Stable across turns.** Later turns, tool results, and new user messages don't change the fingerprint, so a conversation stays in one session.
- **Independent of tool order.** A client that lists the same tools in a different order gets the same fingerprint.
- **Private to your team.** The team ID is part of the hash, so two teams that run the same agent never share a session ID. AI Gateway keeps only the hash as the session ID.

Two conversations that open with the same system prompt, tools, and first user message share a fingerprint. A script that starts every run with a templated message such as "Begin the task." does this. When you run many similar conversations, send a session ID instead.

Fingerprinted sessions pin only the provider, not the credential, because unrelated users can share the same opening. AI Gateway pins a fingerprinted session only for models that support prompt caching, and only when the prompt is large enough to cache. See [Minimum prompt size](#minimum-prompt-size).

There is no separate option for fingerprinting. Sending a session ID replaces the fingerprint.

## Keep caches warm across models

A prompt cache belongs to one model on one provider, so a session can hold several warm caches at once. AI Gateway keeps one pin per model in a session, for up to eight models.

- **Switching models.** When your client moves to another model mid-session, such as from `anthropic/claude-opus-5` to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, AI Gateway pins the new model and keeps the pin for the old one. If you switch back before the old pin expires, the request goes to the provider that still holds that model's cache.
- **Model fallbacks.** When a request falls back to another model with [model fallbacks](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/model-fallbacks), AI Gateway pins the model that served the request and keeps the other pins. If the fallback model already has a pin in the session, AI Gateway tries that provider first. A failed request removes only the pin for the model that failed.
- **One session across models.** Use the same session ID for every model in a workflow, so all of their pins belong to one session.

AI Gateway can't move a cache from one model to another. The first request to a model you haven't used in the session writes a new cache at the cache-write rate. See [Cost tradeoff](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/automatic-caching#cost-tradeoff).

## Pin lifetime

A pin lasts as long as the provider keeps its cache. AI Gateway starts from a default lifetime for each provider, then subtracts 15 seconds so a pin never outlives the cache. Each successful request renews the pin.

| Provider                                                                                                         | Default pin lifetime |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| OpenAI and Azure                                                                                                 | 10 minutes           |
| DeepSeek                                                                                                         | 1 hour               |
| All other providers, including Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google, Google Vertex AI, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI     | 5 minutes            |

When your request asks for a longer cache lifetime, the pin follows it:

- **Anthropic models:** a 1-hour cache lifetime, set with `cacheControl.ttl: '1h'` in the AI SDK, `cache_control.ttl: '1h'` on Anthropic Messages, or `cache_ttl: '1h'` with [`caching: 'auto'`](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/automatic-caching#cache-lifetime).
- **OpenAI and Azure models:** `promptCacheRetention: '24h'` in the AI SDK, or `prompt_cache_retention: '24h'` on OpenAI APIs.

A pin never lasts longer than 1 hour, even when the cache does. This keeps routing flexible when you set a 24-hour retention.

## Minimum prompt size

Providers only cache prompts above a minimum length. For sessions that AI Gateway identifies itself, from the Claude Code header or a fingerprint, AI Gateway skips pinning when the prompt is below that minimum. It follows each provider's documented minimum, for example 1,024 tokens for most OpenAI and Google models, and uses 256 tokens when a model has no documented minimum. Anthropic minimums vary by model. See [Anthropic prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching).

AI Gateway applies this check to those sessions only. It pins explicit session IDs, including `prompt_cache_key`, at any prompt size, because your ID says the prefix matters.

## Opt out

Set `sessionAffinity` to `false` in `providerOptions.gateway` to stop AI Gateway from pinning and promoting providers for a request. The default is `true`.

#### AI SDK

```typescript filename="opt-out.ts"
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5',
  prompt: 'Hello world',
  providerOptions: {
    gateway: {
      sessionAffinity: false,
    },
  },
});
```

#### Chat Completions

```typescript filename="opt-out-chat.ts"
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const openai = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY,
  baseURL: 'https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1',
});

const response = await openai.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello world' }],
  // AI Gateway extension fields are not included in the upstream SDK types.
  ...{
    providerOptions: {
      gateway: {
        sessionAffinity: false,
      },
    },
  },
});
```

The request can still carry a session ID, but AI Gateway doesn't write pins or reorder providers for it. The response reports the outcome `skipped_mode_off`.

## Read session details from responses

AI Gateway reports the session and what it did in `providerMetadata.gateway.routing` in the AI SDK, or in `provider_metadata.gateway.routing` on Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages responses.

| Field                        | Description                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `clientSessionId`            | The session ID AI Gateway used.                                                                                                                                      |
| `clientSessionIdSource`      | `explicit` for IDs you send, including `prompt_cache_key`. `agent` for the Claude Code header. `fingerprint` for IDs AI Gateway derived.                              |
| `affinity.outcome`           | What session affinity did for this request. See the outcomes below.                                                                                                  |
| `affinity.pinnedProvider`    | The provider the session's pin named.                                                                                                                                |
| `affinity.displacedProvider` | The provider AI Gateway would have tried first without the pin. It appears only when the pin moved a different provider to the front.                                |

```json
{
  "provider_metadata": {
    "gateway": {
      "routing": {
        "clientSessionId": "sess_8f3KQ2vXr9mT",
        "clientSessionIdSource": "explicit",
        "affinity": {
          "outcome": "promoted",
          "pinnedProvider": "anthropic",
          "displacedProvider": "bedrock"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `affinity.outcome` field has one of these values. AI Gateway can add values over time, so handle unknown values as "no change".

| Outcome                    | Meaning                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `promoted`                 | AI Gateway moved the pinned provider ahead of the provider it would have tried first.    |
| `confirmed`                | The pinned provider already came first, so nothing moved.                                |
| `no_pin`                   | The session has no pin for this model yet.                                               |
| `pin_expired`              | The session had a pin for this model, but it expired. The provider's cache is likely cold. |
| `skipped_not_in_plan`      | Your routing settings removed the pinned provider from this request.                     |
| `skipped_health_down`      | The pinned provider is unhealthy, so AI Gateway didn't promote it.                       |
| `skipped_below_min_prefix` | The prompt is below the minimum cacheable size.                                          |
| `not_cache_capable`        | AI Gateway identified the session itself, and the model doesn't support prompt caching.  |
| `skipped_mode_off`         | You set `sessionAffinity: false`.                                                        |

# AI Gateway Uptime and Provider Status

When a provider has an outage, AI Gateway falls back to a healthy provider so your requests still go through. The model detail page surfaces this in two views, **Uptime** and **Status**, both calculated from live AI Gateway traffic.

Both views share the same time-range toggle in the top-right corner. Each window uses a different bucket size:

| Toggle | Window | Bucket size |
| ------ | ------ | ----------- |
| `1H`   | 1 hour | Per-minute  |
| `1D`   | 1 day  | 15-minute   |
| `1W`   | 1 week | Per-hour    |

## Uptime

The uptime view charts the percentage of successful requests over time, with one line for AI Gateway and one line for each upstream provider. Use it to compare providers, watch trends, and measure how much fallback is helping.

![1-week uptime for anthropic/claude-opus-5](https://7nyt0uhk7sse4zvn.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/opus-4.7-uptime-1-week)

If a provider has no recent activity, AI Gateway can't measure its uptime, so the chart shows it at 100%. The 100% line is a placeholder, not a trend. It doesn't mean the provider was fully available.

### Where to find uptime

You can open the uptime view from:

- The [AI Gateway model catalog](/ai-gateway/models). Select a model, then choose **Uptime**.
- The [**AI Gateway** tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway\&title=Go+to+AI+Gateway) in your project. Go to **Models**, select a model, then choose **Uptime**.

You can also link directly at `vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/<model-id>#uptime`, replacing `<model-id>` with the model you want to inspect. For example, see [uptime for Claude Opus 4.7](/ai-gateway/models/claude-opus-4.7#uptime).

### Accessing uptime via the API

You can query uptime programmatically through the [model endpoints API](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/rest-api#get-model-endpoints). Each endpoint in the response exposes three rolling uptime windows:

| Field             | Window          |
| ----------------- | --------------- |
| `uptime_last_15m` | Last 15 minutes |
| `uptime_last_1h`  | Last 1 hour     |
| `uptime_last_1d`  | Last 1 day      |

```bash
curl -i https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models/anthropic/claude-opus-5/endpoints \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
```

Replace `anthropic/claude-opus-5` with the model ID you want to inspect, and set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` to a valid [AI Gateway API key](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok#api-keys).

The response returns one entry per provider serving the model, each with the three uptime windows:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "anthropic/claude-opus-5",
    "endpoints": [
      {
        "provider_name": "anthropic",
        "uptime_last_15m": 100,
        "uptime_last_1h": 99.8,
        "uptime_last_1d": 99.6
      },
      {
        "provider_name": "bedrock",
        "uptime_last_15m": 100,
        "uptime_last_1h": 100,
        "uptime_last_1d": 99.9
      },
      {
        "provider_name": "vertex",
        "uptime_last_15m": 100,
        "uptime_last_1h": 100,
        "uptime_last_1d": 99.1
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Status

The status view shows a row of health bars across the selected window, giving you a glanceable read on whether a provider is healthy. Each bar covers one time bucket. The color shows the success rate in that bucket:

| Color | Range                | Meaning  |
| ----- | -------------------- | -------- |
| Green | 95% to 100%          | Healthy  |
| Amber | 75% to less than 95% | Degraded |
| Red   | Less than 75%        | Down     |

If a provider has no activity in a bucket, the bar reads "No activity" instead of a color.

![1-day status for anthropic/claude-opus-5](https://7nyt0uhk7sse4zvn.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/opus-4.7-status)

### Where to find status

You can open the status view from:

- The [AI Gateway model catalog](/ai-gateway/models). Select a model, then choose **Status**.
- The [**AI Gateway** tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway\&title=Go+to+AI+Gateway) in your project. Go to **Models**, select a model, then choose **Status**.

You can also link directly at `vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/<model-id>#status`, replacing `<model-id>` with the model you want to inspect. For example, see [status for Claude Opus 4.7](/ai-gateway/models/claude-opus-4.7#status).

## Sharing a snapshot

Select **Share** in the top-right corner of either view to export the current view as an image. The export captures the selected model, view, and time range so you can share a snapshot in tickets, postmortems, or status updates.

![Example share output for the Uptime view (1-week range)](https://7nyt0uhk7sse4zvn.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/claude-opus-4.7-uptime-1w.png)

![Example share output for the Status view](https://7nyt0uhk7sse4zvn.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/opus-4.7-share-status)

## Scope

Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests aren't included, since their success depends on your own provider credentials rather than AI Gateway's.

These numbers reflect what AI Gateway observes, not a provider's overall availability. They may differ from a provider's own reported uptime due to factors specific to AI Gateway, like account tiering, regions, or routing decisions.

## How success is defined

A provider attempt counts as successful when the provider returns a valid response. Uptime is calculated as:

```
uptime % = (successes / total) × 100
```

The following are excluded from the calculation entirely:

- **`4xx` responses**, since they don't reflect provider uptime issues. Receiving a `4xx` means the provider was reachable and responded.
- **Requests using the [`only` filter](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/provider-filtering-and-ordering#restrict-providers-with-the-only-filter)**, for AI Gateway uptime only. The `only` filter restricts routing to a subset of providers, which limits how AI Gateway can fall back. These requests still count toward provider uptime.

## Provider uptime vs. AI Gateway uptime

AI Gateway reports two uptime metrics, which differ in what they count as successes and totals:

- **Provider uptime** reflects the success rate of every individual attempt to a given provider.
- **AI Gateway uptime** only considers the final attempt in each request, capturing the end-to-end outcome after any fallbacks.

| Metric            | Successes                      | Total                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| Provider uptime   | Provider's successful attempts | Provider's total attempts |
| AI Gateway uptime | Successful final attempts      | Total requests            |

A request that fails on its first provider but succeeds on a fallback counts as a success for AI Gateway uptime. This is why AI Gateway uptime can be higher than any individual provider's uptime, since fallback logic can recover from single-provider failures.

# AI Gateway Virtual Models for Reusable Model Configurations

A virtual model is a saved AI Gateway model configuration with its own model ID, `vmc/<slug>`. It pairs a model with the provider routing, fallbacks, regional inference, compliance settings, provider options, and observability tags its requests should use. Any client that takes a model name gets that configuration without sending the options itself, whether it's your own code, a chat platform, or a coding agent like Claude Code or Codex that can't pass AI Gateway options per request. Virtual models work with every model type in the catalog, and you can change their settings later without redeploying your app or editing anyone's config.

## When to use a virtual model

Use a virtual model to:

- Configure the model that coding agents and harnesses such as Claude Code or Codex use, including routing and provider options they can't send per request, and change it later without touching each developer's config.
- Change the model or routing your app uses without redeploying.
- Set provider order, fallbacks, fast mode, service tier, prompt caching, and provider options once per slug instead of on every request.
- Share one approved configuration across your team's apps, chat platforms, and other tools that list AI Gateway models.
- Enforce zero data retention or block provider training for all traffic through the slug.
- Tag requests for usage attribution.

## Creating a virtual model

Create a virtual model from the dashboard or the [Vercel CLI](/docs/cli/ai-gateway#virtual-models).

#### Dashboard

- ### Open the Virtual Models page
  Go to the [Virtual Models page](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Fvirtual-models\&title=AI+Gateway+Virtual+Models) in your Vercel dashboard, then click **Create Virtual Model**.

- ### Set the slug and model
  Enter a **Slug** for your virtual model. This is the name your app will call with the `vmc/` prefix, for example `abc-123`. The slug cannot be changed after creation.

  Pick a **Model** from the AI Gateway catalog. This is the concrete model that requests to this slug will route to. Models with a fast tier appear twice: the base model and a **(Fast)** variant that locks the slug to the fast tier.

  Optionally add a **Display Name** and **Description** to identify the virtual model in the dashboard.

- ### Set provider routing (optional)
  Under **Provider Order**, select providers and drag them into the order AI Gateway should try them. Provider order only reorders routing. Providers you don't list can still serve the request as fallbacks after the ordered ones.

  Under **Provider Only**, select providers to restrict the slug to exactly that list. This list is a filter, not an order. The routing order still applies within it. There is no fallback outside the list, so the request fails if all listed providers fail.

  Under **Inference Region**, pin requests that use system credentials to a region.

- ### Set behavior (optional)
  Under **Model Fallbacks**, add models AI Gateway should try when every provider of the primary model fails, in order.

  For a decision model, select **Add Condition** on the first model fallback to define the request question conditions that should rerun the complete decision on it. Question IDs are free-form because a virtual model does not know the questions a future request will send. AI Gateway validates the IDs and question types when the request arrives.

  Toggle **Fast Mode** to serve the model's fast tier when available. **Fallback From Fast Mode** is on by default and drops the request back to the base model when the fast tier fails.

  Use **Sort By**, **Service Tier**, and **Prompt Caching** to control how AI Gateway ranks providers, which provider service tier requests run on, and whether repeated prompt prefixes are cached. Each of these also accepts **System Default**, explained in **Unset, `@default`, and cleared settings** below.

  Under **Required Capabilities**, require providers to support implicit caching, reasoning, structured output, tool use, or vision. Under **Compliance**, restrict routing to zero-data-retention providers or providers that don't train on request data.

  Under **Provider Options**, attach arbitrary per-provider AI SDK options as JSON, for example `{ "anthropic": { "effort": "high" } }`. Keys must be known provider slugs.

- ### Add observability tags and create
  Under **Observability Tags**, add a comma-separated list of tags to attach to every request that uses this slug. AI Gateway records the tags with each request for usage attribution, in place of any tags the request itself sends.

  Click **Create Virtual Model** to save.

#### CLI

Make sure you're on the [latest CLI version](/docs/cli). The virtual model is created under your current CLI scope. Check it with `vercel whoami`, change it with `vercel switch`, or pass `--scope <team>` per command.

Run `create` with no arguments to be prompted for the slug and model, or pass them directly:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models create abc-123 --model anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
```

The model, display name, description, and provider routing have their own flags. Set every other field with `--config`, a JSON object of virtual model fields. When a flag and a `--config` key set the same field, the flag wins. This command creates the `vmc/coding-agent-eu` virtual model from the diagram at the top of this page:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models create coding-agent-eu \
  --model anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 \
  --provider-order bedrock,vertex \
  --config '{
    "inferenceRegion": { "scope": "zone", "geoRegion": "eu" },
    "providerOptions": { "anthropic": { "effort": "high" } },
    "observabilityTags": ["coding-agents"]
  }'
```

Each dashboard setting maps to a flag or a `--config` key:

| Dashboard setting | CLI flag | `--config` key | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Slug** | First argument | | `coding-agent-eu` |
| **Model** | `--model` | `modelSlug` | `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` |
| **Display Name** | `--display-name` | `displayName` | `Coding agent (EU)` |
| **Description** | `--description` | `description` | `Opus 5.5 pinned to the EU` |
| **Provider Order** | `--provider-order` | `providerOrder` | `bedrock,vertex` as a flag, `["bedrock", "vertex"]` in `--config` |
| **Provider Only** | `--provider-only` | `providerOnly` | `bedrock,vertex` as a flag, `["bedrock", "vertex"]` in `--config` |
| **Inference Region** | | `inferenceRegion` | `{ "scope": "zone", "geoRegion": "eu" }` |
| **Model Fallbacks** | | `models` | `["anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5"]` |
| **Fast Mode** | | `speed` | `"fast"` |
| **Fallback From Fast Mode** | | `allowFallbackFromFast` | `true` |
| **Sort By** | | `sort` | `"cost"` |
| **Service Tier** | | `serviceTier` | `"priority"` or `"flex"` |
| **Prompt Caching** | | `caching` | `"auto"` |
| Provider timeouts | | `providerTimeouts` | `{ "byok": { "openai": 15000 } }` |
| **Required Capabilities** | | `has` | `["implicit-caching"]` |
| **Compliance**: zero data retention | | `zeroDataRetention` | `true` |
| **Compliance**: no prompt training | | `disallowPromptTraining` | `true` |
| **Provider Options** | | `providerOptions` | `{ "anthropic": { "effort": "high" } }` |
| **Observability Tags** | | `observabilityTags` | `["coding-agents"]` |

`sort`, `serviceTier`, `caching`, and `providerTimeouts` also accept `"@default"`, described in [Unset, `@default`, and cleared settings](#unset-default-and-cleared-settings). For a decision model's conditional fallback, see [Decision Fallbacks](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/decision-fallbacks#store-the-fallback-policy-in-a-virtual-model).

Add `--format json` (or `--json`) to any `virtual-models` subcommand for machine-readable output.

## Using a virtual model with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents

Coding agents send AI Gateway a model ID with each request, but they usually can't attach AI Gateway options such as provider order, model fallbacks, regional inference, or zero data retention. To give an agent those settings, create a virtual model and select `vmc/<slug>` as the agent's model, so every request the agent sends uses the virtual model's configuration. From the terminal, create the virtual model and connect your agents with [`vercel ai-gateway setup`](/docs/cli/ai-gateway#setup):

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models create coding-agent --model anthropic/claude-opus-5.5
vercel ai-gateway setup
```

AI Gateway lists your team's virtual models in the model catalogs it serves to coding agents, so the slug appears next to the catalog models:

- **Claude Code**: the `/model` picker lists `claude-code/vmc/<slug>`, with a `[1m]` suffix when the underlying model has a context window of 1M tokens or more.
- **Codex**: pick the slug from `/model`, pass `codex --model vmc/<slug>`, or set `model = "vmc/<slug>"` in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
- **Other agents**: use `vmc/<slug>` anywhere the agent accepts an AI Gateway model ID.

AI Gateway lists only virtual models that point at a language model. If a running agent doesn't show a new slug yet, restart it so it reloads the model list.

Each agent stores only the slug, so editing the virtual model changes the configuration for every developer at once. For example, `vercel ai-gateway virtual-models edit coding-agent --model anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` moves every agent using `vmc/coding-agent` to Fable 5.1 for new requests within a few minutes.

## Using a virtual model in your app

Once you create a virtual model, call it like any other AI Gateway model with the `vmc/` prefix. The slug works in every request format AI Gateway supports, and you don't need to send any AI Gateway options with it. These examples use AI SDK 7 and the AI SDK for Python beta. Set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` before running them. See [API format differences](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis#api-format-differences) for setup, request fields, and response handling:

#### AI SDK

#### TypeScript

```typescript filename="virtual-model.ts" {4}
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: 'vmc/abc-123',
  prompt: 'Hello, world!',
});

console.log(text);
```

#### Python (beta)

```python filename="virtual_model_ai.py" {5}
import asyncio
import ai

async def main():
    model = ai.get_model("vmc/abc-123")
    messages = [ai.user_message("Hello, world!")]
    async with ai.stream(model, messages) as stream:
        async for event in stream:
            if isinstance(event, ai.events.TextDelta):
                print(event.chunk, end="", flush=True)
    print()

asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Chat Completions

#### TypeScript

```typescript filename="virtual-model-chat.ts" {9}
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY,
  baseURL: 'https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1',
});

const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'vmc/abc-123',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello, world!' }],
});

console.log(response.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

#### Python

```python filename="virtual_model_chat.py" {10}
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="vmc/abc-123",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello, world!"}],
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

#### cURL

```bash filename="virtual-model-chat.sh" {5}
curl --fail-with-body https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "model": "vmc/abc-123",
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Hello, world!" }]
}'
```

#### Messages API

#### TypeScript

```typescript filename="virtual-model-messages.ts" {9}
import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';

const client = new Anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY,
  baseURL: 'https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh',
});

const message = await client.messages.create({
  model: 'vmc/abc-123',
  max_tokens: 1024,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello, world!' }],
});

for (const block of message.content) {
  if (block.type === 'text') console.log(block.text);
}
```

#### Python

```python filename="virtual_model_messages.py" {10}
import os
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    api_key=os.environ["AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh",
)

message = client.messages.create(
    model="vmc/abc-123",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello, world!"}],
)

for block in message.content:
    if block.type == "text":
        print(block.text)
```


## Using a virtual model with other model types

Virtual models work with every model type in the AI Gateway catalog, including embedding, image, video, speech, transcription, reranking, and decision models. Pass the `vmc/` slug to the AI SDK function for that model type, the same way you would pass the underlying model:

#### Embeddings

```typescript filename="embed.ts"
import { embed } from 'ai';

const { embedding } = await embed({
  model: 'vmc/search-embeddings',
  value: 'sunny day at the beach',
});
```

#### Image

```typescript filename="generate-image.ts"
import { generateImage } from 'ai';

const { image } = await generateImage({
  model: 'vmc/product-images',
  prompt: 'A red lighthouse on a rocky coast, flat illustration',
});
```

#### Video

```typescript filename="generate-video.ts"
import { experimental_generateVideo as generateVideo } from 'ai';
import fs from 'node:fs';

const { videos } = await generateVideo({
  model: 'vmc/promo-video',
  prompt: 'A paper boat drifting down a rainy street, slow camera pan',
  duration: 5,
});

fs.writeFileSync('output.mp4', videos[0].uint8Array);
```

#### Text to Speech

```typescript filename="generate-speech.ts"
import { generateSpeech } from 'ai';
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

const result = await generateSpeech({
  model: 'vmc/narrator',
  text: 'Hello from AI Gateway.',
  voice: 'alloy',
});

await writeFile('greeting.mp3', result.audio.uint8Array);
```

#### Speech to Text

```typescript filename="transcribe.ts"
import { transcribe } from 'ai';
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

const result = await transcribe({
  model: 'vmc/meeting-notes',
  audio: await readFile('meeting.mp3'),
});

console.log(result.text);
```

#### Reranking

```typescript filename="rerank.ts"
import { rerank } from 'ai';

const { ranking } = await rerank({
  model: 'vmc/search-rerank',
  query: 'What is the capital of France?',
  documents: [
    'Berlin is the capital of Germany.',
    'Paris is the capital of France.',
    'Madrid is the capital of Spain.',
  ],
  topN: 2,
});
```

#### Decision

```typescript filename="decide.ts"
import { experimental_decide as decide } from 'ai';

const { answers } = await decide({
  model: 'vmc/support-triage',
  state: 'Help! My payouts have been failing for 3 days.',
  questions: {
    urgent: { type: 'boolean', instructions: 'Is this request urgent?' },
  },
});
```

The same slugs work in the HTTP endpoints for each model type, such as `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/images/generations`, `/v2/rerank`, and `/v1/decisions`. In the AI SDK, `providerMetadata.gateway.virtualModelConfig.modelId` on the result names the virtual model that served the request.

A few things to keep in mind:

- **Request options still belong to the underlying model.** Options such as `voice`, `size`, or `duration` pass through unchanged, so use values the model behind the slug accepts.
- **A slug only serves its own model type.** Sending an image virtual model to Chat Completions, for example, returns a `400` error that names the API to use instead.
- **Decision virtual models can store a fallback policy.** See [Decision Fallbacks](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/decision-fallbacks#store-the-fallback-policy-in-a-virtual-model) to escalate uncertain answers to another model for every caller.

## How virtual models interact with team settings

Your team's AI Gateway settings apply to every request, including requests through a virtual model. A virtual model can add restrictions for its own traffic, but it can't bypass or loosen a team setting:

| Team setting | Effect on requests through a virtual model |
| --- | --- |
| [Model allowlist](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/model-allowlist#virtual-models) | AI Gateway checks the model the virtual model points at, not the `vmc/` slug. If that model isn't on the allowlist, the request is blocked. |
| [Provider allowlist](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/provider-allowlist) | Applies on top of the virtual model's **Provider Order** and **Provider Only** lists. A provider your team disabled can't serve the request, even when the virtual model lists it. |
| [Routing rules](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/routing-rules#virtual-models) | A deny rule on the underlying model blocks it through the virtual model too. If the virtual model has model fallbacks, AI Gateway skips the denied attempt and tries the next one. Rewrites run before AI Gateway resolves the virtual model, so a rewrite can send direct callers to a `vmc/` slug, and AI Gateway doesn't apply rewrites again to the model inside it. |
| [Team-wide zero data retention](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/zdr#team-wide-zero-data-retention) | Stays on for virtual model traffic. A virtual model can turn on ZDR for its own traffic, but it can't turn off the team setting. |
| [Budgets](/docs/ai-gateway/observability-and-spend/budgets) | A request through a virtual model counts toward every budget in scope for how it authenticates, the same as a direct request. |
| [BYOK credentials](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/byok) | A virtual model's inference region applies only to attempts on AI Gateway's system credentials, not to attempts on your team's own credentials. |

## How virtual model settings interact with request options

Requests to `vmc/<slug>` go through the same AI Gateway routing as direct model requests, so many options can come from either side. The resolving rule depends on the field:

| Setting | Virtual model sets it | Request also sets it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Provider order (`order`) | Wins | Ignored |
| Provider restriction (`only`) | Wins | Ignored |
| Model fallbacks (`models`) | Wins, replaces the request's string or conditional chain | Ignored |
| Fast mode (`speed`, `allowFallbackFromFast`) | Wins | Ignored |
| Provider sort (`sort`) | Wins | Ignored |
| Service tier (`serviceTier`) | Wins | Ignored |
| Prompt caching (`caching`) | Wins | Ignored |
| Provider timeouts (`providerTimeouts`) | Wins | Ignored |
| Inference region (`inferenceRegion`) | Wins on system-credential attempts | Ignored |
| Required capabilities (`has`) | Wins | Ignored |
| Observability tags (`tags`) | Wins | Ignored |
| Provider options (`providerOptions`) | Wins per option | Applies for options the virtual model doesn't set |
| Compliance (ZDR, block training) | Turns it on | On when either side turns it on, neither side turns it off |

For example, `vmc/coding-agent-eu` from the diagram at the top of this page sets an EU inference region, provider order `bedrock, vertex`, the Anthropic provider option `effort: high`, and the tag `coding-agents`. It leaves prompt caching unset. A caller sends its own options anyway:

```typescript filename="review.ts" {6-15}
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: 'vmc/coding-agent-eu',
  prompt: 'Review this diff for bugs.',
  providerOptions: {
    gateway: {
      order: ['anthropic'],
      tags: ['feature:review'],
      caching: 'auto',
      zeroDataRetention: true,
    },
    anthropic: {
      effort: 'low',
    },
  },
});
```

AI Gateway resolves each option like this:

- **Provider order**: AI Gateway tries `bedrock`, then `vertex`, in the EU. The virtual model sets an order, so the request's `['anthropic']` is ignored.
- **Tags**: AI Gateway records `coding-agents`. The request's `feature:review` tag is ignored.
- **Prompt caching**: `auto`, from the request, because the virtual model leaves caching unset.
- **Zero data retention**: on. The request turned it on, and neither side can turn it off.
- **Reasoning effort**: `high`. Provider options merge option by option, and the virtual model sets `effort`, so its value wins over the request's `low`.

A few details worth knowing:

- **A setting the virtual model leaves unset still comes from the request.** "Wins" applies only to settings the virtual model actually carries, so a slug can decide some options and leave the rest to the caller.
- **Provider options combine option by option.** Every other setting is a single value, so one side's wins outright. Provider options are a map, so the two are merged: the virtual model's value wins for each option it sets, and the request keeps the rest.
- **Required capabilities replace, so check `has: ['free']`.** A virtual model's capability list replaces the request's rather than adding to it, so a request using `has: ['free']` to stay on free providers loses that guard if the slug sets its own capabilities.
- **Compliance settings only tighten.** Zero data retention and blocking prompt training turn on when either side enables them. A virtual model can't relax a restriction the request set, and a request can't relax one the virtual model set. In exchange, these fields reject the `@default` sentinel described below.
- **Model fallbacks resolve per attempt.** You can also use `vmc/<slug>` anywhere in a request's own [model fallbacks](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/model-fallbacks) array. Each model in a chain resolves independently, so a virtual model's routing and settings apply only to its own attempt and don't carry over to the next model in the list.
- **Decision fallbacks rerun the full request.** A decision virtual model can store one conditional policy. When it matches, AI Gateway reruns every question with the fallback and returns only that complete result. See [Decision Fallbacks](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/decision-fallbacks#store-the-fallback-policy-in-a-virtual-model).

## Unset, `@default`, and cleared settings

Sort, service tier, prompt caching, and provider timeouts are tri-state. Understanding the three states matters when a caller and a virtual model could both set the same option:

| State | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Unset (dashboard: **No Preference**) | The virtual model has no opinion. The request's own value applies, and when the request doesn't set one, the system default applies. |
| An explicit value | The virtual model's value wins. AI Gateway ignores the request's value. |
| `@default` (dashboard: **System Default**) | AI Gateway drops the request's value and applies the system default behavior. The virtual model actively removes the caller's choice without replacing it. |
| Cleared (API: `null`) | Removes the virtual model's setting, returning the field to unset, so requests flow with their own value or the system default again. |

Use `@default` when a team wants to guarantee standard behavior for all traffic through a slug, for example to keep callers from pinning priority tier through a shared virtual model.

AI Gateway accepts `@default` only on `sort`, `serviceTier`, `caching`, and `providerTimeouts`. The compliance settings reject it because an off choice would loosen a restriction the caller asked for. `speed`, `allowFallbackFromFast`, and `models` reject it because their unset state already is the default behavior, and `has` rejects it too, so on those a virtual model either sets a value or leaves the caller's alone.

## Managing virtual models

Changes to a virtual model, including archive and restore, take effect for new requests within a few minutes. The slug can't be changed after creation.

#### Dashboard

To edit a virtual model, open it and use the sections on the Configure tab. You can change the model, provider routing, inference region, fallback chain, decision fallback, fast mode, sort, service tier, prompt caching, required capabilities, compliance settings, provider options, observability tags, display name, and description.

To archive a virtual model, open the menu on its row and click **Archive**. Archived virtual models stop serving traffic and return 404 to any request that uses their slug. The row stays visible in the Archived section at the bottom of the list. Open the menu on an archived row and click **Restore** to start serving traffic again.

#### CLI

List your team's virtual models. Add `--include-archived` to also show ones archived in the dashboard:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models list
```

Show every field set on a virtual model:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models inspect coding-agent-eu
```

`edit` takes the same flags and `--config` keys as `create`, except `--kind`, and needs at least one of them. Fields you leave out keep their current values. Set a field to `null` to clear it, or to `"@default"` to drop the caller's value in favor of the system default. To clear model fallbacks, set `models` to `[]`:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models edit coding-agent-eu --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models edit coding-agent-eu --config '{"caching":"auto","serviceTier":"@default"}'
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models edit coding-agent-eu --config '{"inferenceRegion":null,"models":[]}'
```

`remove` runs without a confirmation prompt. Requests to the slug stop resolving, and the virtual model no longer appears in `list`, even with `--include-archived`. AI Gateway keeps its configuration, so `restore` brings it back as it was:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models remove coding-agent-eu
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models restore coding-agent-eu
```

Removing is separate from archiving in the dashboard. An archived virtual model still appears in `list --include-archived`, labeled `archived`.

`vercel ai-gateway models ls` lists your team's virtual models alongside the catalog models. Add `--virtual` to show only virtual models. See the [`vercel ai-gateway virtual-models` reference](/docs/cli/ai-gateway#virtual-models) for every option.

## Permissions

Any member of your team can use a virtual model in their application. Team **Owners** and **Members** can create virtual models. Only the member who created a virtual model or a team **Owner** can edit, archive, remove, or restore it, in the dashboard or the CLI.

# AI Gateway Web Search

AI Gateway provides built-in search tools that let AI models access current web information and source-grounded data. Use them when you need information that may not be in the model's training data.

AI Gateway supports two types of web search:

- **Search for all providers**: Use [Perplexity Search](#using-perplexity-search), [Exa Search](#using-exa-search), [Tako Search](#using-tako-search), [Browserbase Search](#using-browserbase-search), [DeepSeek Search](#using-deepseek-search), or [Parallel Search](#using-parallel-search) with any model regardless of provider. This gives you consistent web search behavior across different models.
- **Provider-specific search**: Use native web search tools from [Anthropic](#anthropic-web-search), [OpenAI](#openai-web-search), [Google](#google-web-search), or [SpaceXAI](#spacexai-web-search). These tools are optimized for their respective providers and may offer [additional features](#provider-specific-search).

For pages the model already has a URL for, [Browserbase Fetch](#using-browserbase-fetch) or [DeepSeek Fetch](#using-deepseek-fetch) retrieves the contents directly instead of searching.

## Search across API formats

Search tool definitions differ by API and provider. The TypeScript AI SDK example uses AI Gateway's Perplexity tool. The Python beta example uses Anthropic's native web search tool. Chat Completions uses its server-tool format. Messages uses Anthropic's native web search tool. Responses uses OpenAI's native web search with an OpenAI model. Don't copy a tool definition between these formats. The Python beta example supports Anthropic's native web search. Gateway's Perplexity search helper is not supported in this beta agent loop.

For provider-specific search, follow the [Anthropic](#anthropic-web-search), [OpenAI](#openai-web-search), and [Google](#google-web-search) sections. Use the [Responses tool reference](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/responses/tool-calling) for function tools. Native search tool availability depends on the selected provider and model.

#### AI SDK

#### TypeScript

See the [AI SDK provider-executed tools reference](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/ai-sdk-providers/ai-gateway#provider-executed-tools) for SDK configuration and usage.

```typescript filename="search.ts"
import { generateText, gateway, isStepCount } from 'ai';

const { text } = await generateText({
  tools: { search: gateway.tools.perplexitySearch({ maxResults: 1 }) },
  stopWhen: isStepCount(3),
  model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5",
  prompt: "Search the web for Vercel AI Gateway and summarize it in one sentence.",
});

console.log(text);
```

#### Python (beta)

```python filename="search_ai.py"
import asyncio
import ai
from ai.providers.anthropic import tools as anthropic_tools

async def main():
    model = ai.get_model("anthropic/claude-sonnet-5")
    messages = [ai.user_message("Search the web for Vercel AI Gateway and summarize it in one sentence.")]
    agent = ai.Agent(tools=[anthropic_tools.web_search(max_uses=1)])
    async with agent.run(model, messages) as stream:
        async for event in stream:
            if isinstance(event, ai.events.TextDelta):
                print(event.chunk, end="", flush=True)
    print()

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Using Perplexity Search

The `perplexitySearch` tool can be used with any model regardless of the model provider or creator. This makes it a flexible option when you want consistent web search behavior across different models, or when you want to use web search with a model whose provider doesn't offer native web search capabilities.

To use Perplexity Search, import `gateway` from `ai` and pass `gateway.tools.perplexitySearch()` to the `tools` parameter. When the model needs current information, it calls the tool and AI Gateway routes the request to [Perplexity's search API](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/search-quickstart).

> **💡 Note:** Perplexity web search requests are charged at $5 per 1,000 requests. See
> [Perplexity's pricing](https://docs.perplexity.ai/getting-started/pricing) for
> more details.

#### streamText

```typescript filename="perplexity-web-search.ts" {9-11}
import { gateway, streamText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const result = streamText({
    model: 'openai/gpt-6-astra', // Works with any model, not just Perplexity
    prompt,
    tools: {
      perplexity_search: gateway.tools.perplexitySearch(),
    },
  });

  for await (const part of result.stream) {
    if (part.type === 'text-delta') {
      process.stdout.write(part.text);
    } else if (part.type === 'tool-call') {
      console.log('Tool call:', part.toolName);
    } else if (part.type === 'tool-result') {
      console.log('Search results received');
    }
  }

  return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
}
```

#### generateText

```typescript filename="perplexity-web-search.ts" {9-11}
import { gateway, generateText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const { text } = await generateText({
    model: 'openai/gpt-6-astra', // Works with any model, not just Perplexity
    prompt,
    tools: {
      perplexity_search: gateway.tools.perplexitySearch(),
    },
  });

  return Response.json({ text });
}
```

### Perplexity parameters

You can configure the `perplexitySearch` tool with these parameters:

- `maxResults`: Number of results to return (1-20). Defaults to 10.
- `maxTokens`: Total token budget across all results. Defaults to 25,000, max 1,000,000.
- `maxTokensPerPage`: Tokens extracted per webpage. Defaults to 2,048.
- `country`: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., `'US'`, `'GB'`) for regional results.
- `searchLanguageFilter`: ISO 639-1 language codes (e.g., `['en', 'fr']`). Max 10 codes.
- `searchDomainFilter`: Domains to include (e.g., `['reuters.com']`) or exclude with `-` prefix (e.g., `['-reddit.com']`). Max 20 domains. Cannot mix allowlist and denylist.
- `searchRecencyFilter`: Filter by content recency. Values: `'day'`, `'week'`, `'month'`, or `'year'`.

#### streamText

```typescript filename="perplexity-web-search-params.ts" {9-19}
import { gateway, streamText } from 'ai';

        maxResults: 5,
        maxTokens: 50000,
        maxTokensPerPage: 2048,
        country: 'US',
        searchLanguageFilter: ['en'],
        searchDomainFilter: ['reuters.com', 'bbc.com', 'nytimes.com'],
        searchRecencyFilter: 'week',
      }),
    },
  });

  return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
```
```typescript filename="perplexity-web-search-params.ts" {9-19}
}
```

## Using Exa Search

The `exaSearch` tool can be used with any model regardless of the model provider or creator. [Exa](https://exa.ai/) returns web results and extracted content for agent workflows that need current information, domain filters, date filters, and token-efficient excerpts.

To use Exa Search, import `gateway` from `ai` and pass `gateway.tools.exaSearch()` to the `tools` parameter. When the model needs current information, it calls the tool and AI Gateway routes the request to [Exa's Search API](https://exa.ai/docs/reference/search-api-guide-for-coding-agents).

> **💡 Note:** Exa web search requests are charged at $7 per 1,000 `auto` or `fast` requests
> and $4 per 1,000 `instant` requests. Each request includes up to 10 results.
> Additional requested results beyond 10 are charged at $1 per 1,000 additional
> results.

#### streamText

```typescript filename="exa-web-search.ts" {9-11}
import { gateway, streamText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const result = streamText({
    model: 'openai/gpt-6-astra', // Works with any model
    prompt,
    tools: {
      exa_search: gateway.tools.exaSearch(),
    },
  });

  for await (const part of result.stream) {
    if (part.type === 'text-delta') {
      process.stdout.write(part.text);
    } else if (part.type === 'tool-call') {
      console.log('Tool call:', part.toolName);
    } else if (part.type === 'tool-result') {
      console.log('Search results received');
    }
  }

  return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
}
```

#### generateText

```typescript filename="exa-web-search.ts" {9-11}
import { gateway, generateText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const { text } = await generateText({
    model: 'openai/gpt-6-astra', // Works with any model
    prompt,
    tools: {
      exa_search: gateway.tools.exaSearch(),
    },
  });

  return Response.json({ text });
}
```

### Exa parameters

You can configure the `exaSearch` tool with these parameters:

- `type`: Search mode. Values: `'auto'` (default), `'fast'`, or `'instant'`.
- `numResults`: Maximum number of results to return (1-100). Defaults to 10.
- `category`: Content category. Values: `'company'`, `'people'`, `'research paper'`, `'news'`, `'personal site'`, or `'financial report'`.
- `userLocation`: Two-letter ISO country code, such as `'US'`, for location-aware search.
- `includeDomains`: List of domains to restrict search results to.
- `excludeDomains`: List of domains to exclude from search results.
- `startPublishedDate`: Only return results published after this ISO 8601 date.
- `endPublishedDate`: Only return results published before this ISO 8601 date.
- `contents`: Controls extracted page content and freshness.
  - `text`: Return page text. You can set `maxCharacters`, `includeHtmlTags`, `verbosity`, `includeSections`, and `excludeSections`.
  - `highlights`: Return concise excerpts. You can set `query` and `maxCharacters`.
  - `maxAgeHours`: Maximum age of cached content in hours.
  - `livecrawlTimeout`: Timeout for live crawling in milliseconds.
  - `subpages`: Number of related subpages to crawl.
  - `subpageTarget`: Target page or pages for subpage crawling.
  - `extras`: Extract links or image links from pages with `links` and `imageLinks`.

#### streamText

```typescript filename="exa-web-search-params.ts" {9-20}
import { gateway, streamText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const result = streamText({
    model: 'openai/gpt-6-astra',
    prompt,
    tools: {
      exa_search: gateway.tools.exaSearch({
        type: 'fast',
        numResults: 5,
        category: 'news',
        includeDomains: ['reuters.com', 'bbc.com', 'nytimes.com'],
        contents: {
          highlights: true,
          maxAgeHours: 24,
        },
      }),
    },
  });

  return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
}
```

#### generateText

```typescript filename="exa-web-search-params.ts" {9-20}

  const { text } = await generateText({
```
