This initial AI Gateway integration supports Exa's standard Search modes and content extraction controls. Deep synthesis modes and generated summaries are not exposed yet because they have separate pricing.

For more details on search parameters and API options, see the [Exa Search API documentation](https://exa.ai/docs/reference/search-api-guide-for-coding-agents).

## Using Tako Search

The `takoSearch` tool searches the web and Tako's curated, real-time knowledge
graph in one call. It returns token-efficient web excerpts and knowledge graph
results backed by structured data, source attribution, and embed-ready
visualizations. Use it when your agent needs access to authoritative, real-time
finance, sports, weather, macroeconomics, and politics data or results from the
web. Set `sources.data.includeContents` to return the raw structured data that
backs the data results.

To use Tako Search, import `gateway` from `ai` and pass
`gateway.tools.takoSearch()` to `tools`:

```typescript filename="tako-search.ts" {9-18}
import { gateway, generateText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const { text } = await generateText({
    model: 'openai/gpt-6-astra',
    prompt,
    tools: {
      tako_search: gateway.tools.takoSearch({
        effort: 'fast',
        sources: {
          data: { count: 2 },
          web: { count: 2 },
        },
      }),
    },
  });

  return Response.json({ text });
}
```

> **💡 Note:** Tako Search costs $7 per 1,000 instant or fast requests and $12 per 1,000 deep
> requests. `sources.data.includeContents` adds variable export surcharges based
> on the requested rows and underlying data source. Guide agents to search without
> it first, then inspect each card's `content.export_pricing` before exporting.
> See [Contents pricing](https://docs.tako.com/documentation/integrating-tako/contents/pricing)
> for details.

### Tako parameters

You can configure the `takoSearch` tool with these parameters:

- `effort`: Retrieval depth. Values: `'instant'` (cached, lowest latency),
  `'fast'` (default), or `'deep'` (broader retrieval with reranking, billed at
  the higher request rate).
- `sources`: Omit it to search both curated `data` and live `web`. When set,
  only the source keys present are searched.
- `sources.web`: Configure web results.
  - `count`: Maximum web results (1-20).
  - `includeDomains` / `excludeDomains`: Only return, or drop, results from
    these bare domains. Up to 20 each.
  - `publishedAfter` / `publishedBefore`: Keep results published on or after,
    or on or before, this `YYYY-MM-DD` date.
  - `highlights`: Return query-relevant passages as each result's snippet
    instead of the opening text of the page. Defaults to `true`.
  - `snippetMaxChars`: Character cap on each result's snippet. Maximum 20,000.
  - `includeContents`: Inline each page's extracted full text.
    `articleContentMaxChars` caps it, defaulting to 30,000 (maximum 1,000,000).
- `sources.data`: Configure knowledge graph results.
  - `count`: Maximum data results (1-20). Defaults to 5. The free row
    allowance is per result, so raising `count` raises both the rows you get
    and the baseline you pay.
  - `includeContents`: Inline each card's underlying rows in `content.dataset`
    as typed, unit-labeled columns. This is the parameter that adds row charges.
  - `maxRows`: Row cap per result. Omit it and each result returns the free
    allowance only (20 rows) with `truncated: true`. You pay for rows actually
    returned, so a value above the series length costs the series length. Each
    card reports its own ceiling in `content.export_pricing.max_rows_ceiling`.
  - `contentFormat`: Serialization for inlined card data. Values:
    `'json_compact'` (default), `'json_records'`, `'csv'`, or `'card_json'`.
  - `nodeIds`: Data Graph node IDs to prioritize. Up to 20.
  - `strict`: Only return cards matching `nodeIds`. Requires at least one
    `nodeIds` value.
- `includeRelated`: Number of related search suggestions to return (1-20).
- `location`: End-user `{ latitude, longitude }` coordinates for localized results.
- `countryCode`: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as `'US'`.
- `locale`: BCP-47 locale, such as `'en-US'`.
- `timezone`: IANA timezone, such as `'America/New_York'`.

AI Gateway applies options you set in `takoSearch()` as developer defaults, overriding model-generated values.

For the complete input and output schema, see the [AI SDK AI Gateway reference](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/ai-sdk-providers/ai-gateway#tako-search). For search behavior, data cards, and Tako-specific options, see the [Tako Search documentation](https://docs.tako.com/documentation/integrating-tako/search/for-coding-agent).

## Using Browserbase Search

The `browserbaseSearch` tool can be used with any model regardless of the model
provider or creator. [Browserbase](https://browserbase.com/) provides fast,
structured web discovery through its
[Search API](https://docs.browserbase.com/reference/api/web-search), returning
result titles, URLs, and metadata without opening a browser session. Use it when
you want the model to find pages, then pair it with
[Browserbase Fetch](#using-browserbase-fetch) to read one.

To use Browserbase Search, import `gateway` from `ai` and pass
`gateway.tools.browserbaseSearch()` to `tools`:

> **💡 Note:** Browserbase Search costs $7 per 1,000 requests, regardless of how many results
> you request.

#### streamText

```typescript filename="browserbase-search.ts" {9-11}
import { gateway, streamText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const result = streamText({
    model: 'openai/gpt-5.6-sol', // Works with any model
    prompt,
    tools: {
      browserbase_search: gateway.tools.browserbaseSearch({ numResults: 3 }),
    },
  });

  for await (const part of result.fullStream) {
    if (part.type === 'text-delta') {
      process.stdout.write(part.text);
    } else if (part.type === 'tool-result') {
      console.log('Search results received');
    }
  }

  return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
}
```

#### generateText

```typescript filename="browserbase-search.ts" {9-11}
import { gateway, generateText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const { text } = await generateText({
    model: 'openai/gpt-5.6-sol', // Works with any model
    prompt,
    tools: {
      browserbase_search: gateway.tools.browserbaseSearch({ numResults: 3 }),
    },
  });

  return Response.json({ text });
}
```

### Browserbase Search parameters

You can configure the `browserbaseSearch` tool with this parameter:

- `numResults`: Maximum number of results to return (1-25). Defaults to 10.

The model supplies the `query`, which must be between 1 and 200 characters.

AI Gateway applies options you set in `browserbaseSearch()` as developer defaults, overriding model-generated values.

For the complete input and output schema, see the [AI SDK AI Gateway reference](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/ai-sdk-providers/ai-gateway#browserbase-search). For search behavior and Browserbase-specific options, see the [Browserbase Search documentation](https://docs.browserbase.com/reference/api/web-search).

## Using Browserbase Fetch

The `browserbaseFetch` tool retrieves the contents of a URL the model already
has, rather than searching for one. It uses
[Browserbase's Fetch API](https://docs.browserbase.com/platform/fetch/overview),
a lightweight option for pages that do not need JavaScript execution or browser
interaction, and can return the raw response body, Markdown, or structured JSON
extracted against a JSON Schema you supply. Pair it with
[Browserbase Search](#using-browserbase-search) when the model needs to find the
page first.

To use Browserbase Fetch, import `gateway` from `ai` and pass
`gateway.tools.browserbaseFetch()` to `tools`:

> **💡 Note:** Browserbase Fetch is priced per option. A plain `raw` fetch costs $1 per 1,000
> requests. Routing through proxies adds $3 per 1,000, and extraction (`markdown`
> or `json` format) adds another $3 per 1,000, so a proxied extraction costs $7
> per 1,000. The surcharges are billed from the options actually sent upstream and
> reported in the gateway usage metadata.

#### streamText

```typescript filename="browserbase-fetch.ts" {9-11}
import { gateway, streamText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const result = streamText({
    model: 'openai/gpt-5.6-sol', // Works with any model
    prompt,
    tools: {
      browserbase_fetch: gateway.tools.browserbaseFetch({ format: 'markdown' }),
    },
  });

  for await (const part of result.fullStream) {
    if (part.type === 'text-delta') {
      process.stdout.write(part.text);
    } else if (part.type === 'tool-result') {
      console.log('Page contents received');
    }
  }

  return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
}
```

#### generateText

```typescript filename="browserbase-fetch.ts" {9-22}
import { gateway, generateText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const { text } = await generateText({
    model: 'openai/gpt-5.6-sol', // Works with any model
    prompt,
    tools: {
      browserbase_fetch: gateway.tools.browserbaseFetch({
        allowRedirects: true,
        format: 'json',
        schema: {
          type: 'object',
          properties: {
            title: { type: 'string' },
            summary: { type: 'string' },
          },
          required: ['title', 'summary'],
        },
      }),
    },
  });

  return Response.json({ text });
}
```

### Browserbase Fetch parameters

You can configure the `browserbaseFetch` tool with these parameters:

- `format`: Output format for the fetched content. Values: `'raw'` (the upstream
  response body unchanged), `'markdown'` (the page converted to
  Markdown), or `'json'` (structured extraction, which requires `schema`).
  Browserbase defaults to `'raw'` when the request omits `format`.
  `'markdown'` and `'json'` run extraction and are billed above the base rate.
- `schema`: JSON Schema describing the object to extract. Only valid when
  `format` is `'json'`. Omitting `schema` with `'json'` passes AI Gateway
  validation but causes an error from Browserbase.
- `allowRedirects`: Follow HTTP redirects. Defaults to `false`.
- `proxies`: Route the request through Browserbase's proxy network. Defaults to
  `false`. Billed above the base rate.
- `allowInsecureSsl`: Skip TLS certificate verification. Defaults to `false`.

The model supplies the `url`, which must be an absolute `http` or `https` URL. It
can also supply `format`, `allow_redirects`, and `proxies` unless you set them.

Because `format` and `proxies` each affect the price, a model that selects
`proxies: true` together with `markdown` or `json` output raises the cost of a
call from $1 to $7 per 1,000. Set either option in `browserbaseFetch()` to pin
it and cap the per-call cost.

> **💡 Note:** `schema` and `allowInsecureSsl` are developer configuration only. A model cannot
> set them, so a prompt-injected value is discarded before the fetch runs.

AI Gateway applies options you set in `browserbaseFetch()` as developer defaults, overriding model-generated values.

If Browserbase extraction is unavailable or its quota is exhausted, `'markdown'`
and `'json'` requests can return `configuration_error` with status code 403 or
402\. Retry with `format: 'raw'` and omit `schema`.

For the complete input and output schema, see the [AI SDK AI Gateway reference](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/ai-sdk-providers/ai-gateway#browserbase-fetch). For fetch behavior and Browserbase-specific options, see the [Browserbase Fetch documentation](https://docs.browserbase.com/platform/fetch/overview).

## Using DeepSeek Search

Use `gateway.tools.deepseekSearch()` with any model that supports tool calling
to find pages with DeepSeek's search engine. Results include titles, URLs,
snippets, summaries, and optional page content. You only need an AI Gateway API
key; a DeepSeek API key is not required.

Use `@ai-sdk/gateway` version `3.0.227` or later with AI SDK 6, or `4.0.133` or
later with AI SDK 7.

```typescript filename="deepseek-search.ts"
import { gateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: gateway('openai/gpt-6.1-terra'),
  prompt: 'Search for the latest Vercel AI Gateway updates.',
  tools: {
    deepseek_search: gateway.tools.deepseekSearch({
      count: 5,
      needContent: true,
    }),
  },
});

console.log(text);
```

### DeepSeek Search parameters

All configuration fields are optional. Values you set override the model's
arguments for that field.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `query` | Pin the search query. Must contain 1 to 128 Unicode characters and cannot be all whitespace. Supports operators such as `site:`, `lang:`, `before:`, and `after:`. |
| `count` | Number of results, from 1 to 50. Defaults to `10`. |
| `needContent` | Include page content when available. Defaults to `false`. |
| `oriQuestion` | The original question that triggered the search, from 1 to 128 characters. `null` is treated as omitted. |
| `localization` | An IP address used to localize results. Set this in tool configuration; it is not a model-generated argument. |

### DeepSeek Search and Fetch pricing

| Tool | Price per 1,000 billable requests |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek Search | $0.75 |
| DeepSeek Fetch | $0.75 |

Search is billable when a successful request returns a nonempty results array,
including results that are filtered before reaching the model. Fetch is billable
when a successful request returns nonempty page content. Failed requests,
timeouts, and empty results are not billed. The requested result count does not
change the price.

The host model's input and output tokens are charged separately, including tool
results in its context. Remove the tools from `tools` to stop further tool calls.
See [AI Gateway pricing](/docs/ai-gateway/pricing) for model pricing and spending
controls.

## Using DeepSeek Fetch

Use `gateway.tools.deepseekFetch()` to read a known HTTP or HTTPS URL. It returns
Markdown content and a page title when available. You can pair it with
[DeepSeek Search](#using-deepseek-search) to find and then read pages.

```typescript filename="deepseek-fetch.ts"
import { gateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';
import { streamText } from 'ai';

const result = streamText({
  model: gateway('openai/gpt-6.1-terra'),
  prompt: 'Fetch https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway and summarize it.',
  tools: {
    deepseek_fetch: gateway.tools.deepseekFetch({
      url: 'https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway',
    }),
  },
});

for await (const part of result.fullStream) {
  if (part.type === 'text-delta') {
    process.stdout.write(part.text);
  } else if (part.type === 'tool-error') {
    console.error('The page could not be fetched.');
  }
}
```

### DeepSeek Fetch parameters

The optional `url` configuration pins the page to fetch. Otherwise, the model
supplies the URL. URLs must be at most 8192 characters, include a host, and have
no username or password. Fetch supports Markdown output only. Access depends on
the target site's availability and policies.

Both tools report failures as `tool-error` stream parts. With `generateText`,
check `result.content` for `tool-error` entries when handling tool failures.
See [DeepSeek Search and Fetch pricing](#deepseek-search-and-fetch-pricing) and
the [DeepSeek documentation](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search) for
more details.

## Using AI Gateway search tools with Chat Completions

Use AI Gateway server tools from the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API. AI
Gateway executes the search, adds the results to the model context, and returns
the final answer in the same response.

Choose the search provider by adding one server tool to `tools`:

| Tool type | Search provider | Required config field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vercel:browserbase_search` | Browserbase | `query` |
| `vercel:deepseek_search` | DeepSeek | `query` |
| `vercel:exa_search` | Exa | `query` |
| `vercel:parallel_search` | Parallel | `objective` |
| `vercel:perplexity_search` | Perplexity | `query` |
| `vercel:tako_search` | Tako | `query` |

Browserbase Fetch and DeepSeek Fetch are also available as server tools. Add
`vercel:browserbase_fetch` or `vercel:deepseek_fetch` with a `url` config field to
fetch a page instead of searching for one.

Put static tool settings in `config`. Use snake case for config keys. AI Gateway
uses these values as developer defaults and overrides model-generated values.

For example, this request requires an Exa search before the model answers:

```bash
curl https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openai/gpt-6-astra",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Summarize Vercel AI Gateway in one sentence."
      }
    ],
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "vercel:exa_search",
        "config": {
          "query": "Vercel AI Gateway",
          "type": "instant",
          "num_results": 1
        }
      }
    ],
    "tool_choice": "required",
    "max_tokens": 128
  }'
```

Use `tool_choice: "auto"` to let the model decide whether to search. Use
`"required"` when the request must make an initial search. Do not use a named
function `tool_choice` for server tools.

AI Gateway executes server tools internally. The final Chat Completions response
has `finish_reason: "stop"` and does not include client-facing `tool_calls` or raw
search results. Inspect `choices[0].message.provider_metadata.gateway.gatewayToolCalls`
for successful search-call counts and the gateway metadata for aggregate cost.

Use distinct names for your own function tools. Do not define a client function
named `browserbase_fetch`, `browserbase_search`, `exa_search`,
`parallel_search`, `perplexity_search`, or `tako_search` in a request that
includes the corresponding AI Gateway server tool.

## Using Parallel Search

The `parallelSearch` tool can be used with any model regardless of the model provider or creator. [Parallel AI](https://parallel.ai/) provides LLM-optimized web search that extracts relevant excerpts from web pages, making it ideal for research tasks and information retrieval.

To use Parallel Search, import `gateway` from `ai` and pass `gateway.tools.parallelSearch()` to the `tools` parameter. When the model needs current information, it calls the tool and AI Gateway routes the request to [Parallel's Search API](https://docs.parallel.ai/api-reference/search/search).

> **💡 Note:** Parallel web search requests are charged at $5 per 1,000 requests in every
> search mode (includes up to 10 results per request). Additional results beyond
> 10 are charged at $1 per 1,000 additional results.

#### streamText

```typescript filename="parallel-web-search.ts" {9-11}
import { gateway, streamText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const result = streamText({
    model: 'anthropic/claude-opus-5', // Works with any model
    prompt,
    tools: {
      parallel_search: gateway.tools.parallelSearch(),
    },
  });

  for await (const part of result.stream) {
    if (part.type === 'text-delta') {
      process.stdout.write(part.text);
    } else if (part.type === 'tool-call') {
      console.log('Tool call:', part.toolName);
    } else if (part.type === 'tool-result') {
      console.log('Search results received');
    }
  }

  return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
}
```

#### generateText

```typescript filename="parallel-web-search.ts" {9-11}
import { gateway, generateText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const { text } = await generateText({
    model: 'anthropic/claude-opus-5', // Works with any model
    prompt,
    tools: {
      parallel_search: gateway.tools.parallelSearch(),
    },
  });

  return Response.json({ text });
}
```

### Parallel parameters

The `mode` parameter trades excerpt depth for latency. Every mode costs the same, $5 per 1,000 requests:

| Mode         | Behavior                                                              |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `'turbo'`    | Lowest latency, shorter excerpts. Supports English and Japanese only. |
| `'fast'`     | Low latency, shorter excerpts.                                        |
| `'basic'`    | Balanced latency and excerpt depth. This is the default.              |
| `'advanced'` | Most thorough results, higher latency.                                |

When you don't set `mode`, the model can choose one for each search, and AI Gateway uses `'basic'` if the model doesn't send one. The `'one-shot'` and `'agentic'` modes are deprecated but still accepted. AI Gateway runs `'one-shot'` as `'basic'` and `'agentic'` as `'advanced'`, at the same price.

You can configure the `parallelSearch` tool with these parameters:

- `mode`: Search mode. Values: `'turbo'`, `'fast'`, `'basic'` (default), or `'advanced'`.
- `maxResults`: Maximum number of results to return (1-20). Defaults to 10.
- `location`: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to localize results, such as `'us'`. Parallel ignores invalid codes and returns a warning.
- `maxCharsTotal`: Maximum total characters across all result excerpts.
- `sourcePolicy`: Controls which domains and date ranges to include or exclude. The include and exclude lists can hold up to 200 entries combined.
  - `includeDomains`: Domains or domain/path prefixes to restrict search results to, such as `['arxiv.org', 'docs.python.org/3']`.
  - `excludeDomains`: Domains or domain/path prefixes to exclude from search results.
  - `afterDate`: Only return results published on or after this date (format: `YYYY-MM-DD`).
- `excerpts`: Controls result excerpt length.
  - `maxCharsPerResult`: Maximum characters per result excerpt.
  - `maxCharsTotal`: Deprecated. Use the top-level `maxCharsTotal` instead.
- `fetchPolicy`: Controls content freshness.
  - `maxAgeSeconds`: Maximum age of cached content, in seconds, before Parallel fetches the page live. The minimum is 600 seconds, and AI Gateway raises lower values to 600.
  - `timeoutSeconds`: Timeout for a live fetch, up to 55 seconds.
  - `disableCacheFallback`: Set to `true` to return an error instead of older cached content when a live fetch fails. Defaults to `false`.

The model supplies the `objective` and two or three keyword `searchQueries` for each search. If the model sends no queries, AI Gateway searches with the objective.

AI Gateway applies options you set in `parallelSearch()` as developer defaults, overriding model-generated values.

Each tool result contains a `search_id`, a `session_id`, and `results`, ordered by decreasing relevance. Each result has a `url`, a `title`, a `publish_date` (both may be `null`), and `excerpts`, an array of markdown strings. The tool result can also include `usage` and `warnings`, for example when Parallel ignores an invalid `location`.

#### streamText

```typescript filename="parallel-web-search-params.ts" {9-22}
import { gateway, streamText } from 'ai';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { prompt } = await request.json();

  const result = streamText({
    model: 'anthropic/claude-opus-5',
    prompt,
    tools: {
      parallel_search: gateway.tools.parallelSearch({
        mode: 'advanced',
        location: 'us',
        maxResults: 5,
        sourcePolicy: {
          includeDomains: ['arxiv.org', 'nature.com', 'science.org'],
          afterDate: '2025-01-01',
        },
        excerpts: {
          maxCharsPerResult: 5000,
        },
      }),
    },
  });

  return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
}
```

#### generateText


# AI Gateway Analytics API

Use the Analytics API to measure requests per minute (RPM) and tokens per minute (TPM) for recorded language model activity. Query hourly trends, compare models and providers, or filter activity to an API key.

> **💡 Note:** The Analytics API requires preview access for your Pro or Enterprise team.
> Hobby teams and Pro trials aren't eligible. Contact Vercel Support through
> your dashboard to request access.

## Endpoint and authentication

Send a `GET` request to the analytics endpoint:

```text
https://api.vercel.com/ai-gateway/analytics
```

Use an [AI Gateway API key](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/api-keys) belonging to the team with preview access. Set the key as `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` in your environment and send it in the `Authorization` header:

```text
Authorization: Bearer <AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY>
```

An API key authenticates access to **team-wide activity** by default. Add `api_key_id=self` to query only the key's activity. To query another key on the same team, pass that key's public ID as `api_key_id`. The public ID is separate from the secret you send in the authorization header.

The endpoint also accepts authorized classic Vercel personal access tokens (PATs) and verified workload [Vercel OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens](/docs/oidc). PATs require the team's `aiGatewayUsage:create` permission. The `self` filter requires AI Gateway API key authentication.

## Query hourly activity

Set `group_by=day&date_part=hour` to get hourly buckets. **One hour is the smallest supported bucket.** Each bucket contains statistics calculated from its completed minutes.

This example queries today's activity in UTC. Change the dates to query another interval within the last 30 UTC dates:

```bash filename="Query hourly activity"
START_DATE="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
END_DATE="$START_DATE"

curl --get 'https://api.vercel.com/ai-gateway/analytics' \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "start_date=$START_DATE" \
  --data-urlencode "end_date=$END_DATE" \
  --data-urlencode 'group_by=day' \
  --data-urlencode 'date_part=hour'
```

A successful request returns HTTP `200` with `results` and `metadata`. The following example uses illustrative values:

```json filename="Hourly response"
{
  "results": [
    {
      "hour": "2026-09-21T12",
      "rpm": {
        "avg": 1,
        "p50": 0,
        "p95": 10,
        "p99": 20,
        "max": 20,
        "sample_count": 60
      },
      "tpm_millions": {
        "avg": 0.01,
        "p50": 0,
        "p95": 0.1,
        "p99": 0.2,
        "max": 0.2,
        "sample_count": 60
      }
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "contract_version": "recorded-language-v1",
    "source_version": "minute-v1-components5-recorded-events-v1@missing-as-no-traffic-r1",
    "scope": "language-recorded-filtered",
    "coverage_start": "2026-08-25T00:00:00.000Z",
    "evaluated_at": "2026-09-23T01:18:18.000Z",
    "completed_minutes_before": "2026-09-23T01:18:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

The `hour` label uses UTC. In this example, `2026-09-21T12` covers 12:00 through 12:59 UTC. The 60 minute samples average one recorded request per minute, with a busiest minute of 20 requests.

## Query parameters

Provide each parameter at most once. The API rejects unknown parameters and supports one grouping dimension per query.

| Parameter             | Required | Default           | Description                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------- | -------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start_date`          | Yes      | None              | Inclusive UTC start date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.                                                                                                                        |
| `end_date`            | Yes      | None              | Inclusive UTC end date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Must be on or after `start_date`, with at most seven dates per query.                                                    |
| `group_by`            | No       | `day`             | One of `api_key_name`, `credential_type`, `day`, `model`, `provider`, `tag`, `user`, or `zero_data_retention`.                                                          |
| `date_part`           | No       | `day`             | `day` or `hour`. Only affects `group_by=day`.                                                                                                                           |
| `api_key_id`          | No       | All keys          | `self` or an exact public API key ID within the authenticated team.                                                                                                     |
| `user_id`             | No       | All users         | Exact user ID attached to inference requests.                                                                                                                           |
| `model`               | No       | All models        | Exact recorded model identifier, such as `moonshotai/kimi-k3`.                                                                                                          |
| `provider`            | No       | All providers     | Exact recorded provider identifier, such as `fireworks`. Provider identifiers retain their recorded spelling, including `vertexAnthropic`.                              |
| `credential_type`     | No       | All types         | `byok` for bring your own key credentials, or `system` for AI Gateway credentials.                                                                                      |
| `zero_data_retention` | No       | All values        | The string `true` or `false`, matching the recorded zero data retention value.                                                                                          |
| `tags`                | No       | All tags          | One to 10 comma-separated tags, each one to 64 Unicode code points.                                                                                                     |
| `tags_match`          | No       | `any`             | Match `any` or `all` supplied tags. Only affects queries with `tags`.                                                                                                   |
| `teamId`              | No       | Credential's team | Team selector for supported authentication methods, such as Vercel access tokens. Mutually exclusive with `slug`. An AI Gateway API key remains scoped to its own team. |
| `slug`                | No       | Credential's team | Team slug instead of `teamId`.                                                                                                                                          |

The API applies exact string filters without trimming whitespace. For `tags`, URL decoding happens before comma splitting, so an encoded comma still separates tags. You can't filter for an individual tag containing a comma. When you group by `tag`, each matching event contributes to every tag attached to that event.

If your PAT has no implicit team context, provide `teamId` or `slug`. This endpoint doesn't use your default team to select one.

### Date range and granularity

- Dates are inclusive. A request from September 21 through September 22 covers two UTC dates.
- Each query can span up to seven dates. The earliest supported start date is the current UTC date minus 29 days.
- The API includes only minutes completed before `metadata.completed_minutes_before`. Future portions of an interval contribute no samples.
- Hourly queries require `group_by=day&date_part=hour`. The API rejects `group_by=hour` and `date_part=minute`.
- With `group_by=model` or `group_by=provider`, statistics cover the full requested interval. Adding `date_part=hour` doesn't split those rows by hour.

### Filter by API key

Using the date variables from the hourly example, query the authenticating key's activity by model:

```bash filename="Query this key's models"
curl --get 'https://api.vercel.com/ai-gateway/analytics' \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "start_date=$START_DATE" \
  --data-urlencode "end_date=$END_DATE" \
  --data-urlencode 'group_by=model' \
  --data-urlencode 'api_key_id=self'
```

Replace `self` with a public key ID to filter another key on your team. A key with no matching recorded inference activity returns an empty `results` array.

### Compare providers for a model

Filter to a model and group its activity by provider:

```bash filename="Query a model's providers"
curl --get 'https://api.vercel.com/ai-gateway/analytics' \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "start_date=$START_DATE" \
  --data-urlencode "end_date=$END_DATE" \
  --data-urlencode 'model=moonshotai/kimi-k3' \
  --data-urlencode 'group_by=provider'
```

Each result contains a `provider` field alongside `rpm` and `tpm_millions`. For hourly activity from one provider, use `group_by=day&date_part=hour` with both `model` and `provider` filters.

## Response fields

Each result includes one grouping field and two metric distributions. For example, a model query returns `model`, `rpm`, and `tpm_millions`. A model row can also include [`custom_rate_limits`](#current-custom-model-limits).

| Field          | Meaning                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Grouping field | Matches `group_by`, except hourly queries return `hour`. Non-time grouping values can be `null` when the recorded event lacks that dimension. |
| `rpm`          | Distribution of recorded event counts per completed minute.                                                                                   |
| `tpm_millions` | Distribution of approximate recorded token volume per minute, expressed in millions. A value of `0.5` means 500,000 tokens per minute.        |

Both metric objects have the same fields:

| Field          | Type             | Meaning                                                                       |
| -------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `avg`          | Number or `null` | Average across completed minute samples.                                      |
| `p50`          | Number or `null` | 50th percentile, or median, minute value.                                     |
| `p95`          | Number or `null` | 95th percentile minute value.                                                 |
| `p99`          | Number or `null` | 99th percentile minute value.                                                 |
| `max`          | Number or `null` | Largest minute value in the interval.                                         |
| `sample_count` | Integer          | Number of completed minute samples. A full hour has 60; a full day has 1,440. |

Percentiles use the nearest-rank method across minute samples. Query the full interval you need instead of averaging percentiles from separate responses.

### Recorded activity and empty results

The Analytics API counts recorded language model events, including recorded failures, cancellations, and repeated event deliveries. It excludes batch activity and marked Realtime usage flushes. For spend and token totals, use [Custom Reporting](/docs/ai-gateway/observability-and-spend/custom-reporting).

Token volume sums recorded input, output, reasoning, cached input, and cache creation tokens. Provider reporting can overlap these components, so treat `tpm_millions` as an approximate activity measure rather than a billing total.

Analytics distributions aren't enforcement counters. BYOK activity, MPI-specific limit buckets, and token normalization can make them differ from rate limit usage, so don't use them to calculate exact remaining capacity.

The API handles missing activity as follows:

- Within a returned group, completed minutes without recorded activity count as zero.
- Groups with no matching records don't appear. This includes entirely empty day or hour buckets.
- A query with no matching groups returns HTTP `200` with `results: []` and metadata.
- If a discovered group has no completed minutes, its `sample_count` is `0` and its five statistics are `null`.
- When you group by `api_key_name`, keys that share a name contribute to the same group. Use `api_key_id` to isolate one key.

### Current custom model limits

With `group_by=model`, a row includes `custom_rate_limits` when your team has explicit custom limits for that exact model. The following illustrative model row shows all three optional dimensions:

```json filename="Model result with custom limits"
{
  "model": "moonshotai/kimi-k3",
  "rpm": {
    "avg": 10,
    "p50": 8,
    "p95": 18,
    "p99": 24,
    "max": 24,
    "sample_count": 1440
  },
  "tpm_millions": {
    "avg": 0.12,
    "p50": 0.1,
    "p95": 0.22,
    "p99": 0.3,
    "max": 0.3,
    "sample_count": 1440
  },
  "custom_rate_limits": {
    "itpm": 1000000,
    "rpm": 3000,
    "ttpm": 4000000
  }
}
```

| Field  | Unit                                                                                   |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rpm`  | Requests per minute                                                                    |
| `itpm` | Uncached input tokens per minute, including cache creation and excluding cache reads   |
| `ttpm` | Total tokens per minute                                                                |

Custom limits use raw integer counts. For example, `itpm: 1000000` means one million uncached input tokens per minute, including cache creation and excluding cache reads. Unset dimensions don't appear; an explicitly configured zero remains `0`.

**Custom limits reflect the configuration when you query, including queries for past dates.** If you change a model's RPM limit from 100 to 500 today, a query for yesterday's activity shows 500. The API reads current limits separately from cached statistics, subject to configuration propagation. Neither `metadata.evaluated_at` nor the requested dates identify when those limits took effect.

The field includes only explicit custom model limits. It doesn't include default limits, provider-specific limits, or remaining quota. An absent field doesn't establish that the model has no limit. The API also omits limits for models with no matching activity.

Provider, daily, and hourly rows don't include `custom_rate_limits`, even with a model filter. A `group_by=model&provider=fireworks` query can include the model-wide custom limits alongside activity filtered to Fireworks.

### Metadata

Every successful response includes metadata, including empty responses:

| Field                      | Meaning                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `contract_version`         | Identifier for the response and metric contract. Currently `recorded-language-v1`.                                                     |
| `source_version`           | Opaque version identifier for the data source and calculation rules. Preserve this value when comparing reports or reporting an issue. |
| `scope`                    | Activity scope. Currently `language-recorded-filtered`.                                                                                |
| `coverage_start`           | Earliest date you can query, expressed as midnight UTC. This is a query boundary; it doesn't guarantee complete ingestion of activity. |
| `evaluated_at`             | Time the API evaluated the statistics. Cached results retain this timestamp. It doesn't timestamp the custom limit configuration.      |
| `completed_minutes_before` | Exclusive UTC cutoff for minute samples. The API excludes the minute beginning at this timestamp and all later minutes.                |

## Caching and request limits

The API can cache statistics for 60 seconds. Responses use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, and cached requests still count toward your analytics request limit.

By default, each team can make a burst of 30 analytics requests, with capacity replenishing at 30 requests per minute. Team overrides can change this limit. A separate concurrency limit applies to distinct queries running at the same time.

When present, response headers describe the analytics request limit:

| Header                  | Meaning                                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit`     | Team's analytics request capacity.                                                       |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Remaining capacity after this request.                                                   |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset`     | Estimated Unix timestamp in seconds when capacity fully replenishes.                     |
| `Retry-After`           | Number of seconds to wait before retrying a rejected or temporarily unavailable request. |

These headers apply to calls to the Analytics API. Use `custom_rate_limits` for any explicit custom model inference limits in the response.

## Error responses

Errors include an `error` object with a `code` and `message`. For example, a team without preview access receives:

```json filename="Preview access error"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "analytics_access_denied",
    "message": "Analytics preview is not available for this team."
  }
}
```

| HTTP status    | Code                                                           | Action                                                                                      |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400`          | `analytics_invalid_query`                                      | Check parameter names, allowed values, duplicate parameters, and the seven-date maximum.    |
| `400`          | `analytics_history_unavailable`                                | Choose dates within the rolling history window.                                             |
| `401` or `403` | Authentication or authorization error                          | Check the credential, team, and access permissions. Missing credentials can return `403`.   |
| `403`          | `analytics_access_denied`                                      | Confirm that your team has an eligible plan and preview access.                             |
| `422`          | `analytics_result_too_large`                                   | Narrow the date interval or add filters. A query can return up to 1,000 groups.             |
| `429`          | `rate_limited` or `analytics_concurrency_limited`              | Wait for the `Retry-After` duration before retrying.                                        |
| `500`          | Internal error                                                 | Retry with backoff. Contact support if the error persists.                                  |
| `502`          | `analytics_invalid_upstream_response`                          | Retry with backoff.                                                                         |
| `503`          | `analytics_eligibility_unavailable` or `analytics_unavailable` | Honor `Retry-After` and retry. Unavailable data returns an error rather than empty results. |

## Related resources

- [Custom Reporting](/docs/ai-gateway/observability-and-spend/custom-reporting) for spend and token totals.
- [Request logs](/docs/ai-gateway/observability-and-spend/logs) for individual requests and routing attempts.
- [API keys](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/api-keys) for creating and managing credentials.
