title: "AI Gateway Provider Allowlist"
description: "Restrict which AI providers your team can route through AI Gateway. Available on Pro and Enterprise."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.122Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/provider-allowlist"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# AI Gateway Provider Allowlist

The provider allowlist lets team owners restrict which AI providers can serve requests through AI Gateway. A request only returns a `403` when no allowed provider can serve it. The feature is opt-in and available on Pro and Enterprise plans.

A common reason to enable this is compliance: your team has reviewed a specific set of providers, and you want to guarantee that AI Gateway never routes to one you haven't approved.

## Pricing

The provider allowlist is a team-wide setting that applies to every request, and the [`only` parameter](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/provider-options#provider-filtering-ordering-and-sorting) in `providerOptions` applies the same kind of restriction per request at no additional cost. Both controls remove failover to providers outside the list, so reserve them for when you need to name the exact providers that can serve traffic. When the requirement is about data handling, [zero data retention](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/zdr), [disallow prompt training](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/disallow-prompt-training), and [regional inference](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/regional-inference) filter by that requirement while keeping every qualifying provider eligible. Regional inference passes through the provider's [regional price](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/regional-inference#regional-pricing), which can be higher.

| Option                       | Cost                                | Availability       |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| Per-request `only` filter    | No additional cost                  | All plans          |
| Team-wide provider allowlist | $0.10 per 1,000 successful requests | Pro and Enterprise |

The team-wide surcharge applies only to successful responses. Requests blocked by the allowlist (`403`) and other failures are not charged.

## Enabling the allowlist

Only team owners can change this setting.

1. Open the [AI Gateway **Settings** tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Fsettings\&title=AI+Gateway+Settings).
2. Toggle on **Restrict allowed providers**.

When you toggle on, every provider currently available on AI Gateway is added to the allowlist by default. This guarantees that turning the feature on never breaks existing traffic. You then remove providers you want to block as an explicit action.

## Disabling specific providers

With the allowlist enabled, switch off any providers your team should not use. The list is searchable. The footer shows how many providers are currently enabled.

Disabling a provider removes it from the routing candidates for any request. If the model has other providers that are still allowed, AI Gateway falls back to one of them. If every candidate provider for the request is disabled, the request returns:

```json
{
  "error": "Your team has restricted access to this provider. Contact the owner of the account for more details.",
  "type": "no_providers_available",
  "statusCode": 403
}
```

The allowlist filters by provider only. A model like `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` is served by both `openai` and `azure`; disabling `openai` alone still routes that model through `azure`. To block a model entirely, disable every provider that serves it.

## New providers

When AI Gateway adds a new provider after you enable the allowlist, the new provider is disabled by default and shows a **New** badge in the settings list. An info note at the top of the list tells you how many new providers are waiting for a decision.

To clear the badges, decide which new providers to enable and click **Save**. A save with no changes also counts as acknowledgment and clears the badges. Disabled new providers stay disabled until you enable them.

## Request-level filtering

If you also use the request-level [`only`](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/provider-options#provider-filtering-ordering-and-sorting) filter in `providerOptions`, both filters apply. A request must satisfy both:

- The provider must be in the request's `only` list, and
- The provider must be in your team's allowlist.

If either filter rejects every candidate, the request returns a `403`.

## BYOK

The allowlist applies to [BYOK](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/byok) requests too. Disabling a provider means your team does not want any traffic to that provider through AI Gateway, even with your own credentials.

## Plan and role requirements

| Requirement | Detail                                              |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Plan        | Pro or Enterprise (not Pro trial)                   |
| Role        | Owner                                               |

Team members on non-owner roles can view the current configuration but cannot modify it.

> **💡 Note:** Allowlist changes can take a couple of minutes to propagate. In-flight
> requests finish under the previous settings. Once the change has propagated,
> new requests respect the updated allowlist.

title: "AI Gateway Regional Inference"
description: "Route AI Gateway inference to the region you choose, team-wide or per request, and control where providers store data, for data residency and compliance requirements."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.122Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/regional-inference"

# AI Gateway Regional Inference

AI Gateway lets you choose the region where your model's provider runs
inference, where the provider supports it. This may help with your data
residency, compliance, and latency requirements. You can pin one of these
regions, or leave inference on the default:

- 🇺🇸 **United States** (`us`): [available models](/ai-gateway/models?inferenceRegionUs=true)
- 🇪🇺 **European Union** (`eu`): [available models](/ai-gateway/models?inferenceRegionEu=true)
- 🇦🇺 **Australia** (`au`): [available models](/ai-gateway/models?inferenceRegionAu=true)
- 🇯🇵 **Japan** (`jp`): [available models](/ai-gateway/models?inferenceRegionJp=true)
- 🌐 **Any region** (`global`, the default): AI Gateway picks whichever region can serve the model

AI Gateway routes your data to the provider in a data center in the region you
choose, and to the extent the provider stores data, it's configured to store it
there. If AI Gateway can't honor the chosen region, the request fails instead of
silently running somewhere else. Tools that AI Gateway runs for you, such as web
search, are an exception (see [where your data goes](#where-your-data-goes)).

There are two ways to pin a region:

- **Team-wide**: Pin one or more regions for the whole team from the [AI Gateway Dashboard Settings tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Fsettings\&title=AI+Gateway+Settings). AI Gateway then restricts the team's requests to providers that can serve a selected region. See [team-wide region pinning](#team-wide-region-pinning).
- **Per-request**: Set [`inferenceRegion`](#choosing-a-region-per-request) in `providerOptions` for individual requests. This gives you fine-grained control over which requests you pin and where.

A per-request `inferenceRegion` takes precedence over the team-wide pin, and it
must stay inside it: a request that asks for a region the team hasn't pinned
fails with HTTP 400 instead of routing outside the pin. See
[how team-wide and per-request pinning interact](#how-team-wide-and-per-request-pinning-interact).

> **💡 Note:** `inferenceRegion` pins where the provider runs inference and stores your data.
> It doesn't pin where your request reaches AI Gateway: your request can
> terminate and be processed in any Vercel region before AI Gateway forwards it
> to the provider. Region-pinned gateway hosts that terminate TLS and run gateway
> processing in a single region are coming.

## Pricing

| Option                     | Cost                     | Availability       |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------ |
| Per-request region pinning | No additional cost       | All plans          |
| Team-wide region pinning   | $0.10 per 1,000 requests | Pro and Enterprise |

While your team has a team-wide pin, AI Gateway charges the team-wide pinning
surcharge on every successful request from the team, including:

- Requests that set their own `inferenceRegion`, because the team-wide pin still
  checks that the region is inside it
- Requests that use your [BYOK](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/byok)
  keys

AI Gateway doesn't charge it on failed requests, including a request that fails
because it asked for a region outside the pin. On WebSocket connections, AI
Gateway charges the surcharge once per session instead of once per response. You
also pay the provider's rate for the region that serves the request (see
[regional pricing](#regional-pricing)).

To stop the surcharge, remove the team-wide pin: uncheck every region under
**Region Pinning** in the [AI Gateway Dashboard Settings tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Fsettings\&title=AI+Gateway+Settings),
then click **Save**.

## What regional routing controls

Set `inferenceRegion` on a request and the provider runs inference in that
region. To the extent it stores anything at rest, it stores it in the same
region. One setting covers both:

| What happens to your data | Where it happens |
|---------------------------|------------------|
| The provider runs inference on your prompt | The region you set with `inferenceRegion` |
| The provider stores data at rest, if it stores anything | The same region |

What varies by provider is whether anything is stored at rest at all. Many
providers store nothing for inference, and
[zero data retention](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/zdr) has the
provider delete prompts and responses after the request (see
[where your data goes](#where-your-data-goes)).

## Team-wide region pinning

On Pro and Enterprise plans, a team can pin regions for every request it sends,
so callers don't have to set `inferenceRegion` themselves. This is useful when
residency is a team-level policy instead of a per-call decision. Only team
[**Owners**](/docs/rbac/access-roles/team-level-roles) can change the pin, and
teams on a Pro trial can't turn it on.

To pin regions team-wide:

1. Go to the [AI Gateway Dashboard](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway\&title=AI+Gateway).
2. Open the [**Settings** tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Fsettings\&title=AI+Gateway+Settings).
3. Under **Region Pinning**, check the regions you want to allow.
4. Drag the selected regions into your preference order, then click **Save**.
5. If the team had no regions pinned before, review the surcharge in the
   **Enable Region Pinning** dialog and click **Enable Region Pinning**.

To remove the pin, uncheck every region and click **Save**. With no regions
selected, the team is unpinned, which is the default: requests may use providers
in any region.

The order of the selected regions is the fallback priority. A provider that can
serve more than one of your regions gets an attempt in each, in the order listed.
By default, AI Gateway tries your
[BYOK](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/byok) keys before system
credentials, and applies the region order within each group. With `us` then `eu`
selected, that means your keys in `us`, then your keys in `eu`, then system
credentials in `us`, then system credentials in `eu`. Without BYOK keys, AI
Gateway tries every provider in `us` before any provider in `eu`. Either way, if
your first region fails, the request falls back to the next selected region
instead of failing.

Once you pin regions:

- AI Gateway drops providers that can't serve any selected region from routing.
  If no provider remains for the requested model, the request fails instead of
  routing out of region.
- Only models with regional endpoints work while the pin is on (see
  [keeping a request in-region](#keeping-a-request-in-region) to find them). AI
  Gateway doesn't have regional endpoints for image, video, speech,
  transcription, or realtime models yet, so requests and sessions for those
  models fail.
- An authenticated request to
  [`/v1/models`](https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models) with
  `include_availability` sets `model_eligibility.reason` to
  `inference_region_unavailable` on models that no provider serves in a pinned
  region, so you can check the pin's effect before sending a request. See
  [team availability annotations](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/rest-api#team-availability-annotations).
- Responses still report the region that served the request, so you can verify
  residency the same way (see [confirming where a request ran](#confirming-where-a-request-ran)).

Team-wide pinning carries a surcharge. See [pricing](#pricing).

## How team-wide and per-request pinning interact

A per-request `inferenceRegion` wins over the team-wide pin, within the bounds of
the pin:

| Team-wide pin | Request sets `inferenceRegion` | Result | [Surcharge](#pricing) |
|---------------|--------------------------------|--------|-----------------------|
| None | No | Routes globally, the default | No |
| None | Yes | Routes to the requested region | No |
| `us` | No | Routes to `us` | Yes |
| `us`, `eu` | No | Tries `us`, then falls back to `eu` (see [team-wide region pinning](#team-wide-region-pinning)) | Yes |
| `us` | `us` | Routes to `us` | Yes |
| `us` | `eu` | Fails with HTTP 400, `eu` is outside the pin | No, the request failed |
| `us` | `global` | Fails with HTTP 400, `global` isn't inside the pin | No, the request failed |

## Choosing a region per request

Set `providerOptions.gateway.inferenceRegion` on the request, and AI Gateway
routes inference to that region:

| Value | Where AI Gateway routes inference |
|-------|-----------------------------------|
| `{ scope: 'zone', geoRegion: 'us' }` | A US data center |
| `{ scope: 'zone', geoRegion: 'eu' }` | An EU data center |
| `{ scope: 'zone', geoRegion: 'au' }` | An Australian data center |
| `{ scope: 'zone', geoRegion: 'jp' }` | A Japanese data center |
| `{ scope: 'global' }` (or omitted) | Any region |

- The default (no `inferenceRegion`) is `global`, which means AI Gateway picks
  whichever region can serve the model, based on availability and latency. It can
  resolve to a different region on each request, and that region may be outside
  your users' jurisdiction. Residency is opt-in: pin a region if where inference
  runs matters to you.
- `zone` requires `geoRegion` (`us`, `eu`, `au`, or `jp`). If you omit it, the
  request fails.
- If your team has a [team-wide pin](#team-wide-region-pinning),
  `{ scope: 'global' }` fails with HTTP 400 because it asks to route outside the
  pin. Leave `inferenceRegion` out to route within the pin.
- You set the region in the request body or config only. There's no HTTP header
  for it.

These examples use AI SDK 7 and the AI SDK for Python beta. Set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` before running them. See [API format differences](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis#api-format-differences) for setup, request fields, and response handling.

#### AI SDK

#### TypeScript

```typescript filename="regional-inference.ts" {8-11}
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: 'openai/gpt-6-astra',
  prompt: 'Explain quantum computing in two sentences.',
  providerOptions: {
    gateway: {
      inferenceRegion: {
        scope: 'zone',
        geoRegion: 'us',
      },
    },
  },
});

console.log(text);
```

#### Python (beta)

```python filename="regional-inference_ai.py" {8}
import asyncio
import ai

async def main():
    model = ai.get_model("openai/gpt-6-astra")
    messages = [ai.user_message("Explain quantum computing in two sentences.")]
    params = ai.InferenceRequestParams(
        extra_body={"providerOptions": {"gateway": {"inferenceRegion": {"scope": "zone", "geoRegion": "us"}}}}
    )
    async with ai.stream(model, messages, params=params) as stream:
        async for event in stream:
            if isinstance(event, ai.events.TextDelta):
                print(event.chunk, end="", flush=True)
    print()

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Per-provider overrides (advanced)

Most callers set one region and stop. If more than one provider can serve a single
request, you can set a default plus per-provider overrides. The top-level value
applies to every provider unless you list that provider under `providers`:

```jsonc {2-9}
{
  "inferenceRegion": {
    "scope": "zone",
    "geoRegion": "us",           // default for all providers
    "providers": {
      "bedrock": { "scope": "zone", "geoRegion": "eu" },  // Bedrock only: EU
      "anthropic": null                                   // Anthropic: no region pinned
    }
  }
}
```

This reads as: AI Gateway routes your data to every provider in the US, except it
routes Bedrock traffic to the EU and leaves Anthropic unconstrained. AI Gateway
ignores unknown provider keys.

## Where your data goes

AI Gateway routes your data to the provider in the region you pin. To the extent
that provider stores your request data at rest, it's configured to store it in
that region. Each provider's own terms set what it keeps and for how long, so
check the provider's documentation for the specifics.

Tools that AI Gateway runs for you aren't pinned. When a model calls
[web search](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/web-search) tools such as
Perplexity Search, Exa Search, or Parallel Search, AI Gateway calls the tool
vendor's API wherever the vendor runs it, whether the region comes from the
request or a team-wide pin, so search queries built from your prompt can leave
the region.

Abuse and safety monitoring is separate. Regardless of your pinned region or
retention settings, a provider handles and retains requests it flags for abuse
or safety review under its own policies, which can fall outside your region.
Vercel doesn't control that or guarantee it beyond what the provider documents,
so check the provider's terms.

To limit retention, add [zero data retention (ZDR)](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/zdr),
where available. With ZDR, the provider deletes your prompts and responses after
the request rather than retaining them. Some provider models do not have ZDR. For
example, Anthropic's `fable-5` is ineligible for ZDR on every provider, so a
request with ZDR configured fails rather than route to it.

Not every provider serves every region, so coverage varies by provider and model
(see [Current limits](#current-limits)). Don't assume a request ran where you
asked; confirm the resolved region from the response (see [Confirming where a
request ran](#confirming-where-a-request-ran)).

## Regional pricing

Pinning a region can raise what a request costs. Providers often price regional
inference above their default routing, and one region can cost more than another
for the same model. The provider sets that price.

AI Gateway passes the provider's regional price straight through. Setting
`inferenceRegion` on a request adds no AI Gateway markup on top of it: you pay
the provider's rate for the region you picked.

AI Gateway bills team-wide pinning separately from the provider's rate. See
[pricing](#pricing).

To see what a model charges per region, open it from the
[model list](/ai-gateway/models) and hover the price in the **Providers** table.
The **Price by region** card shows each region's rate as a percentage difference
from the global price, for example `EU +10%`. A region that costs the same as
global reads `Same as global`.

The `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models` endpoint returns the same rates as
absolute per-token numbers, under `pricing.regional`:

```jsonc {4-7}
{
  "pricing": {
    "input": "0.000005",
    "regional": {
      "eu": { "input": "0.0000055" },
      "us": { "input": "0.0000055" }
    }
  }
}
```

To see what a specific request cost, check the cost reported in the response
metadata.

You pay a region's rate only when the request's `inferenceRegion` or your
team-wide pin selects that region. With neither (the `global` default), you pay
the provider's standard rate.

## BYOK and data residency

Bringing your own key doesn't opt you out of residency. When you use
[BYOK credentials](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/byok), AI Gateway
applies `inferenceRegion` the same way it does with system credentials:

- **AI Gateway routes your key's requests to in-region endpoints.** Your key
  material is untouched; AI Gateway regionalizes how it's used, calling the
  provider's in-region endpoint with your key.
- **An explicit region overrides a region saved on the credential.** If your
  Vertex credential is saved with a `location` and the request asks for a
  different region, the request's region wins. If you don't set a region, the
  credential's saved location applies where it has one.
- **Failure behavior is the same.** If no provider can honor the region with
  your credentials, the request fails with HTTP 400. AI Gateway doesn't fall
  back to an out-of-region endpoint, even when the credentials are your own.
- **Verification is the same.** Responses report the resolved region for BYOK
  requests too, so you can confirm residency from the response metadata.
- **Zero data retention skips BYOK keys by default.** If you pair a pinned region
  with ZDR, AI Gateway routes around your own credentials unless you mark a key as
  ZDR-compliant, since those keys run under your provider agreements rather than
  Vercel's. See [ZDR and BYOK](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/zdr#byok).

## Keeping a request in-region

Set `inferenceRegion` and the provider processes your prompts and completions,
and stores anything it keeps at rest, only in your chosen region. If it can't,
the request fails instead of running elsewhere.

To limit retention, add
[zero data retention](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/zdr) and
[disallow prompt training](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/disallow-prompt-training),
so the provider deletes your data after the request and doesn't train on it.
Whether a provider stores anything by default is provider-dependent (see
[where your data goes](#where-your-data-goes)).

Region coverage varies by model. To find models that support a region, filter the
[model list](/ai-gateway/models):

- [Models available in the US](/ai-gateway/models?inferenceRegionUs=true)
- [Models available in the EU](/ai-gateway/models?inferenceRegionEu=true)
- [Models available in Australia](/ai-gateway/models?inferenceRegionAu=true)
- [Models available in Japan](/ai-gateway/models?inferenceRegionJp=true)

The [`/v1/models`](https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models) endpoint returns the
same coverage as a `regions` array per model (for example, `["eu", "us"]`); a
model with no `regions` field doesn't support regional routing.

This pins where the provider processes and stores your data. It doesn't pin the
network path your request takes to reach the provider.

## Defaults and failure behavior

- If you request no region, AI Gateway routes your data globally. This isn't an
  error.
- If AI Gateway can't honor the region, the request fails with HTTP 400
  (`invalid_request_error`). AI Gateway doesn't silently fall back to another
  region.
- There's no automatic downgrade from a preferred region to a broader one.

## Confirming where a request ran

When you pin a region, every response reports where AI Gateway actually ran
inference, so you can verify residency instead of assuming it. The resolved region is in the gateway routing
metadata, on the provider attempt that served the request.

With the AI SDK, read it from `providerMetadata.gateway`. On the OpenAI-compatible
endpoints, the same object sits on each choice's message as
`provider_metadata.gateway`:

```jsonc {10-14}
{
  "gateway": {
    "routing": {
      "finalProvider": "openai",
      "modelAttempts": [
        {
          "providerAttempts": [
            {
              "provider": "openai",
              "inferenceEndpoint": {
                "slug": "geo-us",
                "scope": "zone",
                "geoRegion": "us"
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Read `inferenceEndpoint.geoRegion` (here `us`) and compare it against the region
you asked for; `finalProvider` names the provider that served the request. When
you don't pin a region, `inferenceEndpoint` is `null`, matching the `global`
default, which doesn't pin a region.

## GDPR and regional routing

If GDPR is the driver for pinning a region, consider your compliance needs: where
personal data is processed is one obligation among many. Regional routing answers
the location question; it doesn't by itself make a workload GDPR-compliant.

## Current limits

- The regions available today are `us`, `eu`, `au`, and `jp`, and not every
  model supports all of them. Check a model's `regions` in the [model list](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers)
  or from `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models`.
- Region selection is opt-in; the default is `global`, both per request and
  team-wide.
- There's no cross-region fallback: a region that AI Gateway can't honor fails the
  request. Team-wide pinning falls back across the regions you selected, in order,
  but never outside them.
- Regional routing doesn't apply to web search tools that AI Gateway runs for
  you (see [where your data goes](#where-your-data-goes)).
- Image, video, speech, transcription, and realtime models don't have regional
  endpoints yet, so they don't work with a region pinned.

title: "AI Gateway Safety Identifiers"
description: "Learn how to send a unique safety identifier per end user through AI Gateway so provider-side abuse action isolates individual users instead of your whole team."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.122Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/safety-identifiers"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# AI Gateway Safety Identifiers

A safety identifier tells providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta which of your end users a request belongs to, without sending anything that identifies that person. It gives providers a way to detect abuse at the level of a single user, so when one is flagged for a policy violation, the action targets that identifier instead of all of your team's traffic.

## Set a safety identifier per request

Set `safetyIdentifier` in `providerOptions.gateway` to a unique, opaque ID for the end user on whose behalf the request is made, such as a UUID or a hash of your internal user ID. Hash a username or email address rather than sending it, and do not include personal information of any kind. For users who are not signed in, send a session ID instead. The value can be at most 64 characters.

> **💡 Note:** The Messages and Responses examples use `providerOptions.gateway`, which
> isn't part of the upstream SDK types. Their TypeScript examples spread these
> extension fields into the request, and their Python examples use `extra_body`.
> Chat Completions accepts the typed `safety_identifier` field directly.

These examples use AI SDK 7 and the AI SDK for Python beta. Set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` before running them. See [API format differences](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis#api-format-differences) for setup, request fields, and response handling.

#### AI SDK

#### TypeScript

```typescript filename="safety-identifier.ts"
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: 'openai/gpt-6-astra',
  prompt: 'Explain quantum computing in two sentences.',
  providerOptions: {
    gateway: {
      safetyIdentifier: 'user_9f8e7d6c5b',
    },
  },
});

console.log(text);
```

#### Python (beta)

```python filename="safety-identifier_ai.py"
import asyncio
import ai

async def main():
    model = ai.get_model("openai/gpt-6-astra")
    messages = [ai.user_message("Explain quantum computing in two sentences.")]
    params = ai.InferenceRequestParams(
        extra_body={"providerOptions": {"gateway": {"safetyIdentifier": "user_9f8e7d6c5b"}}}
    )
    async with ai.stream(model, messages, params=params) as stream:
        async for event in stream:
            if isinstance(event, ai.events.TextDelta):
                print(event.chunk, end="", flush=True)
    print()

asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Chat Completions

Set `safety_identifier` at the top level of the Chat Completions request body. AI Gateway maps this field to `providerOptions.gateway.safetyIdentifier`, so it works across the [supported providers](#which-providers-receive-the-identifier). The value must be a non-empty string. AI Gateway truncates values longer than 64 characters.

#### TypeScript

```typescript filename="safety-identifier-chat.ts"
import OpenAI from 'openai';

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY,
  baseURL: 'https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1',
});

const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'openai/gpt-6-astra',
  messages: [
    {
      role: 'user',
      content: 'Explain quantum computing in two sentences.',
    },
  ],
  safety_identifier: 'user_9f8e7d6c5b',
});

console.log(response.choices[0]?.message.content);
```

#### Python

```python filename="safety-identifier_chat.py"
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-6-astra",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing in two sentences."}],
    safety_identifier="user_9f8e7d6c5b",
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

#### cURL

```bash filename="safety-identifier-chat.sh"
curl --fail-with-body https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "model": "openai/gpt-6-astra",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Explain quantum computing in two sentences."
    }
  ],
  "safety_identifier": "user_9f8e7d6c5b"
}'
```

#### Messages API

#### TypeScript

```typescript filename="safety-identifier-messages.ts"
import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';

  model: 'openai/gpt-6-astra',

      role: 'user',
      content: 'Explain quantum computing in two sentences.',
    },
  ],
  max_tokens: 1024,
  ...{
    providerOptions: {
      gateway: {
        safetyIdentifier: 'user_9f8e7d6c5b',
      },
    },
  },
});

for (const block of response.content) {
  if (block.type === 'text') console.log(block.text);
}
```

```bash filename="safety-identifier.sh"
      }
    }
  }'
```

## Which providers receive the identifier

AI Gateway forwards the identifier to whichever provider serves the request, using that provider's field:

- OpenAI models, including when served by Azure or Bedrock, receive it as OpenAI's `safety_identifier`
- Models served by Meta receive it as `safety_identifier`
- Anthropic models, including when served by Vertex or Claude Platform on AWS, receive it as Anthropic's `metadata.user_id`

The identifier follows the request across provider and model fallbacks, so the same value reaches whichever provider ultimately serves the request.

## Precedence

The `providerOptions.gateway.safetyIdentifier` option applies when you have not set a provider-specific identifier. If you set `providerOptions.openai.safetyIdentifier` or `providerOptions.anthropic.metadata.userId` directly, those values win for requests they apply to.

On the Chat Completions API, `providerOptions.gateway.safetyIdentifier` takes precedence over the top-level `safety_identifier` field. Both take precedence over the legacy `user` field, which also maps to a safety identifier for backwards compatibility.

# AI Gateway Zero Data Retention (ZDR)

Zero data retention (ZDR) is available on AI Gateway for Pro and Enterprise teams and for any team that has purchased AI Gateway credits. See [Availability](#availability) for details. There are two ways to enforce ZDR:

- **Team-wide**: Enable ZDR globally from the [AI Gateway Dashboard Settings tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway\&title=AI+Gateway). Once enabled, all requests are routed to ZDR-compliant providers.
- **Per-request**: Set `zeroDataRetention: true` in `providerOptions.gateway` for individual requests. This gives you fine-grained control over which requests require ZDR.

These two methods work as an OR: if either is enabled, ZDR is enforced for that request.

ZDR is a superset of [disallowing prompt training](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/disallow-prompt-training). All ZDR-compliant providers also disallow prompt training, but not all providers that disallow prompt training offer full zero data retention.

> **💡 Note:** AI Gateway skips your [BYOK (Bring Your Own
> Key)](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/byok) keys by default when ZDR
> is enabled, since BYOK keys operate under your own agreements with providers.
> You can mark individual BYOK keys as ZDR-compliant to include them in the ZDR
> routing set. See [BYOK](#byok) for details.

## Pricing

| Option                          | Cost                     |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Per-request zero data retention | No additional cost       |
| Team-wide zero data retention   | $0.10 per 1,000 requests |

Team-wide ZDR is only charged on successful responses that return usage data. Requests that fail or return errors are not charged.

## Availability

Per-request and team-wide ZDR both require a paid account, which means a Pro or Enterprise plan or purchased AI Gateway credits. Hobby teams and teams on a Pro trial can use ZDR once they [purchase credits](/docs/ai-gateway/pricing#top-up-your-ai-gateway-credits). Free credits don't count.

If you request ZDR from a team that isn't eligible, AI Gateway returns a `403`:

```json
{
  "error": "Zero Data Retention (ZDR) requires a paid account. Current plan: hobby. Please purchase AI Gateway credits at https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai%3Fmodal%3Dtop-up or upgrade your plan at https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fsettings%2Fbilling to access this feature. If you purchased credits in the last few minutes, retry shortly.",
  "type": "permission_denied",
  "statusCode": 403
}
```

AI Gateway checks your payment status again before it returns this error, so a credit purchase usually applies to your next request. If you purchased credits in the last few minutes and still get a `403`, retry shortly.

## Vercel

AI Gateway has a ZDR policy and does not retain prompts, outputs, or sensitive data. User data is immediately and permanently deleted after requests are completed. No action is needed on the user side.

## Providers

AI Gateway has agreements in place to offer ZDR with specific providers. A provider's default policy may not match with the status that AI Gateway has in place due to these agreements.

By default, AI Gateway does not route based on the data retention policy of providers.

> **💡 Note:** If we do not know a provider's ZDR stance or have not yet established an
> agreement with them, they are treated as not being ZDR-compliant. If ZDR is
> enabled for a request, it will not be routed through this provider.

## Team-wide zero data retention

Pro and Enterprise teams, and teams that have purchased AI Gateway credits, can enable ZDR globally for all requests from the [AI Gateway Dashboard](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway\&title=AI+Gateway). If your team isn't eligible, you can't turn on the toggle, and the settings page links to buying AI Gateway credits. If your team stops being eligible while team-wide ZDR is on, for example after downgrading from Pro, you can still turn it off.

To enable team-wide ZDR:

1. Go to the [AI Gateway Dashboard](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway)
2. Navigate to the [**Settings** tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Fsettings\&title=AI+Gateway+Settings)
3. Toggle on the **Zero Data Retention** option

Once enabled, team-wide ZDR applies to all requests through the Vercel team you configured it for. For how team-wide ZDR interacts with [BYOK](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/byok) keys, see [BYOK](#byok).

## Per-request zero data retention

You can enforce ZDR on individual requests using the `zeroDataRetention` parameter in `providerOptions.gateway`. Set `zeroDataRetention` to `true` to route the request only through providers that have zero data retention agreements with Vercel AI Gateway.

If your team isn't eligible for ZDR, the request fails with a `403` (see [Availability](#availability)). If no ZDR-compliant providers are available for the requested model, the request fails with an error:

```json
{
  "error": "No ZDR (Zero Data Retention) providers available for model: example/model-name. Providers considered: provider-a, provider-b",
  "type": "no_providers_available",
  "statusCode": 400
}
```

When ZDR is enabled, the routing metadata in successful responses shows how AI Gateway filtered providers. The `planningReasoning` field indicates which providers were considered:

```json
{
  "gateway": {
    "routing": {
      "planningReasoning": "ZDR requested: 5 attempts → 2 ZDR attempts. ZDR execution order: anthropic(system) → bedrock(system)"
    }
  }
}
```

ZDR enforcement also applies to any fallback providers. For how per-request ZDR interacts with [BYOK](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/byok) keys, see [BYOK](#byok).

These examples use AI SDK 7 and the AI SDK for Python beta. Set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` before running them. See [API format differences](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis#api-format-differences) for setup, request fields, and response handling.

#### AI SDK

#### TypeScript

See the [AI SDK zero-data-retention reference](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/ai-sdk-providers/ai-gateway#zero-data-retention-example) for SDK configuration and usage.

```typescript filename="zdr.ts" {8}
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5',
  prompt: 'Analyze this example business data: revenue grew by 5%.',
  providerOptions: {
    gateway: {
      zeroDataRetention: true,
    },
  },
});

console.log(text);
```

#### Python (beta)

```python filename="zdr_ai.py" {8}
import asyncio
import ai

async def main():
    model = ai.get_model("anthropic/claude-sonnet-5")
    messages = [ai.user_message("Analyze this example business data: revenue grew by 5%.")]
    params = ai.InferenceRequestParams(
        extra_body={"providerOptions": {"gateway": {"zeroDataRetention": True}}}
    )
    async with ai.stream(model, messages, params=params) as stream:
        async for event in stream:
            if isinstance(event, ai.events.TextDelta):
                print(event.chunk, end="", flush=True)
    print()

asyncio.run(main())
```

## BYOK

When ZDR is enabled, either team-wide or per-request, AI Gateway skips your [BYOK](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/byok) keys by default. BYOK keys operate under your own agreements and permissions with providers, which can differ from the ZDR agreements Vercel has negotiated for AI Gateway system credentials.

If you have your own ZDR agreement with a provider, you can mark a BYOK key as ZDR-compliant. AI Gateway then includes that key in the ZDR routing set. This option applies to both team-wide and request-level ZDR.

Marking a key as ZDR makes it eligible for ZDR routing. It does not enable ZDR by itself. ZDR routing applies only when team-wide ZDR is on or the request sets `zeroDataRetention: true`.

To mark a BYOK key as ZDR:

1. Go to the [AI Gateway Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) page](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Fbyok\&title=AI+Gateway+BYOK) in your Vercel dashboard.
2. Add a new key or edit an existing one.
3. Toggle on **Zero Data Retention**.

> **💡 Note:** You take responsibility for any BYOK key you mark as ZDR. Vercel has no
> visibility into your agreements with providers, so confirm your contract
> covers zero data retention before marking a key.

### Fallback behavior

When ZDR is enabled, AI Gateway filters the routing set for each model to ZDR-compliant providers only:

1. If you have BYOK keys for a ZDR-compliant provider that you marked as ZDR, AI Gateway tries those keys first.
2. If those BYOK keys fail or are unavailable, AI Gateway falls back to AI Gateway system credentials for the ZDR-compliant providers in the routing set.
3. If no ZDR-compliant providers are available for the model, the request fails with a `no_providers_available` error.

### Example

Consider the following setup:

- You have a BYOK key for Anthropic, marked as ZDR, because you have a direct ZDR agreement with Anthropic.
- You have a BYOK key for Google Vertex, not marked as ZDR.
- You have a BYOK key for OpenAI, not marked as ZDR.
- You send a request to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` with `zeroDataRetention: true`.

AI Gateway builds the ZDR routing set in two parts.

**BYOK routing set:**

- Your BYOK keys: Anthropic, Google Vertex, OpenAI
- Filter to ZDR-marked keys: Anthropic
- Filter to keys for providers serving `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`: Anthropic

**System credentials routing set:**

- System providers serving `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`: Anthropic, Google Vertex, Amazon Bedrock
- Filter to providers Vercel has ZDR agreements with: Anthropic, Google Vertex, Amazon Bedrock

**Final routing order:**

1. Anthropic BYOK (ZDR-marked) is tried first.
2. If that fails, AI Gateway falls back to system credentials for Anthropic, Google Vertex, or Amazon Bedrock.

Your Google Vertex BYOK is filtered out because you didn't mark it as ZDR, but Google Vertex is still reachable through system credentials. Your OpenAI BYOK is filtered out because OpenAI doesn't serve `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`.

## Using both account and request-level ZDR

Team-wide ZDR toggled to enabled overrides request-level `zeroDataRetention: false` since these options work together as an OR. If either option is enabled, ZDR is enforced on the request.

## Caching and zero data retention

When you use [prompt caching](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/automatic-caching) through AI Gateway, caching happens at the provider level. Whether that caching is ZDR-compliant depends on the provider.

## ZDR providers and policies

The following providers currently offer ZDR on AI Gateway. Please review each provider's ZDR policy and terms carefully. A provider's default policy may not match with the status that AI Gateway has in place due to negotiated agreements. We are constantly coordinating and revising agreements to be able to enforce stricter retention policies for customers. The full terms of service are available for each provider on the [model pages](/ai-gateway/models).

All ZDR-compliant providers also disallow prompt training, since ZDR is a superset of [disallowing prompt training](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/disallow-prompt-training). In some cases, certain models or functionalities may be excluded from a provider's ZDR policy. AI Gateway will not fail these requests if zero data retention is enabled, so review the provider's policy in the table below to understand the nuances of specific tools and how they affect data retention.

> **💡 Note:** Tool calls may not be covered by a provider's ZDR policy. When a model invokes
> a provider-executed tool, such as a provider-side [web
> search](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/web-search) or grounding tool,
> the data sent to that tool can be processed and retained by a separate service
> under its own terms. AI Gateway does not block or fail these requests when ZDR
> is enabled. It is your responsibility to review the provider's and the tool's
> terms to confirm whether tool calls are in scope of the ZDR policy before
> using provider-side tools with sensitive data.

last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.122Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass/billing"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Token Pass Credits and Billing

Token Pass is a monthly add-on to your team's Pro subscription. Vercel charges it on the same invoice, and it follows the same billing period.

## Summary

| Item           | Details                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Price          | $30 per team per month                                                   |
| Credit         | $80 per billing period                                                   |
| Billing period | Your team's Pro billing period                                           |
| First period   | Vercel prorates the charge and credit for the days left in the period    |
| Expiry         | Credit expires at the end of each billing period. It doesn't roll over   |
| Overage        | None. When credit runs out, Token Pass requests fail until the next period |
| Scope          | Per team. All members and Token Pass API keys on the team share the credit |
| Cancelling     | Takes effect at the end of the billing period. No refund for that period |

## How Token Pass credit works

AI Gateway prices each Token Pass request at the model's [list price](/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass#list-price) and deducts the cost from your Token Pass credit.

Token Pass credit is a separate balance from your AI Gateway credits:

- Token Pass credit only pays for [featured models](/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass/models-and-routing#featured-models) served by the Token Pass provider. It can't pay for other models.
- Your AI Gateway credit balance doesn't include Token Pass credit, and Token Pass requests don't use your AI Gateway credits.

## Subscribing mid-period

If you subscribe partway through your Pro billing period, your first charge covers only the days left in that period. Vercel prorates your first credit the same way. The confirmation screen shows the exact amount, including taxes and fees, and the date your $30 monthly charge starts.

After that, at the start of each billing period, Vercel charges $30 and adds $80 of credit.

## Credit reset

At the end of each billing period, unused credit expires. When the next period starts, your credit resets to $80. To see your remaining credit and reset date, open the [Token Pass tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Ftoken-pass\&title=Go+to+Token+Pass).

## When credit runs out

Token Pass doesn't charge overages or top up automatically. Once you use up your credit, requests with your Token Pass API key fail with a `403` error until your next billing period. To continue with paid usage, switch to a regular AI Gateway API key, which bills to your AI Gateway credits. See [Switch to regular AI Gateway usage](/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass/models-and-routing#switch-to-regular-ai-gateway-usage).

## Cancel

To cancel Token Pass:

1. In AI Gateway, open [**Token Pass**](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Ftoken-pass\&title=Go+to+Token+Pass).
2. Under **Billing Settings**, select **Unsubscribe from Token Pass**.
3. Confirm.

Team owners and members with permission to manage billing can cancel. Cancellation takes effect at the end of your current billing period:

- You keep your remaining credit and can use it until the period ends.
- Vercel doesn't refund the current period.
- Vercel doesn't charge you for Token Pass again.

## Downgrading from Pro

Token Pass requires a Pro plan. If you downgrade your team to Hobby:

- Your Pro plan downgrades under its normal terms.
- Vercel doesn't refund Token Pass.
- You keep Token Pass and your remaining credit until the end of the current billing period. Then Token Pass ends.

## Team-wide ZDR fee

If your team has [team-wide zero data retention](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/zdr#team-wide-zero-data-retention) on, the $0.10 per 1,000 requests fee applies to Token Pass requests too. Per-request ZDR has no extra cost.

## Changes to Token Pass

Token Pass is in Early Access, and the [Token Pass Terms](/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass#terms) apply:

- Vercel may change the featured models and the providers that serve them at any time.
- If Vercel ends Token Pass, you receive a pro-rata refund of that month's fee.
- If Vercel reasonably believes someone is misusing Token Pass, including through multiple accounts, it may cancel Token Pass and remove unused credit without a refund.

## Where to see usage and charges

Check these places:

- **Token Pass tab**: remaining credit, usage this billing period, reset date, and the featured models.
- **[Observability](/docs/ai-gateway/observability-and-spend/observability)**: Token Pass requests, listed under the Vercel Token Pass provider.
- **Invoices**: the $30 charge, listed as an add-on on your Pro invoice.

# Using Token Pass with Coding and Personal Agents

Token Pass works in any agent that connects to AI Gateway with an API key. For each agent, you connect it with your Token Pass API key and then select a featured model. This page covers the agent-specific settings that decide whether a request succeeds on Token Pass.

## Before you start

Make sure that:

- Your team has an active Token Pass. See [Getting started](/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass/getting-started).
- `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` holds your Token Pass API key.

Use one of the featured model IDs:

| Model               | Model ID                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Kimi K3             | `moonshotai/kimi-k3`           |
| GLM 5.3             | `zai/glm-5.3`                  |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` |

A Token Pass API key only works with featured models. These agent settings send requests elsewhere, so those requests fail with a `403`:

- **Fast mode.** Fast variants aren't featured models.
- **Background models.** Some agents send side requests, such as titles, summaries, and subagents, to a different model. Point them at a featured model too.
- **Provider order.** If your agent's config routes a featured model to a provider other than `token-pass`, put `token-pass` first or remove the setting.

Token Pass only works with an API key. Signing in to an agent with your Vercel account doesn't use Token Pass.

To configure every installed agent at once, run:

```bash filename="terminal"
npx vercel@latest ai-gateway setup --key "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
```

## fx

Connect fx:

```bash filename="terminal"
npx vercel@latest ai-gateway setup --agent fx --key "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
```

This exports `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` from your shell startup file and pins fx's `credential_source` to that key. Open a new terminal so the key loads.

In fx, run `/model` and choose `zai/glm-5.3`, `moonshotai/kimi-k3`, or `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. When you pick Kimi K3, fx preselects **Fast** in the speed step. Choose standard speed instead. If Fast is already on, run `/fast` to turn it off.

To start fx on a featured model without changing your saved default:

```bash filename="terminal"
fx --provider gateway --model zai/glm-5.3
```

To confirm Token Pass served a request, run a one-off prompt and check `resolved_provider` in the output:

```bash filename="terminal"
fx ask --json --model zai/glm-5.3 "Reply with one short sentence."
```

`resolved_provider` should be `token-pass`.

> **💡 Note:** Don't use `fx login vercel` for Token Pass, because Token Pass only works with
> an API key. If you set `provider_order` in `.fx.json` or
> `~/.fx/settings.json`, put `token-pass` first or remove it.

## Claude Code

Connect Claude Code:

```bash filename="terminal"
npx vercel@latest ai-gateway setup --agent claude-code --key "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
```

This points Claude Code at `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/claude-code` and turns on gateway model discovery, so featured models appear in `/model`.

Start Claude Code on a featured model:

```bash filename="terminal"
claude --model zai/glm-5.3
```

Claude Code also sends requests, such as background tasks and subagents, to separate model slots. By default those slots use Claude models, which a Token Pass API key can't use. To keep every request working, point the slots at a featured model in `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```json filename="~/.claude/settings.json"
{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "zai/glm-5.3",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "zai/glm-5.3",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "zai/glm-5.3",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "zai/glm-5.3",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL": "zai/glm-5.3"
  }
}
```

Merge these keys into the `env` block the setup command wrote. Don't replace the file.

## Codex

Connect Codex:

```bash filename="terminal"
npx vercel@latest ai-gateway setup --agent codex --key "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
```

Start Codex on a featured model:

```bash filename="terminal"
codex --model zai/glm-5.3
```

To make Token Pass a profile you can switch to, create `~/.codex/token-pass.config.toml`:

```toml filename="~/.codex/token-pass.config.toml"
model = "zai/glm-5.3"
```

Then run `codex --profile token-pass`. You can also switch models in a session with `/model`.

> **💡 Note:** Remove `supports_websockets = true` from the `vercel` provider in
> `~/.codex/config.toml` if you added it. WebSocket streaming only works with
> OpenAI models. Codex may also warn that it can't find metadata for non-OpenAI
> models. You can ignore that warning.

## Cline

To connect the Cline CLI and set a featured model, run:

```bash filename="terminal"
npx vercel@latest ai-gateway setup --agent cline --key "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
cline auth -p vercel-ai-gateway -m zai/glm-5.3
```

To set up the Cline VS Code extension, open Cline's settings and follow these steps:

1. Set **API Provider** to **Vercel AI Gateway**.
2. Paste your Token Pass API key.
3. Set the model to `zai/glm-5.3`, `moonshotai/kimi-k3`, or `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`.

## OpenCode

Connect OpenCode:

```bash filename="terminal"
npx vercel@latest ai-gateway setup --agent opencode --key "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
```

In OpenCode, run `/models` and choose GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash under Vercel AI Gateway. To make one the default, set `model` in `opencode.json`:

```json filename="opencode.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "model": "vercel/zai/glm-5.3"
}
```

If `opencode.json` sets `options.order` for a featured model, put `token-pass` first or remove the entry.

## Other agents

Any agent in [Coding Agents](/docs/ai-gateway/coding-agents) can use Token Pass. Connect it with `npx vercel@latest ai-gateway setup --agent <name> --key "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"`, then select a featured model ID. The rules in [Before you start](#before-you-start) apply to every agent.

## Personal agents

You can also use Token Pass in agents you build and run yourself, such as an Eve agent or an AI SDK app on your laptop or deployed to Vercel. Authenticate with your Token Pass API key and use a featured model ID:

```ts filename="agent.ts"
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: 'zai/glm-5.3',
  prompt: 'Summarize my open pull requests.',
});
```

The AI SDK reads `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` from the environment. On Vercel, add your Token Pass API key as an [environment variable](/docs/environment-variables) on your project. A deployment's OIDC token can't spend Token Pass, so the key has to be set explicitly.

When your credit runs out, requests with the Token Pass API key fail with a `403` error until your next billing period. AI Gateway doesn't switch to paid usage for you. If a deployed agent has to keep running, catch the error and retry with a regular AI Gateway API key.

This example stores the Token Pass API key in `TOKEN_PASS_API_KEY` and the regular key in `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`:

```ts filename="agent.ts"
import { createGateway } from '@ai-sdk/gateway';
import { generateText } from 'ai';

const tokenPass = createGateway({ apiKey: process.env.TOKEN_PASS_API_KEY });
const gateway = createGateway({ apiKey: process.env.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY });

export async function run(prompt: string) {
  try {
    return await generateText({ model: tokenPass('zai/glm-5.3'), prompt });
  } catch {
    // The Token Pass request failed, for example because credit ran out.
    // Retry on another provider, billed to AI Gateway credits.
    return await generateText({
      model: gateway('zai/glm-5.3'),
      prompt,
      providerOptions: { gateway: { order: ['zai'] } },
    });
  }
}
```

See [When credit runs out](/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass/models-and-routing#when-credit-runs-out) for the error details.

# Getting Started with Token Pass

This guide covers subscribing, creating a Token Pass API key, connecting a coding agent, and confirming that AI Gateway billed your first request to Token Pass credit.

## Prerequisites

Before you start, you need:

- A Pro team. Hobby teams can upgrade from the Token Pass tab.
- Permission to manage billing on that team.
- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) installed, to run the Vercel CLI with `npx`.

- ### Subscribe
  Open the [Token Pass tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Ftoken-pass\&title=Go+to+Token+Pass) in AI Gateway and click **Subscribe**.

  The confirmation shows today's prorated charge and the date your $30 monthly charge starts. Click **Enable and Pay** to subscribe and accept the [Token Pass Terms](/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass#terms).

  After checkout, the tab shows your credit balance and the featured models.

- ### Create a Token Pass API key
  On the Token Pass tab, click **Create API Key**. AI Gateway creates a Token Pass API key on the team that has Token Pass.

  A Token Pass API key only works with featured models, and you can't change its type later. Keep a regular AI Gateway API key for other models.

  Export the key in your shell:
  ```bash filename="terminal"
  export AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY="your-token-pass-api-key"
  ```

- ### Connect your coding agent
  Run the Vercel CLI setup command with your Token Pass API key:
  ```bash filename="terminal"
  npx vercel@latest ai-gateway setup --key "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
  ```
  The command detects the agents installed on your machine and asks which ones to configure. It backs up every file it changes, and on macOS it stores the key in your Keychain. Add `--dry-run` to preview the changes, or `--agent <name>` to configure one agent.

  Pass `--key`. Without it, the command creates a regular AI Gateway API key instead of using your Token Pass API key.
  > **💡 Note:** Each agent you configure uses the Token Pass API key for every request, so it
  > can only use featured models. To use other models in that agent, run the
  > setup command again with a regular AI Gateway API key.

- ### Select a featured model
  In your agent's model picker, choose `zai/glm-5.3`, `moonshotai/kimi-k3`, or `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. If the agent has a fast mode, turn it off. Fast variants aren't featured models, so a Token Pass API key can't use them.

  Each agent handles model selection differently. [Coding and personal agents](/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass/coding-agents) has the steps for fx, Claude Code, Codex, Cline, and OpenCode.

- ### Confirm Token Pass served the request
  Send a prompt from your agent, then check either of these:
  - The [Token Pass tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Ftoken-pass\&title=Go+to+Token+Pass), where your remaining credit goes down.
  - [Observability](/docs/ai-gateway/observability-and-spend/observability), where the request's provider is **Vercel Token Pass**.
  If the request failed or used another provider, see [When a request doesn't use Token Pass](/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass/models-and-routing#when-a-request-doesnt-use-token-pass).

## Test with cURL

To check your key and subscription without an agent, send a request to a featured model:

```bash filename="terminal"
curl --fail-with-body https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "model": "moonshotai/kimi-k3",
  "messages": [
    { "role": "user", "content": "Reply with one short sentence." }
  ]
}'
```

You don't need `providerOptions`. A Token Pass API key sends featured models to the Token Pass provider.

The same model IDs work with the [AI SDK](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/ai-sdk), the [OpenAI-compatible API](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/openai-chat-completions), and the [Anthropic-compatible API](/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/anthropic-messages-api).

## Set up with an agent

To have a coding agent do the setup for you, export your Token Pass API key as `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, then give the agent this prompt:

```text filename="prompt"
Connect my coding agent to Vercel AI Gateway so it uses my Token Pass credit.
My Token Pass API key is in the AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY environment variable. Run
`npx vercel@latest ai-gateway setup --key "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY"` and let me
choose which installed agent to configure. Show me the proposed changes before
applying them. Then select `zai/glm-5.3` in that agent's model picker, turn off
any fast mode, and send one test request. Confirm the provider was Vercel Token
Pass (`token-pass`). Never print, log, or commit an API key. Follow
https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass/coding-agents.
```

title: "Token Pass Models and Routing"
description: "Which requests Token Pass covers, how Token Pass API keys route requests, what happens when credit runs out, and the errors you can get."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.122Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass/models-and-routing"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Token Pass Models and Routing

AI Gateway bills a request to Token Pass when all of these are true:

- Your team has an active Token Pass with credit remaining.
- You authenticate with an AI Gateway API key. Use a Token Pass API key.
- The request uses a featured model ID.
- The Token Pass provider (`token-pass`) serves the request.

All other requests follow normal AI Gateway routing and billing.

## Featured models

| Model               | Model ID                       | Provider                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| Kimi K3             | `moonshotai/kimi-k3`           | Vercel Token Pass (`token-pass`) |
| GLM 5.3             | `zai/glm-5.3`                  | Vercel Token Pass (`token-pass`) |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | Vercel Token Pass (`token-pass`) |

Token Pass currently serves these models through Wafer. AI Gateway deducts usage from your credit at each model's [list price](/docs/ai-gateway/token-pass#list-price).

## Token Pass API keys

A Token Pass API key is an AI Gateway API key marked for Token Pass when you create it. You can't change a key's type later.

With a Token Pass API key:

- AI Gateway serves featured models only through the `token-pass` provider and bills them to your Token Pass credit.
- Requests never fall back to other providers or to your AI Gateway credits.
- Requests to any other model or endpoint fail with a `403`.

Token Pass only works with AI Gateway API keys. AI Gateway doesn't use Token Pass for requests authenticated with an OIDC token, a Vercel access token, or an app token. It routes those requests as usual and bills your AI Gateway credits.

## What isn't covered

These requests don't use Token Pass credit:

- Any model that isn't featured, including image, video, audio, and embedding models.
- Fast variants of featured models, including fast modes in coding agents.
- Featured models that you send with a regular AI Gateway API key and route to another provider.

With a Token Pass API key, these requests fail with a `403`. With a regular AI Gateway API key, they bill to your AI Gateway credits.

## Routing

With a Token Pass API key, AI Gateway sends featured models to the Token Pass provider. You don't need to set [provider options](/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/provider-filtering-and-ordering).

Because a Token Pass API key can't use other providers, an `order` or `only` setting that leaves out `token-pass` makes the request fail. An `order` that lists `token-pass` first works as usual.

To use a featured model with another provider, send the request with a regular AI Gateway API key and name that provider:

```bash filename="terminal" {9-11}
curl --fail-with-body https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "model": "zai/glm-5.3",
  "messages": [
    { "role": "user", "content": "Reply with one short sentence." }
  ],
  "providerOptions": {
    "gateway": { "only": ["zai"] }
  }
}'
```

## Failover

Token Pass requests don't fail over. If the Token Pass provider returns an error, the request fails with that error. Retry the request, or [switch to regular AI Gateway usage](#switch-to-regular-ai-gateway-usage), billed to your AI Gateway credits.

## When credit runs out

Once you use up your Token Pass credit, requests with your Token Pass API key fail with a `403` until your next billing period starts. AI Gateway doesn't charge your AI Gateway credits for these requests, and Token Pass doesn't top up. To see your remaining credit and reset date, open the [Token Pass tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway%2Ftoken-pass\&title=Go+to+Token+Pass).

To continue with paid usage before your credit resets, switch your coding agent or application to a regular AI Gateway API key and remove any routing options that select the `token-pass` provider. These requests use your AI Gateway credit balance at the selected provider's rates, so you need enough AI Gateway credits to keep making requests.

For automatic failover, your application has to catch the failed Token Pass request and retry it with a regular AI Gateway API key. Setting a provider order alone doesn't switch API keys.

## Switch to regular AI Gateway usage

Regular AI Gateway usage bills to your AI Gateway credits at each provider's rates. It covers every model, including featured models served by other providers. To set it up:

1. **Add AI Gateway credits.** Go to [**AI Gateway**](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fai-gateway\&title=Go+to+AI+Gateway), click the button that shows your AI Gateway credits balance, and add credits. To keep your balance from running out, [configure auto top-up](/docs/ai-gateway/pricing#configure-auto-top-up).

2. **Connect your agent with a regular API key.** Run the setup command without `--key`. It creates a regular AI Gateway API key and configures your agent with it:

   ```bash filename="terminal"
   npx vercel@latest ai-gateway setup --agent <name>
   ```

   To use an existing key instead, [create a key](/docs/ai-gateway/authentication-and-byok/api-keys#create-a-key) with the **Standard** key type and pass it with `--key`.

3. **Remove Token Pass routing options.** Delete any `order` or `only` setting that selects `token-pass`, such as `provider_order` in fx or `options.order` in `opencode.json`.

4. **Set a budget (optional).** To cap what the key can spend, set a [budget](/docs/ai-gateway/observability-and-spend/budgets).

To go back to Token Pass after your credit resets, run the setup command again with your Token Pass API key.

## Errors

Token Pass errors return HTTP status `403` with the error type `no_providers_available`. Check the message to find the cause:

| Cause                                                     | Message includes                                                                                  | Fix                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Your credit for this billing period is used up            | `Your Vercel Token Pass credits are used up until your next billing cycle.`                       | Wait for the reset, or [switch to regular AI Gateway usage](#switch-to-regular-ai-gateway-usage) |
| A Token Pass API key called a model that isn't featured   | `This API key is scoped to Vercel Token Pass and can only be used with Token Pass models.`        | Use a regular AI Gateway API key for that model                                     |
| The request needs a Token Pass API key                    | `requires a Vercel Token Pass API key.`                                                           | Create a Token Pass API key and use it for featured models                          |
| The key's team doesn't have an active Token Pass          | `requires an active Vercel Token Pass.`                                                           | Subscribe, or use a key from the team that has Token Pass                           |

Errors from the Token Pass provider come back unchanged. See [Failover](#failover).

## Team settings that affect Token Pass

| Setting                                                                                       | Effect on Token Pass                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Zero data retention](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/zdr)                           | Token Pass has zero data retention, so requests still route to it. Team-wide ZDR's per-request fee applies |
| [Disallow prompt training](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/disallow-prompt-training) | Token Pass doesn't train on prompts, so requests still route to it                                      |
| [Provider allowlist](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/provider-allowlist)             | Add `token-pass` to the list. Otherwise, requests with a Token Pass API key fail                        |
| [Model allowlist](/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/model-allowlist)                   | Add the featured model IDs to the list. Otherwise, AI Gateway blocks requests to them                   |
| Region and HIPAA restrictions                                                                 | If a restriction excludes the Token Pass provider, requests with a Token Pass API key fail             |

## Check which provider served a request

Use any of these:

- **Dashboard**: in [Observability](/docs/ai-gateway/observability-and-spend/observability), the provider is **Vercel Token Pass**.
- **API**: `providerMetadata.gateway.routing.resolvedProvider` is `token-pass`.
- **fx**: `fx ask --json` returns `token-pass` in `resolved_provider`.

## When a request doesn't use Token Pass

If a featured model request failed, or another provider served it, check these in order:

1. The request uses a Token Pass API key, not an OIDC token or a Vercel sign-in.
2. The key belongs to the team that has Token Pass.
3. The model ID is exactly `zai/glm-5.3`, `moonshotai/kimi-k3`, or `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, with fast mode off.
4. Your agent config doesn't set an `order` or `only` that leaves out `token-pass`.
5. Your provider allowlist and model allowlist include Token Pass and the featured models.
6. You still have credit this billing period. Check the Token Pass tab.
