title: "vercel logs"
description: "View and filter runtime logs or CDN request records for your Vercel project."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:45.890Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/cli/logs"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# vercel logs

The `vercel logs` command shows runtime logs for your project. Use `vercel logs requests` to list CDN request records.

> **💡 Note:** This page describes `vercel logs` in Vercel CLI v64.0.0 and later. For
> earlier versions, see
> [Removed and changed options](#removed-and-changed-options).

By default, you get the latest 100 records from the last 30 minutes for the linked project, across production, preview, and custom environments. How far back you can query, and which request fields you can filter, depend on your plan. See [runtime log limits](/docs/logs/runtime#limits) and [Observability Plus limitations](/docs/observability/observability-plus#limitations).

You can find more detailed logs on the [Logs](/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%5Bproject%5D%2Flogs\&title=Open+Logs) page in the Vercel Dashboard.

## Usage

```bash filename="terminal"
# Runtime logs from the last 30 minutes
vercel logs

# CDN request records with a 5xx status
vercel logs requests --query 'httpStatus >= 500'
```

*Using the \`vercel logs\` command to view runtime logs or CDN request records.*

## Unique options

These options only apply to the `vercel logs` command.

### Project

The `--project` option, shorthand `-p`, sets the project ID or name. It defaults to the linked project.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs --project my-app
```

### Deployment

The `--deployment` option filters by a deployment ID or URL.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs --deployment dpl_xxxxx
```

### Environment

The `--environment` option filters by deployment environment, including custom environments.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs --environment production
```

### Query

The `-q, --query` option filters results using Vercel's supported subset of [Kibana Query Language (KQL)](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/kql).

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs runtime --query 'level:error AND timeout'
```

*Filtering runtime logs to error entries that mention "timeout".*

The following KQL syntax is supported:

| Syntax             | Description                                 |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `field:value`      | The field equals the value.                 |
| `field:(a OR b)`   | The field matches any listed value.         |
| `field:*`          | The field is present.                       |
| `field != value`   | The field does not equal the value.         |
| `field > value`, `field >= value`, `field < value`, `field <= value` | Compare a numeric field on request records, such as `httpStatus`. |
| `field:*text*`     | The field value contains `text`.            |
| `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` | Combine clauses.                            |
| `(...)`            | Group clauses.                              |

When you write a query:

| Rule | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Quoting | Wrap the complete query in single quotes. Double-quote values that contain spaces or KQL-reserved characters, including request IDs that contain colons. |
| Runtime logs | A bare word searches the message, case-insensitive. Multiple bare words combine with `AND`. |
| `requestId` | Uses the query time window. When the request is older than 30 minutes, widen the window with [`--since`](#since). |
| Fields | Run `vercel logs runtime --help` or `vercel logs requests --help` to list the fields you can filter. |

### Since

The `--since` option, shorthand `-s`, sets the start of the time window. You can use a relative duration such as `1h` or `30m`, an ISO 8601 timestamp, or `now`. If you omit it, the window starts 30 minutes before `--until`, or 30 minutes before now.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs --since 2h
```

### Until

The `--until` option, shorthand `-u`, sets the end of the time window. It accepts the same values as `--since`. If you omit it, the command uses the current time.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs --since 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z --until 2026-01-15T11:00:00Z
```

### Limit

The `-n, --limit` option sets the maximum number of records to return. The default is 100, and the maximum is 10,000.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs --limit 500
```

### Next

The `--next` option, shorthand `-N`, continues a previous query. The cursor keeps the team, project, filter, and time window.

When the query matches more records than the command returned, table output prints a `Next page:` command. With `--json`, pass the summary line's `pagination.next` value. You can change `--limit` on the next page. Passing `--next` together with `--project`, `--deployment`, `--environment`, `--query`, `--since`, or `--until` fails with a usage error.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs --next <cursor>
```

### JSON

The `--json` option prints one JSON object per line. `-F json` prints the same output.

- Each record uses `{"type":"log"|"request","data":<event>}`. Read fields under `.data`.
- The last line is a `summary` with `recordsReturned`, `timeRange`, `pagination` (`hasMore` and `next`), and `excludedIntervals`.

An empty result prints only the summary line.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs runtime --query 'level:error' --json | jq 'select(.type == "log") | .data'
```

*Printing runtime logs as JSON Lines and reading each record with \`jq\`.*

[`--non-interactive`](/docs/cli/global-options#non-interactive) implies `--json`.

## Removed and changed options

If you pass a removed option, the command fails with a usage error and prints the replacement.

| Old usage                    | Replacement                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--search <text>`            | `--query` with a bare word, for example `--query 'timeout'`.             |
| `--level error`              | `--query 'level:error'`.                                                 |
| `--source serverless`        | `--query 'source:function'`.                                             |
| `--source static`            | Static and CDN traffic is in `vercel logs requests`.                     |
| `--status-code 500`          | `vercel logs requests --query 'httpStatus:500'`.                         |
| `--status-code 5xx`          | `vercel logs requests --query 'httpStatus >= 500 AND httpStatus < 600'`. |
| `--request-id <id>`          | `--query 'requestId:"<id>"'`.                                            |
| `--branch <name>`            | No longer supported. Remove it from the command.                         |
| `--expand`                   | Removed. The command shows full runtime messages by default.             |
| `--no-follow`, `--no-branch` | Removed. The command runs a query for the time window you set.           |
| Positional deployment, `-d`  | `--deployment`. The `-d` shorthand is now always `--debug`.              |
| `-j` shorthand for JSON      | `--json` or `-F json`.                                                   |

`--follow` is deprecated. The command prints a warning and returns the query results instead of streaming.

## Examples

Show production runtime errors from the last hour:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs runtime --environment production --query 'level:error' --since 1h
```

*Filtering production runtime logs to errors from the last hour.*

Show POST requests that missed the cache:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel logs requests --query 'requestMethod:POST AND cacheResult:MISS'
```

*Querying CDN request records for POST requests with a cache miss.*

## Global Options

The following [global options](/docs/cli/global-options) can be passed when using the `vercel logs` command:

- [`--cwd`](/docs/cli/global-options#current-working-directory)
- [`--debug`](/docs/cli/global-options#debug)
- [`--global-config`](/docs/cli/global-options#global-config)
- [`--help`](/docs/cli/global-options#help)
- [`--local-config`](/docs/cli/global-options#local-config)
- [`--no-color`](/docs/cli/global-options#no-color)
- [`--non-interactive`](/docs/cli/global-options#non-interactive)
- [`--scope`](/docs/cli/global-options#scope)
- [`--team`](/docs/cli/global-options#team)
- [`--token`](/docs/cli/global-options#token)
- [`--version`](/docs/cli/global-options#version)

For more information on global options and their usage, refer to the [options section](/docs/cli/global-options).

# vercel mcp

The `vercel mcp` command helps you set up MCP clients (Claude Code, Claude.ai and Claude for desktop, Cursor, and VS Code with Copilot) to use Vercel MCP, Vercel's hosted Model Context Protocol endpoint at `https://mcp.vercel.com`. For Claude Code, Cursor, and VS Code with Copilot, the command configures the client directly. For Claude.ai and Claude for desktop, it prints manual setup instructions for adding a custom connector.

By default, clients are pointed at the shared endpoint. With `--project`, they're pointed at a project-specific URL (`https://mcp.vercel.com/<org>/<project>`) so the MCP session is scoped to the linked Vercel Project.

The command does not deploy any MCP server of your own. It only adjusts the client-side configuration on your machine.

## Usage

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mcp [options]
```

*Using the \`vercel mcp\` command to configure local MCP clients to use Vercel
MCP.*

By default, `vercel mcp` runs an interactive picker that lets you choose which MCP clients to set up. In non-interactive environments such as CI, you must pass `--clients` to skip the picker.

## Examples

### Interactively set up MCP clients

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mcp
```

*Launches the interactive client picker.*

### Set up specific clients without prompts

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mcp --clients "Cursor,VS Code with Copilot"
```

*Configures the listed MCP clients without launching the interactive picker.
Required in non-interactive environments.*

### Initialize project-specific MCP access

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mcp --project
```

*Sets up project-specific MCP access for the currently linked Vercel Project.*

## Unique options

These are options that only apply to the `vercel mcp` command.

### Clients

The `--clients` option accepts a comma-separated list of MCP clients to set up. In interactive mode, it skips the client picker. In non-interactive mode (for example, CI), `--clients` is required.

Supported values:

- `Claude Code`
- `Claude.ai and Claude for desktop`
- `Cursor`
- `VS Code with Copilot`

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mcp --clients "Cursor,VS Code with Copilot"
```

*Using \`--clients\` to set up Cursor and VS Code with Copilot without prompts.*

> **💡 Note:** In non-interactive mode without `--clients`, `vercel mcp` fails with a
> `missing_clients` error.

### Project

The `--project` option sets up project-specific MCP access for the currently linked project instead of global configuration.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mcp --project
```

*Use the \`--project\` flag to configure MCP access scoped to your linked project.*

## Global Options

The following [global options](/docs/cli/global-options) can be passed when using the `vercel mcp` command:

- [`--cwd`](/docs/cli/global-options#current-working-directory)
- [`--debug`](/docs/cli/global-options#debug)
- [`--global-config`](/docs/cli/global-options#global-config)
- [`--help`](/docs/cli/global-options#help)
- [`--local-config`](/docs/cli/global-options#local-config)
- [`--no-color`](/docs/cli/global-options#no-color)
- [`--non-interactive`](/docs/cli/global-options#non-interactive)
- [`--scope`](/docs/cli/global-options#scope)
- [`--team`](/docs/cli/global-options#team)
- [`--token`](/docs/cli/global-options#token)
- [`--version`](/docs/cli/global-options#version)

For more information on global options and their usage, refer to the [options section](/docs/cli/global-options).

title: "vercel metrics"

# vercel metrics

The `vercel metrics` command, also available as `vc metrics`, lets you discover and query metrics from the command line. Querying observability metrics requires [Observability Plus](/docs/observability/observability-plus), with product-specific exceptions listed below.

> Metrics other than Web Analytics and Speed Insights metrics are available on Enterprise and Pro plans with Observability Plus

Use `vercel metrics schema` before you build a query. Without an argument, the command lists the metrics available to your account. Pass a metric name or prefix to inspect its dimensions and aggregations.

## Usage

```bash filename="terminal"
# List queryable metrics for the current team context
vercel metrics schema

# Inspect a metric or metric prefix
vercel metrics schema <metric-or-prefix>

# Query a custom metric and filter by an attribute
vercel metrics database.duration_ms --filter 'plan:pro'

# Query production data for a specific project
vercel metrics <metric_name> --since 7d --granularity 1d --project project-name --prod

# Query grouped results
vercel metrics <metric_name> --group-by <dimension> --since 1d --limit 5 --project project-name --prod

# Query across every project in the current team
vercel metrics <metric_name> --all --group-by projectId --since 24h --prod
```

*Using the \`vercel metrics\` command to discover metrics before querying them.*

## Available metrics

Platform metric names start with `vercel.`. The tables below group metrics by prefix and describe what each metric measures. Use the full metric name as the `<metric_name>` argument:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics vercel.function_invocation.count --since 24h
```

Run `vercel metrics schema` to see the current catalog for your team, including custom metrics. To inspect the dimensions and supported aggregations for a group or a specific metric, pass its prefix or full name:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics schema vercel.function_invocation
vercel metrics schema vercel.function_invocation.function_duration_ms
```

### Requests

Prefix: `vercel.request`

| Metric name | Description |
| - | - |
| `vercel.request.count` | Number of incoming requests. |
| `vercel.request.fdt_in_bytes` | Incoming Fast Data Transfer, in bytes. |
| `vercel.request.fdt_out_bytes` | Outgoing Fast Data Transfer, in bytes. |
| `vercel.request.fdt_total_bytes` | Total Fast Data Transfer, in bytes. |
| `vercel.request.route_cpu_duration_ms` | CPU time spent routing requests, in milliseconds. |
| `vercel.request.external_rewrite_dns_ms` | DNS lookup time for external rewrites, in milliseconds. |
| `vercel.request.external_rewrite_connect_ms` | Connection time for external rewrites, in milliseconds. |

### Custom metrics

[Custom metrics](/docs/observability/custom-metrics) use the names you pass to `metric()` in your application, such as `database.duration_ms`. Their names and prefixes depend on your application, so they don't appear in the platform tables above.

Run `vercel metrics schema` to discover your team's custom metrics, then inspect a name or prefix before querying:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics schema database
vercel metrics database.duration_ms --filter 'plan:pro'
```

## Query output

By default, `vercel metrics` prints a human-readable table or time series summary. Use `--format` to output structured JSON for scripts, agents, and continuous integration checks.

## Feature access

Web Analytics metrics are available through `vercel metrics` without Observability Plus.

Speed Insights metrics are available through `vercel metrics` without Observability Plus.

Metrics other than Web Analytics and Speed Insights metrics require [Observability Plus](/docs/observability/observability-plus).

The dashboard and CLI are complementary:

- Use product dashboards for curated views.
- Use `vercel metrics` for custom filtering, grouping, aggregations, JSON output, and agent workflows.
- Use `--all` to query across every project in the current team when you need team-wide comparisons.

## Unique options

These options only apply to the `vercel metrics` command.

### Metric

The `<metric_name>` positional argument specifies the full metric name to query, such as `vercel.function_invocation.count` or `database.duration_ms`. Run `vercel metrics schema` to list queryable metrics for the current team context.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name>
vercel metrics schema
```

### Schema subcommand

Use the `schema` subcommand to inspect the dimensions and aggregations available for a metric. Pass a metric name or prefix to inspect a narrower part of the schema.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics schema
vercel metrics schema <metric-or-prefix>
```

Use `--format` when you are building scripts or agent workflows that need to validate available fields before querying.

### Aggregation

The `--aggregation` option, shorthand `-a`, selects the aggregation for the metric.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --aggregation <aggregation>
```

If omitted, the CLI selects a supported aggregation based on the metric's unit. Use `vercel metrics schema <metric-or-prefix>` to inspect the available aggregations.

### Group-by

The `--group-by` option groups results by a dimension. Repeat it to group by multiple dimensions.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --group-by <dimension>
vercel metrics <metric_name> --group-by <dimension> --group-by <dimension>
```

### Filter

The `--filter` option, shorthand `-f`, filters the query using Vercel's supported subset of [Kibana Query Language (KQL)](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/kql). For custom metrics, use `<attribute>:<value>` to filter by an attribute:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics database.duration_ms --filter 'plan:pro'
```

For platform metrics, use a dimension from the metric schema:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --filter 'environment:production'
vercel metrics <metric_name> --filter 'httpStatus >= 500'
vercel metrics <metric_name> --filter 'requestPath:(/docs* OR /guides*)'
```

The following KQL syntax is supported:

| Syntax | Description | Example |
| - | - | - |
| `field:value`, `field = value`, or `field == value` | Match a value. Values are interpreted using the dimension's type. | `environment:production` |
| `field != value`, `field > value`, `field >= value`, `field < value`, or `field <= value` | Exclude a value or compare numeric dimensions. | `httpStatus >= 500` |
| `field:(value1 OR value2)` | Match any of several values for one dimension. | `country:(US OR DE)` |
| `field:*`, `field=*`, or `field==*` | Match data where the dimension exists. | `errorCode:*` |
| `field:prefix*`, `field:*suffix`, or `field:*text*` | Match a string by prefix, suffix, or substring. | `requestPath:/api/*` |
| `field =~ "pattern"` | Match a string using a regular expression. The pattern must be double-quoted. | `requestPath =~ "^/api/(v1\|v2)/"` |
| `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, or `-expression` | Combine or negate expressions. Adjacent expressions imply `AND`. | `environment:production AND NOT country:US` |
| `(expression)` | Control how expressions are grouped. | `(country:US OR country:DE) AND deviceType:mobile` |

Wrap the complete filter in single quotes in your shell. Double-quote values that contain spaces or KQL-reserved characters. Use a backslash to escape the next character in a quoted or unquoted value:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --filter 'requestPath:"/pricing enterprise"'
```

Repeat `--filter` to combine filters with `AND`:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> -f 'country:US' -f 'deviceType != mobile'
```

The filter implementation is KQL-inspired and does not support every KQL feature. The following limits apply:

- Filter dimensions must be available to the selected metric. Run `vercel metrics schema <metric-or-prefix>` to inspect them.
- Numeric dimensions require finite numeric values, and boolean dimensions require `true` or `false`.
- Wildcards and regular expressions require string dimensions. Wildcards are only supported at the beginning or end of a value; infix patterns such as `i*d` are rejected.
- Bare quoted phrases and unfielded wildcard searches are not supported.
- KQL nested-object syntax and Lucene fuzzy, proximity, and boosting operators are not supported.
- Each filter can contain up to 2,048 characters and 8 levels of nesting. A query can contain up to 50 expression nodes across all filters.

OData filter syntax is deprecated. Use KQL for new queries.

### Production environment

The `--prod` option limits the query to production data. It is equivalent to `--filter 'environment:production'`.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --prod
```

### Since

The `--since` option, shorthand `-s`, sets the start of the time range. You can use a relative duration like `1h`, `24h`, or `7d`, a date, or an ISO timestamp. If omitted, the CLI defaults to the last hour.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --since 24h
```

### Until

The `--until` option, shorthand `-u`, sets the end of the time range. If omitted, the command uses the current time.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --since 24h --until 2026-03-19T12:00:00Z
```

### Granularity

The `--granularity` option, shorthand `-g`, controls the time bucket size. If omitted, the CLI computes a granularity for the selected time range.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --granularity 1h --since 7d
```

### Limit

The `--limit` option, shorthand `-l`, sets the maximum number of grouped results returned per time bucket. The default is `10`.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --group-by <dimension> --limit 50
```

### Order by

The `--order-by` option only applies to grouped results, so use it with `--group-by`. The default is `count` when the metric supports counting data points and `value` otherwise. Use `--order-by value` to order groups by the actual metric value returned by the query.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --group-by <dimension> --order-by count
vercel metrics <metric_name> --group-by <dimension> --order-by value
```

### Order

The `--order` option sets the ordering direction for grouped results. It accepts `asc` or `desc`. The default is `desc`.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --group-by <dimension> --order-by value --order asc
```

### Project

The `--project` option, shorthand `-p`, specifies the project name or project ID to query. Use it when you want results for a specific project. It defaults to the linked project when `--all` is not set.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --project project-name --prod
```

### All

The `--all` option queries across all projects in the current team scope. It cannot be combined with `--project`.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --all --group-by projectId --prod
```

### Format

The `--format` option outputs JSON instead of text. Use it for automation and agents.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --format json
vercel metrics schema <metric-or-prefix> --format json
```

## Examples

Inspect the schema before building a query:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics schema <metric-or-prefix>
```

List all available metrics:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics schema
```

Query a custom metric for the `pro` plan:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics database.duration_ms --filter 'plan:pro'
```

Query a metric for the last seven days:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --since 7d --granularity 1d --project project-name --prod
```

Query grouped results for a specific project:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --group-by <dimension> --since 24h --project project-name --prod
```

Query production data across every project in the current team:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel metrics <metric_name> --all --group-by projectId --since 24h --prod
```

# vercel microfrontends

The `vercel microfrontends` command (alias: `vercel mf`) provides utilities for managing Vercel Microfrontends from the CLI.

> **💡 Note:** To learn more about the architecture and config format, see
> [Microfrontends on Vercel](/docs/microfrontends).
> For a polyrepo setup walkthrough, see
> [Accessing the configuration file](/docs/microfrontends/local-development#accessing-the-configuration-file).

## Subcommands

| Subcommand                                | Description                                     |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| [`create-group`](#create-group)           | Create a new microfrontends group               |
| [`add-to-group`](#add-to-group)           | Add the current project to a group              |
| [`remove-from-group`](#remove-from-group) | Remove the current project from its group       |
| [`delete-group`](#delete-group)           | Delete a microfrontends group                   |
| [`inspect-group`](#inspect-group)         | Inspect a microfrontends group and its projects |
| [`pull`](#pull)                           | Pull remote configuration for local development |

## create-group

Create a new microfrontends group to compose multiple projects into one cohesive application with shared routing. The group is created in the current scope (team or user). The command is interactive if options are omitted.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends create-group [options]
```

### Options

| Option                    | Description                                                                             |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--name`                  | Name of the microfrontends group                                                        |
| `--project`               | Project name to include (repeatable)                                                    |
| `--default-app`           | Project name for the default application                                                |
| `--default-route`         | Default route for the default application                                               |
| `--project-default-route` | Default route for a non-default project, in the format `<project>=<route>` (repeatable) |
| `-y, --yes`               | Skip creation confirmation prompt                                                       |

### Examples

#### Create a group interactively

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends create-group
```

#### Create a group with flags

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mf create-group --name="My Group" --project=web --project=docs --default-app=web --project-default-route=docs=/docs --yes
```

## add-to-group

Add the current project to a microfrontends group as a child application. The project can then be independently deployed as part of the group. The command is interactive if options are omitted.

To set a project as the default application, use `create-group` with the `--default-app` option or configure it in the dashboard.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends add-to-group [options]
```

### Options

| Option            | Description                                           |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `--group`         | Name of the microfrontends group to add to            |
| `--default-route` | Default route for this project (for example, `/docs`) |

### Examples

#### Add the current project to a group interactively

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends add-to-group
```

#### Add the current project to a group with flags

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mf add-to-group --group="My Group" --default-route=/docs
```

## remove-from-group

Remove the current project from its microfrontends group so it's no longer part of the composed application.

> **💡 Note:** You cannot remove the default application from a group using the CLI. To remove the default application, use the dashboard or delete the entire group with `delete-group`.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends remove-from-group [options]
```

### Options

| Option      | Description                                                                                              |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip the project-link prompt and removal confirmations, including the warning for referenced projects. |

### Examples

#### Remove the current project from its group

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends remove-from-group
```

## delete-group

Delete a microfrontends group and all its settings. This action is not reversible.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends delete-group [options]
```

### Options

| Option      | Description                                                                            |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--group`   | Name or ID of the microfrontends group to delete                                     |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip the deletion confirmation. Combine with `--group` to delete without prompting. |

### Examples

#### Delete a group interactively

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends delete-group
```

#### Delete a group without prompts

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mf delete-group --group="My Group" --yes
```

## inspect-group

Inspect a microfrontends group and return metadata about the group and its projects. This command is useful for setup automation and scripts.

If you omit `--group`, the command is interactive and lets you select a group. In non-interactive environments, pass `--group`.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends inspect-group [options]
```

### Options

| Option               | Description                                                                                                      |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--group`            | Name, slug, or ID of the microfrontends group to inspect                                                         |
| `--config-file-name` | Custom microfrontends config file path/name relative to the default app root (must end with `.json` or `.jsonc`) |
| `-F, --format`       | Output format. Use `json` for machine-readable output                                                            |

### Examples

#### Inspect a group interactively

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends inspect-group
```

#### Inspect a group as JSON

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mf inspect-group --group="My Group" --format=json
```

#### Inspect a group with a custom config filename

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mf inspect-group --group="My Group" --config-file-name=microfrontends.jsonc --format=json
```

## pull

Pull the remote microfrontends configuration to your local repository for development.

> **💡 Note:** For a polyrepo setup walkthrough, see
> [Accessing the configuration file](/docs/microfrontends/local-development#accessing-the-configuration-file).
> This subcommand requires Vercel CLI 44.2.2 or newer.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends pull [options]
```

### Options

| Option       | Description                                                                       |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-y, --yes`  | Skip confirmation when linking is required (for example, in non-interactive mode) |
| `--dpl`      | The deployment ID to use for pulling the microfrontends configuration             |

### Examples

#### Pull configuration for the linked project

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel microfrontends pull
```

#### Pull configuration for a specific deployment

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel mf pull --dpl dpl_123xyz
```

title: "vercel monitors"
description: "Create, list, inspect, update, and delete monitors for projects and teams with the Vercel CLI."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:45.890Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/cli/monitors"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# vercel monitors

The `vercel monitors` command manages monitors (the rules that decide when Vercel [alerts](/docs/alerts) your team) from the terminal. It replaces the deprecated [`vercel alerts rules`](/docs/cli/alerts#rules) command tree.

Use [monitor schemas](#schema) to inspect the fields available to your selected team, then create, list, inspect, update, or delete monitors.

Use `vercel monitors --help` to see the command tree.

Monitor IDs are returned by `monitors add` and shown by `monitors ls`. Use those IDs with `monitors inspect`, `monitors update`, and `monitors rm`.

## Usage

```bash filename="terminal"
# List monitors for the linked project
vercel monitors ls

# Add a monitor from a JSON body file
vercel monitors add --project my-app --body ./monitor.json
```

*Using the \`vercel monitors\` command to list monitors and add a monitor.*

## Subcommands

| Command | Aliases | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ls` | `list` | List monitors for a project or team. |
| `schema` | None | Show available monitor types, request fields, constraints, and examples. |
| `add` | `create` (deprecated) | Add a monitor from a JSON body file. |
| `inspect` | `get` | Show one monitor by ID. |
| `rm` | `remove`, `delete` | Delete a monitor. |
| `update` | `patch` | Patch a monitor or change its project scope. |
| `notifications` | None | List and manage the Slack channels and webhooks linked to monitors. Run `vercel monitors notifications --help` for its subcommands. |

### `ls`

List monitors that affect the linked project. Use `--project` to select another project or `--all` to list every accessible monitor in the selected team.

Aliases: `list`.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors ls
```

#### Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-p, --project` | List monitors that affect a project by name or ID, for example `my-app` or `prj_abc123`. |
| `-a, --all` | List every accessible monitor in the selected team. |
| `--type` | Filter by monitor type. The option is repeatable and accepts comma-separated values. |
| `--format` | Output format. Supports `json`. |

Use `built-in` to list built-in monitors. For compatibility with previous CLI versions, `monitors ls --type` also accepts supported built-in trigger types such as `usage_anomaly` and `error_anomaly`. Use `vercel monitors schema --type built-in` to inspect the trigger types available to your team.

Use `custom` to list custom monitors. For compatibility with previous CLI versions, the option also accepts `custom_alert`.

#### List monitor examples

```bash filename="terminal"
# List monitors for the linked project
vercel monitors ls

# List every monitor in the selected team
vercel monitors ls --all

# JSON output
vercel monitors ls --all --format json
```

List custom monitors affecting a specific project:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors ls --project my-app --type custom
```

`monitors ls` retrieves every available page before printing results. JSON output contains a `monitors` array with the matching monitor objects.

### `schema`

Fetch the API-owned authoring schema for the monitor types available to the selected team. Run the command without `--type` to list the available types, or select a type to see its create and update fields, constraints, and examples.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors schema
```

#### Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--type` | Monitor type to describe. |
| `--format` | Output format. Supports `json`. |

#### Monitor schema examples

```bash filename="terminal"
# Show the fields and examples for built-in monitors
vercel monitors schema --type built-in
```

Show the fields and examples for custom monitors:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors schema --type custom
vercel monitors schema --type custom --format json
```

For custom monitors, run `vercel metrics schema <metric-or-prefix>` before authoring the body. The command returns current metric names, aggregations, dimensions, and filter fields. Use a returned metric name directly in `evaluation.query.metrics.<alias>.metric`.

### `add`

Add a monitor from a JSON body file. The request body must set `type`. For a built-in monitor, set `type` to `built-in`. For a custom monitor, set `type` to `custom`.

`create` remains a deprecated compatibility alias, but prints a deprecation warning. Use `add` for new commands.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors add --project my-app --body ./monitor.json
```

#### Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--body` | Path to a JSON file containing the new monitor. |
| `-p, --project` | Apply a monitor to one project. |
| `-a, --all` | Apply a built-in monitor to every project in the selected team. |
| `--format` | Output format. Supports `json`. |

Custom monitors require `--project` and do not support `--all`.

#### Add monitor body examples

Create a JSON file for the monitor body, then select the monitor's project scope in one of these ways:

- Add `ruleScope` to the body.
- Pass `--project <name-or-id>`.
- Pass `--all` for a built-in monitor.

Do not combine `ruleScope` with `--project` or `--all`. A linked project does not supply the scope automatically when you add a monitor.

Add a built-in error anomaly monitor for one project:

```json filename="monitor.json"
{
  "type": "built-in",
  "name": "Production server errors",
  "triggers": {
    "mode": "selected",
    "items": [
      {
        "type": "error_anomaly",
        "filter": "statusGroup:5xx AND route:/api/*"
      }
    ]
  },
  "matchMinimumSeverityLevel": "high"
}
```

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors add --project my-app --body ./monitor.json
```

Use `vercel monitors schema --type built-in` for additional validated examples, filter syntax, and current constraints.

Add a custom threshold monitor for one project:

```json filename="monitor.json"
{
  "type": "custom",
  "name": "Checkout server errors",
  "severity": "high",
  "evaluation": {
    "window": "5m",
    "query": {
      "metrics": {
        "errors": {
          "metric": "vercel.request.count",
          "aggregation": "count",
          "filter": "httpStatus >= 500"
        }
      },
      "outputs": ["errors"]
    }
  },
  "trigger": {
    "type": "threshold",
    "output": "errors",
    "operator": "gt",
    "threshold": 20
  }
}
```

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors add --project my-app --body ./monitor.json
```

Use `vercel monitors schema --type custom` for additional validated examples, filter syntax, and current constraints.

#### Migrate previous rule bodies

The current command rejects request bodies that contain the previous `alertTypes` field. Rewrite saved bodies using the current schema:

| Previous shape | Current shape |
| --- | --- |
| `alertTypes` | Top-level `type` and, for built-in monitors, `triggers` |
| `projectId` expression or raw project ID | `ruleScope`, `--project`, or `--all` |
| `autosubscribeOwnersInKnock` | `notificationSettings.enableTeamOwnerNotifications` |

Built-in filters use the syntax shown by the current schema. For example, an error anomaly filter uses `statusGroup:5xx` instead of the previous OData expression.

#### Migrate previous custom rule bodies

The current command also rejects request bodies that contain the previous `customAlert` or `queryJsonString` fields. Rewrite custom monitor fields using the current schema:

| Previous shape | Current shape |
| --- | --- |
| `customAlert.queryJsonString` | `evaluation.query` object |
| `triggerType`, `triggerOperator`, and `triggerThreshold` | `trigger` object |
| `formula.left` and `formula.right` | `evaluation.query.formulas` and `evaluation.query.outputs` |

Custom filters use the syntax shown by the current schema.

### `inspect`

Show one monitor by ID.

Aliases: `get`.

Monitor IDs are unique within a team. Use the global `--scope <team>` option when the monitor belongs to a team other than your current team.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors inspect <monitorId>
```

#### Arguments

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `monitorId` | Required. ID of the monitor to inspect. |

#### Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--format` | Output format. Supports `json`. |

#### Inspect monitor examples

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors inspect ar_abc123
vercel monitors inspect ar_abc123 --format json
```

### `rm`

Delete a monitor. The selected team's default monitor cannot be deleted.

Aliases: `remove`, `delete`.

Monitor IDs are unique within a team. Use the global `--scope <team>` option when the monitor belongs to a team other than your current team.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors rm <monitorId>
```

#### Arguments

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `monitorId` | Required. ID of the monitor to delete. |

#### Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--format` | Output format. Supports `json`. |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip the confirmation prompt. |

#### Delete monitor examples

```bash filename="terminal"
# Delete with confirmation
vercel monitors rm ar_abc123

# Delete without prompt
vercel monitors rm ar_abc123 --yes

# Delete by using the delete alias
vercel monitors delete ar_abc123 --yes
```

### `update`

Patch a monitor from a JSON body file, change its project scope, or do both. Omitted body fields remain unchanged, and `type` is optional because the API infers it from the stored monitor.

Aliases: `patch`.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel monitors update <monitorId> --body ./patch.json
vercel monitors update <monitorId> --project my-app
```

#### Arguments

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `monitorId` | Required. ID of the monitor to update. |

#### Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--body` | Path to a partial JSON file with fields to update. |
| `-p, --project` | Apply a monitor to one project. |
| `-a, --all` | Apply a built-in monitor to every project in the selected team. |
| `--format` | Output format. Supports `json`. |

You must provide `--body`, `--project`, or `--all`. Do not combine a `ruleScope` field in the body with `--project` or `--all`.

Custom monitors require `--project` and do not support `--all`.

#### Update monitor examples

Save the fields you want to change in a JSON file:

```json filename="patch.json"
{
  "name": "Critical production errors",
  "matchMinimumSeverityLevel": "critical"
}
```

```bash filename="terminal"
# Update fields from a file
vercel monitors update ar_abc123 --body ./patch.json

# Patch by using the patch alias
vercel monitors patch ar_abc123 --body ./patch.json

# Change scope without a body file
vercel monitors update ar_abc123 --project my-app
```

The authoring schema includes restrictions based on the stored monitor. For example, the default monitor accepts notification updates only.

A custom monitor with `querySupported: false` accepts changes to `name`, `severity`, and `notificationSettings` only.

## JSON output

Use `--format json` for scripting and automation. Monitor commands write only JSON to standard output:

| Command | Output shape |
| --- | --- |
| `monitors ls` | `{ "monitors": [...] }` |
| `monitors schema` | `{ "schemaVersion": number, "monitorTypes": [...] }` |
| `monitors add`, `monitors inspect`, `monitors update` | `{ "monitor": {...} }` |
| `monitors rm` | `{ "ok": true, "monitorId": "ar_...", "deleted": true }` |

Validation failures return an `error` object with `code` and `message`. When the API identifies individual invalid fields, the object also includes an `issues` array with field paths and messages.

## Migrate from `vercel alerts rules`

`vercel monitors` replaces the deprecated [`vercel alerts rules`](/docs/cli/alerts#rules) command tree. The options and request bodies are unchanged:

| Previous command | Current command |
| --- | --- |
| `vercel alerts rules ls` | `vercel monitors ls` |
| `vercel alerts rules schema` | `vercel monitors schema` |
| `vercel alerts rules create` | `vercel monitors add` |
| `vercel alerts rules inspect` | `vercel monitors inspect` |
| `vercel alerts rules rm` | `vercel monitors rm` |
| `vercel alerts rules update` | `vercel monitors update` |

JSON output renames the `rule` keys to `monitor` keys: `rules` becomes `monitors`, `ruleTypes` becomes `monitorTypes`, `rule` becomes `monitor`, and `ruleId` becomes `monitorId`. Update scripts that read these fields when you migrate. See [JSON output](#json-output) for the current shapes.

## Related resources

- To learn how to configure and receive alerts, see [Alerts](/docs/alerts).
- To configure monitors from the dashboard, see [Configure alerts](/docs/alerts/configure-alerts).
- To list and inspect the alerts your monitors raise, see [`vercel alerts`](/docs/cli/alerts).

## Global Options

The following [global options](/docs/cli/global-options) can be passed when using the `vercel monitors` command:

- [`--cwd`](/docs/cli/global-options#current-working-directory)
- [`--debug`](/docs/cli/global-options#debug)
- [`--global-config`](/docs/cli/global-options#global-config)
- [`--help`](/docs/cli/global-options#help)
- [`--local-config`](/docs/cli/global-options#local-config)
- [`--no-color`](/docs/cli/global-options#no-color)
- [`--non-interactive`](/docs/cli/global-options#non-interactive)
- [`--scope`](/docs/cli/global-options#scope)
- [`--team`](/docs/cli/global-options#team)
- [`--token`](/docs/cli/global-options#token)
- [`--version`](/docs/cli/global-options#version)

For more information on global options and their usage, refer to the [options section](/docs/cli/global-options).

# vercel open

The `vercel open` command opens your current project in the Vercel Dashboard. It automatically opens your default browser to the project's dashboard page, making it easy to access project settings, deployments, and other configuration options.

> **💡 Note:** This command is available in Vercel CLI v48.10.0 and later. If you're using an older version, see [Updating Vercel CLI](/docs/cli#updating-vercel-cli).

This command requires your directory to be [linked to a Vercel project](/docs/cli/project-linking). If you haven't linked your project yet, run [`vercel link`](/docs/cli/link) first.

## Usage

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel open
```

*Using the \`vercel open\` command to open the current
project in the Vercel Dashboard.*

## How it works

When you run `vercel open`:

1. The CLI checks if your current directory is linked to a Vercel project
2. It retrieves the project information, including the team slug and project name
3. It constructs the dashboard URL for your project
4. It opens the URL in your default browser

The command opens the project's main dashboard page at `https://vercel.com/{team-slug}/{project-name}`, where you can view deployments, configure settings, and manage your project.

## Examples

### Open the current project

From a linked project directory:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel open
```

*Opening the current project in the Vercel Dashboard.*

This opens your browser to the project's dashboard page.

## Troubleshooting

### Project not linked

If you see an error that the command requires a linked project:

```bash filename="terminal"
# Link your project first
vercel link

# Then open it
vercel open
```

*Linking your project before opening it in the dashboard.*

Make sure you're in the correct directory where your project files are located.

## Global Options

The following [global options](/docs/cli/global-options) can be passed when using the `vercel open` command:

- [`--cwd`](/docs/cli/global-options#current-working-directory)
- [`--debug`](/docs/cli/global-options#debug)
- [`--global-config`](/docs/cli/global-options#global-config)
- [`--help`](/docs/cli/global-options#help)
- [`--local-config`](/docs/cli/global-options#local-config)
- [`--no-color`](/docs/cli/global-options#no-color)
- [`--non-interactive`](/docs/cli/global-options#non-interactive)
- [`--scope`](/docs/cli/global-options#scope)
- [`--team`](/docs/cli/global-options#team)
- [`--token`](/docs/cli/global-options#token)
- [`--version`](/docs/cli/global-options#version)

For more information on global options and their usage, refer to the [options section](/docs/cli/global-options).

## Related

- [vercel link](/docs/cli/link)
- [vercel project](/docs/cli/project)
- [Project Linking](/docs/cli/project-linking)

title: "vercel organizations"
description: "Create and manage organizations and their child teams with the vercel organizations CLI command."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:45.890Z"

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# vercel organizations

Use the `vercel organizations` command to create and manage [organizations](/docs/organizations) from the terminal. An organization groups several Vercel teams under one billing team, and the billing team pays for every team in the organization.

> Organizations are available in Private Beta to Enterprise plans with Flexible Commitment (Flex) billing. Contact your account team to request access.

`vercel organization` is an alias for the same command. The command is available in `vercel@65.2.0` and later.

## Usage

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel organizations list
vercel organizations inspect acme
vercel organizations teams list acme
```

*Listing your organizations, showing the \`acme\` organization, and listing its
teams*

The `vercel organizations` command supports these subcommands:

- [`list`](#vercel-organizations-list): List the organizations you can view
- [`inspect`](#vercel-organizations-inspect): Show the details of an organization
- [`create`](#vercel-organizations-create): Create an organization from an existing team
- [`update`](#vercel-organizations-update): Change the slug of an organization
- [`teams list`](#vercel-organizations-teams-list): List the teams in an organization
- [`teams create`](#vercel-organizations-teams-create): Create a child team in an organization
- [`teams add`](#vercel-organizations-teams-add): Add an existing team to an organization

## Select an organization

Every subcommand except `list` and `create` acts on one organization. Pass the organization ID, which starts with `org_`, or the organization slug as the first argument. A slug matches the organizations that `vercel organizations list` shows. For any other organization, pass its ID.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel organizations inspect org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012
vercel organizations inspect acme
```

*Selecting an organization by ID or by slug*

When you omit the organization, the command uses the organization of the active team. Select the active team with the global `--scope` option. The billing team and every child team select the same organization.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel --scope acme-web organizations inspect
```

*Selecting the organization of the \`acme-web\` team*

## vercel organizations list

Use `vercel organizations list` to list the organizations you can view. The `ls` alias runs the same command.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel organizations list
```

*Listing the organizations you can view*

The command prints a table with the ID, slug, billing team, and number of teams of each organization.

When more organizations exist than `--limit` allows, the command prints the `vercel organizations list --next` command that shows the next page.

### Options

| Option    | Required | Description                                                                               |
| --------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--limit` | No       | Shorthand `-n`. The number of organizations to return, between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20. |
| `--next`  | No       | Show the next page of results. Pass the cursor from the previous page.                    |
| `--json`  | No       | Print the organizations and the next-page cursor as JSON.                                 |

## vercel organizations inspect

Use `vercel organizations inspect` to show the details of an organization, including its billing team and its number of teams.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel organizations inspect acme
```

*Showing the details of the \`acme\` organization*

### Options

| Option   | Required | Description                     |
| -------- | -------- | ------------------------------- |
| `--json` | No       | Print the organization as JSON. |

## vercel organizations create

Use `vercel organizations create` to create an organization from the active team. The active team becomes the billing team of the organization, and you become the owner of the organization. The billing team must be an Enterprise team with Flexible Commitment (Flex) billing.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel --scope acme organizations create --slug acme --name "Acme Inc"
```

*Creating the \`acme\` organization from the \`acme\` team*

The organization exists when the command returns. Vercel then moves the projects of the billing team to the organization in the background.

### Options

| Option   | Required | Description                                                                                                                 |
| -------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--slug` | Yes      | The slug of the organization: 1 to 48 lowercase letters, numbers, or hyphens, beginning and ending with a letter or number. |
| `--name` | No       | The display name of the organization. If you omit it, Vercel generates one from the slug.                                   |
| `--json` | No       | Print the new organization as JSON.                                                                                         |

## vercel organizations update

Use `vercel organizations update` to change the slug of an organization.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel organizations update org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012 --slug acme-corp
```

*Changing the slug of an organization to \`acme-corp\`*

### Options

| Option   | Required | Description                                                                                                                     |
| -------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--slug` | Yes      | The new slug of the organization: 1 to 48 lowercase letters, numbers, or hyphens, beginning and ending with a letter or number. |
| `--json` | No       | Print the updated organization as JSON.                                                                                         |

## vercel organizations teams list

Use `vercel organizations teams list` to list the teams in an organization, including the billing team. The `teams` subcommand also has the `team` alias, and `list` has the `ls` alias.

```bash filename="terminal"
$ vercel organizations teams list acme
ID                     Slug       Name       Billing Plan
team_aBcD1234EfGh5678  acme       Acme Inc   -
team_UvWx9012YzAb3456  acme-web   Acme Web   platform
team_CdEf3456GhIj7890  acme-docs  Acme Docs  enterprise
```

*Listing the teams in the \`acme\` organization*

The **Billing Plan** column shows how Vercel bills each child team. The billing team has no billing plan in the organization, so its column shows `-`.

### Options

| Option    | Required | Description                                                                       |
| --------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--limit` | No       | Shorthand `-n`. The number of teams to return, between 1 and 100. Defaults to 20. |
| `--next`  | No       | Show the next page of results. Pass the cursor from the previous page.            |
| `--json`  | No       | Print the teams and the next-page cursor as JSON.                                 |

## vercel organizations teams create

Use `vercel organizations teams create` to create a new child team in an organization. You become an owner of the new team, and the billing team of the organization pays for its usage.

Before the command creates the team, it shows the team, its billing plan, and the billing change, then asks you to confirm.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel organizations teams create acme --slug acme-web --name "Acme Web"
```

*Creating the \`acme-web\` child team in the \`acme\` organization*

The `--billing-plan` option sets how Vercel bills the new team:

- `platform`: The default. Vercel adds the team's usage to the organization at the end of the team's billing cycle. Use it for a team for each tenant of a multi-tenant platform.
- `enterprise`: The team draws down the Flex commitment of the organization in real time. Use it for an internal team that needs Enterprise features.

For more detail, see [Choosing a billing plan for a child team](/docs/organizations#choosing-a-billing-plan-for-a-child-team).

To run the command in CI, from an AI agent, or with `--json`, pass `--yes` after a person approves the billing change.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel organizations teams create acme --slug acme-docs --name "Acme Docs" --billing-plan enterprise --yes
```

*Creating an \`enterprise\` child team without a confirmation prompt*

### Options

| Option           | Required | Description                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--slug`         | Yes      | The slug of the new team: 1 to 48 lowercase letters, numbers, or hyphens, beginning and ending with a letter or number. |
| `--name`         | Yes      | The display name of the new team.                                                                                       |
| `--billing-plan` | No       | The billing plan of the new team: `platform` or `enterprise`. Defaults to `platform`.                                   |
| `--yes`          | No       | Shorthand `-y`. Confirm the billing change without a prompt.                                                            |
| `--json`         | No       | Print the new organization team as JSON.                                                                                |

## vercel organizations teams add

Use `vercel organizations teams add` to move an existing team into an organization. Select the team with `--child-team` and its team ID or slug. You must be an owner of the team that you add. After the move, the billing team of the organization pays for the team's usage.

Before the command adds the team, it shows the team, its billing plan, and the billing change, then asks you to confirm.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel organizations teams add acme --child-team acme-web
```

*Adding the existing \`acme-web\` team to the \`acme\` organization*

If you omit `--billing-plan`, Vercel derives the billing plan from the team's current plan. To add a team that is already on the Enterprise plan, contact your account team. For the rules that decide which teams you can add, see [Adding an existing team to an organization](/docs/organizations#adding-an-existing-team-to-an-organization).

The team joins the organization when the command returns. Vercel then moves the team's projects to the organization in the background. To run the command in CI, from an AI agent, or with `--json`, pass `--yes` after a person approves the billing change.

### Options

| Option           | Required | Description                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--child-team`   | Yes      | The team ID or slug of the existing team to add.                                                                   |
| `--billing-plan` | No       | The billing plan of the team: `platform` or `enterprise`. Defaults to a plan derived from the team's current plan. |
| `--yes`          | No       | Shorthand `-y`. Confirm the billing change without a prompt.                                                       |
| `--json`         | No       | Print the organization team as JSON.                                                                               |

## Use the command in scripts

With `--json`, each subcommand prints one JSON document to stdout. The document holds the result under the name of the resource, such as `organization`, `organizations`, `team`, or `teams`. A list also includes `pagination.next`, the cursor for the next page or `null` on the last page. A change also includes `outcome`, which is `created`, `updated`, or `added`.

```bash filename="terminal"
$ vercel organizations inspect acme --json
{
  "organization": {
    "organizationId": "org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012",
    "slug": "acme",
    "name": "Acme Inc",
    "avatar": null,
    "teamId": "team_aBcD1234EfGh5678",
    "teamCount": 3,
    "createdAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

*Printing an organization as JSON*

In the `organization` object, `teamId` is the ID of the billing team.

Without `--json`, the `create`, `update`, `teams create`, and `teams add` subcommands print the slug of the changed organization or team to stdout when stdout isn't a terminal. Use this output to pass the slug to the next command.

```bash filename="terminal"
team=$(vercel organizations teams create acme --slug acme-web --name "Acme Web" --yes)
vercel --scope "$team" project ls
```

*Creating a child team and listing its projects in a script*

# Vercel CLI Overview

Vercel gives you multiple ways to interact with and configure your Vercel Projects. With the command-line interface (CLI) you can interact with the Vercel platform using a terminal, or through an automated system, enabling you to [retrieve logs](/docs/cli/logs), manage [certificates](/docs/cli/certs), replicate your deployment environment [locally](/docs/cli/dev), manage Domain Name System (DNS) [records](/docs/cli/dns), and more.

If you'd like to interface with the platform programmatically, check out the [REST API documentation](/docs/rest-api).

## Installing Vercel CLI

To download and install Vercel CLI, run the following command:

**pnpm**

```bash
pnpm i -g vercel
```

**yarn**

```bash
yarn global add vercel
```

**npm**

```bash
npm i -g vercel
```

**bun**

```bash
bun add -g vercel
```

## Updating Vercel CLI

When there is a new release of Vercel CLI, running any command will show you a message letting you know that an update is available.

If you have installed our command-line interface through [npm](http://npmjs.org/) or [Yarn](https://yarnpkg.com), the easiest way to update it is by running the installation command yet again.

**pnpm**

```bash
pnpm i -g vercel@latest
```

**yarn**

```bash
yarn global add vercel@latest
```

**npm**

```bash
npm i -g vercel@latest
```

**bun**

```bash
bun add -g vercel@latest
```

If you see permission errors, please read npm's [official guide](https://docs.npmjs.com/resolving-eacces-permissions-errors-when-installing-packages-globally). Yarn depends on the same configuration as npm.

## Checking the version

The `--version` option can be used to verify the version of Vercel CLI currently being used.

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel --version
```

*Using the \`vercel\` command with the \`--version\` option.*

## Using in a CI/CD environment

Vercel CLI requires you to log in and authenticate before accessing resources or performing administrative tasks. In a terminal environment, you can use [`vercel login`](/docs/cli/login), which requires manual input. If you don't have a Vercel account yet, you can create one with [`vercel signup`](/docs/cli/signup). In a CI/CD environment where manual input is not possible, you can create a token on your [tokens page](/account/tokens) and then authenticate using one of these methods:

- Set the `VERCEL_TOKEN` environment variable
- Pass the [`--token` option](/docs/cli/global-options#token) to the command

Using the `VERCEL_TOKEN` environment variable is recommended for CI/CD because it avoids exposing the token in command-line arguments, which can be visible in process lists and logs. If both are provided, the `--token` flag takes precedence over the environment variable.

## Available Commands

### activity

View activity events for your Vercel project or team, filtered by type, date range, and project.

```bash
vercel activity
vercel activity ls --all --since 30d
vercel activity ls --type deployment --since 7d
```

[Learn more about the activity command](/docs/cli/activity)

### agent

Generate an `AGENTS.md` file in the current project with Vercel deployment best practices for coding agents.

```bash
vercel agent init
vercel agent init --yes
```

[Learn more about the agent command](/docs/cli/agent)

### agent-runs

Find projects with Agent Runs activity, list recent runs, and inspect run metadata and conversation traces.

```bash
vercel agent-runs projects
vercel agent-runs list
vercel agent-runs inspect run_1234567890
vercel agent-runs trace run_1234567890 --json
```

[Learn more about the agent-runs command](/docs/cli/agent-runs)

### ai-gateway

Manage [AI Gateway](/docs/ai-gateway) resources, including API keys, from the CLI.

```bash
vercel ai-gateway api-keys create
vercel ai-gateway api-keys create --name my-key --budget 500 --refresh-period monthly
```

[Learn more about the ai-gateway command](/docs/cli/ai-gateway)

### alerts

List recent alerts for a linked project, a specific project, or an entire team.

```bash
vercel alerts
vercel alerts --all
vercel alerts --project [project-name]
```

[Learn more about the alerts command](/docs/cli/alerts)

### alias

Apply custom domain aliases to your Vercel deployments.

```bash
vercel alias set [deployment-url] [custom-domain]
vercel alias rm [custom-domain]
vercel alias ls
```

[Learn more about the alias command](/docs/cli/alias)

### api

Make authenticated HTTP requests to the Vercel API from your terminal.

```bash
vercel api [endpoint]
vercel api /v2/user
vercel api /v9/projects -X POST -F name=my-project
```

[Learn more about the api command](/docs/cli/api)

### billing

View usage and costs, contract commitments, your [Spend Management](/docs/spend-management) budget, and invoices for your team.

```bash
vercel billing usage
vercel billing contract
vercel billing budgets set --amount 200 --pause --webhook https://example.com/spend
vercel billing invoices list
vercel billing invoices download [invoice-id]
```

[Learn more about the billing command](/docs/cli/billing)

### bisect

Perform a binary search on your deployments to help surface issues.

```bash
vercel bisect
vercel bisect --good [deployment-url] --bad [deployment-url]
```

[Learn more about the bisect command](/docs/cli/bisect)

### blob

Interact with Vercel Blob storage to upload, download, list, delete, and copy files.

```bash
vercel blob list
vercel blob put [path-to-file]
vercel blob get [url-or-pathname]
vercel blob del [url-or-pathname]
vercel blob copy [from-url] [to-pathname]
```

[Learn more about the blob command](/docs/cli/blob)

### build

Build a Vercel Project locally or in your own CI environment.

```bash

```

[Learn more about the build command](/docs/cli/build)

### buy

Purchase Vercel products like credits, addons, subscriptions, and domains directly from the CLI.

```bash

vercel buy domain example.com
```

[Learn more about the buy command](/docs/cli/buy)

### cache

Manage cache for your project (CDN cache and Data cache).

```bash

vercel cache purge --type data
vercel cache invalidate --tag foo
vercel cache dangerously-delete --tag foo
```

[Learn more about the cache command](/docs/cli/cache)

### certs

Manage certificates for your domains.

```bash

```

[Learn more about the certs command](/docs/cli/certs)

### comments

Review and manage existing [Vercel Toolbar comment threads](/docs/comments) from the terminal.

```bash

```

[Learn more about the comments command](/docs/cli/comments)

### connect

Manage connectors: create, list, attach to projects, request runtime tokens, and remove them.

```bash

vercel connect attach <id>
vercel connect detach <id>
vercel connect update <id>
vercel connect remove <id>
vercel connect open <id>
```

Run `vercel connect create <service> --help` to see how you can connect to a specific service.

[Learn more about the connect command](/docs/cli/connect)

### crons

Manage [Cron Jobs](/docs/cron-jobs) for a project: add cron entries to `vercel.json`, list them, and trigger them on demand. This command is in beta.

```bash

vercel crons run /api/cron
```

[Learn more about the crons command](/docs/cli/crons)

### curl

Make HTTP requests to your Vercel deployments with automatic deployment protection bypass.


### deploy


[Learn more about the telemetry command](/docs/cli/telemetry)

### tokens

Manage your personal Vercel authentication tokens: list, create, and revoke API tokens.

```bash
vercel tokens ls
vercel tokens add "CI deploy"
vercel tokens rm tok_abc123
```

[Learn more about the tokens command](/docs/cli/tokens)

### traces

Inspect request traces for your project, and manage the sampling rules that decide which requests Vercel traces.

```bash

vercel traces inspect [request-id] --open

vercel traces config rm --environment production
```

Open a trace directly in the tree or waterfall view:

```bash

vercel traces inspect [request-id] --open --view=waterfall
```

[Learn more about the traces command](/docs/cli/traces)

### upgrade


# vercel pricing

The `vercel pricing` command reads the public pricing table and lists features grouped by the lowest plan that includes them. Use it to look up feature availability on Hobby, Pro, and Enterprise. See [Pricing](/docs/pricing) for plan and billing details.

## Usage

List all features or search for a feature:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel pricing
vercel pricing "skew protection"
vercel pricing firewall --json
```

*Using \`vercel pricing\` to look up plan features.*

## Arguments

The optional `query` argument filters the pricing table. Multiple words form one search query, so `vercel pricing skew protection` and `vercel pricing "skew protection"` use the same query. The command fetches the public table each time it runs.

## Unique options

### JSON output

Use `--format json` (shorthand `-F json`) or `--json` to return structured JSON:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel pricing "skew protection" --format json
vercel pricing firewall --json
```

The JSON result includes the query, source URL, feature groups, and a summary of matches. When the CLI can resolve your current team or account, it also includes plan information and feature availability for that plan.

## Global Options

The following [global options](/docs/cli/global-options) can be passed when using the `vercel pricing` command:

- [`--cwd`](/docs/cli/global-options#current-working-directory)
- [`--debug`](/docs/cli/global-options#debug)
- [`--global-config`](/docs/cli/global-options#global-config)
- [`--help`](/docs/cli/global-options#help)
- [`--local-config`](/docs/cli/global-options#local-config)
- [`--no-color`](/docs/cli/global-options#no-color)
- [`--non-interactive`](/docs/cli/global-options#non-interactive)
- [`--scope`](/docs/cli/global-options#scope)
- [`--team`](/docs/cli/global-options#team)
- [`--token`](/docs/cli/global-options#token)
- [`--version`](/docs/cli/global-options#version)

For more information on global options and their usage, refer to the [options section](/docs/cli/global-options).
