title: "Organizations"
description: "Learn how organizations let you group multiple Vercel teams under a single entity with consolidated billing and central management."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.006Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/organizations"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Organizations

An organization groups multiple Vercel [teams](/docs/accounts) under a single entity. It's built for enterprises that run more than one team and want consolidated billing and central management without configuring each team by hand.

> Organizations are available in Private Beta to Enterprise plans with Flexible Commitment (Flex) billing. Contact your account team to request access.

## When to use organizations

Use an organization when you run more than one Vercel team and want to bill and manage them together. Organizations support two setups:

- **Multi-tenant platforms**: You build a platform, such as a vibe coding product, and create a child team for each tenant. Each child team keeps its tenant's projects, members, and usage isolated. Vercel aggregates each team's usage to the organization at the end of the team's billing cycle, for example monthly. These teams use the `platform` billing plan.
- **Internal company structure**: You mirror your company's structure with a team for each department, such as engineering, design, and marketing. These teams draw down the organization's Flex commit in real time and use the `enterprise` billing plan. An organization supports up to 200 `enterprise` child teams.

## How organizations relate to teams

An organization groups your existing [teams](/docs/accounts). Each team in it is a member team, including the team that stores billing:

- **Member teams**: Each team keeps its own [projects](/docs/projects/managing-projects), [members](/docs/rbac/managing-team-members), and settings.
- **Billing team**: The Enterprise team you create the organization from. It stores the organization's billing configuration, and you can't remove it from the organization.
- **Billing roll-up**: Member teams don't pay their own bills. Vercel consolidates every team's usage onto the billing team's Enterprise invoice.

A team can belong to only one organization, and teams can't move between organizations.

## Managing organizations in the dashboard

You can manage an organization from the Vercel dashboard as well as the API. To open the organization dashboard, select your organization in the team switcher. The organization dashboard has these pages:

- **Usage**: Compare usage and spend across the organization's teams, set a budget for each team, and download usage as a CSV file.
- **Teams**: List the organization's teams. To create a team, click **Create Team** and choose `enterprise` or `platform` as its [billing plan](#choosing-a-billing-plan-for-a-child-team).
- **Admins**: Grant or remove Organization Admin access for members of the billing team.
- **Billing**: Review the organization's billing information and organization-wide budget.
- **Invoices**: Review the organization's current and upcoming invoices.
- **Settings**: Configure the organization's details, identity and access, Enterprise Managed Users, Deployment Protection defaults, and audit log export.

## Features that work with organizations

An organization lets you configure Single Sign-On, Directory Sync, Enterprise Managed Users, and Deployment Protection one time for all of its teams. To change these settings, open the organization dashboard and navigate to **Settings**.

### Share one SAML Single Sign-On connection across teams

An organization can have one [SAML Single Sign-On](/docs/saml) connection that every team in the organization can use for sign-in. In the **Identity & Access** section, click **Configure** next to **Single Sign-On** to connect your identity provider. To require SAML sign-in for members of every team that uses the connection, turn on **SAML Enforcement**.

### Manage team access with organization Directory Sync

Organization Directory Sync maps groups in your identity provider to roles on your teams, so access on Vercel follows group membership in your directory. Configure it in the Identity & Access section. For each directory group, you can grant Organization access and choose a Default access role, which the group's members get on every team in the organization, including teams created later. To give the group a different role on a specific team, set a team-level role. That role overrides the default for that team only.

You must be an Organization Admin to configure organization Directory Sync. Vercel doesn't start syncing the directory until at least one directory group has the Organization Admin permission. Until then, the Directory Sync row shows **Setup Required** and notes that syncing starts once a group has Organization Admin.

To grant the Organization Admin permission to a directory group:

1. Open the organization's **Settings** page and go to the **Identity & Access** section.
2. In the **Directory Sync** row, select **Configure** and complete the walkthrough to connect a directory from your identity provider.
3. In the **Directory Sync** row, open the actions menu and select **Manage**.
4. Select a directory group from the list.
5. In the **Organization access** dropdown, select **Organization Admin**.
6. Select **Save**.

After at least one group has Organization Admin, Vercel begins syncing the directory and applies each group's Default access role and any team-level overrides.

### Turn on Enterprise Managed Users for organization teams

[Enterprise Managed Users](/docs/security/enterprise-managed-users) (EMU) lets your organization own and manage the Vercel accounts of its members. In the **Enterprise Managed Users** section, add the **Verified Domains** that your organization owns, then click **Review Teams** to choose which teams use EMU.

Organization Directory Sync converts synced members to managed accounts only after the organization meets these requirements:

- An Enterprise plan
- SAML Single Sign-On that is configured and enforced
- An active Directory Sync connection

### Set Deployment Protection defaults for new projects

Organization [Deployment Protection](/docs/deployment-protection) defaults control access to deployments for new projects across the organization's teams. In the **Deployment Protection Defaults** section, you can configure these settings:

- **Vercel Authentication**: Require visitors to log in to Vercel and belong to a team in your organization before they can view deployments. Choose **Standard Protection** to protect all deployments except production custom domains, or **All Deployments** to protect all domains.
- **Who Can Change Protection**: Require the Owner role to change or disable Vercel Authentication, to change or disable Password Protection, or to create Shareable Links in projects.
- **External Access**: Let users request access to deployments that Vercel Authentication protects.

## Managing organizations with the CLI

You can manage organizations from the terminal with the [`vercel organizations`](/docs/cli/organizations) command. The command is available in Vercel CLI `65.2.0` and later. It lists, inspects, creates, and updates organizations, and it lists, creates, and adds child teams.

```bash
vercel organizations list
vercel organizations inspect acme
vercel organizations teams create acme --slug acme-web --name "Acme Web"
```

For every subcommand and option, see the [`vercel organizations` reference](/docs/cli/organizations).

## Managing organizations with the API

You can also manage organizations through the [Vercel REST API](/docs/rest-api). Authenticate each request with a Vercel [access token](/docs/rest-api#authentication) that has access to the teams involved. For the full request and response schemas, see the [Organizations REST API reference](/docs/rest-api/organizations).

The API supports these operations:

| Action                        | Endpoint                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Create an organization        | `POST /v1/organizations`                                     |
| List your organizations       | `GET /v1/organizations`                                      |
| Get an organization           | `GET /v1/organizations/{organizationId}`                     |
| Update an organization        | `PATCH /v1/organizations/{organizationId}`                   |
| Delete an organization        | `DELETE /v1/organizations/{organizationId}`                  |
| Create or add a team          | `POST /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/teams`              |
| List an organization's teams  | `GET /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/teams`               |
| Remove a team                 | `DELETE /v1/organizations/{organizationId}/teams/{teamId}`   |

### Creating an organization

Create an organization from an existing Enterprise team with Flexible Commitment (Flex) billing by passing that team's ID in the `teamId` query parameter. The team becomes the organization's billing team, and you get Organization Admin access to the organization. If you omit `name`, Vercel generates one from the slug.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.vercel.com/v1/organizations?teamId=team_aBcD1234EfGh5678" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "slug": "acme", "name": "Acme" }'
```

The response is the new organization, including the `organizationId` you use in later requests:

```json
{
  "organizationId": "org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012",
  "slug": "acme",
  "name": "Acme",
  "avatar": null,
  "teamId": "team_aBcD1234EfGh5678",
  "teamCount": 1,
  "createdAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

### Choosing a billing plan for a child team

Each child team has a `billingPlan` that sets its features and billing model. Choose the plan before you create or add a team:

- `platform`: For multi-tenant platforms that run a Pro team for each tenant, at any number of tenants. Vercel emits each team's usage to the organization at the end of the team's billing cycle under a consolidated `Platform Customer Usage` SKU.
- `enterprise`: For internal teams that need Enterprise permissions, except the add-ons in [Current limitations](#current-limitations). Each team draws down the organization's Flex commit in real time. An organization can have up to 200 `enterprise` child teams.

If you omit `billingPlan` when you create a team, the team joins as `platform`. When you add an existing team without `billingPlan`, Vercel derives the plan from the team's current plan.

### Creating a team in an organization

Create a new team directly under the organization by calling the organization's `teams` endpoint with `mode` set to `create`. Pass a `slug` and a `name` for the new team. The new team joins the organization as a `platform` child team, so its usage and billing roll up to the organization's billing team. To create an `enterprise` child team, set `billingPlan` to `enterprise`. You become an owner of the new team.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.vercel.com/v1/organizations/org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012/teams" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "mode": "create", "slug": "acme-customer-1", "name": "Acme Customer 1" }'
```

The response is the organization-team link, including the new team's `teamId`:

```json
{
  "organizationId": "org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012",
  "teamId": "team_MnOp3456QrSt7890",
  "ssoMode": "team",
  "dsyncMode": "organization",
  "billingPlan": "platform",
  "createdAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

### Adding an existing team to an organization

To bring an existing team under the organization, call the organization's `teams` endpoint with `mode` set to `link` and identify the team with its `teamId` or `slug`. You must be an owner of the team you're adding, and you can't add the organization's billing team as a child. Set `billingPlan` as described in [Choosing a billing plan for a child team](#choosing-a-billing-plan-for-a-child-team). To add a team that is already on the Enterprise plan, contact your account team.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.vercel.com/v1/organizations/org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012/teams" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "mode": "link", "teamId": "team_UvWx9012YzAb3456", "billingPlan": "platform" }'
```

The response is the organization-team link:

```json
{
  "organizationId": "org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012",
  "teamId": "team_UvWx9012YzAb3456",
  "ssoMode": "team",
  "dsyncMode": "organization",
  "billingPlan": "platform",
  "createdAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

### Listing organizations and teams

List the organizations that you manage:

```bash
curl "https://api.vercel.com/v1/organizations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN"
```

To fetch a single organization by ID, call `GET /v1/organizations/$ORGANIZATION_ID`.

List an organization's teams, including the billing team, with the teams endpoint. Set `includeMemberCount` to `true` to get the number of members in each team:

```bash
curl "https://api.vercel.com/v1/organizations/$ORGANIZATION_ID/teams?includeMemberCount=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN"
```

```json
{
  "teams": [
    {
      "organizationId": "org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012",
      "teamId": "team_MnOp3456QrSt7890",
      "createdAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-06-01T12:00:00.000Z",
      "ssoMode": "team",
      "dsyncMode": "organization",
      "billingPlan": "platform",
      "slug": "acme-customer-1",
      "name": "Acme Customer 1",
      "avatar": null,
      "memberCount": 12
    }
  ]
}
```

`ssoMode` shows whether the team signs in with the organization's SAML Single Sign-On connection (`organization`) or its own (`team`). `dsyncMode` shows whether the organization's Directory Sync manages the team's members (`organization`) or the team does (`team`).

For organizations with many teams, the response includes a `cursor`. Pass the `cursor` value as a query parameter to fetch the next page, and keep paginating until the response has no `cursor`.

### Removing a team from an organization

Removing a team from an organization deletes the team itself, not only its link to the organization. The team must pass the same billing checks as any team deletion. You can't remove the billing team. This endpoint removes `platform` child teams.

```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://api.vercel.com/v1/organizations/$ORGANIZATION_ID/teams/$TEAM_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN"
```

The response confirms the removed team:

```json
{
  "organizationId": "org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012",
  "teamId": "team_MnOp3456QrSt7890"
}
```

### Updating an organization

Update an organization's slug, name, or avatar. Slugs must be lowercase, start and end with an alphanumeric character, and can contain dashes:

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://api.vercel.com/v1/organizations/$ORGANIZATION_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "slug": "acme-inc" }'
```

To set the avatar, upload the image with [`POST /v2/files`](/docs/rest-api/reference/endpoints/deployments/upload-deployment-files), then send the 40-character SHA-1 hash of the file as `avatar`. Send `null` to remove the avatar.

The response is the updated organization.

### Deleting an organization

Delete an organization after removing all of its child teams. The request fails with an `organization_has_teams` error while child teams remain. The billing team must also have no unresolved billing issues. Deleting the organization doesn't delete the billing team, which continues as a standalone team.

```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://api.vercel.com/v1/organizations/$ORGANIZATION_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN"
```

The response confirms the deleted organization:

```json
{ "id": "org_aBcD1234EfGh5678IjKl9012" }
```

## Billing

An organization's charges roll up to the billing team's Enterprise account.

Vercel bills seats on the billing team's subscription as the unique paid members across the organization's Enterprise teams (the billing team plus every `enterprise` child team). A member who belongs to several of those teams counts once.

To understand how Enterprise billing and invoicing work, see:

- [Enterprise plan](/docs/plans/enterprise)
- [Enterprise billing](/docs/plans/enterprise/billing)

## Current limitations

Organizations are in private beta, and some capabilities aren't available yet:

- **Marketplace integrations**: Child teams can use the Neon integration. To use it in a `platform` child team, install it on the billing team first. Other [Marketplace integrations](/docs/integrations) aren't available to child teams yet.
- **Delayed billing for `platform` teams**: Vercel aggregates usage from `platform` child teams at the end of each team's billing cycle. Usage from `enterprise` child teams draws down the organization's Flex commit in real time.
- **Enterprise add-ons**: Child teams, including `enterprise` child teams, can't use these Enterprise add-ons:
  - Observability Plus
  - Static IPs
  - Secure Compute
  - SIEM Log Streaming
  - Microfrontends Projects
  - Bulk Redirects
  - Rolling Releases
  - Flags Explorer
  - Web Analytics Plus
  - Speed Insights Plus
  - HIPAA BAA

title: "Package Managers"
description: "Discover the package managers supported by Vercel for dependency management. Learn how Vercel detects and uses npm, Yarn, pnpm, and Bun for optimal build performance."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.007Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/package-managers"

# Package Managers

Vercel will automatically detect the package manager used in your project and install the dependencies when you [create a deployment](/docs/builds#build-infrastructure). It does this by looking at the lock file in your project and inferring the correct package manager to use.

If you are using [Corepack](/docs/builds/configure-a-build#corepack), Vercel will use the package manager specified in the `package.json` file's `packageManager` field instead.

## Supported package managers

The following table lists the package managers supported by Vercel, with their install commands and versions:

| Package Manager                                                                                                                   | Lock File                                                                                                                     | Install Command                                                         | Supported Versions |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| Yarn                                                                                                                              | [`yarn.lock`](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/lang/en/docs/yarn-lock/)                                                            | [`yarn install`](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/lang/en/docs/cli/install/) | 1, 2, 3            |
| npm                                                                                                                               | [`package-lock.json`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/configuring-npm/package-lock-json)                                       | [`npm install`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v8/commands/npm-install)     | 8, 9, 10           |
| pnpm                                                                                                                              | [`pnpm-lock.yaml`](https://pnpm.io/git)                                                                                       | [`pnpm install`](https://pnpm.io/cli/install)                           | 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 |
| Bun 1                                                                                                                             | [`bun.lockb`](https://bun.sh/docs/install/lockfile) or [`bun.lock`](https://bun.sh/docs/install/lockfile#text-based-lockfile) | [`bun install`](https://bun.sh/docs/cli/install)                        | 1                  |
| Vlt Beta | `vlt-lock.json`                                                                                                               | [`vlt install`](https://docs.vlt.sh/)                                   | 0.x                |

While Vercel automatically selects the package manager based on the lock file present in your project, the specific version of that package manager is determined by the version information in the lock file or associated configuration files.

The npm and pnpm package managers create a `lockfileVersion` property when they generate a lock file. This property specifies the lock file's format version, ensuring proper processing and compatibility. For example, a `pnpm-lock.yaml` file with `lockfileVersion: 9.0` will be interpreted by pnpm 9 or 10, while a `pnpm-lock.yaml` file with `lockfileVersion: 5.4` will be interpreted by pnpm 7.

| Package Manager | Condition                    | Install Command                    | Version Used   |
| --------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------- |
| pnpm            | `pnpm-lock.yaml`: present    | `pnpm install`                     | Varies         |
|                 | `lockfileVersion`: 9.0       | -                                  | pnpm 9 or 10\* |
|                 | `lockfileVersion`: 7.0       | -                                  | pnpm 9         |
|                 | `lockfileVersion`: 6.0/6.1   | -                                  | pnpm 8         |
|                 | `lockfileVersion`: 5.3/5.4   | -                                  | pnpm 7         |
|                 | Otherwise                    | -                                  | pnpm 6         |
| npm             | `package-lock.json`: present | `npm install`                      | Varies         |
|                 | `lockfileVersion`: 2         | -                                  | npm 8          |
|                 | Node 20                      | -                                  | npm 10         |
|                 | Node 22                      | -                                  | npm 10         |
| Bun             | `bun.lockb`: present         | `bun install`                      | Bun <1.2      |
|                 | `bun.lock`: present          | `bun install --save-text-lockfile` | Bun 1          |
|                 | `bun.lock`: present          | `bun install`                      | Bun >=1.2      |
| Yarn            | `yarn.lock`: present         | `yarn install`                     | Yarn 1         |
| Vlt             | `vlt-lock.json`: present     | `vlt install`                      | Vlt 0.x        |

> **💡 Note:** `pnpm-lock.yaml` version 9.0 can be generated by pnpm 9 or 10. Newer projects
> will prefer 10, while older prefer 9. Check [build
> logs](/docs/deployments/logs) to see which version is used for your project.

When no lock file exists, Vercel uses npm by default. Npm's default version aligns with the Node.js version as described in the table above. Defaults can be overridden using [`installCommand`](/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json#installcommand) or [Corepack](/docs/builds/configure-a-build#corepack) for specific package manager versions.

## Manually specifying a package manager

You can manually specify a package manager to use on a per-project, or per-deployment basis.

### Project override

To specify a package manager for all deployments in your project, use the **Override** setting in your project's [**Build & Development Settings**](/docs/project-configuration/project-settings#build-and-deployment-settings):

1. Navigate to your [dashboard](/dashboard) and select your project
2. Open **Settings** in the sidebar and select [**General**](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%5Bproject%5D%2Fsettings%2Fgeneral\&title=Go+to+General+settings)
3. Enable the **Override** toggle in the [**Build & Development Settings**](/docs/project-configuration/project-settings#build-and-deployment-settings) section and add your install command. Once you save, it will be applied on your next deployment

> **💡 Note:** When using an override install command like
> `pnpm install`, Vercel will use the oldest version of
> the specified package manager available in the build container. For example,
> if you specify `pnpm install` as your override install
> command, Vercel will use pnpm 6.

### Deployment override

To specify a package manager for a deployment, use the [`installCommand`](/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json#installcommand) property in your projects `vercel.json`.

```json filename="vercel.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json",
  "installCommand": "pnpm install"
}
```

title: "Partial Prerendering (PPR)"
description: "Partial Prerendering serves a cached static shell instantly, then renders and streams the dynamic parts of a page per request."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.007Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/partial-prerendering"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Partial Prerendering (PPR)

> Partial Prerendering is available on all plans

Partial Prerendering (PPR) is a rendering strategy that combines fast cached static content with the ability to render fresh dynamic content, all in one response. This strategy allows you to personalize pages while still having a performant site.

PPR requests have two parts to them: a static shell that is cached and served quickly, and a dynamic execution that fills in personalized content into the static shell. PPR uses [Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)](/docs/incremental-static-regeneration) for the static shell of the page, and [Vercel Functions](/docs/functions) to render the dynamic parts of the page.

Use PPR when a page is mostly static but has a few parts that change per request or per user:

- **Product or catalog pages**: a static layout with a live price, inventory count, or cart contents.
- **Dashboards and app shells**: a cached layout with a personalized widget, such as a user greeting or a notification count.
- **Articles and marketing pages**: static content with personalized recommendations or an auth-aware header.

If your page is fully static, use ISR since there is no dynamic content.

To get started:

- Follow the [getting started guide](/docs/partial-prerendering/quickstart) to enable PPR in a Next.js App Router project
- [Set up PPR](#using-ppr) with your framework
- Learn [how PPR works](#how-ppr-works) from build time through revalidation
- Understand [usage and pricing](#usage-and-pricing)

## Benefits of Vercel's CDN for PPR

When you deploy PPR with your framework on Vercel, the CDN adds these optimizations:

- **Instant shell with dynamic content in one response**: Once a region has pulled the shell into its [CDN cache](/docs/caching/cdn-cache), Vercel serves it from the nearest of Vercel's 19 [regions](/docs/regions) for a fast Time to First Byte, while your function renders the dynamic parts and streams them into the same response.
- **Durable storage**: At deployment time, Vercel writes the shell to the [global ISR cache](/docs/incremental-static-regeneration/limits-and-pricing#isr-cache-region). On the first request in each region, Vercel pulls the shell into the regional [CDN cache](/docs/caching/cdn-cache). The shell persists in the global ISR cache until you revalidate it.
- **Cache shielding and request collapsing**: on a CDN cache miss, Vercel reads from the global ISR cache before invoking your function, and it [collapses](/docs/incremental-static-regeneration/request-collapsing) concurrent requests to the same path into one invocation per region.
- **Globally consistent purging**: when you revalidate content, all caches across all regions update within 300 milliseconds. Vercel purges HTML and data payloads together, so visitors see consistent content across full page loads and client-side transitions.
- **Instant rollbacks**: cached content from previous deployments isn't purged, so you can roll back without regenerating it.

## Using PPR

PPR is configured through your framework's APIs. Your framework code defines which parts of a route are static and which are dynamic, and Vercel handles the caching and function execution automatically.

Partial Prerendering is currently available with Next.js:

| Framework                | How to enable PPR                                          |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Next.js** (App Router) | Enable Cache Components and mark cached segments with `use cache` |

In Next.js, Cache Components and the `use cache` directive define the cached shell and the dynamic sections. You set how long cached content stays fresh with `cacheLife` and invalidate it on demand with `cacheTag`.

**app/page.tsx**

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" framework=nextjs-app
import { Suspense } from 'react';
import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache';
import { cookies } from 'next/headers';

type Product = { id: string; name: string; price: number };

async function ProductsList() {
  'use cache';
  cacheTag('products-list');

  const products: Product[] = await fetch(
    'https://api.example.com/products',
  ).then((res) => res.json());
  return (
    <ul>
      {products.map((product) => (
        <li key={product.id}>{product.name} - ${product.price}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}

async function LoginState() {
  const user = (await cookies()).get('user')?.value;
  return <p>Welcome back, {user}</p>;
}

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <body>
      <h1>Product List Page</h1>

      {/* Dynamic: streamed in at request time */}
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
        <LoginState />
      </Suspense>

      {/* Cached: prerendered into the static shell */}
      <ProductsList />
    </body>
  );
}
```

**app/page.js**

```jsx filename="app/page.js" framework=nextjs-app
import { Suspense } from 'react';
import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache';
import { cookies } from 'next/headers';

async function ProductsList() {
  'use cache';
  cacheTag('products-list');

  const products = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products').then((res) =>
    res.json(),
  );
  return (
    <ul>
      {products.map((product) => (
        <li key={product.id}>{product.name} - ${product.price}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}

async function LoginState() {
  const user = (await cookies()).get('user')?.value;
  return <p>Welcome back, {user}</p>;
}

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <body>
      <h1>Product List Page</h1>

      {/* Dynamic: streamed in at request time */}
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
        <LoginState />
      </Suspense>

      {/* Cached: prerendered into the static shell */}
      <ProductsList />
    </body>
  );
}
```

For the full explanation and tutorial for how to use this, see [Cache Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/caching). To cache data inside the dynamic sections separately from the page response, see [Runtime Cache](/docs/caching/runtime-cache).

## How PPR works

PPR executes at build time, request time, and through revalidation. The sections below walk through each stage.

### At build time

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Deploy"] --> B["Generate shell + resume data"] --> C["Store in global ISR cache"]
```

Your framework generates two things for each PPR route: a static shell with placeholders where dynamic content goes, and the data your function needs to resume rendering the dynamic parts. When you deploy, Vercel prepopulates the shell in the [global ISR cache](/docs/incremental-static-regeneration/limits-and-pricing#isr-cache-region).

### At request time

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Request"] --> B["CDN"]
    B --> C["Serve cached shell"]
    B --> D["Invoke function"]
    C -->|"Instant"| E["Browser"]
    D -->|"Streams in"| E
```

A request arrives at the nearest [Vercel region](/docs/regions). If the regional [CDN cache](/docs/caching/cdn-cache) already has the shell, Vercel serves it right away. If not, the first request in that region pulls the shell from the global ISR cache and populates the CDN cache. In both cases, your function renders the dynamic holes in parallel. The shell reaches the browser first. The function output streams into the same response as it completes, so dynamic content fills in after the initial paint.

This is the key difference from ISR: even when the shell is served from the CDN cache, your function still runs to render the dynamic holes. It is possible to have a fully cached page, but most PPR requests incur a function invocation.

### At revalidation time

Revalidation updates the cached shell in two steps. First, your function regenerates the shell in the background. Then, the next request in each region pulls the updated shell into the regional CDN cache.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Timer or API trigger"] --> B["Generate new shell"]
    B --> C["Update ISR cache"]
    C --> D["Purge CDN caches"]
```

Two triggers can update the cached content for a shell:

- **Time-based revalidation** runs automatically after a set interval
- **On-demand revalidation** runs when you call an API

Both triggers run in the background, so visitors keep receiving the last generated shell while your function generates the new one. Once the new shell is in the global ISR cache, the next request in each region pulls it into the regional CDN cache and serves it:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Request"] --> B["Regional CDN cache"]
    B -->|"Miss"| C["Global ISR cache"]
    C -->|"Updated shell"| B
    B --> D["Serve cached shell"]
    B --> E["Invoke function"]
    D -->|"Instant"| F["Browser"]
    E -->|"Streams in"| F
```

### On failure

If revalidation fails, Vercel keeps serving the existing shell from the global ISR cache and regional CDN caches, and retries shortly after. For the full failure behavior, see [how ISR works](/docs/incremental-static-regeneration#on-failure).

## Observability

You can observe how your PPR routes behave from the [**Observability**](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F~%2Fobservability\&title=Try+Observability) tab in the Vercel dashboard.

The PPR observability page displays

- **Shell hit rate**: See the hit rates for the static shell portion of the page. A high shell hit rate means most visitors get an instant first paint.
- **Dynamic invocations**: The number of requests that required executing a function to fill in the dynamic portions of the page.

> **💡 Note:** PPR uses Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) for the static shell portion of the page and Vercel Functions for the dynamic portion, so additional observability details are available from the ISR and Functions observability pages.

## Usage and pricing

When you use PPR with a framework on Vercel, you incur usage for:

- **[ISR reads and writes](/docs/incremental-static-regeneration/limits-and-pricing)**: Vercel reads the cached shell from the global ISR cache when the CDN cache misses, and writes fresh content back when it revalidates.
- **[Function invocations](/docs/functions/usage-and-pricing)**: your function runs to render the dynamic holes on most requests, plus any background revalidations.
- **[Fast Origin Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-origin-transfer)**: rendered output transferred from your function to the CDN cache and global ISR cache.

## More resources

- [Partial Prerendering with Next.js](/docs/frameworks/full-stack/nextjs#partial-prerendering)
- [Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)](/docs/incremental-static-regeneration)
- [Vercel Functions](/docs/functions)
- [Runtime Cache](/docs/caching/runtime-cache)

title: "Partial Prerendering State"
description: "Understand the PPR state that describes how a Partial Prerendering page was served: as a static shell, a partial resume, or fully dynamic."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.007Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/partial-prerendering/ppr-state"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Partial Prerendering State

For [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/partial-prerendering) routes, Vercel records a **PPR state** that describes how the page was served for a request. A PPR response is a cached static **shell** with dynamic holes that are **postponed** during prerendering, then resumed and streamed in per request. The PPR state tells you which parts of that model actually applied. It shows whether the whole page came from the static shell, part of it was resumed dynamically, or all of it was rendered dynamically.

## States

Every PPR request resolves to one of these states:

| State     | What it means                                                                                                  |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Static`  | The whole page was prerendered. It was served entirely from the static shell, with no dynamic holes to resume. |
| `Partial` | A static shell was served, and the postponed dynamic parts were resumed and streamed from your function.       |
| `Dynamic` | The static shell was empty, so the entire response came from postponed content resumed by your function.       |

## Static

The page was fully prerendered, so the entire response came from the static shell and there were no postponed parts to resume. Nothing needed to be rendered dynamically for this request, so your function was not invoked.

This is the fastest PPR outcome: the whole page is served from cached static content. A route lands here when it has no dynamic data, or when all of its data is cacheable, so it can be prerendered into the static shell at build time or through later regeneration.

The [cache status](/docs/caching/cache-status) observed for a `Static` request can be `HIT`, `MISS`, `PRERENDER`, `STALE`, or `REVALIDATED`.

For example, a page whose data is all cacheable prerenders into a full static shell:

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" framework=nextjs-app
type Post = { id: number; title: string };

async function Posts() {
  'use cache';
  // Cached: prerendered into the static shell
  const posts: Post[] = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog').then((res) =>
    res.json(),
  );
  return (
    <ul>
      {posts.map((post) => (
        <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}

export default function Page() {
  return <Posts />;
}
```

![A Static request, served entirely from the static shell.](https://7nyt0uhk7sse4zvn.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/front/docs/partial-prerendering/ppr-state/ppr-state-static-light-v2.png?lightbox)

## Partial

A static shell was served immediately, and the page's postponed dynamic parts were resumed and streamed in from your function. This is the core Partial Prerendering behavior: the visitor gets the cached shell right away, while the dynamic holes are filled per request.

A `Partial` state means the page has both a meaningful static shell and dynamic content, such as a cached layout around a personalized or request-specific section.

The [cache status](/docs/caching/cache-status) observed for a `Partial` request can be `HIT`, `MISS`, `PRERENDER`, `STALE`, or `REVALIDATED`.

For example, a cached list of posts with a personalized greeting resumed per request:

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" framework=nextjs-app
import { Suspense } from 'react';
import { cookies } from 'next/headers';

type Post = { id: number; title: string };

async function Posts() {
  'use cache';
  const posts: Post[] = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog').then((res) =>
    res.json(),
  );
  return (
    <ul>
      {posts.map((post) => (
        <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}

async function Greeting() {
  const user = (await cookies()).get('user')?.value;
  return <p>Welcome back, {user}</p>;
}

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <main>
      {/* Cached: prerendered into the static shell */}
      <Posts />
      {/* Dynamic: streamed in per request */}
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
        <Greeting />
      </Suspense>
    </main>
  );
}
```

![A Partial request, where the static shell is served and the dynamic parts stream from your function.](https://7nyt0uhk7sse4zvn.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/front/docs/partial-prerendering/ppr-state/ppr-state-partial-light-v2.png?lightbox)

## Dynamic

The static shell was empty, so the entire response came from postponed content resumed by your function. There was no static content to serve ahead of the dynamic render.

Since the page is fully dynamic, the [cache status](/docs/caching/cache-status) for a `Dynamic` request can only be `MISS`.

For example, an empty `<Suspense>` boundary above `<body>` in the root layout opts the route out of a static shell, so nothing below the boundary is prerendered:

```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" framework=nextjs-app
import { Suspense } from 'react';

export default function RootLayout({
  children,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      {/* Empty fallback above <body>: nothing below this boundary is
          prerendered, so the route's static shell is empty */}
      <Suspense fallback={null}>
        <body>{children}</body>
      </Suspense>
    </html>
  );
}
```

```tsx filename="app/inbox/page.tsx" framework=nextjs-app
import { cookies } from 'next/headers';

type Message = { id: string; subject: string };

export default async function InboxPage() {
  // Per-request data: nothing on this page can be prerendered
  const token = (await cookies()).get('session-token')?.value;
  const messages: Message[] = await fetch('https://api.example.com/inbox', {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  }).then((res) => res.json());

  return (
    <ul>
      {messages.map((message) => (
        <li key={message.id}>{message.subject}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

With an empty shell, there is nothing for the CDN to serve ahead of the render, so the visitor waits on your function for the first byte. A route that consistently shows `Dynamic` is the signal to move whatever can be cached back above the boundary so a shell exists.

![A Dynamic request, rendered entirely by your function.](https://7nyt0uhk7sse4zvn.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/front/docs/partial-prerendering/ppr-state/ppr-state-dynamic-light-v2.png?lightbox)

title: "Getting started with Partial Prerendering"
description: "Set up Partial Prerendering (PPR) in a Next.js App Router project: enable Cache Components, cache a static shell, and stream dynamic content per request."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.007Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/partial-prerendering/quickstart"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Getting started with Partial Prerendering

This guide walks through setting up [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/partial-prerendering) in a Next.js App Router project. Vercel serves the cached static shell from its CDN, then streams the dynamic parts from your function into the same response.

## Prerequisites

- A project deployed on Vercel
- A Next.js App Router project (PPR is available with Next.js)

## Enable Cache Components

As of Next.js 16, PPR is built into the Cache Components model. Opt in by enabling `cacheComponents` in your `next.config.ts`:

```ts filename="next.config.ts" framework=nextjs-app
import type { NextConfig } from 'next';

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
};

export default nextConfig;
```

With Cache Components, data is dynamic by default; you choose what to cache with the `use cache` directive.

> **💡 Note:** Enabling `cacheComponents` inverts rendering defaults across your whole project. Existing routes that read uncached data can surface build errors until that data is wrapped in a `<Suspense>` boundary or marked with `use cache`.

## Cache a static shell

Mark the content you want prerendered with `use cache`. This becomes the static shell:

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" framework=nextjs-app
type Post = { id: number; title: string };

async function Posts() {
  'use cache';
  // Cached: prerendered into the static shell
  const posts: Post[] = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog').then((res) =>
    res.json(),
  );
  return (
    <ul>
      {posts.map((post) => (
        <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}

export default function Page() {
  return <Posts />;
}
```

A page whose content is entirely cached prerenders into a full static shell. On a cache hit it is served from the CDN without invoking your function; your function still runs when the shell is regenerated. By default the shell revalidates on an interval, so set how long it stays fresh with [`cacheLife`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and invalidate it on demand with [`cacheTag`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag).

## Stream dynamic content

Add per-request content and wrap it in a `<Suspense>` boundary:

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" framework=nextjs-app
import { Suspense } from 'react';
import { cookies } from 'next/headers';

type Post = { id: number; title: string };

async function Posts() {
  'use cache';
  // Cached: prerendered into the static shell
  const posts: Post[] = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog').then((res) =>
    res.json(),
  );
  return (
    <ul>
      {posts.map((post) => (
        <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}

async function Greeting() {
  const user = (await cookies()).get('user')?.value;
  return <p>Welcome back, {user}</p>;
}

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <main>
      {/* Cached: prerendered into the static shell */}
      <Posts />
      {/* Dynamic: streamed in per request */}
      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
        <Greeting />
      </Suspense>
    </main>
  );
}
```

Keep per-request data inside a `<Suspense>` boundary. With Cache Components, reading uncached data like `cookies()` outside a boundary fails the build with an error about uncached data accessed outside a `<Suspense>` boundary, rather than silently rendering the whole route dynamically. The boundary is what lets Next.js prerender the static shell and stream the dynamic part into it.

## Next steps

- [How PPR works](/docs/partial-prerendering#how-ppr-works): the request flow from build through revalidation
- [Usage and pricing](/docs/partial-prerendering#usage-and-pricing): the cost of PPR requests

title: "Configure additional identity scopes"
description: "Request group membership and other provider-specific identity claims when using Passport."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.007Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/passport/additional-identity-scopes"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Configure additional identity scopes

Passport requests identity information through the Connect application assigned to your project. An OAuth scope asks your identity provider for a category of information. A claim is the value the provider returns, such as a visitor's email address or group membership.

Passport uses the standard OpenID Connect scopes, including `openid`, `profile`, and `email`. You can configure Connect to include additional claims, such as group membership, in the Passport token when your identity provider supports them.

## Add a scope to the Connect application

For example, configure the `groups` scope when your application needs to make authorization decisions based on group membership:

1. In the [Vercel dashboard](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%5Bproject%5D%2Fsettings%2Fpassport\&title=Project+Passport+Settings), open the Connect application that Passport uses.
2. Under **Grant Types**, enable **User Authorization**.
3. Add `groups` to the **User Authorization** scopes.
4. Under **Forwarded ID Token Claims**, add `groups`. This is the allowlist for additional identity claims that Connect can include in the Passport token.
5. Save the application.

The scope must also be enabled for the OAuth application in your identity provider. The exact setup varies by provider. Requesting a scope does not grant access by itself: your provider must authorize the scope and return the selected claim from its UserInfo endpoint before Connect can include it in the Passport token.

> **💡 Note:** Scope suggestions come from your provider's OAuth metadata and can include
> non-identity API permissions. Request only the scopes your application needs.
> For example, Okta's `okta.*` management scopes are not required to include a
> visitor's groups in a Passport token.

## Configure groups in Okta

Configure the group claim in the Okta authorization server that matches the issuer in your Connect application. Do not combine an issuer or endpoint from one authorization server with a group claim configured in another.

### Organization authorization server

An organization authorization server has an issuer without `/oauth2/{authorization_server_id}`, such as `https://your_okta_domain.okta.com`.

1. In Okta, go to **Applications** > **Applications**, then select your OpenID Connect application.
2. Open the **Sign On** tab.
3. Under **OpenID Connect ID Token**, click **Edit**.
4. In **Group Claims**, select **Filter**.
5. Set the claim name to `groups`.
6. Select **Matches regex** and enter `.*` to return all groups for the signed-in visitor.
7. Save the change. If Okta shows **Refresh Application Data** in the application menu, select it.

`Starts with .*` does not match every group. Okta treats that value as literal text. Use **Matches regex** with `.*` instead.

### Custom authorization server

A custom authorization server has an issuer such as `https://your_okta_domain.okta.com/oauth2/default`.

1. In Okta, go to **Security** > **API** > **Authorization Servers**, then select the authorization server.
2. Open **Claims** and add a `groups` claim.
3. Include the claim in the **ID Token**.
4. Select **Groups** as the value type.
5. Select **Matches regex** and enter `.*`.
6. Save the claim.

Assigning people or groups to an Okta application controls who can sign in. It does not automatically add group membership to an OAuth token. Configure the claim as described above as well.

## Confirm the claim is present

Start a new Passport session after changing your provider configuration. For example, use a private browser window, then inspect the verified Passport identity in server-side code:

```js filename="app/api/me/route.js"
import { getIdentity } from '@vercel/passport';

export async function GET() {
  const identity = await getIdentity();

  return Response.json({
    groups: identity?.payload.groups,
  });
}
```

When the provider does not return the requested claim, Passport omits it. Treat the claim as optional input and deny access when your authorization policy requires a missing or invalid claim.

## Use identity claims safely

Treat identity claims as input to application-level authorization, not as a replacement for Passport's deployment protection. Passport decides whether the visitor may enter the protected deployment. Your application can then use verified identity claims to decide whether the visitor may access a particular route or action.

Read identity only in server-side code and use the verified Passport token. See [Read Passport identity in your application](/docs/passport/read-identity) for the recommended helper and [Verify forwarded Passport tokens](/docs/passport/verify-identity) when another backend receives the token.

Do not assume a claim is always present or has the same shape for every provider. Check that it exists, validate its type, and deny access when your authorization policy requires a claim that is absent or invalid.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Forward Passport identity to another backend"
description: "Forward a Passport visitor identity to another backend that you operate."
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.007Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/passport/forward-identity"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Forward Passport identity to another backend

A Passport-protected Vercel app can call another backend with the Passport token. Forward the token in the `Authorization` header, then verify it at the receiving service before trusting any claims.

```js filename="app/api/report/route.js"
import { getIdentity } from '@vercel/passport';

export async function POST() {
  let identity;

  try {
    identity = await getIdentity();
  } catch {
    return Response.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 });
  }

  if (!identity?.token) {
    return Response.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 });
  }

  const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/do-stuff', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${identity.token}`,
    },
  });

  return Response.json(await response.json(), { status: response.status });
}
```

Only forward Passport tokens over HTTPS to backends that you operate. A Passport token authenticates the visitor to your backend. It is not an access token for your identity provider or a downstream service. If the backend needs to exchange or store credentials for another service, use Vercel Connect for that credential flow. If the backend only needs to know who the Passport visitor is, it can use `verifyIdentity()` to [verify the Passport token](/docs/passport/verify-identity) directly.

# Restrict access to deployments with Passport

> Passport is available on Enterprise plans
>
> Those with the owner role can manage Passport

Passport lets you protect deployments with your own identity provider. Visitors authenticate with your identity provider before they can view a protected deployment.

Use Passport when you want visitors to sign in with an external identity provider, such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, or another OpenID Connect compatible provider. Vercel Connect stores the OAuth application configuration that talks to your identity provider.

## How Passport works

Passport has two parts:

- **Vercel Connect application**: The OAuth or OpenID Connect configuration that stores your identity provider's issuer, endpoints, client ID, and client secret.
- **Project or team setting**: The Passport configuration that selects the Connect application and controls whether Passport is enabled.

When a visitor opens a protected deployment, Vercel redirects them to your identity provider. After the identity provider authenticates the visitor, Vercel validates the response and sets a session cookie for the protected deployment.

New to Passport? [Set up Passport with an identity provider](/docs/passport/set-up-identity-provider) first, then return to the other guides when you need to use identity in application code.

## Getting started

Follow these guides to choose a protection method and connect your identity provider:

- [Protect internal apps with Passport](/kb/guide/vercel-passport): Configure your identity provider, enable Passport for projects or a team, and read visitor identity.
- [Compare Passport with other Deployment Protection methods](/kb/guide/vercel-passport-vs-deployment-protection): Choose between Passport, Vercel Authentication, Password Protection, and Trusted IPs.
- [Set up Passport with Microsoft Entra ID](/kb/guide/vercel-passport-microsoft-entra-id): Configure an Entra ID application, restrict access to assigned users, and read identity in a Next.js app.

## Use Passport with Chat SDK

Use a verified Passport identity to keep a browser chatbot's conversation history associated with the signed-in visitor. With Chat SDK's History API, the bot can use messages from that visitor's earlier conversations as context for a reply.

Follow [Chat SDK with Vercel Passport](/docs/chat-sdk/integrations/passport) to authenticate Web Adapter requests and derive a per-user history key from the verified issuer and subject. Sharing that history with Slack, Teams, or Discord requires a separate verified account link.

## Use Passport with microfrontends

For a URL that uses [microfrontends routing](/docs/microfrontends/routing), the default application's Passport configuration protects every path, including paths served by child applications. Configure Passport on the default application to protect the composed microfrontend experience.

Passport completes authentication at `/.well-known/vercel/passport/callback` on the requested hostname. Vercel handles this callback before routing to your application, so you do not need to create the path in the default or child application.

For URLs with microfrontends routing, child paths use the default application's Passport configuration. Child applications cannot have an independent Passport connection while they belong to the group.

The default application's Passport configuration does not protect a child application's direct domains. Protect those domains with another [Deployment Protection method](/docs/deployment-protection/methods-to-protect-deployments). To configure Passport on the child project, remove it from the group first.

Learn more about [Deployment Protection and microfrontends](/docs/microfrontends/managing-microfrontends/security#deployment-protection-and-microfrontends).

## Guides

**Set up Passport with an identity provider**: Configure Passport for Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, and other OIDC providers. [Learn more →](/docs/passport/set-up-identity-provider)

**Configure additional identity scopes**: Request group membership and other provider-specific identity claims. [Learn more →](/docs/passport/additional-identity-scopes)

**Read Passport identity in your application**: Read a verified visitor identity from route handlers, server actions, and server components. [Learn more →](/docs/passport/read-identity)

**Passport token claims**: Review the standard, deployment, and visitor identity claims in a Passport token. [Learn more →](/docs/passport/token-claims)

**Verify forwarded Passport tokens**: Verify a forwarded token as a signed JWT. [Learn more →](/docs/passport/verify-identity)

**Forward Passport identity to another backend**: Pass a Passport token to a backend you operate over HTTPS. [Learn more →](/docs/passport/forward-identity)

## Framework examples

Use verified Passport identity to personalize your application, restrict access by group, and attribute actions to visitors. These guides include local development, authorization, and identity forwarding examples:

| Framework                         | Guide                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Next.js                           | [Identify visitors and control access in App Router pages, Route Handlers, and Server Actions](/kb/guide/vercel-passport-nextjs) |
| Nuxt                              | [Read visitor identity and protect Nuxt server routes](/kb/guide/vercel-passport-nuxt)                                           |

| Express, Hono, Nitro, and FastAPI | [Read and verify identity in Node.js and Python backends](/kb/guide/vercel-passport-backend-frameworks)                          |

## Govern internal apps

Passport controls who can reach a deployment. Your application must also enforce which records each visitor can access and which actions they can perform. For employee-built apps and agents, assign an owner and define when changes require human review. Read [How do you govern AI apps and agents built by employees?](/i/govern-employee-built-ai-apps-and-agents) for guidance on ownership, data access, spending limits, and rollout reviews.

## Monitor Passport access

When a visitor successfully authenticates to a Passport-protected project, Vercel records a `passport-access-granted` event in both the [Activity Log](/dashboard/activity?types=passport-access-granted) and [Audit Logs](/docs/audit-log). The event identifies the visitor and records the protected hostname and project context.

In the Activity Log, select **Filter by Event**, then select **passport-access-granted** to view Passport access events.

## Pricing

Passport is available as an Enterprise feature. Contact your Vercel account team for pricing.

# Python SDK Reference

`vercel-passport` reads and verifies [Vercel Passport](/docs/passport) visitor identities in server-side Python code. Use it to read the current request, require an identity with a token, or verify a token forwarded from another application.

## Install

The SDK requires Python 3.10 or later:

```bash filename="Terminal"
uv add vercel-passport
```

If you use pip, run `pip install vercel-passport` instead.

Import asynchronous helpers from `vercel.passport`. For synchronous applications, import the same names from [`vercel.passport.sync`](#synchronous-api).

## Choose an identity helper

| Function | Returns | Use it to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_identity()` | `PassportIdentity` or `None` | Read the current visitor, allowing no identity or a local development fixture. |
| `require_identity()` | `PassportIdentity` | Read an identity that has a token, raising when the identity or token is missing. |
| `verify_identity(source)` | `PassportIdentity` | Always verify a token supplied by another application, with no development fallback. |

All three helpers verify tokens read from request headers or cookies. `get_identity()` and `require_identity()` also support explicit debugging tokens whose verification depends on the `verify` option. See [Token resolution](#token-resolution).

## `get_identity()`

Returns the current visitor's identity, or `None` when no token or local identity is available. Invalid tokens raise an error rather than returning `None`.

With no `request` argument, the helper reads the current request headers recorded by the Vercel Python runtime. You can also pass a header mapping or a request object with a `headers` mapping, such as a FastAPI, Starlette, Django, Flask, or httpx request.

For example, read a visitor in a FastAPI route:

```py filename="main.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
from vercel.passport import PassportIdentityError, get_identity

app = FastAPI()


@app.get('/api/me')
async def me(request: Request):
    try:
        identity = await get_identity(request, cookies=request.cookies)
    except PassportIdentityError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail='Unauthorized') from None

    if identity is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail='Unauthorized')

    return {
        'issuer': identity.payload['iss'],
        'subject': identity.subject,
        'email': identity.email,
    }
```

Use `identity.subject` as the visitor identifier for a single Passport issuer. If you accept multiple issuers, store `identity.payload['iss']` with the subject. Treat profile fields such as `email` and `name` as optional. Your application must still [authorize each visitor's actions](/docs/passport/read-identity#apply-application-level-authorization).

### Parameters

All parameters after `request` are keyword-only. `require_identity()` accepts the same parameters.

| Parameter | Type | Default and behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `request` | `object` or `None` | Defaults to `None`, which reads the runtime request context. Accepts a header mapping or an object exposing one as `headers`. |
| `token` | `str` or `None` | Explicit token. Takes precedence over request headers and cookies. Intended for debugging; use `verify=True` to verify it. |
| `cookies` | `Mapping[str, str]` or `None` | Explicit cookies, such as `request.cookies`. For each cookie, the SDK checks this mapping before the `Cookie` header. |
| `verify` | `bool` | Defaults to `False`. Controls verification only for `token` and `VERCEL_PASSPORT_TOKEN`; request tokens are always verified. |
| `allow_unverified` | `bool` or `None` | Defaults to allowing unverified debugging tokens only in local development. `False` rejects them. `True` explicitly permits them even on deployments; it doesn't skip verification of request tokens. |
| `project_id` | `str` or `None` | Expected source project ID. Defaults to `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID`. |
| `environment` | `str` or `None` | Expected source environment. Defaults to `VERCEL_TARGET_ENV`, then `VERCEL_ENV`. |
| `owner_id` | `str` or `None` | Expected source team ID. Checked only when supplied. |
| `audience` | `str`, `Sequence[str]`, or `None` | Expected audience or accepted audiences. Checked only when supplied. |

### Token resolution

`get_identity()` and `require_identity()` use the first available token in this order:

1. The `token` argument.
2. The `x-vercel-oidc-passport-token` header.
3. The `_vercel_passport` cookie.
4. The `VERCEL_PASSPORT_TOKEN` environment variable.

The SDK reassembles chunked Passport cookies and checks their checksum before verification. A missing chunk or invalid checksum raises `PassportIdentityError`. A valid higher-priority header takes precedence over a malformed cookie.

These two helpers don't read `Authorization: Bearer`. Use [`verify_identity()`](#verify_identity) for forwarded bearer tokens.

If no token is available, the helpers resolve [local identities](#local-development). `get_identity()` can return these fixtures; `require_identity()` rejects them because they have no token.

## `require_identity()`

Resolves identity with the same arguments and precedence as `get_identity()`, but raises `PassportIdentityError` when no identity exists or the identity has no token. The returned identity's `token` is set, which lets you [forward it to a backend you operate](/docs/passport/forward-identity).

For example, build an authorization header for a server-to-server request:

```py filename="identity.py"
from vercel.passport import require_identity


async def backend_headers(request: object) -> dict[str, str]:
    identity = await require_identity(request, verify=True)
    return {'Authorization': f'Bearer {identity.token}'}
```

`require_identity()` requires a token, not unconditional verification. An explicit debugging token can still produce `verified=False` when `verify=False` and unverified tokens are allowed. Use `verify=True` or `verify_identity()` when accepting an explicit token as proof of identity.

## `verify_identity()`

Always verifies a supplied token and returns a `PassportIdentity` with `verified=True`. It never uses runtime request context, debugging environment variables, or development identities.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `str`, `object`, or `None` | Required argument. A token string, header mapping, or request object with a `headers` mapping. `None` can be used with explicit `cookies`; it doesn't read runtime headers. |
| `cookies` | `Mapping[str, str]` or `None` | Explicit cookies, checked before the `Cookie` header. |
| `project_id` | `str` or `None` | Expected source project ID. Defaults to `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID`. |
| `environment` | `str` or `None` | Expected source environment. Defaults to `VERCEL_TARGET_ENV`, then `VERCEL_ENV`. |
| `owner_id` | `str` or `None` | Expected source team ID. Checked only when supplied. |
| `audience` | `str`, `Sequence[str]`, or `None` | Expected audience or accepted audiences. Checked only when supplied. |

For a request or header mapping, the helper checks `Authorization: Bearer` first, then `x-vercel-oidc-passport-token`, then `_vercel_passport`. Header names are case-insensitive. A missing or malformed token raises an error.

A receiving backend must validate the **source** project and environment that minted the token. For example:

```py filename="main.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
from vercel.passport import PassportIdentityError, verify_identity

app = FastAPI()


@app.post('/api/orders')
async def orders(request: Request):
    try:
        identity = await verify_identity(
            request,
            owner_id='team_your_team_id_here',
            project_id='prj_your_project_id_here',
            environment='production',
        )
    except PassportIdentityError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail='Unauthorized') from None

    return {'subject': identity.subject, 'email': identity.email}
```

### Verification rules

Verification accepts only RS256 signatures using Vercel's signing keys. It checks the Passport issuer family, including `https://passport.vercel.com` and owner-scoped issuers under it. A regular Vercel OpenID Connect (OIDC) token doesn't satisfy the required Passport claims.

The expected project and environment must both resolve from arguments or environment variables. If either is missing, verification fails. Both use exact equality: `'*'` is a literal value, and lists of projects or environments aren't supported. `owner_id` and `audience` add checks only when you provide them; the SDK doesn't infer an audience from the project.

The verifier requires `exp` and checks time claims with a fixed 60-second clock-skew allowance, including `nbf` and `iat` when present. See [Passport token claims](/docs/passport/token-claims) for the token schema.

## Identity models

### `PassportIdentity`

The returned identity exposes these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | `str` | Passport visitor identifier from `sub`. Treat it as opaque. |
| `external_subject` | `str` | Visitor identifier at the upstream identity provider, from `external_sub`. |
| `connector_id` | `str` | Passport Connector ID. |
| `owner` | `PassportOwner` | Source team, with `slug: str` and optional `id: str`. |
| `project` | `PassportProject` or `None` | Source project, with `id: str` and optional `name: str`. Present only when the claims contain a project ID; every verified token has one. |
| `environment` | `str` or `None` | Source deployment environment. |
| `external_issuer` | `str` or `None` | Upstream identity provider issuer, from `external_iss`. |
| `email`, `name` | `str` or `None` | Optional profile fields returned by the identity provider. |
| `token` | `str` or `None` | Encoded token. Local fixtures have no token. |
| `token_source` | `TokenSource` | `'header'`, `'cookie'`, or `'local'`. Explicit token strings and environment tokens use `'local'`, even after verification. |
| `verified` | `bool` | Whether the SDK verified the token's signature and claims. |
| `payload` | `dict[str, Any]` | All claims, including additional claims without dedicated fields. |

`PassportIdentity`, `PassportOwner`, and `PassportProject` are frozen Pydantic models. Use `identity.model_dump()` or `identity.model_dump_json()` to serialize an identity. Both exclude `token`; the representation also excludes `token` and `payload`. Serialized claims can still include profile data, so return only fields your client needs.

The model fields cannot be reassigned, but `payload` is a mutable deep copy of the original claims. Mutating it doesn't update the derived identity fields or rerun verification. Constructing a `PassportIdentity` yourself validates its shape; it doesn't cryptographically verify a token. Use the helpers for verification.

### Constants and type aliases

| Export | Value or type |
| --- | --- |
| `PASSPORT_HEADER_NAME` | `'x-vercel-oidc-passport-token'` |
| `PASSPORT_COOKIE_NAME` | `'_vercel_passport'` |
| `PassportClaims` | `Mapping[str, Any]` |
| `TokenSource` | `Literal['header', 'cookie', 'local']` |

## Local development

Without a Passport token or an explicit local fixture, `get_identity()` returns `None`. Unlike the JavaScript helper, the Python SDK doesn't synthesize a test visitor by default.

### `local_identity()`

Use this context manager to supply an identity for local requests without a token. It accepts a `PassportDevelopmentIdentity` or a mapping of full Passport claims. The same synchronous `with` block works inside async functions:

```py filename="local_identity.py"
import asyncio

from vercel.passport import PassportDevelopmentIdentity, get_identity, local_identity


async def main():
    fixture = PassportDevelopmentIdentity(owner='acme', external_subject='user_dev')
    with local_identity(fixture):
        identity = await get_identity({})
        assert identity is not None
        print(identity.external_subject)
        print(identity.verified)


asyncio.run(main())
```

This local example prints `user_dev` and `False`. On leaving the block, the previous context identity is restored. Tasks started inside the block inherit the identity, as do threads started with `anyio.to_thread` or `asyncio.to_thread`. Plain `threading.Thread` instances don't inherit it.

### Environment-based fixtures

When no token is available, local identity resolution checks:

1. The current `local_identity()` context.
2. Full claims supplied as JSON in `VERCEL_PASSPORT_IDENTITY`.
3. A synthesized `PassportDevelopmentIdentity` when `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV=1` or `true`.

Enable the synthesized fixture in your local process environment:

```bash filename="Terminal"
export VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV=1
```

The SDK emits `PassportDevelopmentIdentityWarning` once per process when it uses a synthesized identity. All local fixtures have `verified=False`, `token=None`, and `token_source='local'`. `require_identity()` rejects them.

Local fixtures are disabled when `VERCEL_ENV` is set to anything other than `development`, or when `VERCEL=1` without `VERCEL_ENV=development`. Setting the fixture's own `environment` field doesn't override this restriction. The SDK reads process environment variables; it doesn't load `.env.local` itself.

### `PassportDevelopmentIdentity`

Unset constructor fields read the environment variables below, then use their defaults. Explicit constructor values take precedence. Passing `None` clears an optional field even when its environment variable is set.

| Field | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV_OWNER` | `'local'` |
| `owner_id` | `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV_OWNER_ID` | `None` |
| `connector_id` | `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV_CONNECTOR_ID` | `'local'` |
| `external_subject` | `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV_EXTERNAL_SUB` | `'test-user'` |
| `external_issuer` | `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV_EXTERNAL_ISS` | `None` |
| `environment` | `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV_ENVIRONMENT` | `'development'` |
| `project` | `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV_PROJECT` | `'local'` |
| `project_id` | `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV_PROJECT_ID`, then `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` | `None` |
| `issuer` | `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV_ISSUER` | `https://passport.vercel.com/{owner}` |
| `audience` | `VERCEL_PASSPORT_DEV_AUDIENCE` | `https://vercel.com/{owner}/{project}/{environment}` |

`to_claims()` returns the fixture as Passport claims, with `email='test-user@passport.local'` and `name='Test User'`. To customize profile or additional claims, update this claims mapping and pass it to `local_identity()`.

### Debugging with an explicit token

The `token` argument and `VERCEL_PASSPORT_TOKEN` support local debugging. By default, the SDK decodes these tokens without verifying them in local development. Outside local development, it rejects them unless you set `verify=True` or explicitly allow unverified tokens.

For authentication, use `verify_identity()` or pass `verify=True`. The `allow_unverified` option applies only to explicit debugging tokens and never disables verification of request headers or cookies.

## Synchronous API

`vercel.passport.sync` exposes the same functions, models, constants, and arguments. Call its helpers without `await`:

```py filename="identity.py"
from vercel.passport.sync import get_identity


def visitor_subject(request: object) -> str | None:
    identity = get_identity(request)
    return identity.subject if identity is not None else None
```

The synchronous helpers can block while fetching signing keys on a cold cache. Use the asynchronous API in async routes to avoid blocking the event loop.

## Errors and warnings

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PassportError` | Base exception for Passport operations. |
| `PassportIdentityError` | Missing required identity or token, malformed token or claims, invalid chunked cookie, or disallowed unverified token. |
| `PassportVerificationError` | Signature or claim verification failed, or required project/environment expectations couldn't resolve. Subclass of `PassportIdentityError`. |
| `PassportValidationError` | Invalid model fields, unknown constructor arguments, or an attempt to change frozen fields. Also a `ValueError`. |
| `PassportDevelopmentIdentityWarning` | Warning emitted once per process when the SDK uses a synthesized development identity. |

Catch `PassportIdentityError` to handle both identity and verification failures. Invalid request objects or unsupported `local_identity()` argument types raise `TypeError`. Don't return token contents or verification error details to unauthenticated clients.

- [Forward Passport identity](/docs/passport/forward-identity)
