**api/file.js**

```js filename="api/file.js" framework=other
import { get } from '@vercel/blob';

export default async function handler(request) {
  // Your auth goes here: await authRequest(request)

  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);
  const pathname = searchParams.get('pathname');
  if (!pathname) {
    return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Missing pathname' }), {
      status: 400,
    });
  }

  const result = await get(pathname, {
    access: 'private',
    ifNoneMatch: request.headers.get('if-none-match') ?? undefined,
  });

  if (!result) {
    return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });
  }

  // Blob hasn't changed — tell the browser to use its cached copy
  if (result.statusCode === 304) {
    return new Response(null, {
      status: 304,
      headers: {
        ETag: result.blob.etag,
        'Cache-Control': 'private, no-cache',
      },
    });
  }

  return new Response(result.stream, {
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': result.blob.contentType,
      'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff',
      ETag: result.blob.etag,
      'Cache-Control': 'private, no-cache',
    },
  });
}
```

How it works:

1. **First request**: The blob store returns a `200` response with the content and an `ETag`. The browser caches the response.
2. **Subsequent requests**: The browser sends `If-None-Match` with the cached ETag. When forwarded to the blob store, it returns a `304` response without content, so no data is re-downloaded.

> **💡 Note:** Avoid caching private blob responses in Vercel's CDN cache (e.g. with
> `s-maxage`) and avoid relying on middleware for auth. While both can work, a
> middleware bug or misconfiguration could expose cached private content to the
> wrong users.Instead, always verify auth directly in your route handler, right next to the
> code that reads the blob.

See [Cache-Control headers](/docs/caching/cache-control-headers) for more details.

Learn more about [Vercel's CDN cache](/docs/caching/cdn-cache).

## Custom domains

Since private blobs are delivered through your own [Functions](/docs/functions), you can serve them from any custom domain. A common pattern is to create a dedicated Vercel project (e.g. "assets") for blob delivery:

1. Create a new Vercel project with a route handler that serves private blobs (as shown in [delivering private blobs](#delivering-private-blobs))
2. [Connect your private Blob store](/docs/vercel-blob#connecting-a-store-to-your-projects) to this project
3. [Assign a custom domain](/docs/domains/working-with-domains) to the project (e.g. `content.mywebsite.com`)

Requests to `content.mywebsite.com/api/file?pathname=documents/report.pdf` will then go through your auth logic and stream the blob to the user.

## SEO and search engine indexing

Private blobs cannot be indexed by search engines since all read access requires authentication.

## Download charges

When serving private blobs through [Functions](/docs/functions), you pay for:

1. **Function fetches the blob from the store**: [Blob Data Transfer](/docs/vercel-blob#blob-data-transfer) + [Fast Origin Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-origin-transfer) on cache miss
2. **Function responds to the browser**: [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/cdn) + [Fast Origin Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-origin-transfer)

Recommendations:

- Private Blob stores are ideal for smaller sensitive files or when you need precise auth control
- We do not recommend serving files larger than 100 MB through private Blob stores unless traffic is low
- For large public media, use [public storage](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage) which benefits from BDT rates (3x cheaper than FDT)

See [pricing documentation](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing) for full details.

## Upload charges

Upload charges depend on your implementation method:

- [Client Uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload): No data transfer charges for uploads
- [Server Uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/server-upload): [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-data-transfer) charges apply when your Vercel application receives the file

See [pricing documentation](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing) for full details.

# Public Storage

> Vercel Blob is available on all plans
>
> Those with the owner, member, developer role can access this feature

Public Blob stores make files accessible to anyone with the URL. Use public storage for images, videos, large media, and public assets where authentication isn't needed.

See [differences with private storage](/docs/vercel-blob#private-and-public-storage).

## Creating a public Blob store

Create a public Blob store from the dashboard or the Vercel CLI.

#### Dashboard

1. Go to your project's [**Storage** tab](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%5Bproject%5D%2Fstores\&title=Go+to+Storage)
2. Select **Create Storage**, then choose **Blob**
3. Select **Continue**, then set the access to **Public**

#### CLI

Run [`vercel blob create-store`](/docs/cli/blob#create-store) from your linked project directory with `--access public`. The `--yes` flag connects the new store to the project in all environments:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel blob create-store my-public-store --access public --yes
```

When your code runs on Vercel, the SDK authenticates using OIDC by default. Connect your store to a project so Vercel adds the OIDC token and `BLOB_STORE_ID` to your environment automatically. For team-level stores or code that runs outside Vercel, see Authentication in the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#authentication) or [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference#authentication) reference.

## Uploading files

Upload files to a public Blob store by setting the upload's access to public:

**app/api/upload/route.ts**

```ts filename="app/api/upload/route.ts"
import { put } from '@vercel/blob';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const form = await request.formData();
  const file = form.get('file') as File;

  const blob = await put(file.name, file, {
    access: 'public',
  });

  return Response.json(blob);
}
```

**main.py**

```py filename="main.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile

from vercel import blob

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/api/upload")
async def upload(file: UploadFile) -> blob.PutResult:
    return await blob.put_blob(
        file.filename or "upload",
        await file.read(),
        access="public",
    )
```

See the [server uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/server-upload) and [client uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) guides for detailed instructions on uploading files.

## Delivering public blobs

Every file uploaded to a public Blob store gets a URL in the form of `https://<store-id>.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/<pathname>`. You can use this URL directly in your HTML:

### Displaying an image

```html
<img
  src="https://my-store-id.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/avatar.png"
  alt="User avatar"
/>
```

To use [`next/image`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/image), add the blob store hostname to your `next.config.js`:

```js filename="next.config.js"
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  images: {
    remotePatterns: [
      new URL('https://my-store-id.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/**'),
    ],
  },
};

module.exports = nextConfig;
```

Then use `Image` instead of `img`:

```jsx
import Image from 'next/image';

<Image
  src="https://my-store-id.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/avatar.png"
  alt="User avatar"
  width={200}
  height={200}
/>
```

> **💡 Note:** `next/image` with direct blob URLs only works with public Blob stores. For
> private blobs, [serve files through your Functions](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#delivering-private-blobs)
> and use the function route URL as the image source.

### Linking a file for download

```html
<a href="https://my-store-id.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/report.pdf?download=1">
  Download report
</a>
```

Adding `?download=1` to a blob URL forces a file download, regardless of file type. The SDK also returns this URL as the download URL of each uploaded blob. Without it, the URL displays the file in the browser when the MIME type supports it (images, videos, audio, PDFs, plain text, XML, and JSON). All other MIME types automatically trigger a download.

This behavior is controlled by the `content-disposition` header. Vercel Blob sets it to `inline` for displayable types and `attachment` for everything else. This also prevents hosting HTML pages on Vercel Blob.

## Caching

When you request a public blob URL, the content is cached in two places:

1. Vercel's [CDN cache](/docs/caching/cdn-cache)
2. Your browser's cache

Both caches store blobs for up to 1 month by default to ensure optimal performance when serving content. While both systems aim to respect this duration, blobs may occasionally expire earlier.

Vercel will cache blobs up to [512 MB](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#size-limits). Bigger blobs will always be served from the origin (your store).

### Configuring cache duration

You can customize the caching duration by setting a cache max age when you upload a blob from your server or generate a token for a [client upload](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload). See the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#put) and [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference#put_blob) references.

The minimum configurable value is 60 seconds (1 minute). This represents the maximum time needed for our cache to update content behind a blob URL. For applications requiring faster updates, consider using a [Vercel function](/docs/functions) instead.

See [caching best practices](/docs/vercel-blob#caching) on the overview page for guidance on updating and overwriting blobs.

### Browser caching with conditional requests

When a browser requests a public blob URL, the CDN automatically includes an `ETag` header in the response. On subsequent requests, the browser sends an `If-None-Match` header with the cached ETag. If the blob hasn't changed, the CDN responds with `304 Not Modified` and the browser uses its cached copy, avoiding a full re-download.

This works automatically for public blobs accessed by URL. You don't need to write any code to benefit from conditional requests.

If you download public blobs server-side, you can also make a conditional read with the [`ifNoneMatch`](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#get) option to avoid re-downloading unchanged blobs:

```js
import { get } from '@vercel/blob';

const result = await get('images/hero.png', {
  access: 'public',
  ifNoneMatch: previousEtag,
});

if (result.statusCode === 304) {
  // Blob hasn't changed, use the version you already have
}
```

## Protecting public blobs with the firewall

Anyone with the URL can request a public blob, and each download counts toward your [Blob Data Transfer](/docs/vercel-blob#blob-data-transfer) usage. You can control this traffic with [Vercel WAF](/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf) rules, such as [rate limiting](/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/rate-limiting) or [IP blocking](/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/ip-blocking), to stop hotlinking, scraping, and abusive download patterns. To enable it:

1. Open [your Blob store](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fstores%2Fblob%2F%5Bstore%5D%2Fsettings\&title=Go+to+your+Blob+store) in the dashboard and select the **Settings** tab.
2. In the **Firewall** section, select **Protect your store**, then **Enable firewall**.

This connects your store to `vercel-blob-default-project`, a Vercel-managed, team-wide project that holds the firewall rules for all your protected Blob stores. See [Firewall and WAF integration](/docs/vercel-blob/security#firewall-and-waf-integration) for details and limitations.

## SEO and search engine indexing

### Search engine visibility of blobs

While Vercel Blob URLs can be designed to be unique and unguessable (when you add a random suffix to the pathname), they can still be indexed by search engines under certain conditions:

- If you link to blob URLs from public webpages
- If you embed blob content (images, PDFs, etc.) in indexed content
- If you share blob URLs publicly, even in contexts outside your application

By default, Vercel Blob does not provide a `robots.txt` file or other indexing controls. This means search engines like Google may discover and index your blob content if they find links to it.

### Preventing search engine indexing

If you want to prevent search engines from indexing your blob content, you need to upload a `robots.txt` file directly to your blob store from the dashboard or the Vercel CLI.

#### Dashboard

1. Go to your [**Storage** page](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F~%2Fstores\&title=Go+to+Storage) and select your blob store
2. Upload a `robots.txt` file to the root of your blob store with appropriate directives

#### CLI

Run [`vercel blob put`](/docs/cli/blob#put) to upload the file to the root of your blob store:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel blob put ./robots.txt --pathname robots.txt --access public
```

Example `robots.txt` content to block all crawling of your blob store:

```
User-agent: *
Disallow: /
```

### Removing already indexed blob content

If your blob content has already been indexed by search engines:

1. Verify your website ownership in [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console/)
2. Upload a `robots.txt` file to your blob store as described above
3. Use the "Remove URLs" tool in Google Search Console to request removal

## Download charges

When a public blob is downloaded, you pay for:

1. **Browser fetches the blob**: [Blob Data Transfer](/docs/vercel-blob#blob-data-transfer) + [Fast Origin Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-origin-transfer) on cache miss

Blob Data Transfer is 3x more cost-efficient than [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/cdn) on average, making public storage ideal for large media files like images, videos, and documents.

Blobs larger than 512 MB won't be cached, so every download is a cache miss that incurs both Blob Data Transfer and Fast Origin Transfer charges. See [size limits](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#size-limits) for details.

See [pricing documentation](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing) for full details.

## Upload charges

Upload charges depend on your implementation method:

- [Client Uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload): No data transfer charges for uploads
- [Server Uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/server-upload): [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-data-transfer) charges apply when your Vercel application receives the file

See [pricing documentation](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing) for full details.

# Python SDK Reference

> Vercel Blob is available on all plans
>
> Those with the owner, member, developer role can access this feature

Use the Vercel Blob Python SDK to upload, download, inspect, list, copy, and delete blobs from Python applications. The SDK provides an asynchronous API in `vercel.blob` and a matching synchronous API in `vercel.blob.sync`.

For JavaScript and TypeScript, see the [JS SDK Reference](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk).

Follow [Store and serve files from Python with Vercel Blob](/kb/guide/python-and-vercel-blob) to build private receipt storage with uploads, downloads, and per-user authorization in FastAPI.

## Install the SDK

Install the Vercel Python package. It requires Python 3.10 or later:

```bash filename="Terminal"
uv add vercel
```

The `vercel` package includes the Blob SDK from the `vercel-blob` package. To install only the Blob SDK, add `vercel-blob` instead. This page documents `vercel-blob` 0.5.0 and later. Earlier `vercel-blob` releases on PyPI are an unrelated package that doesn't provide the `vercel.blob` module.

The examples on this page use the asynchronous API. You can import it as a module:

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel import blob
```

The SDK creates and reuses a default session when you first use it. Most applications don't need to create one. See [SDK sessions](#sdk-sessions) when you need a custom HTTP client or custom credentials.

## Authentication

By default, the SDK resolves credentials in this order:

1. A Vercel OpenID Connect (OIDC) token, from the current Vercel request or `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`, paired with `BLOB_STORE_ID`
2. `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`, then `VERCEL_BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`

If the SDK finds an OIDC token but `BLOB_STORE_ID` isn't set, and no read-write token is available, it raises `BlobCredentialsError`. `BLOB_STORE_ID` can include the `store_` prefix.

When you [connect a store to a project](/docs/vercel-blob#connecting-a-store-to-your-projects), Vercel adds `BLOB_STORE_ID` and the OIDC token to the project, so code running on Vercel works without configuration. For local development, run `vercel link` and `vercel env pull`, then load `.env.local` into your Python process with a tool such as `python-dotenv`. When a development OIDC token expires, the SDK refreshes it with your Vercel CLI credentials.

To supply credentials from your own configuration, pass a credentials factory to the session. See [Configure Blob](#configure-blob).

## The `access` argument

Uploads, copies, and downloads require `access="public"` or `access="private"`, and the value must match the store's [access mode](/docs/vercel-blob#private-and-public-storage). `head_blob()`, `delete_blob()`, `query_blobs()`, and `query_blob_entries()` don't take an `access` argument.

## Pathnames and URLs

Operations that read, inspect, copy, or delete a blob accept either a pathname or a Blob delivery URL. Uploads and copy destinations accept a pathname.

A pathname is a literal object name relative to the store, not a URL-encoded string or a local file path. The SDK removes one leading slash and rejects:

- Empty pathnames
- Control characters and invalid Unicode
- `//`
- `.` and `..` path segments

Pathnames for `put_blob()`, `multipart_upload_blob()`, and `copy_blob()` destinations can contain up to 950 UTF-16 code units, the same limit as the JS SDK. Characters outside the Unicode Basic Multilingual Plane count as two units.

The SDK encodes characters such as `?`, `#`, and `%` when it builds a delivery URL from a pathname. Delivery URLs must use HTTPS and a `<store-id>.<access>.blob.vercel-storage.com` host. The SDK keeps query strings, removes fragments, and doesn't follow redirects. Custom delivery domains aren't supported.

A private delivery URL must belong to the store identified by your credentials. You can download a public delivery URL without credentials, but a pathname always needs credentials to identify the store.

> **💡 Note:** Pathname validation isn't a shell-escaping or filesystem-safety guarantee.
> Don't use untrusted pathnames as commands or unchecked local file paths.

## Upload a blob

### `put_blob()`

Upload bytes to a blob:

```python filename="main.py"
import asyncio

from vercel import blob


async def main() -> None:
    uploaded = await blob.put_blob(
        "reports/summary.txt",
        b"Quarterly summary",
        access="private",  # or "public"
        add_random_suffix=True,
    )
    print(uploaded.url)


asyncio.run(main())
```

`put_blob()` accepts these arguments:

| Parameter               | Type                                          | Default  | Description                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pathname`              | `str`                                         | Required | Destination pathname in the store.                                                                                                |
| `body`                  | `bytes \| bytearray \| memoryview \| PutBody` | Required | Content to upload. See [Stream an upload](#stream-an-upload) for streaming sources.                                               |
| `access`                | `"public" \| "private"`                       | Required | Must match the store's access mode.                                                                                               |
| `content_length`        | `int \| None`                                 | `None`   | Length in bytes. Optional for in-memory buffers and required for streaming sources.                                               |
| `content_type`          | `str \| None`                                 | `None`   | Media type to store. When omitted, Vercel Blob determines it.                                                                     |
| `add_random_suffix`     | `bool`                                        | `False`  | Add a random suffix to the pathname to avoid collisions.                                                                          |
| `allow_overwrite`       | `bool`                                        | `False`  | Replace an existing blob at the same pathname. Without it, uploading to an existing pathname fails.                               |
| `cache_control_max_age` | `int \| None`                                 | `None`   | Cache lifetime in whole seconds. The service default of one month applies when omitted. See [Caching](/docs/vercel-blob#caching). |

`put_blob()` copies in-memory buffers when you call it, so later changes to a `bytearray` don't affect the upload. It returns a `PutResult`:

| Property              | Type  | Description                                                          |
| --------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`                 | `str` | Blob delivery URL.                                                   |
| `download_url`        | `str` | Delivery URL that forces a download.                                 |
| `pathname`            | `str` | Stored pathname, including the random suffix when you requested one. |
| `content_type`        | `str` | Stored media type.                                                   |
| `content_disposition` | `str` | Stored `Content-Disposition` header value.                           |
| `etag`                | `str` | Entity tag for the stored content.                                   |

`PutResult` doesn't include the blob's size or upload time. Use [`head_blob()`](#head_blob) to retrieve them. When you set `add_random_suffix=True`, use the returned `pathname` or `url` to refer to the blob.

### Stream an upload

`put_blob()` also accepts streaming sources when you pass `content_length`. Each API accepts only sources of its own shape:

| API                | Accepted streaming sources                                                      |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vercel.blob`      | `AsyncByteReader`, an object with `async def read()`, or `AsyncIterable[bytes]` |
| `vercel.blob.sync` | `SyncByteReader`, an object with a blocking `read()`, or `Iterable[bytes]`      |

The SDK sends exactly `content_length` bytes with a `Content-Length` header and doesn't spool the source to a temporary file. If the source ends early or produces more bytes, the SDK raises `BlobContentLengthError` and doesn't send the excess data. Uploads with an unknown length aren't supported.

Streaming sources remain yours: the SDK doesn't close, seek, or retry them, and a source's position is unspecified after a failed upload.

The asynchronous API doesn't run blocking reads on worker threads for you, and it raises `TypeError` for sync readers and sync iterables, such as a file opened with `open()`. Pass an async byte reader from your async file library, or wrap blocking reads in an async iterable. This example reads a local file on a worker thread:

```python filename="main.py"
import asyncio
import os
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from typing import BinaryIO

from vercel import blob

CHUNK_SIZE = 64 * 1024


async def read_in_thread(file: BinaryIO) -> AsyncIterator[bytes]:
    # Read each chunk on a worker thread so the event loop isn't blocked
    while chunk := await asyncio.to_thread(file.read, CHUNK_SIZE):
        yield chunk


async def upload_report() -> blob.PutResult:
    with open("report.pdf", "rb") as file:
        return await blob.put_blob(
            "reports/report.pdf",
            read_in_thread(file),
            access="private",
            content_length=os.fstat(file.fileno()).st_size,
        )
```

## Upload a blob in parts

### `multipart_upload_blob()`

Use `multipart_upload_blob()` when you want to choose each part of a large upload. Enter it with `async with`, upload parts in order, and the SDK publishes the blob when the block exits successfully:

```python filename="main.py"
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

from vercel import blob

PART_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024


async def first_part() -> AsyncIterator[bytes]:
    for _ in range(80):
        yield b"x" * (64 * 1024)


async def upload_parts() -> blob.PutResult:
    async with blob.multipart_upload_blob(
        "videos/intro.bin",
        access="private",
    ) as upload:
        await upload.upload_part(first_part(), content_length=PART_SIZE)
        await upload.upload_part(b"tail")

    return upload.result
```

`multipart_upload_blob()` accepts `pathname`, `access`, `content_type`, `add_random_suffix`, `allow_overwrite`, and `cache_control_max_age` with the same meaning as in [`put_blob()`](#put_blob). Don't await the returned upload; enter it as a context manager.

`upload_part(body, *, content_length=None)` accepts the same bodies as `put_blob()`. It infers the length of in-memory buffers and requires `content_length` for streaming sources. The SDK numbers parts in the order you upload them and tracks their entity tags, so there are no part numbers or manual completion step.

Parts follow these rules:

- Each part contains between 1 byte and 5 GiB, and an upload contains at most 10,000 parts.
- Every part except the last one must contain at least 5 MiB. The SDK rejects a part that follows a smaller part before reading its source.
- Upload one part at a time. Overlapping `upload_part()` calls fail the upload, and the SDK doesn't retry failed parts.
- An upload with no parts raises `BlobError` on exit. Use `put_blob(pathname, b"", ...)` to create an empty blob.

A successful exit from the `async with` block, including an early `return` or `break`, publishes the uploaded parts and sets `upload.result` to a `PutResult`. An exception or cancellation inside the block prevents publishing. A failed part fails the whole upload, even if you catch its exception, and exiting the block then raises `BlobError` instead of publishing a partial blob. Reading `upload.result` before a successful exit raises `BlobError`.

> **💡 Note:** Vercel Blob has no abort action for multipart uploads. When an upload fails,
> the SDK doesn't delete the parts it already sent. If the completion response
> is lost, the blob may or may not be published, and the SDK doesn't retry
> completion.

## Download a blob

### `get_blob()`

Download a complete blob into memory:

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel import blob

result = await blob.get_blob("reports/summary.txt", access="private")
print(result.metadata.content_type)
print(result.body.decode())
```

`get_blob()` accepts a pathname or delivery URL and `access`. It returns a `GetResult` with `metadata`, a [`DownloadMetadata`](#download-metadata) value, and `body`, the complete content as `bytes`. The SDK closes the response before returning, and a read error raises an exception instead of returning a partial body.

### `stream_blob()`

Read a blob incrementally without buffering it in memory:

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel import blob

received = 0
async with blob.stream_blob("videos/intro.bin", access="private") as download:
    print(download.metadata.size)
    async for chunk in download:
        received += len(chunk)
```

`stream_blob()` accepts the same arguments as `get_blob()`. Don't await it; enter it with `async with`. Entering the block sends the request, so `download.metadata` is available before you read the body.

A download has one consumer. Iterate it once inside its block. Each chunk contains at most 64 KiB. The SDK closes the response at the end of the content, when the block exits early, and on read errors or cancellation. You can also close it with `await download.aclose()`. The SDK doesn't restart partial downloads.

This FastAPI route streams a private blob to the browser. A background task closes the download after the response finishes:

```python filename="main.py"
from contextlib import AsyncExitStack

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from starlette.background import BackgroundTask

from vercel import blob

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/api/file")
async def get_file(pathname: str) -> StreamingResponse:
    # Your auth goes here

    stack = AsyncExitStack()
    try:
        download = await stack.enter_async_context(
            blob.stream_blob(pathname, access="private")
        )
    except blob.BlobNotFoundError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Not found") from None

    return StreamingResponse(
        download,
        media_type=download.metadata.content_type,
        headers={"X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff"},
        background=BackgroundTask(stack.aclose),
    )
```

### Download metadata

`GetResult.metadata` and `download.metadata` are `DownloadMetadata` values derived from the response:

| Property              | Type                | Description                                |
| --------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `url`                 | `str`               | Delivery URL the SDK requested.            |
| `status_code`         | `int`               | HTTP status code.                          |
| `size`                | `int \| None`       | Value of the `Content-Length` header.      |
| `content_type`        | `str \| None`       | Value of the `Content-Type` header.        |
| `content_disposition` | `str \| None`       | Value of the `Content-Disposition` header. |
| `cache_control`       | `str \| None`       | Value of the `Cache-Control` header.       |
| `etag`                | `str \| None`       | Value of the `ETag` header.                |
| `last_modified`       | `datetime \| None`  | Parsed `Last-Modified` header.             |
| `headers`             | `Mapping[str, str]` | All response headers.                      |

Header-derived properties are `None` when the response omits the header. `metadata.size` stays `None` without a `Content-Length` header, even after `get_blob()` reads the body, so use `len(result.body)` for the number of downloaded bytes.

## Get blob metadata

### `head_blob()`

Retrieve a blob's metadata without downloading its content:

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel import blob

metadata = await blob.head_blob("reports/summary.txt")
print(metadata.size, metadata.uploaded_at)
```

`head_blob()` accepts a pathname or delivery URL and returns a `HeadResult`:

| Property              | Type          | Description                                |
| --------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `url`                 | `str`         | Blob delivery URL.                         |
| `download_url`        | `str`         | Delivery URL that forces a download.       |
| `pathname`            | `str`         | Stored pathname.                           |
| `size`                | `int`         | Size in bytes.                             |
| `etag`                | `str`         | Entity tag for the stored content.         |
| `uploaded_at`         | `datetime`    | Upload time.                               |
| `content_type`        | `str \| None` | Stored media type.                         |
| `content_disposition` | `str`         | Stored `Content-Disposition` header value. |
| `cache_control`       | `str`         | Stored `Cache-Control` header value.       |

## List blobs

### `query_blobs()`

Iterate over the blobs in a store, including blobs in nested folders:

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel import blob

total_bytes = 0
async for item in blob.query_blobs(prefix="reports/"):
    print(item.pathname, item.size)
    total_bytes += item.size
```

`query_blobs()` returns an async iterator and follows pagination cursors automatically. Don't await it; iterate it with `async for`. It accepts these keyword arguments:

| Parameter   | Type          | Default | Description                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `prefix`    | `str \| None` | `None`  | Literal pathname prefix. Only blobs whose pathname starts with it are returned.             |
| `page_size` | `int \| None` | `None`  | Maximum number of blobs fetched per request, from 1 to 1,000. The service default is 1,000. |
| `cursor`    | `str \| None` | `None`  | Opaque cursor at which to start listing. The iterator follows later cursors itself.         |

`page_size` doesn't limit the total number of blobs the iterator yields. To stop early, break out of the loop. The iterator doesn't fetch further pages after you stop.

Creating the iterator doesn't send a request. The SDK validates the arguments and fetches the first page when iteration begins, then fetches each following page only after it yields the current page's blobs. Errors propagate during iteration, and the SDK doesn't retry or restart the listing. A listing isn't a snapshot, so blobs that change while you iterate may or may not appear. Iterate within the session that created the iterator.

Each item is a `ListBlob`:

| Property       | Type       | Description                          |
| -------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `url`          | `str`      | Blob delivery URL.                   |
| `download_url` | `str`      | Delivery URL that forces a download. |
| `pathname`     | `str`      | Stored pathname.                     |
| `size`         | `int`      | Size in bytes.                       |
| `uploaded_at`  | `datetime` | Upload time.                         |
| `etag`         | `str`      | Entity tag for the stored content.   |

`ListBlob` doesn't include the content type or cache settings. Use [`head_blob()`](#head_blob) to retrieve them for a single blob.

### `query_blob_entries()`

Browse one folder level at a time. `query_blob_entries()` yields `ListBlob` values for the blobs directly inside the prefix and `BlobPrefix` values for its subfolders:

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel import blob


async def print_tree(prefix: str = "", indent: str = "") -> None:
    async for entry in blob.query_blob_entries(prefix=prefix):
        match entry:
            case blob.BlobPrefix(prefix=folder):
                print(f"{indent}{folder.removeprefix(prefix)}")
                await print_tree(folder, indent + "  ")
            case blob.ListBlob(pathname=pathname, size=size):
                print(f"{indent}{pathname.removeprefix(prefix)} ({size} bytes)")
```

`query_blob_entries()` accepts the same `prefix`, `page_size`, and `cursor` arguments as `query_blobs()` and paginates the same way. These rules also apply:

- A nonempty `prefix` must end with `/`. Omit it, or pass `""`, to browse the root of the store. The SDK doesn't normalize or URL-decode prefixes.
- `BlobPrefix.prefix` contains the subfolder's full prefix, including its trailing slash, so you can pass it to another `query_blob_entries()` call. Folders are virtual groupings of pathnames, not stored blobs, so they have no size or entity tag.
- `page_size` counts both blobs and folders. Within each page, blobs come before folders, and there's no sort order across pages.

## Copy a blob

### `copy_blob()`

Copy a blob to a new pathname in the same store:

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel import blob

draft = await blob.head_blob("drafts/getting-started.md")

published = await blob.copy_blob(
    draft.url,
    "published/getting-started.md",
    access="private",
    content_type="text/markdown",
    cache_control_max_age=3600,
    if_match=draft.etag,
)
print(published.url)
```

Vercel Blob copies the content on the server, so the SDK doesn't download the source. `copy_blob()` accepts these arguments:

| Parameter               | Type                    | Default  | Description                                                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `source`                | `str`                   | Required | Pathname or delivery URL of the blob to copy.                                                    |
| `pathname`              | `str`                   | Required | Destination pathname in the same store.                                                          |
| `access`                | `"public" \| "private"` | Required | Must match the store's access mode.                                                              |
| `content_type`          | `str \| None`           | `None`   | Media type to store on the copy.                                                                 |
| `add_random_suffix`     | `bool`                  | `False`  | Add a random suffix to the destination pathname.                                                 |
| `allow_overwrite`       | `bool`                  | `False`  | Replace an existing blob at the destination. Without it, copying to an existing pathname fails.  |
| `cache_control_max_age` | `int \| None`           | `None`   | Cache lifetime in whole seconds. The service default of one month applies when omitted.          |
| `if_match`              | `str \| None`           | `None`   | Entity tag the **source** blob must still have. A mismatch raises `BlobPreconditionFailedError`. |

The copy doesn't inherit the source's content type or cache lifetime. Pass `content_type` and `cache_control_max_age` again when the copy needs them.

`copy_blob()` returns a `CopyResult` with the same properties as [`PutResult`](#put_blob): `url`, `download_url`, `pathname`, `content_type`, `content_disposition`, and `etag`.

## Delete blobs

### `delete_blob()`

Delete one blob, or up to 1,000 blobs in one request, by pathname or delivery URL:

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel import blob

await blob.delete_blob("reports/summary.txt")

await blob.delete_blob(["reports/2025.pdf", "reports/2026.pdf"])
```

`delete_blob()` returns `None`. Deleting a blob that doesn't exist succeeds, but other failures, such as an unknown store, raise an error. Deleted blobs can remain in the CDN cache for up to one minute.

The SDK validates every target before it sends the request, and it doesn't split larger lists into several requests. Batch deletion isn't atomic, and the SDK doesn't retry it, so a failed request can leave some blobs deleted. Because deleting a missing blob succeeds, you can retry the whole batch.

Pass `if_match` to delete a blob only if it still has that entity tag. `if_match` works only with a single target:

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel import blob

metadata = await blob.head_blob("config.json")
await blob.delete_blob("config.json", if_match=metadata.etag)
```

## Synchronous API

The synchronous API mirrors the asynchronous API and doesn't need an event loop. Import it explicitly from `vercel.blob`:

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel.blob import sync as blob

uploaded = blob.put_blob("hello.txt", b"Hello, Blob!", access="private")
try:
    result = blob.get_blob(uploaded.url, access="private")
    print(result.body)

    with blob.stream_blob(uploaded.url, access="private") as download:
        for chunk in download:
            print(len(chunk))

    print(blob.head_blob(uploaded.url).size)
finally:
    blob.delete_blob(uploaded.url)
```

Remove `await` and use regular context managers and iterators. Iterate `query_blobs()` and `query_blob_entries()` with `for`, and close a sync download early with `download.close()`.

The sync `put_blob()` and `upload_part()` accept sync readers, such as open binary files, and sync iterables:

```python filename="main.py"
from pathlib import Path

from vercel.blob import sync as blob

path = Path("report.pdf")
with path.open("rb") as file:
    uploaded = blob.put_blob(
        "reports/report.pdf",
        file,
        access="private",
        content_length=path.stat().st_size,
    )
```

Use the asynchronous API unless your application is synchronous. Don't call the synchronous API from an active async event loop.

## Errors

Catch `BlobError` to handle any Blob service error. Every `BlobError` exposes `status_code` and `code` when they're available. Catch a more specific type when your application can recover differently:

| Error                            | Meaning                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BlobNotFoundError`              | The blob doesn't exist. Also a `FileNotFoundError`.                                                   |
| `BlobAccessError`                | The credentials can't access the blob. Also a `PermissionError`.                                      |
| `BlobCredentialsError`           | The SDK couldn't resolve valid credentials.                                                           |
| `BlobStoreNotFoundError`         | The store doesn't exist.                                                                              |
| `BlobStoreSuspendedError`        | The store is suspended. See [Blocked Blob Store](/docs/vercel-blob/blocked-store).                    |
| `BlobContentTypeNotAllowedError` | The service rejected the content type.                                                                |
| `BlobFileTooLargeError`          | The blob exceeds a size limit.                                                                        |
| `BlobPreconditionFailedError`    | The blob's entity tag didn't match `if_match`, or the blob changed while the operation was in flight. |
| `BlobServiceRateLimited`         | The service rate limited the request. `retry_after` contains the suggested wait in seconds, or `0`.   |
| `BlobServiceNotAvailable`        | The service is temporarily unavailable.                                                               |
| `BlobContentLengthError`         | A streaming source didn't match its `content_length`.                                                 |
| `BlobStreamError`                | A response was malformed or a download was read incorrectly. Also an `OSError`.                       |
| `BlobUnknownError`               | The request failed for an unrecognized reason.                                                        |

Invalid arguments, such as a malformed pathname, raise before the SDK resolves credentials or sends a request. The SDK doesn't retry failed requests.

```python filename="main.py"
from vercel import blob

try:
    metadata = await blob.head_blob("reports/summary.txt")
except blob.BlobNotFoundError:
    metadata = None
except blob.BlobServiceRateLimited as error:
    print(f"Retry in {error.retry_after} seconds")
    raise
```

## Features available in the JS SDK

The Python SDK supports conditional copies and deletes, but it doesn't currently support conditional uploads or conditional reads, renaming blobs, cache bypass on reads, [client uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload), [Vercel Signed URLs](/docs/vercel-blob/vercel-signed-urls), optimized image uploads, or upload progress callbacks. Use the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk) or the [Vercel CLI](/docs/cli/blob) for these operations.

## SDK sessions

An SDK session owns the HTTP connection pool and service clients used by Vercel Python SDK calls. The SDK creates and reuses a default session, so most applications should call the SDK directly. Create an explicit session only when you need to customize its HTTP client or Blob's configuration.

Import `session` from `vercel.api` and use it as an async or sync context manager. It accepts `service_options`, a sequence of service-specific options, and `httpx_client_factory`, a factory for the HTTP client that the session closes when its context exits. See [SDK sessions](/docs/sandbox/python-sdk-reference#sdk-sessions) in the Sandbox Python SDK reference for the full parameter reference.

Nested sessions inherit their parent's configuration. Run Blob calls inside their session's scope, including `stream_blob()` and `multipart_upload_blob()` blocks, and don't use sync Blob calls inside an async session or async Blob calls inside a sync session.

### Configure Blob

Pass `BlobServiceOptions` to configure Blob calls in an async session. This example reads a read-write token and store ID from custom environment variables:

```python filename="main.py"
import asyncio
import os

from vercel import blob
from vercel.api import session


async def resolve_credentials() -> blob.BlobCredentials:
    return blob.BlobCredentials(
        token=os.environ["ACME_BLOB_TOKEN"],
        store_id=os.environ["ACME_BLOB_STORE_ID"],
    )


async def main() -> None:
    options = blob.BlobServiceOptions(credentials_factory=resolve_credentials)

    async with session(service_options=[options]):
        metadata = await blob.head_blob("reports/summary.txt")
        print(metadata.size)


asyncio.run(main())
```

`BlobCredentials` accepts `token`, `store_id`, and `kind`. `kind` defaults to `CredentialKind.READ_WRITE`, and the store ID must match the store in the read-write token. Set `kind=blob.CredentialKind.OIDC` to authenticate with an OIDC token. The SDK calls the factory for each operation that needs credentials, so it can return refreshed tokens, but every call within a session must identify the same store.

`BlobServiceOptions` accepts these parameters:

| Parameter             | Default                                                | Description                                                                             |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `credentials_factory` | Default OIDC and environment resolver                  | Callable that returns `BlobCredentials`. Async sessions accept sync or async callables. |
| `base_url`            | `VERCEL_BLOB_API_URL` or `https://vercel.com/api/blob` | Blob API base URL. Override it only for testing.                                        |

For sync calls, use `SyncBlobServiceOptions` from `vercel.blob.sync` with a synchronous factory and a sync session. The sync API rejects async factories.

title: "Security"
description: "Learn how your Vercel Blob store is secured"
last_updated: "2026-11-05T17:25:46.081Z"
source: "https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/security"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Security

> Vercel Blob is available on all plans
>
> Those with the owner, member, developer role can access this feature

## Private storage

For files that require authentication, use [private storage](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage). Private Blob stores require authentication for all read and write operations. When your code runs on Vercel, the SDK uses OpenID Connect (OIDC) by default. OIDC is preferred over the long-lived `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` because its tokens rotate automatically. Use `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` when code runs outside Vercel or for client uploads. Files in private Blob stores cannot be accessed via public URLs. You deliver them to your users through [Vercel Functions](/docs/functions) where you implement your own authentication logic.

## Public storage security

Vercel Blob URLs, although publicly accessible, are unique and hard to guess when you add a random suffix to the pathname at upload time. They consist of a unique store id, a pathname, and a unique random blob id generated when the blob is created.

> **💡 Note:** This is similar to [Share a file
> publicly](https://support.google.com/drive/answer/2494822?hl=en\&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop#zippy=%2Cshare-a-file-publicly)
> in Google Docs. You should ensure that the URLs are only shared to authorized
> users

Headers that enhance security by preventing unauthorized downloads, blocking external content from being embedded, and protecting against malicious file type manipulation, are enforced on each blob. They are:

- `content-security-policy`: `default-src "none"`
- `x-frame-options`: `DENY`
- `x-content-type-options`: `nosniff`
- `content-disposition`: `inline; filename="filename.extension"` or `attachment; filename="filename.extension"`

### Encryption

All files stored on Vercel Blob are secured using AES-256 encryption. This encryption process is applied at rest and is transparent, ensuring that files are encrypted before being saved to the disk and decrypted upon retrieval.

### Firewall and WAF integration

Vercel Blob is protected by Vercel's [platform-wide firewall](/docs/vercel-firewall#platform-wide-firewall) which provides DDoS mitigation and blocks abnormal or suspicious levels of incoming requests.

You can also protect a store with your own [Vercel WAF](/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf) rules, such as [custom rules](/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/custom-rules), [IP blocking](/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/ip-blocking), and [rate limiting](/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/rate-limiting). To enable it:

1. Open [your Blob store](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%7E%2Fstores%2Fblob%2F%5Bstore%5D%2Fsettings\&title=Go+to+your+Blob+store) in the dashboard and select the **Settings** tab.
2. In the **Firewall** section, select **Protect your store**, then **Enable firewall**.

This connects your store to `vercel-blob-default-project`, a Vercel-managed project that holds the firewall rules for your team's Blob stores. The project is team-wide, so other stores that enable firewall protection reuse it and share its rules. After enabling, Vercel redirects you to the project's firewall page where you create your rules. To update them later, return to the store's **Settings** tab and select **Configure firewall**.

> **⚠️ Warning:** The **Challenge** action serves a JavaScript challenge that only a web
> browser can solve, so requests from the Blob SDKs ([JS](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk) and
> [Python](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference)) and other server-side code fail with a
> 429 response. Only use **Challenge** in rules that never match your
> application's SDK traffic.

The [OWASP core ruleset](/docs/vercel-firewall/vercel-waf/managed-rulesets#configure-owasp-core-ruleset) is not supported for Blob stores.

# Server Uploads with Vercel Blob

> Vercel Blob is available on all plans
>
> Those with the owner, member, developer role can access this feature

In this guide, you'll learn how to do the following:

- Use the Vercel dashboard or the [CLI](/docs/cli/blob) to create a Blob store connected to a project
- Upload a file using the Blob SDK from the server

> **💡 Note:** Vercel has a [4.5 MB request body size
> limit](/docs/functions/limitations#request-body-size) on Vercel Functions. If you
> need to upload larger files, use [client
> uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload).

## Prerequisites

Vercel Blob works with any frontend framework. First, install the SDK. The Python examples in this guide use [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/):

**Terminal**

```bash filename="Terminal" framework=node package-manager="pnpm"
pnpm add @vercel/blob
```

**Terminal**

```bash filename="Terminal" framework=node package-manager="yarn"
yarn add @vercel/blob
```

**Terminal**

```bash filename="Terminal" framework=node package-manager="npm"
npm install @vercel/blob
```

**Terminal**

```bash filename="Terminal" framework=node package-manager="bun"
bun add @vercel/blob
```

**Terminal**

```bash filename="Terminal" framework=fastapi
uv add vercel "fastapi[standard]" python-dotenv
```

- ### Create a Blob store
  Create a Blob store from the dashboard or the Vercel CLI.
  #### Dashboard
  1. Go to your project's [**Storage** section in the sidebar](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F%5Bproject%5D%2Fstores\&title=Go+to+Storage)
  2. Select **Create Storage**, then choose **Blob**
  3. Select **Continue**, then set the access to **Private** or **Public**
  4. Use the name "Images" and select **Create a new Blob store**
  5. Select the environments where you would like the read-write token to be included. **Production** and **Preview** are preselected; include **Development** if you plan to work with the store locally. You can also update the prefix of the Environment Variable in Advanced Options
  Once created, you are taken to the Vercel Blob store page.
  #### CLI
  Run [`vercel blob create-store`](/docs/cli/blob#create-store) from your linked project directory. The `--access` flag is required and accepts `private` or `public`. The `--yes` flag connects the new store to the project in all environments, including **Development**, which `vercel env pull` reads from:
  ```bash filename="terminal"
  vercel blob create-store Images --access private --yes
  ```
  To connect only some environments, use `--environment` instead of `--yes`, once for each environment, for example `--environment production --environment development`.

- ### Prepare your local project
  Since you created the Blob store in a project, we automatically created and added the following Environment Variables to the project for you.

  By default, connected stores use OIDC-based authentication with short-lived, automatically rotated credentials:
  - `BLOB_STORE_ID`: Identifies your Blob store
  - `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`: A short-lived token issued at runtime; rotated automatically
  The following variable is also added as a fallback for code running outside Vercel or to generate client tokens for browser uploads:
  - `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`: A long-lived static read-write token
  To use these Environment Variables locally, we recommend pulling them with the Vercel CLI:
  ```bash
  vercel env pull
  ```
  > **💡 Note:** If the Blob variables don't show up in your `.env.local` file, your store
  > connection likely doesn't include the **Development** environment, which is
  > the one `vercel env pull` reads from. You can add it from the store's
  > **Projects** tab: open the context menu (⋯) next to your project, select
  > **Update Project Connection**, and include **Development**.

Server uploads are perfectly fine as long as you do not need to upload files larger than [4.5 MB on Vercel](/docs/functions/limitations#request-body-size). If you need to upload larger files, consider using [client uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload).

## Upload a file using Server Actions

If you use Next.js App Router, you can upload a file to Vercel Blob with a [Server Action](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions-and-mutations):

```tsx filename="app/components/form.tsx" framework="all"
import { put } from '@vercel/blob';
import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache';

export async function Form() {
  async function uploadImage(formData: FormData) {
    'use server';
    const imageFile = formData.get('image') as File;
    const blob = await put(imageFile.name, imageFile, {
      access: 'private' /* or 'public' */,
      addRandomSuffix: true,
    });
    revalidatePath('/');
    return blob;
  }

  return (
    <form action={uploadImage}>
      <label htmlFor="image">Image</label>
      <input
        type="file"
        id="image"
        name="image"
        accept="image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp"
        required
      />
      <button>Upload</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

Read more about [Server Actions](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions-and-mutations) and [App Router](https://nextjs.org/docs) on the Next.js documentation.

## Upload a file using a server upload page and route

You can upload files to Vercel Blob from a server route. The following example shows how to upload a file to Vercel Blob using a server upload page and route.

- ### Create a server upload page
  This page will upload files to your server. The files will then be sent to Vercel Blob.

  **src/app/avatar/upload/page.tsx**
  ```tsx filename="src/app/avatar/upload/page.tsx" framework=nextjs-app
  'use client';

  import type { PutBlobResult } from '@vercel/blob';
  import { useState, useRef } from 'react';

  export default function AvatarUploadPage() {
    const inputFileRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
    const [blob, setBlob] = useState<PutBlobResult | null>(null);
    return (
      <>
        <h1>Upload Your Avatar</h1>

        <form
          onSubmit={async (event) => {
            event.preventDefault();

            if (!inputFileRef.current?.files) {
              throw new Error('No file selected');
            }

            const file = inputFileRef.current.files[0];

            const response = await fetch(
              `/api/avatar/upload?filename=${file.name}`,
              {
                method: 'POST',
                body: file,
              },
            );

            const newBlob = (await response.json()) as PutBlobResult;

            setBlob(newBlob);
          }}
        >
          <input
            name="file"
            ref={inputFileRef}
            type="file"
            accept="image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp"
            required
          />
          <button type="submit">Upload</button>
        </form>
        {blob && (
          <div>
            Blob url: <a href={blob.url}>{blob.url}</a>
          </div>
        )}
      </>
    );
  }
  ```
  **app/avatar/upload/page.jsx**
  ```jsx filename="app/avatar/upload/page.jsx" framework=nextjs-app

            Blob url: <a href={blob.url}>{blob.url}</a>
          </div>
        )}
      </>
    );
  }
  ```
  **pages/avatar/upload.tsx**

  **main.py**
  ```python filename="main.py" framework=fastapi
  from dotenv import load_dotenv
  from fastapi import FastAPI
  from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse

  load_dotenv(".env.local")

  app = FastAPI()

  UPLOAD_PAGE = """<!doctype html>
  <h1>Upload Your Avatar</h1>
  <form id="upload-form">
    <input name="file" type="file" accept="image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp" required />
    <button type="submit">Upload</button>
  </form>
  <p id="result"></p>
  <script>
    document.getElementById("upload-form").addEventListener("submit", async (event) => {
      event.preventDefault();
      const file = event.target.file.files[0];
      const response = await fetch(
        `/api/avatar/upload?filename=${encodeURIComponent(file.name)}`,
        { method: "POST", body: file },
      );
      const blob = await response.json();
      document.getElementById("result").textContent = `Blob url: ${blob.url}`;
    });
  </script>
  """


  @app.get("/avatar/upload", response_class=HTMLResponse)
  async def avatar_upload_page() -> str:
      return UPLOAD_PAGE
  ```

- ### Create a server upload route
  This route forwards the file to Vercel Blob and returns the URL of the uploaded file to the browser.

  **src/app/api/avatar/upload/route.ts**
  ```ts filename="src/app/api/avatar/upload/route.ts" framework=nextjs-app
  import { put } from '@vercel/blob';
  import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';

  export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<NextResponse> {
    const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);
    const filename = searchParams.get('filename');

    const blob = await put(filename, request.body, {
      access: 'private' /* or 'public' */,
      addRandomSuffix: true,
    });

    return NextResponse.json(blob);
  }
  ```
  **src/app/api/avatar/upload/route.js**
  ```js filename="src/app/api/avatar/upload/route.js" framework=nextjs-app
  import { put } from '@vercel/blob';
  import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';

  export async function POST(request) {
    const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);
    const filename = searchParams.get('filename');

    const blob = await put(filename, request.body, {
      access: 'private' /* or 'public' */,
      addRandomSuffix: true,
    });

    return NextResponse.json(blob);
  }
  ```
  **pages/api/avatar/upload.ts**
  ```ts filename="pages/api/avatar/upload.ts" framework=nextjs
  import { put } from '@vercel/blob';
  import type { NextApiResponse, NextApiRequest, PageConfig } from 'next';

  export default async function handler(
    request: NextApiRequest,
    response: NextApiResponse,
  ) {
    const blob = await put(request.query.filename as string, request, {
      access: 'private' /* or 'public' */,
      addRandomSuffix: true,
    });

    return response.status(200).json(blob);
  }

  export const config: PageConfig = {
    api: {
      bodyParser: false,
    },
  };
  ```
  **pages/api/avatar/upload.js**
  ```js filename="pages/api/avatar/upload.js" framework=nextjs
  import { put } from '@vercel/blob';

  export default async function handler(request, response) {
    const blob = await put(request.query.filename, request, {
      access: 'private' /* or 'public' */,
      addRandomSuffix: true,
    });

    return response.status(200).json(blob);
  }

  export const config = {
    api: {
      bodyParser: false,
    },
  };
  ```
  **main.py**
  ```python filename="main.py" framework=fastapi
  from fastapi import Request

  from vercel import blob


  # Add this route to the app from the previous step
  @app.post("/api/avatar/upload")
  async def upload_avatar(filename: str, request: Request) -> blob.PutResult:
      return await blob.put_blob(
          filename,
          await request.body(),
          access="private",  # or "public"
          add_random_suffix=True,
      )
  ```

### Testing your page

- ### Run your application locally
  Run your application locally and visit `/avatar/upload` to upload the file to your store. The browser will display the unique URL created for the file.

- ### Review the Blob object metadata
  - Go to the Vercel Project where you created the store
  - Open **Storage** in the sidebar and select your new store
  - Paste the blob object URL returned in the previous step in the **Blob URL** input box in the **Browser** section and select **Lookup**
  - The following blob object metadata will be displayed: file name, path, size, uploaded date, content type and HTTP headers
  - You also have the option to download and delete the file from this page

You have successfully uploaded an object to your Vercel Blob store and are able to review its metadata, download, and delete it from your Vercel Storage Dashboard.

## Next steps

- Learn about the methods available in the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk) and the [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference)

# Vercel Blob Pricing

> Vercel Blob is available on all plans
>
> Those with the owner, member, developer role can access this feature

## Usage

Vercel Blob usage is measured based on the following:

- **Storage Size**: Monthly average of your blob store size (GB-month)
- **Simple Operations**: Counts when a blob is accessed by its URL and it's a cache MISS, or when you retrieve blob metadata without downloading the blob
- **Advanced Operations**: Counts when you upload, copy, or list blobs, and when you create a Blob store
- **Blob Data Transfer**: Charged when blobs are downloaded or viewed
- **[CDN Requests](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#cdn-requests)**: Each blob access by its URL counts as one CDN Request, regardless if it's a MISS or HIT
- **[Fast Origin Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-origin-transfer)**: Applied only for cache MISS scenarios

See the [usage details](#usage-details) and [pricing example](#pricing-example) sections for more information on how usage is calculated.

> **💡 Note:** Stored files are referred to as "blobs" once they're in the storage system,
> following cloud storage terminology.

## Pricing

| Resource | Price | Included (Pro) | Included (Hobby) |
|----------|-------|----------------|-----------------|
| [Blob Storage Size](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#pricing) | Regional | Usage-based | 1GB/month |
| [Blob Simple Operations](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#pricing) | Regional | Usage-based | First 10,000 |
| [Blob Advanced Operations](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#pricing) | Regional | Usage-based | First 2,000 |
| [Blob Data Transfer](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#pricing) | Regional | Flat Rate CDN | First 10 GB |


<br />

> **💡 Note:** [CDN Requests](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#cdn-requests) and [Fast Origin
> Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-origin-transfer) for blobs are billed
> at standard [CDN rates](/docs/cdn#pricing-and-usage). The included resource usage for
> the Hobby plan is shared across all Vercel services in your project.

## Usage details

- Cache HITs do not count as Simple Operations
- Cache HITs do not incur Fast Origin Transfer charges
- The maximum size of a blob in cache is [512 MB](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#size-limits). Any blob larger than this will generate a cache MISS on every access, resulting in a Fast Origin Transfer and CDN Request charge each time it is accessed
- Uploads do not incur data transfer charges when using [Client Uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload)
- Uploads incur [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-data-transfer) charges when using [Server Uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/server-upload) if your Vercel application is the one receiving the file upload
- [Multipart uploads](/docs/vercel-blob#multipart-uploads) count as multiple Advanced Operations: one when starting, one per part, one for completion
- Creating a Blob store counts as one Advanced Operation; deleting a store is free
- Delete operations are free
- **Dashboard interactions count as operations**: Each time you interact with the Vercel dashboard to browse your blob store, upload files, or view blob details, these actions count as Advanced Operations and will appear in your usage metrics.

## Private and public storage delivery costs

Private and public Blob stores are priced the same for storage, operations, and uploads. The difference is in how files are delivered, which affects data transfer costs.

**Private blob delivery** (e.g. a 10 KB document served through a [Function](/docs/functions)):

- Your Function fetches the blob from the store, then streams it to the browser
- You pay [Blob Data Transfer](/docs/vercel-blob#blob-data-transfer) + [Fast Origin Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-origin-transfer) on cache miss for the Function-to-store fetch, plus [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/cdn) + [Fast Origin Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-origin-transfer) for the Function-to-browser response

**Public blob delivery** (e.g. a 150 KB image on a page):

- The browser fetches the blob directly from the store
- You pay [Blob Data Transfer](/docs/vercel-blob#blob-data-transfer) + [Fast Origin Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-origin-transfer) on cache miss
- Blob Data Transfer (BDT) is 3x more cost-efficient than Fast Data Transfer (FDT) on average

For full details on how delivery works, see [delivering private blobs](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#delivering-private-blobs) and [delivering public blobs](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage#delivering-public-blobs).

## Hobby

Vercel Blob is free for Hobby users within the [usage limits](#pricing).

Vercel will send you emails as you are nearing your usage limits. You **will not pay for any additional usage**. However, you will not be able to access Vercel Blob if limits are exceeded. In this scenario, you will have to wait until 30 days have passed before using Blob storage again.

To remove these limits, you can start a Pro trial using the button below.

## Pro

You pay for usage using your [monthly credit](/docs/plans/pro-plan#monthly-credit), which switches to on-demand once you have used it.

Pro teams can [set up Spend Management](/docs/spend-management#managing-your-spend-amount) to get notified or to automatically take action, such as [using a webhook](/docs/spend-management#configuring-a-webhook) or pausing your projects when your usage hits a set spend amount.

## Enterprise

Vercel Blob Enterprise pricing is custom. Contact your account team for contracted rates and support questions.

## Pricing Example

Let's say during one month of usage, you upload 120,000 blobs of which 30% (36,000 blobs) are uploaded using multipart uploads with 5 parts each.
Your storage averages 50 GB and your blobs are downloaded 2.5 million times, with a 70% cache HIT ratio (meaning 30% or 750,000 downloads are cache MISSes), for a total of 350 GB of data transfer.

Here's the cost breakdown:

- **Storage**: 50 GB total at $0.023/GB = $1.15
- **Simple Operations**: 750K (30% cache MISSes of 2.5M downloads + head calls) at $0.40/1M = $0.30
- **Advanced Operations**:
  - Single uploads: 84K (70% of 120K blobs)
  - Multipart uploads: 36K × (1 start + 5 parts + 1 completion) = 252K operations
  - Total: 336K at $5.00/1M = $1.68
- **Data Transfer** (iad1): 350 GB total at $0.05/GB = $17.50
- **CDN Requests**: 2.5M requests (all downloads) - 10M included = $0.00
- **Fast Origin Transfer** (iad1): 105 GB (30% cache MISSes of 350 GB) at $0.06/GB = $6.30

**Total**: $26.93/month

## Limits

Vercel Blob has certain [limits](/docs/limits) that you should be aware of when designing your application.

### Store limits

You can create as many Blob stores as you need. Creating a store counts as one [Advanced Operation](#usage). Deleting a store is free.

You pay for storage, operations, and data transfer based on what you use. Splitting the same data across more stores doesn't change those costs. Use separate stores to isolate projects, environments, customers, or public and private content.

### Operation rate limits

| Plan       | Simple Operations | Advanced Operations |
| ---------- | ----------------- | ------------------- |
| Hobby      | 1,200/min (20/s)  | 900/min (15/s)      |
| Pro        | 7,200/min (120/s) | 4,500/min (75/s)    |
| Enterprise | 9,000/min (150/s) | 7,500/min (125/s)   |

**Note:** Rate limits are based on the number of operations, not HTTP requests. For example, when using `del([pathnames])` to delete multiple blobs in one call, each blob deletion counts as a separate operation toward your rate limit. Deleting 100 blobs in a batch counts as 100 operations, not one.

### Size limits

- **Cache Size Limit**: 512 MB per blob
  - Blobs larger than 512 MB will not be cached
  - Accessing these blobs will always count as a cache MISS (generating one [Simple Operation](/docs/vercel-blob#simple-operations))
  - These large blobs will also incur [Fast Origin Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-origin-transfer) charges for each access

- **Maximum File Size**: 5TB (5,000GB)
  - This is the absolute maximum size for any individual file uploaded to Vercel Blob
  - For files larger than 100MB, we recommend using [multipart uploads](/docs/vercel-blob#multipart-uploads)

## Observability

You can monitor and analyze your Vercel Blob usage with the [Observability section in the sidebar](https://vercel.com/d?to=%2F%5Bteam%5D%2F~%2Fobservability%2Fblob\&title=Go+to+Blob+Observability) in the Vercel Dashboard.
